statement: A donation is not void because the donor exercised his liberality and munificence under the influence of affection, whether of creditable affection or of discreditable affection.
supporting_quote: "Affectionis gratia neque honestce, neque inhonestm donationes sunt. prohibitce; honestce erga bent merentes amicos vel necessarios inhonestce circa meretrices " (Digest, XXXIX., tit. 5, section 5)."

statement: A deed of gift is not considered fraudulent if the donor was solvent at the time of the gift and the disposition did not cause them to become insolvent.
supporting_quote: "neither a donation nor sale would be considered fraudulent if the donor or vendor were solvent at the time he made it, and if the disposition had not caused him to cease to be so."

statement: A gift cannot be successfully impeached unless it is shown that the donor defrauded his creditors at the time of the gift.
supporting_quote: "We hold that the deed could not be successfully impeached, unless it were shown that Kandapodi, in gifting away this land, defrauded his creditors;"

statement: The Colombo firm was a branch of the London partnership, and the London liquidator has priority over the Ceylon deed of arrangement.
supporting_quote: "With respect to the first point, we are of opinion that it has been clearly established that the Colombo firm was only a branch of the London house of John Anderson & Co. The partners in both were the same, the business of the same nature, the capital one, and the ratio of profits of the partners in either place the same."

statement: In equity, a defendant notary public is entitled to set off any additional sum recovered by the plaintiff from other debtors against the amount of judgment obtained for misfeasance.
supporting_quote: I am of opinion that in equity, supposing plaintiff to have got judgment against defendant for a certain amount as damages in this case, computed as the difference between what plaintiff could have recovered on his mortgage bond if defendant had not made the mistake and what, plaintiff using all lawful means was actually able to recover; and supposing that plaintiff afterwards by some unforeseen means recovered a further sum from the Janszes, such further sum ought in equity to be set off against the amount of the judgment.

statement: A lessee is not entitled by virtue alone of the title to possession passed to him by the lease to maintain an action of ejectment against a stranger to the lease in respect of lands, of which he, the lessee, was never put into possession by his lessor.
supporting_quote: A lessee is not entitled by virtue alone of the title to possession passed to him by the lease to maintain an action of ejectment against a stranger to the lease in respect of lands, of which he, the lessee, was never put into possession by his lessor.

statement: In Ceylon, as per the Roman-Dutch Law, there is a presumption in favor of marriage rather than concubinage when a man and woman are proved to have lived together as husband and wife.
supporting_quote: "According to the law of Ceylon, as in England, where a man and woman are proved to have lived together as man and wife, the law will presume, unless the contrary be clearly proved, that they were living together in consequence of a valid marriage, and not in a state of concubinage."

statement: A subject can sue the Crown for a declaration of title, but not in an action seeking substantial damages for wrongful possession.
supporting_quote: "The proper order to make in this case is that the case be remitted to the District Court to make the necessary amendments in the pleadings arising out of the undertaking made in open 74 Court by plaintiff's counsel, withdrawing all claims in respect of tort and confining his claim to a simple one of title."

statement: The bond was executed by the defendant for the benefit of the plaintiffs, and not in his personal capacity.
supporting_quote: "It is again important to observe who are the parties to this bond: clearly, Mohamado Cassim Mohamado Usoof and Pe. Le. Venaitirtan Chetty."

statement: A deed of gift creating a fidei commissum must have a valid acceptance to be effective, and the terms of such a deed should not be construed to create multiple separate fidei commissa unless explicitly stated.
supporting_quote: "The defendants also contended that the deed of gift created not one fidei commissum but five separate fidei commissa and that the plaintiffs did not succeed to the share of any of the donees who died without issue or without issue in the male line. In the alternative that if the deed created one fidei commissum the plaintiffs had no interest in the property donated as long as Marthinus was alive."

statement: A notary who attests a deed which by law ought to be stamped, but which bears no stamp, is guilty of attesting a deed insufficiently stamped under sub-section 13 of section 26 of Ordinance No. 2 of 1877.
supporting_quote: "The essence of the offence is that the accused attested this insufficiently stamped deed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 2 of 1877, s. 26, sub-section 13

statement: A mortgage decree against a representative of the deceased mortgagor will estop such representative from questioning the right of the mortgagor to mortgage the lands decreed executable.
supporting_quote: If the representative, who was the widow of the mortgagor, was entitled to the land in her own right, she should not have assumed the representative character imposed on her.

statement: No right of servitude can be claimed in respect of an overhanging tree under the Roman-Dutch Law.
supporting_quote: The reason for it is plain, because the alleged servitude is not a fixed and defined one like that of an overhanging beam, but an ever-varying one with every moment of time and every change of position and bulk.

statement: A cestui que trust can sue a trustee to recover a specific sum of money due under the trust, even if no accounts have been taken.
supporting_quote: "The action is one brought by a cestui que trust to recover a sum of money due him under the trust from the trustee. The plaintiff alleges that a certain definite sum is in the defendant's hands, and if he has proved what he alleged, I cannot see any obstacle whatever to his recovering it in this suit"

statement: It is not possible to set up a mere parol agreement to establish an interest on title to land under Sri Lankan law.
supporting_quote: and by our law. differing in this respect from the English Statute it is not possible to set up a mere parol agreement to establish an interest on title to land.

statement: Upon the death of one spouse, half of the acquired property vests absolutely in the children, subject to the rights of the administrator as to payment of debts.
supporting_quote: "On death of one spouse, half the thediathetam or 'acquired property' vests absolutely in the children, subject to the rights of the administrator as to payment of debts, &c."

statement: The surviving wife, upon the death of her husband, acquires a right to one-half of the property held in community during the marriage, but this is subject to the debts of the deceased. The administrator or executor can only administer and realize such estate as the deceased had testing powers over.
supporting_quote: "On the death of either spouse the other has right to half of the property lately the subject of the marriage community. All that the heirs or legatees of the deceased have right to is the one-half to which the deceased was entitled."

statement: An heir who acquires rights by operation of law, such as through intestate succession, is not considered a purchaser for value and cannot claim priority over the original fraudulent transaction.
supporting_quote: "There is no evidence to support a finding that the second petitioner was in any manner a party to the fraud of her father. It must, therefore, be assumed that so far as her own acts are concerned, she is innocent of any fraud. But her innocence does not help her. She is a mere volunteer so far as the devolution of the right under the otty deed is concerned, for she acquired those rights by operation of the law of intestate succession, and was therefore not a purchaser for value."

statement: A District Court has no jurisdiction to interfere in the concerns of religious communities unless, in the rules which any religious community has made for its members in relation to the religious object which it has combined to maintain and support, a civil element enters, which brings the matter within the sphere of the civil jurisdiction of the courts.
supporting_quote: "A District Court has no jurisdiction to interfere in the concerns of religious communities unless, in the rules which any religious community has made for its members in relation to the religious object which it has combined to maintain and support, a civil element enters, which brings the matter within the sphere of the civil jurisdiction of the courts."

statement: A contract relating to immovable property entered into by a minor without the sanction of a competent Court with or by a guardian is prima facie void against such minor, but can be ratified by the minor after attaining majority.
supporting_quote: "Where a contract entered into by a minor with or without the assistance of a guardian or by a guardian on behalf of a minor has been executed by the alienation of immovable property of the minor without the sanction of a Court, the alienation is prima facie void, as against the minor, and the guardian before majority or the minor, during or after a minority is entitled to vindicate the property. But the alienation is not strictly devoid of legal effect in as much as it is not open to the alienee to assert that the alienation was invalid, as the alienation is capable of being made binding on the minor by being ratified either expressly or impliedly by him on his attaining majority, and as the alienation will be held to be valid even as against the minor where the alienee has been misled, 'by the minor expressly or impliedly representing himself to be of full age.'"

statement: When the provisions of a Colonial Statute are identical with those of an English Statute, the Colonial Courts should follow the decisions of the Court of Appeal on the Imperial Statute.
supporting_quote: "When the provisions of a Colonial Statute are identical with those of an English Statute, the Colonial Courts should follow the decisions of the Court of Appeal on the Imperial Statute."

statement: The District Court should have investigated the claimant's application under sections 241 and 242 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: Held, that it was not competent to the District Court to refer the claimant to a separate action, but that her claim was one to be investigated and determined under sections 241 and 242.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 241

statement: A sale by a Fiscal does not necessarily divest an execution-debtor of all right in the property until the Fiscal's conveyance is registered, and even then, the debtor may still lease, mortgage, or sell the property.
supporting_quote: My opinion is that, as the Fiscal could transfer a debtor's property only if he strictly conformed to the provision of the Ordinance No. 4 of 1867, the purchaser got, because the Fiscal could give, nothing except by written conveyance in the terms laid down in the schedule to the Ordinance.

statement: A tenant is not liable to pay rent to a new landlord unless there is an express contract of lease with the new landlord or an implied attornment or assignment by the previous landlord.
supporting_quote: For I cannot discover under what contract, express or implied, the defendant is bound to pay plaintiff this money. It is clearly under no express contract of lease with the plaintiff. At the date of plaintiff's lease defendant, as the plaintiff alleged, was a monthly tenant of Laity Ramanaden.

statement: District Judges should not give effect to merely technical objections that prevent the administration of justice.
supporting_quote: "It is 'not the duty of a Judge to throw technical difficulties in the way' of the administration of justice, but when he sees that he is 'prevented receiving material or available evidence merely by reason of a technical objection, he ought to remove the technical objection out of the way upon proper terms as to costs and otherwise.'"

statement: The builder of a house on another man's land does not acquire a saleable right to the house, but the house becomes the property of the owner of the soil.
supporting_quote: A house becomes the property of the owners of the soil on which it is built.

statement: A wife, who lives apart from her husband by mutual consent, cannot validly alienate property belonging to the marriage community.
supporting_quote: A wife, who lives apart from her husband by mutual consent, cannot validly alienate property belonging to the marriage community. Semble , per Bonser C. J .

statement: The District Judge should have discharged the order for delivery of possession and made an interlocutory order dismissing the petition.
supporting_quote: "The District Judge ought also to have discharged the order for delivery, and we now discharge it under the powers of revision given by section 753."

statement: A notarial lease is a pro tanto alienation, and gives the lessee during his term the legal remedies of an owner and possessor.
supporting_quote: "It appears that, according to the Roman Law, where a land or house was let, the 'conductor,' who in the case of hind was termed colonus, and in the case of a house inquilinus, was not regarded as possessing the demised premises, for he did not claim to hold them ut dominus, which was of the essence of possession, so that the lessor was still the possessor, notwithstanding the letting. If, therefore, the tenant were ejected by a third person, he was not entitled to the action rei vindicatio, nor to the ordinary possessory interdicts. But by the Roman-Dutch Law, where a lease was for a substantial period, the tenant had the right to sue his lessor to compel him to give up the use of the premises during the term, and was not restricted to an action for damages for breach of contract."

statement: A District Judge has no right to delay the forwarding of a case in due course to the Supreme Court after the appeal has been perfected.
supporting_quote: "A District Judge has no right to delay the forwarding of a case in due course to the Supreme Court after the appeal has been perfected."

statement: A plaintiff must possess the title they are seeking at the time of filing a suit for declaration of title.
supporting_quote: "When this plaintiff brought this action he had not got a conveyance: he was not entitled to possession, he was not the owner of the land. The action must necessarily be dismissed, with costs."

statement: A minor holding a general power of attorney for his principal abroad is competent to act as his agent for the limited purposes mentioned in section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: The question here is really this,-May not a minor holding the general powers of attorney for his principal abroad, which is indicated in section 25 (6) of the Civil Procedure Code, act as a recognized agent for the limited powers mentioned in section 24 ? The said Somasundaram Chetty holds such a power; then why should he be not allowed to appear and act as the recognized agent of his principal ?
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 24

statement: The proviso of section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code is competent for the District Court to appoint a person to represent the deceased mortgagor's estate for the purposes of an action intended to recover a mortgage debt, even if the deceased had died before the Code came into operation.
supporting_quote: The proviso stands independently of the testamentary chapters of the Code, and applies to cases where the deceased had died before as well as after the Code came into operation.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 642

statement: A creditor cannot sue under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code to establish a claim for another, such as a mortgagor's title by prescriptive possession.
supporting_quote: "The words are limited to his claim and prima facie relating to his own personal claim in and for his own personal rights have no words added thereto, which would give them this larger effect of establishing a claim for another, although in its other parts the section is so suggestive of and helpful to establish a claim through another."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The judge had the discretion to order a pleading to be taken off the file when the proceedings were unauthorized, but this was not warranted in the circumstances of the case.
supporting_quote: It has not been usual, so far as I can find, to order a pleading to be 'taken off the file' when the proceedings are unauthorized. In the English Equity cases an opportunity is given to perfect the authority, if possible.

statement: A plaintiff who reduces a claim by amendment of plaint, reducing the class of the case, is entitled to pay stamp duty as on an action in the lower class.
supporting_quote: Where a plaintiff, by reducing his claim by amendment of plaint, reduces the class of the case, the stamp duty payable on proceedings after such amendment is as on an action in the lower class.

statement: The owner of an undivided share of a land may, in support of his claim to such share, call evidence to show that he had taken the produce of a certain number of trees in the garden.
supporting_quote: It is quite competent for the owners of undivided shares to make arrangements among themselves as to the enjoyment of the produce of the land, and evidence showing that the plaintiff had enjoyed the fruit of these trees would go to support his title to 5/16 .

statement: An agent who acts without formal authority from the principal is not personally liable for damages if there was no fraudulent intent or recklessness, and the agent did not enter into a valid contract with the third party.
supporting_quote: "Held , per Withers, J., and Browne, A.J. (dissentiente Lawrie, A.C.J .), that, in the absence of fraudulent intent or recklessness, A was not personally liable in damages ; and that he had not entered into a valid contract with C, nor was he under a legal duty to him to state the truth."

statement: The effect of a certificate of sale signed by the Government Agent under section 22 of Ordinance No. 11 of 1878 is not to dispense with proof that the grain duty was in arrear and that a sale took place in accordance with the Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The effect of a certificate of sale signed by the Government Agent under section 22 of the Ordinance No. 11 of 1878, is not to dispense with proof that the grain duty was in arrear and that a sale took place in accordance with the Ordinance."

statement: A will that refers to a property being enjoyed by children and their descendants for as long as the law allows, creates a fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: "I think there can be little doubt that it was the intention of the testatrix to impress a fidei commissum on the property, in the interest of the three children and their descendants, for such time as the law might allow to be possessed by them, and no others."

statement: In a case where the mortgage decree has been executed and followed by possession, the title of the person who obtained the property through judicial sale takes precedence over a subsequent private conveyance.
supporting_quote: "This case again differs from Government Agent v. Hendrickhamy (3 G. L. R. 86), for the land there was the subject of a judicial sale between the mortgage decree and execution thereof."

statement: A mortgage bond can be satisfied by the delivery and acceptance of goods equivalent to money, provided such payment does not contradict or vary the original contract.
supporting_quote: I conceive it to be good law that the breach of even a notarial contract for payment of interest in money may be satisfied by delivery and acceptance of goods, or other consideration equivalent to money in satisfaction of the interest.

statement: The defendant's possession was not interrupted or disturbed within the ten years preceding the action, thus entitling him to a decree in his favor.
supporting_quote: "I do not know who is the Peris Sinho by whom he mentions an attempt was made to disturb him 'five or eight years ago,' and as to what Susey Pulle did when he 'tried to oust' defendant and the latter shot a man in 'regular riot.' No particulars are given. It may be that not a man ever set foot on the land itself, nor that the defendant was a loser of a not thereby."

statement: A broker is entitled to commission on a sale which he negotiated if the relation of buyer and seller was really caused and brought about by what the broker did.
supporting_quote: "The 'question whether the agent is entitled to be paid commission' on the sale has been often litigated, and the rule has been to 'hold that there has been a sale by an agent, which would entitle him to such commission if the relation of buyer and seller has been really caused and brought about by what he has done, if in other words he was the causa causans by which the property was sold.'"

statement: An action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code for a debt of Rs. 39.95 should have been brought in the Court of Requests, regardless of the value of the land involved.
supporting_quote: Held, that as the value of the right that the plaintiff was seeking to establish was Rs. 39 . 95 , his action under section 247 should have been brought in the Court of Requests, although the value of the land affected was in excess of the jurisdiction of such Court.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The burden of proving the authenticity of a will lies on the petitioner, and they should begin with presenting evidence.
supporting_quote: Where in a proceeding to obtain probate of a will the Judge, on objection raised by the respondent on the petition for probate, frames the issue, 'Did the deceased execute the will or not? '- the burden of proving the affirmative of such issue lies on the petitioner, and ho should begin.

statement: A payment made by a possessor interrupts prescription under section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance No. 22 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "such payment, if true, was an acknowledgment of a right existing in 0, and interrupted prescription under section 3 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, s. 3

statement: A legatee may maintain an action for the legacy against the executor of the will without alleging or proving the latter's assent to the request, nor need he allege or prove sufficiency of assets in the hands of the executor to meet the request.
supporting_quote: "Neither section 720 (b) of the Civil Procedure Code nor the provisions of the Code for judicial settlement of executors' accounts have the effect of taking away the legatee's right to such action."

statement: In a petition under section 712 of the Civil Procedure Code to discover property withheld from an executor, if the respondent puts in an affidavit claiming to be owner of such property, the Court can only dismiss the petition and cannot order costs.
supporting_quote: The Court had no power to dismiss the petition with costs, for there are no costs in these cases. The present respondent was not there as a party to contested proceedings. She was simply cited as a witness under section 712, and section 713 provides that persons so cited need take no notice of the citation unless it is accompanied with payment or tender of the sum required by law to be paid or tendered to a witness subpoenaed to attend a trial in a civil court.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 712-Discovery of property withheld from an executor-'Costs

statement: In an action rei vindicatio by a person deriving title from a grantee under the Crown, the plaintiff must prove some entry on, or exercise of right over, the land by his vendors in addition to the bare fact of its being included in the Crown plan attached to the grant.
supporting_quote: "In an action rei vindicatio by a person deriving title from a grantee under the Crown, the plaintiff must prove some entry on, or exercise of right over, the land by his vendors " in addition to the bare fact of its being included in the Grown plan " attached to the grant."

statement: A plaintiff who has commenced an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code to challenge a seizure and sale of property is entitled to a declaration that, as at the date of the action, the property was not liable to be seized and sold in execution of a writ, even if the sale has since taken place.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that, when the Judge found that the plaintiff's immovable property had been wrongfully seized and sold to pay another's debt, he ought to have given the plaintiff judgment in the action: he ought to have given him a declaration that at the date of the action the property was not liable to be seized and sold in execution of the defendant's writ, and left the plaintiff to get such benefit from that declaration as he could."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247; section 363

statement: The guarantee of the mortgage did not extend to and bind the members of the firm of Alston, Scott & Co.
supporting_quote: "For the reasons I have given I am of opinion that the guarantee did not extend to or bind the firm of Alston, Scott & Co. There is nothing to show that the members of that firm incurred any subsequent liability to pay the money."

statement: A stipulated payment for breach of contract should be construed as liquidated damages if it is not extravagant, unconscionable, or absurd at the time the agreement was made.
supporting_quote: "It is impossible to lay down any abstract rule as to what it may or may not be extravagant or unconscionable to insist upon, without reference to the particular facts and circumstances which are established in the individual case."

statement: Possession, as defined in clause 3 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, of Crown land for fifteen years prior to alienation thereof by the Crown cannot avail as a plea in bar to a claim to such land by a private individual who has purchased it from the Crown.
supporting_quote: Possession, as defined in clause 3 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, of Crown land for fifteen years prior to alienation thereof by the Crown cannot avail as a plea in bar to a claim to such land by a private individual who has purchased it from the Crown.

statement: The Court of Ceylon has the power to decree specific performance of agreements.
supporting_quote: "Our Courts in Ceylon are Courts of Equity, and I do not doubt that they have power to interfere and decree a specific performance of agreement."

statement: A gift to children not yet born can be valid under certain conditions, but the court must consider the circumstances and events that have occurred since the date of the donation.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me difficult to construe this deed of gift without knowing the circumstances existing at the date of the donation, and the events which have happened since."

statement: A prohibition against alienation without naming the beneficiary is void.
supporting_quote: "Section 3 of that Ordinance provides that 'where the will, deed, or instrument in which any prohibition, restriction, or condition against alienation is contained does not name, describe, or designate the person or persons in whose favour, or for whose benefit such prohibition, restriction, or condition is provided, such prohibition, restriction, or condition shall be absolutely void.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 3 of Ordinance No. 11 of 1876

statement: The Court should not regard a partition suit as one to be decided merely on issues raised by and between the parties, and it ought not to make a decree unless it is perfectly satisfied that the persons in whose favour the decree is asked for are entitled to the property sought to be partitioned.
supporting_quote: "The Court should not regard a partition suit as one to be decided merely on issues raised by and between the parties, and it ought not to make a decree, unless it is perfectly satisfied that the persons in whose favour the decree is asked for are entitled to the property sought to be partitioned."

statement: An action by a member of the public for obstructing a public pathway is not maintainable unless special injury to that individual is proven.
supporting_quote: "In the absence of proof of special injury to plaintiffs, such action was not maintainable."

statement: A plaintiff can at most ask that a conveyance be declared void and the land declared executable to his judgment, not have it cancelled.
supporting_quote: What he could at the most ask was that the conveyance be declared void, and the land declared, executable to his judgment.

statement: An action for the recovery of the balance purchase money of a steam launch sold and delivered cannot be maintained unless brought within one year of such sale and delivery.
supporting_quote: "It may be that 'goods' would not include a British ship, the property in which cannot be transferred by mere sale and delivery, but it is unnecessary to decide this, for in the present case there is no proof that this launch is a British ship. The Master Attendant, with whom this launch is said to have been registered, is not the Registrar of British Ships. That being so this action is not maintainable, for it was not brought within one year after the debt became due."

statement: When an executor or administrator brings an action for the benefit of his testator's or intestate's estate and fails, and is ordered to pay the costs, those costs can be recovered from him personally and not from the estate.
supporting_quote: In the present case the executrix, who had been married in community and had made a joint will with her husband, the testator, whereby certain lands, the property of the community, were settled on the survivor for life with remainder to the children, brought an action in respect of certain lands belonging to the estate, and was condemned to pay the costs. The interest of the executrix in the land, the subject of this present action, being part of the settled land, was accordingly sold by the Fiscal for payment of these costs, and the Fiscal conveyed to the purchaser that interest.

statement: An incoming tenant has no general right of action against the outgoing tenant for damages for waste committed by the latter on the land leased, but facts admitted or proved may disclose liability in the outgoing tenant to the incoming tenant.
supporting_quote: "As a general rule an. incoming tenant has no right of action against the outgoing tenant for damages for waste committed by the latter on the land leased. He must look to his landlord to put him in possession of the land leased in such order as ho and the landlord agreed on. If, however, the outgoing tenant has acted contrary to local custom, facts admitted or proved in a case may disclose liability in him to the incoming tenant."

statement: In the calculation of a lease term, the day on which possession is taken should be included, and the lease expires on the night before the specified end date.
supporting_quote: That being so, at the time that the defendant plucked these nuts the plaintiff's lease had expired and the defendant's lease had begun to run.

statement: Time was of the essence of the contract, and if the four years expired without payment or legal tender of the money, the defendant was absolved from his promise.
supporting_quote: "I would affirm with costs. Withers, J. -I concur."

statement: The purchaser took the lands subject to the mortgage impressed upon them by an order of the Court.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that that, order impressed plaintiff's mortgage on those lands, and, whether or not it is expressed in the Fiscal's conveyance, the purchaser took them subject to the mortgage so impressed upon them."

statement: The transfer of movable property through a contract of sale is complete upon consensus, merx, and pretium, but the risk passes to the purchaser as soon as the contract is complete, while ownership does not fully vest until delivery and payment are made.
supporting_quote: It is true that the risk of the article is with the purchaser as soon as the contract is complete, but the article does not become the purchaser's own till he has secured the vacua possessio of it by 102 delivery and has paid the price, or, if the contract is in writing, has granted the payment of the price.

statement: A will of a 'Mussulman native' under the Charter of 1801 should be construed according to the laws and usages of the Mussulmans, as provided by clause 32 of that Charter.
supporting_quote: "The will of a person falling under the designation "Mussulman native", as used in the Charter of 1801, must be construed, not according to the Roman-Dutch Law, but according to the laws and usages of the Mussulmans, as provided by clause 32 of that Charter."

statement: A preliminary decree in a partition suit should determine the limits and extent of the land sought to be partitioned with as much precision as it adjudicates on the individual interests of the parties, and should include an adequate description of the property by reference to a sufficient sketch, map, or plan.
supporting_quote: The plaintiffs in a partition suit should append a plan or sketch to their plaint, and should lead such proof of the metes and bounds of the land as will enable the Court to adjudicate on that part of the case. The person to whom the commission issues should know precisely what the land is which he has to partition according to the instructions of his commission.

statement: A plaintiff who has satisfactorily proved uninterrupted possession of land for over ten years may be entitled to a declaratory decree even if the benefit of a specific prescription ordinance was not expressly claimed in the plaint.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff has satisfactorily proved that he and Salgado have since the Fiscal's sale in 1883 down to the time of the ouster in 1885 held uninterruptedly his share. I have some doubts as to whether we ought to do more than give plaintiff a merely possessory decree without dealing with the question of title. But my brothers are of opinion that we ought to put and end to this litigation by making a declaratory decree now, and I yield to their opinion."

statement: An action for breach of warranty of title arising from an implied contract can be brought within six years if the vendor had no shadow of a title to the property sold, even without formal notice of legal proceedings resulting in eviction.
supporting_quote: I am unable to agree with that contention. Section 7 appears to me clearly to relate to a case where the agreement or promise or contract or bargain, the breach of which is complained of, was reduced to writing. Now, in this case, the contract to warrant the property sold was not reduced to writing: it is implied from the fact of there being a contract of sale.

statement: A gift to minor children by a parent is not invalid merely because the donees are infant children of the donor, but acceptance must still be proven.
supporting_quote: "These children were one and all incompetent to accept this gift. As I said before, the deed professed to surrender itself and the title deeds to one of the children. Now, the case for the plaintiff was that the fifth plaintiff accepted the gift for the children."

statement: The power of a Court to allow the withdrawal of an action, with liberty to re-institute on the same cause, can be used only on sufficient grounds which ought to be recited in the order.
supporting_quote: The power of a Court to allow the withdrawal of an action, with liberty to re-institute on the same cause, can be used only on sufficient grounds which ought to be recited in the order.

statement: An heir cannot bring an action to recover property which belonged to the estate of a deceased intestate without taking out administration, unless the estate is a small one as defined by law.
supporting_quote: "Now it seems to me, as I said before, that she has misconceived her rights; that she was not competent to bring this action to recover property which belonged to the estate of her mother Anso, either under the old law or the new law, whether the case falls to be decided under the Code or under the law as it existed before the passing of the Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: By section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code of 1889, no estate which amounted to the sum of Rs. 1,000 was to be considered small, and in every case where the estate amounted to or exceeded in value Rs. 1,000 administration should be taken.

statement: Minors cannot be regarded as adiating heirs or parties in possession.
supporting_quote: The retention of an intestate's property by a guardian ad litem is not adiation or possession of such property of the minors represented by him, but such adiation or possession on the part of the minors may take place through a guardian appointed for all purposes over their persons and property before institution of an action.

statement: Among co-heirs the very strongest evidence of adverse possession should be given. In my judgment, such evidence can very rarely prove division unless it comes in the form of notarial conveyances, either cross between the heirs or so specifying the shares they severally deal with at different times as to indicate their acquiescence and possession on that basis.
supporting_quote: Amongst co-heirs the very strongest evidence of adverse possession should be given. In my judgment, such evidence can very rarely prove division unless it comes in the form of notarial conveyances, either cross between the heirs or so specifying the shares they severally deal with at different times as to indicate their acquiescence and possession on that basis.

statement: To obtain a decree of partition, which is binding against all the world, the Court should require parties to prove their title.
supporting_quote: "I regret to find that when this Court repeatedly enjoined the necessity that to obtain a decree of partition, which is binding against all the world (9 S, C, C. 64; 1,375, D. C, Matara; C 6,840, D. C, Colombo; C 4,981, Colombo; Examiner Reports, &c), the Court should require parties to prove their title"

statement: Under the Roman-Dutch Law, a person who buys land in another's name and retains possession becomes the owner of the land if there is no mandate from the other to nominate them as the purchaser.
supporting_quote: According to the weight of evidence the father has always retained the conveyance with the land. This land may yet become the first plaintiff's, but it cannot be said to belong to her now. The judgment is consequently wrong, and the plaintiff's action must be dismissed with costs.

statement: A decree under section 9 of the Partition Ordinance of 1863 would not bind the Crown.
supporting_quote: "But a decree under this section would not bind the Crown."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 9 of the Partition Ordinance of 1863

statement: A man not in possession, whose title is disputed, should not bring a partition suit.
supporting_quote: 'A partition suit should not be brought by a man not in possession, whose title is disputed.'

statement: A Court of competent jurisdiction may proceed under the Partition Ordinance in respect of land subject to a fidei commissum since the Entail and Settlement Ordinance, 1876.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the Court cannot order a sale unless the procedure prescribed by Ordinance No. 11 of 1876 is adopted, and a petition is presented under section 5 of that Ordinance. This has not been done, and the land cannot at present be sold. The Court is of opinion, therefore, that the plaintiff cannot bring a suit under the Partition Ordinance."

statement: The interest created by the joint will of Don Siman de Silva and Nona Baba was not a fidei commissum, but rather an immediate gift to their seven children with restrictions on alienation.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that the deed does not create a fidei commission Each of the seven children take a seventh in fee, no trust is created in them for any one else; the donors clearly expressed 296 their desire that the lands should not be sold or burdened by their children"

statement: The entire moiety settled upon grandchildren is made the subject of one and the same fidei commission.
supporting_quote: "Their Lordships have had little difficulty in coming to the conclusion that according to the terms of the will the entire moiety settled upon grandchildren is made the subject of one and the same fidei commission."

statement: The Supreme Court has power to review a judgment of its own passed in appeal where it appears that fresh evidence has been discovered since such judgment was pronounced.
supporting_quote: The Supreme Court has power to review a judgment of its own passed in appeal where it appears that fresh evidence has been discovered since such judgment was pronounced.

statement: An action to set aside a deed of gift on the complaint of its being inofficiosa is barred after the lapse of three years under section 11 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "An action to set aside a deed of gift on the complaint of its being inofficiosa is barred after the lapse of three years under section 11 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 11 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: Where a mortgagor has sold to a third party the land mortgaged, the mortgagee, in a suit against the mortgagor only, is not entitled to a decree for the sale of the land in execution, but to a money decree only for the debt due on the bond.
supporting_quote: Where a mortgagor has sold to a third party the land mortgaged, the mortgagee, in a suit against the mortgagor only, is not entitled to a decree for the sale of the land in execution, but to a money decree only for the debt due on the bond.

statement: A document is not saved by the proviso to section 7 of Ordinance No. 6 of 1866 if it was not registered within the time frame specified, even if the holder did not register it due to reasons beyond their control.
supporting_quote: "Apart from this sannas, it appears to me that the evidence led by the defendant has not displaced the Crown's presumptive title to the soil of the forest from which the defendants have cleared and appropriated ten acres."
statute_citation_verbatim: Proviso to section 7 of Ordinance No. 6 of 1866: Provided that if it shall be established to the satisfaction of the court before which any such deed, sannas, ola, or other instrument is produced that the same was not registered owing to his absence from the island of the holder thereof, or of his being under some legal disability, or from other causes utterly beyond the control of the person producing if in evidence, such court may allow the production of such deed, sannas, ola, or instrument, and the same shall be received in evidence notwithstanding that it has not been registered.

statement: Partition proceedings are not intended to determine contested questions of title but rather for those whose shares in the land are admitted at least to some extent.
supporting_quote: The primary object of partition proceedings is not to try and determine contested questions of title, and a contest as to title should not be made the subject of such proceedings. They are really meant for those whose shares in the land are admitted at least to some extent.

statement: Probate of a will or letters of administration for trust property need not be stamped under the Stamp Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The words of the Ordinance seem to be conclusive. It may be that the Stamp Ordinance does not contemplate nor provide for a case when the deceased had no property of his own. When administration is sought only to administer trust property, the case may be a casus improvisus. But if it be, the letters are exempt from stamp duty, which is only exigible when clearly imposed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Stamp Ordinance of 1890, s. 28.

statement: If an agreement to sell land contains a stipulation for damages, it may be intended as an alternative obligation rather than a mere accessory to the principal obligation, in which case specific performance cannot be compelled.
supporting_quote: "The answer to this question seems to me to depend on the wording of the agreement and the intention of the parties as indicated by their contract. If the penal stipulation is intended to be merely accessory to the principal obligation, then it is surely open to the seller to exact specific performance. If, on the other hand, the penal stipulation is an alternative obligation, and it is intended that the party making it may break the principal obligation, but shall pay the consequent damages, then the other party is restricted to his right of action to recover those damages."

statement: Sections 325 and 326 of the Civil Procedure Code do not apply to an order for delivery of possession under section 287, as such an order is considered an 'order' rather than a 'decree'.
supporting_quote: "Now, section 217 provides that a decree or order may command the person against whom it operates (c) to yield up possession of immovable property, and therefore we have to ascertain what provision is made for the enforcement of an order under head (c) of section 217. It will be noticed that the word is 'order' and not 'decree.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 325 and 326, sections 287, 217, 323

statement: An order confirming a sale, even without an express order of Court as required by section 58 of Ordinance No. 4 of 1867, can be considered equivalent to such an order if it effectively directs the conveyance.
supporting_quote: "I think, therefore, that the objection ought not to have been upheld."

statement: The rejection of a mortgagee's claim to have property sold subject to the mortgage in an execution proceeding does not bar the mortgagee from subsequently suing on the mortgage bond or seizing the mortgaged property, even if it is later purchased by a third party.
supporting_quote: It seems to me that the refusal did not-touch the mortgagee's rights as against his mortgagor, nor against the land into whosoever possession it might afterwards come.

statement: The owners of undivided shares can make arrangements among themselves as to the enjoyment of the produce of the land, and evidence showing that a co-owner has enjoyed the fruits of certain trees would support his title to an undivided share.
supporting_quote: It is competent for the owners of undivided shares of a land to make arrangements among themselves as to the enjoyment of the produce of the land; and evidence showing that any one co-owner has enjoyed the fruits of a certain number of trees in pursuance of such arrangement would go to support his title to an undivided share of the land.

statement: A surviving spouse can alienate the property of the estate to pay debts.
supporting_quote: It was laid down so long ago as the time of Chief Justice Sir Edward Creasy, that a surviving spouse can alienate the property of the estate to pay debts, and this decision has been followed in the case of Wijeratna v. Abeyweera ( 5 S. C. C. 70), in the case of Pasupathy Chettiar v. Cantar Pandary (8 S. C. C. 118 205), and in case of Hadjiar v. Hendrick Appu et al (2 N. L. R. 26),

statement: A sale of land by the Crown and the issue of a Crown grant to the purchaser do not raise a presumption that the land was one over which the Crown had disposing power.
supporting_quote: "No Ordinance has ever given that privilege to a Crown grant, and this court has never held that there is a presumption."

statement: Parties to a contract should be bound by their bargains, but circumstances may arise where it would be unconscionable to demand performance.
supporting_quote: If the circumstances under which a contract is made remained constant, then it would be all very well, but a state of things may emerge in which it would be unconscionable to demand the ground leased.

statement: An indorsee of a promissory note has the same position as the payee if the indorsee had full notice of matters that would preclude the latter from recovering on the note.
supporting_quote: The position of the indorsee of the note is not better than that of the payee, if the indorsee had full notice of the matters which would preclude the latter from recovering thereon.

statement: Notaries must strictly comply with their legal duties, and neglect to do so is a culpable omission.
supporting_quote: It is of the utmost importance for the welfare of the community that notaries should strictly comply with the duties imposed on them by law. There is a distinction between �neglect� and �failure ': �failure ' may be due to inevitable accident, ' neglect ' is a culpable omission.

statement: A notary public must either personally search the register at the Land Registry or employ someone else to ascertain whether any prior deed affecting the land has been registered before attesting a deed.
supporting_quote: For although it appears that a prior deed affecting the land had, in fact, been registered, it was not proved that that deed came to the appellant's knowledge. Therefore he was under no obligation to note the number.

statement: A tenant entering into possession of land under a lease void in law becomes a tenant from month to month upon the terms of the writing as far as they are applicable and not inconsistent with a monthly tenancy, and is bound to pay rent to the lessor so long as the landlord-tenant relationship exists in fact.
supporting_quote: "A tenant entering into possession of land, under a written lease void in law, thereupon becomes tenant from month to month upon the terms of the writing as far as they are applicable to and not inconsistent with a monthly tenancy; and so long as the relation of landlord find tenant exists in fact, the tenant is bound to pay the rent to his lessor."

statement: A person who is let into occupation of property as a tenant, or as a licensee, must be deemed to continue to occupy on the footing on which he was admitted, until by some overt act he manifests his intention of occupying in another capacity. No secret act will avail to change the nature of his occupation.
supporting_quote: "A person who is let into occupation of property as a tenant, or as a licensee, must be deemed to continue to occupy on the footing on which he was admitted, until by some overt act he manifests his intention of occupying in another capacity. No secret act will avail to change the nature of his occupation."

statement: In an action to recover house rent, where the landlord's right is a derivative one he should state in his plaint and prove how he derived it and from whom.
supporting_quote: in his plaint and prove how he derived it. and from whom.

statement: In a partition case where the Crown has an interest in part of the land, it is generally convenient for the plaintiff to begin by making out their prima facie case before the Crown can present evidence.
supporting_quote: "I cannot affirm the order dismissing the claim of the Crown. In the first place it is an ambiguous order, and the order of a Court should be clear and unambiguous. It may mean that the onus lay on the Attorney-General for the Crown, and because he did not lead evidence, the issue whether the land be the property of the Crown is finally answered in the negative. If that be the meaning which the District Judge puts on his order, it would have been well to have made it clear. But I do not read the appearance of the Attorney-General in the case and his answer as more than a notice that the Crown asserts title to a part of the land."

statement: The Commissioner has a duty to award owelty in adjusting the values of divided portions without special directions from the Court.
supporting_quote: "But it seems to me that it was the Commissioner's duty to do so without special directions. The Ordinance requires that his return should show the estimated value of the land and the mode in which the Commissioner proposes that the partition should be made."

statement: A sale by a curator of the estate of minors, with leave of court and subsequent approval of accounts, cannot be impeached in a later action by an administrator unless there is fraud.
supporting_quote: "The only ground on which it is competent for any other executor or any person interested in the estate to question in a new suit the proceedings in a former action which has resulted in a judgment against the property of the testator, is fraud."

statement: A partition suit should not be brought by a man not in possession whose title is disputed, but this does not apply to the facts of the present case.
supporting_quote: "It has often been held by this Court that a partition suit should not be brought by a man not in possession whose title is disputed."

statement: To succeed in an action for rescission of sale on the ground of enormis I�sio, the plaintiff must prove that the property was at the date of the sale worth double the price the defendant paid for it.
supporting_quote: "For the plaintiff to succeed in an action of this kind he must prove that the property was at the date of the sale worth double the price the defendant paid for it."

statement: Illegitimate children have no claim to land inherited from their father among Kandyans, but can inherit property acquired by the father.
supporting_quote: "I understand the law to be that among Kandyans illegitimate children have no claim to land which their father inherited. I regard Mr. Sawers as the best authority on Kandyan Law."

statement: The added defendant's possession of the property was not sufficient to establish adverse possession under Ceylon law.
supporting_quote: 'In my opinion he has not done so. He admits that he was "given charge of the house." That being so, it is for him to show that his quasi fiduciary position was changed by some overt act to possession, i.e., a holding with the intention of keeping the property to himself. This he has failed to do.'

statement: A transfer by a husband to his wife is not for valuable consideration under the Matrimonial Rights Ordinance, 1876.
supporting_quote: "By the Ordinance of 1876 all movable property to which a married woman is entitled during her marriage vests absolutely in her husband, so that presumably the money handed by the plaintiff to her husband Telenis as the consideration for the transfer was his own money. In other words, the transfer to her was not for valuable consideration."
statute_citation_verbatim: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No.15 of 1876, s. 19

statement: The law of Ceylon does not recognize the acquisition by user of servitudes personal to a single individual.
supporting_quote: In my opinion our law of prescription does not recognize the acquisition by user of servitudes personal to a single individual. Even if the use by the plaintiff of this path had been proved for a third of a century, he would not have acquired right of way.

statement: A wife who is separated from her husband can alienate land for the sake of procuring maintenance without her husband joining in the deed.
supporting_quote: According to the Thesavalamai of Jaffna, it is competent for a wife who is separated from her husband to alienate; without her husband joining in the deed, a land for the sake of procuring maintenance for herself.

statement: A judgment-debtor who avers that his creditor holds movable property belonging to him as security for the debt is entitled to the protection of the court.
supporting_quote: It is the duty of the court to inquire into the matter, and for that purpose to suspend execution. If the judgment-debtor cannot point out any other property for execution, the plaintiff may be called upon to surrender for execution the property left with him.

statement: A lessee can claim compensation for improvements made on leased land, even if the lease was not registered.
supporting_quote: "The remedy is a purely equitable one, and it has been held by this Court in the case of Muttiah v. Clements 2 that a lessee can, in certain circumstances, claim compensation for improvements."

statement: A lessee is a 'person interested' under the Land Acquisition Ordinance and can claim his share of the compensation.
supporting_quote: "The value of the premises " as accepted by the claimants is Rs.36,000. and the rental at " 5 per cent, will be 11s.. 1,825 per annum. The sixth claimant is " entitled to the difference between Rs . 1,825 and the Rs. 1,200

statement: The costs of a successful appellant will be disallowed for discreditable and perverse conduct.
supporting_quote: "Then there was a cross-appeal, and in my opinion that appeal should be dismissed without costs. The District Judge ought not to have entered up a decree after an appeal had been filed against his decision refusing to set aside the award, but should have waited until it had been finally decided whether the award was to stand or not. I should have wished to allow the appeal, but the words of section 692 of the Code are too clear to be disregarded, and provide that there is to be no appeal from such a decree as this. No doubt the parties are in some difficulty owing to entry of the decree, for the District Court has apparently no jurisdiction to set it aside when it has once been entered up. Possibly there may be some means, as by an application in revision, by which the matter may be set right."

statement: The purchaser of hypothecated land at a sale by the Fiscal in execution of a decree in a suit to realize the mortgage has a superior title over the purchaser at a sale by the Fiscal of the same land in execution of the judgment of an unsecured creditor against the mortgagor.
supporting_quote: 'I am of opinion that the appeal must be allowed. The question to be decided is, whether the purchaser of hypothecated land at a sale by the Fiscal in execution of a decree in a suit to realize the mortgage, or the purchaser at a sale by the Fiscal of the same land in execution of the judgment of an unsecured creditor against the mortgagor, has the better title.'

statement: At the stage of an application for probate, it is not open to respondents to raise objections regarding the validity of requests in a will on the grounds that the beneficiaries are adulterine bastards.
supporting_quote: Held that, at that stage of the proceedings, it was not open to the respondents to raise this contention, but that the applicant was entitled to probate.

statement: No action for the recovery of property belonging to an intestate's estate in Ceylon, where the estate exceeds Rs. 1,000 in value, is maintainable without letters of administration being taken out.
supporting_quote: It appears that they set up a claim to succeed to his property and took possession of this piece of land. The plaintiffs, who allege that they were in possession and were dispossessed, did not bring a possessory suit to be restored to possession, but after the lapse of some years have brought the present action to have it declared that they are entitled to this land, and they claim that the defendants be ejected there from and plaintiffs put in possession. Ratnapala Unnanse died intestate, and no letters of administration have been taken out to his estate.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 547

statement: Land that was chena for at least 60 years prior to the passing of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840, and which has not been granted or taxed within 20 years of its passage, is presumed to be forest land belonging to the Crown.
supporting_quote: "If it had been a chena for sixty years since 1840, the Ordinance No. 12 of 1840 applies. If it has ceased to be a chena and is now a forest, then too the Ordinance applies."

statement: The presumption created by section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840 can only arise in a case where the Crown is a party, and it cannot be used by the defendant without specifically pleading it.
supporting_quote: "Nor can defendant take advantage of that presumption without specially pleading it in his answer."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840

statement: A regular and perfect attachment is an essential preliminary in the sale in execution of simple decrees for money. Where there has been no such attachment, any sale that may have taken place is not simply voidable, but de facto void.
supporting_quote: "Now, it will be noticed that what purports to be attached there is the property itself ' with right of mortgage and other privileges ', whatever that may mean. But it would appear that what the Fiscal seized was the property itself, for the notice of seizure affixed to the property is that prescribed by section 28 in the case of immovable property. But what ought to have been seized was the mortgage debt, and the mode of seizure in such a case is pointed out by section 229 of the Civil Procedure Code, a notice written and signed by the Fiscal prohibiting the creditor from recovering the debt and the debtor from paying. A copy of such notice shall be fixed in a conspicuous part of the court-house, and a copy is to be delivered or sent to the debtor. That is the mode of seizure prescribed in the case of a debt."

statement: The onus was on the defendant to prove payment, and he had a duty to adduce all evidence supporting his claim before closing his case.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that plaintiff is not entitled to adduce any evidence in reply. The onus was on him to prove the issue, which is one of payment. He should have adduced all his evidence before he closed his case."

statement: A purchaser from an administrator cannot be in a worse position than a purchaser from the intestate himself, and subsequent registered deeds by administrators can defeat prior unregistered deeds executed by the intestate.
supporting_quote: "The instrument first registered, though last in date, which purports to dispose of the right, title, and interest of the party affected, shall if for value and without taint of fraud, prevail over all prior unregistered instruments affecting the same immovable property, whether they purport to dispose of the same interests or carve a small estate out of a fee simple, and shall, like Aaron's rod, swallow them up with all their charges, encumbrances, leases, and interests whatsoever affecting the property."

statement: The District Judge has an inherent power to vacate an erroneous order made ex parte, especially when the absence of a party was due to illness or other circumstances over which he had no control.
supporting_quote: "As a rule, he has power to open or rescind his own orders made, not in ter partes but ex parte. on being satisfied that the order was made to the prejudice of a party who was unable to attend in consequence of illness or other circumstances over which he had no control."

statement: A person who abstained from acts of possession because he feared a beating cannot be said to have been ousted.
supporting_quote: "A person who abstained from acts of possession because he feared a beating cannot be said to have been ousted."

statement: The term 'charge' in condition 3 of the deed refers to mortgages and not leases, as prohibited by condition 1.
supporting_quote: "I hold, therefore, that the appellant is not entitled to claim any rights under 1 D1 against the plaintiffs."

statement: A seizure under section 287 of a bond secured by mortgage of land should not be allowed to be as efficacious as a seizure under section 229, and possibly indeed that it should be held to be the proper way to proceed to realize the debt is not appropriate in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "I think that there was reason in Mr. Sampayo's objection that to entertain such a contention now would in effect be to revise the order of the 26th February, and (in the absence of Bonser C.J.) by a Court properly constituted, which could be properly done only in revision for the purposes of appeal to a higher tribunal;"

statement: A lessee is not entitled to compensation for a lease that has not commenced at the time of acquisition by the government.
supporting_quote: "I do not see that that passage applies to this case. I am of opinion that the lessee is entitled to compensation to the extent of his interest in the land acquired."

statement: A district judge has no discretion to refuse issuing a commission for partition based on the inability to personally serve defendants who are not found in the island, as long as notice is given to those that can be located.
supporting_quote: "I do not think so. The defendants are entitled to know who is to execute the commission and to agree or object to the commission being issued to him. How can they do the one or the other unless they have notice?"

statement: A claim for fees for teaching falls under section 11 of the Prescription Ordinance and is not prescribed for three years.
supporting_quote: "There are other cases (1 Lorenz 22 and 115: 2 Lorenz 67; 4 S. C.C. 47). Bawa. for respondent,-Section 9 applies, as the section says nothing about manual work only (2 Thomson's Institutes, p. 194). The cases from Lorenz applied to artisan's wages. This is a claim for work done."

statement: In doubtful cases, the intendment of a warranty clause must be construed against the vendor.
supporting_quote: "In doubtful cases the intendment must be construed against the vendor."

statement: A conveyance of real estate by an executrix for valuable consideration in connection with a marriage cannot be set aside at the instance of creditors, especially when there is no evidence of fraud and the deceased's estate was not insolvent.
supporting_quote: "In spite of this defence the plaintiff simply put in the papers relative to the case. He called witnesses, but made no effort to contradict the statement in the answer or to show that Juwanis Fernando's estate was insolvent at the date of the transfer."

statement: The Supreme Court will exercise its power of revision to set aside an order releasing property from seizure when such order is wholly based on a misapprehension.
supporting_quote: The Supreme Court will exercise its power of revision in order to set: aside an order releasing property, from seizure, when such order is wholly based on a misapprehension.

statement: A cause of action for the same debt cannot be pursued separately if it was part of a previous claim that was dismissed with costs.
supporting_quote: "Now 'cause of action' is defined under section 5 of the Civil Procedure Code as 'the wrong for the prevention or redress of which an action may be brought,' and as including 'the denial to a right, the refusal to fulfil an obligation, the neglect to perform a duty, and the infliction of an affirmative injury.' I think that the word 'obligation' in this definition is to be understood not in the narrower sense in which a parol promise to pay a promissory note and a mortgage, although given for the same debt, may be described as three different 'obligations,' but in the more generally understood sense of a liability to pay that sum of money."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 5 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A sale by the Fiscal without proper authorization and notice is invalid.
supporting_quote: The Fiscal was, I believe, also the District Judge, and I presume notice of the claim to him was notice to the Judge. But, suppose he were a different person? He knows that he has no right to sell property which does not belong to the judgment-debtor. What right has he to sell property which has been claimed, and which has been claimed 'at the earliest opportunity', without the authority of the Court, or until the Court has adjudicated upon the claim?

statement: An unregistered mortgage decree is void against a subsequently registered conveyance, and the plaintiff must establish both the debt and the charge as against the defendant in an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Of course, it will be open to the plaintiff by a proper proceeding to render the land, of which they are owners, subject to the mortgage executable for the mortgage debt. But he must establish the debt and the charge as against them."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: Section 402 of the Civil Procedure Code does not apply to cases where the Fiscal has been unable to serve summons on a defendant for a considerable period, but rather applies to cases where the defendant appears and subsequently fails to prosecute the action.
supporting_quote: "Now, can it be said that the Court was justified, in the circumstances, assuming that it had the power of its own motion to order the action to abate, to make such an order on the ground that the plaintiff had not taken the necessary steps to prosecute the action?"

statement: A person aggrieved by a preliminary or interlocutory order made by a Court of requests under section 4 of the Partition Ordinance has the right to appeal at once to the Supreme Court.
supporting_quote: "I think he is entitled to appeal. Section 19 of the Ordinance gives an appeal from 'all decisions and orders of any Court made under the authority of the Ordinance.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 19 of the Partition Ordinance, No. 10 of 1863

statement: An executor of an executor can be sued for amounts due to a legatee, even if other executors are alive.
supporting_quote: "In any case, he is now, in my opinion, in the absence of proof to the contrary, responsible for this money just as his testator would have been."

statement: A donation by a minor is ipso jure void, not merely voidable.
supporting_quote: "These authorities, I think, show that the donation by a minor. unassisted by a guardian, is null and void."

statement: The words 'executors, administrators, and assigns' are not mere notarial flourish but imply a specific designation of parties to be benefited, which is essential for creating a fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: "When the persons in whose interest the prohibition is made are assigns, they may be anybody in the world. There is then no designation of persons such as is essential to the creation of a fidei commissum."

statement: When parties who claim to be owners of land bring an action alleging an ouster which they are unable to prove, the court should not deprive them of all further opportunities of maintaining their claim to the land.
supporting_quote: "If that case is to decide that, when parties who claim to be owners of land bring an action alleging an ouster which they are unable to prove, they are to be punished by having their action dismissed, and being deprived of all further opportunities of maintaining their claim to the land, I think it will be inconsistent with the law and procedure of this Court which has been established for the last nine or ten years."

statement: A person claiming to be an intending purchaser of land is entitled to inspect the book of registration in which deeds relating to that land are registered, provided they furnish reasonable information satisfying the Registrar-General of their genuine claim.
supporting_quote: "A person who claims to be the intending purchaser of a land and applies to the Registrar-General, under section 15 of the Ordinance No. 14 of 1891, to inspect the book of registration in which the deeds relating to such land are registered, is bound to furnish to that officer reasonable information which satisfies him of the genuineness of his claim that he has an interest in the entries in question"
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 14 of 1891, section 15

statement: A license to open a mine granted under the Ordinance No. 10 of 1894 to a person does not justify the opening and working of it by any other person who owns a share in it.
supporting_quote: A license to open a mine granted under the Ordinance No. 10 of 1894 to a person does not justify the opening and working of it by any other person who owns a share in it.

statement: A person claiming to be the owner of an undivided share of land and entitled to possession thereof is competent to maintain an action for partition, even if neither he nor his predecessor in title has had possession and the defendants wholly deny his title.
supporting_quote: "Where such an action is brought in good faith, its failure ought not to render the plaintiff liable to be cast in double costs under section 4 of the Ordinance No. 10 of 1897."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 4 of the Ordinance No. 10 of 1897

statement: A receipt must bear a 5-cent stamp, under the Ordinance No. 3 of 1890, and therefore endorsements on the document without proper stamps are inadmissible to prove payment of interest so as to avoid prescription.
supporting_quote: A receipt must bear a 5-cent stamp, under the Ordinance No. 3 of 1890. Sampayo, for plaintiff, respondent.-The defendant does not dispute the payments, appearing on the back of the document. He does not object to them in his petition of appeal.

statement: Courts should strictly construe the conditions of letters of administration and insist on approval of sale conditions by the District Court before a sale is carried out.
supporting_quote: "So much injury and damage to the heirs comes to be engendered in our Courts by the practice of giving administrators general leave to sell property, that I think we ought to be careful strictly to construe the conditions in the form of the letters of administration issued from the Court, and I think District Courts would do well to insist on the conditions of sale being submitted to them for approval by the administrator before the sale itself is carried out."

statement: The principle that the alienation, pendente lite, of the interest of one of the parties to an action will not be allowed to prejudice the rights of the other party is well-established.
supporting_quote: It is a well-established principle that the alienation, pendente lite, of the interest of one of the parties to an action will not be allowed to prejudice the rights of the other party. The action, in fact, is to proceed, and the decree in it to operate, as if the interest alienated was still the property of the original owner.

statement: The dismissal of an action for partition cannot be pleaded as res judicata in a subsequent action brought by the plaintiff for a declaration of title to that share, because while in the partition action he has to prove an absolutely good title as against all the world, in the other action he has to prove only a better title than the defendants.
supporting_quote: "Although nominally a partition suit, it was really an action for declaration of title, and the Supreme Court dismissed the action in these terms: ' We think that plaintiff has not proved, as against the parties in possession, that he had a right to a share.'"

statement: An administrator's duty is to pay debts by selling a sufficient portion of the estate, rather than allowing judgment-creditors to seize property through execution.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that the former action has nothing to do with this. I must say that I do not understand why, in the present case, the administrator, when judgment went against him, and this debt was established against the estate, did not take measures, by selling and realizing sufficient of the estate, to pay this debt."

statement: When a claimant under a will produces it in court, they are not required to prove that the will has not been cancelled by a subsequent will or is otherwise valid. The onus of proof lies with any opponent who may come forward.
supporting_quote: "The applicant does not know how the District Judge came to inquire into the matters connected with the grandfather and father of Mrs. Wigley. No one moved him to institute these inquiries. He, however, believes that this will of 1881 and the codicil thereto are genuine. It was his duty then to have made an order nisi and caused it to be served on the possible opponents he had in view."

statement: Section 339 of the Civil Procedure Code enacts substantive law and cannot be waived. The rule it embodies is not a mere rule of arbitrary enactment or convenience, but one resting on solid grounds of principle and equity.
supporting_quote: "The rule embodied in this section is not a mere rule of arbitrary) enactment or of convenience, but one resting on solid grounds of principle and equity."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 339 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A lessee who has possession under an invalid lease for over ten years can acquire a title by prescription to possess the land as lessee for the remainder of the period of lease.
supporting_quote: Held, that as the defendant had possession under the lease for over ten years he was entitled to possess the land for the remaining period by right of prescription

statement: The secretary of the district court has no right to draw a petition of appeal for any suitor in the District Court of Tangalla.
supporting_quote: "Mr. Moldrech has no right to draw a petition of appeal for any suitor in the District Court of Tangalla."

statement: A petition of appeal should contain a plain and concise statement of the grounds of objection to the decree appealed against, along with sufficient facts of the case and judgment.
supporting_quote: Section 758 of the Civil Procedure Code directs that a 'petition shall contain a plain and concise statement of the grounds of objection to the decree appealed against.' That necessarily implies that there shall also be a sufficient statement of the facts of the case and of the judgment to render the grounds of objection intelligible.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 758 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A plaintiff must obtain probate or letters of administration for an estate exceeding Rs. 1,000 in value before maintaining an action to recover property included in that estate.
supporting_quote: "That section is imperative, and before a plaintiff can maintain an action for the recovery of any property in Ceylon he must comply with the provisions of that section."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A trustee under the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance can bring a partition suit when it is inexpedient to hold the land together with co-owners.
supporting_quote: "I think the power which that section gives to trustees to sue for any other purpose requisite for carrying into effect the objects of the Ordinance ' is so wide that it would include the right of the trustee, when he finds that it is inexpedient to hold the land vested in him together with his other co-owners, to bring a partition suit under Ordinance No. 10 of 1863"
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 3 of 1889, s. 30; Ordinance No. 10 of 1863

statement: A Court has no jurisdiction to confirm a sale under a decree that has been reversed in appeal before the confirmation takes place.
