supporting_quote: "Now, the section of the Indian Code which deals with confirmation of sales in execution by the Court is section 312, and that section corresponds to section 283 of our Code, and contains no provision directing the Court to refrain from confirming a sale in execution where the decree on which the writ of execution has issued has been set aside before the application for confirmation was made; still the Indian Courts held that the power of the Court to confirm the sale under a decree ceased when such decree was reversed in appeal before the confirmation took place, and that the Court had no jurisdiction to confirm such sale."

statement: In an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code, the plaintiff must prove that they were in possession of the property at the time of seizure, or that it was in possession of the execution-debtor at such time in trust for the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: It is admitted by appellant's counsel that the executrix, who is no party to this action, is in the actual possession of her testator's property, and that she has power to mortgage such property to pay the debts of the testator. In an action under section 247 the plaintiffs must prove that they were in possession of the property at the time of seizure, or that it was in possession of the execution-debtor at such time in trust for the plaintiffs, and that therefore the Court ought not to have refused to release the property.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 247

statement: It is not open to the Court to frame an issue on what really formed the consideration unless both parties consent.
supporting_quote: "The contention of the first defendant's proctor in the Court below appears to me to be sound. While by our law, both before and after the Evidence Ordinance of 1895, a party to a deed may be allowed merely to negative the statement therein as to what I may call the transit of consideration, or to show that the particular consideration mentioned therein has failed, it is not open to him to show that the consideration was other than that stated in the deed, and that there was a failure of that other consideration."

statement: A co-owner cannot build on common land without the consent of other co-owners, and an injunction may be granted to prevent such unauthorized construction.
supporting_quote: "The act of building without obtaining the consent of the co-owner upon land held in common is a violation of that co-owner's rights"

statement: A part-owner can maintain a possessory action for an undivided share of land, provided the other co-owners are joined as parties either plaintiff or defendant.
supporting_quote: "The owner of an undivided share of land can maintain a possessory action in respect of such share, provided he joins the other co-owners as parties either plaintiff or defendant."

statement: Appellants must show they have suffered damage by irregular partition proceedings to set them aside.
supporting_quote: "It may be that Manuel Fernando intended to conserve his children's interest by giving them half, or perhaps even the whole, of the parcel to be allotted to him in severalty, or he may have intended in some other way to compensate them, and he may in fact have carried out this intention. Certainly the appellants are now the owners of that entire parcel, as they are the heirs of their father and they are in possession."

statement: A creditor who takes a cheque may present it for payment at any time until it is barred by the Statute of Limitations; however, after a reasonable time (within the next day after receiving it) has elapsed, he holds it at his own risk against the failure of the bank. If the money is lost through such failure, the drawer to that extent is discharged.
supporting_quote: "Finally, a creditor who takes a cheque may present it for payment at any time until it is barred by the Statute of Limitation; but after a reasonable time (within the next day after receiving it) for presenting it has elapsed, he holds it at his own risk against the failure of the bank; and if the money is lost through that failure the drawer to that extent is discharged, the holder becoming creditor of the banker to the same extent"
statute_citation_verbatim: Bills of Exchange Act, 1882, section 74

statement: An order giving a plaintiff liberty to re-institute an action after it has been dismissed without calling on the defense is inoperative if made without jurisdiction, and does not prevent the defendant from raising res judicata.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the order giving the plaintiff liberty to re-institute the action was inoperative, as being made without jurisdiction, and that the said order did not prevent the defendant from successfully raising the plea of res judicata, if sued again on the same cause of action."

statement: In a hypothecary action it is irregular to raise questions of title.
supporting_quote: "A CTION upon a mortgage bond. Certain persons came into the suit as added parties denying the right of the mortgagor to mortgage to the plaintiff the lands which formed the subject of the mortgage. Thereupon the plaintiffs moved for leave to withdraw their prayer for the mortgage decree."

statement: The plaintiffs may present parol evidence to interpret the meaning of initials or vilasam in a deed, particularly if they are not commonly intelligible characters.
supporting_quote: "The 98th section 342 of the Evidence Ordinance admits evidence 'to show the meaning of.......not commonly intelligible characters, of technical, local, and provincial expressions, of abbreviations, and of words used in a peculiar sense.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: The 98th section 342 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: A legatee must either stand by the will as a whole, or repudiate it as a whole under Roman-Dutch Law in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "We ought only to apply the Roman-Dutch Law, under which a legatee must either stand by the will as a whole, or repudiate it as a whole."

statement: A father cannot make a gift to his minor son who is still subject to his power, but the practice in Ceylon is for parents to donate to their minor children. Acceptance is necessary to make a donation fully effectual, but as minors cannot accept it, their grandparent and parents, when not also the donors, may accept for them.
supporting_quote: Though some Roman-Dutch Lawyers declare that a father cannot make a gift to his minor son who is still subject to his power, yet the practice in Ceylon is for parents to donate to their minor children. Acceptance is necessary to make a donation fully effectual, but as minors cannot accept it, their grandparent and parents, when not also the donors, may accept for them.

statement: A father making a donation cannot accept it on his child's behalf.
supporting_quote: I fail to see how a donor, even though a father, can act in two capacities at the same time. I cannot persuade myself that a father can even expressly accept on his child's behalf a gift he has himself made.

statement: The appellants are estopped by the deed of 1870 from making any claim to any share in the residue of the estate of Manuel Fernando and Adriana Swaris.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, the word 'inheritance' would include not only property derived by intestacy, but also by will, a demand to be considered one of the persons entitled to the residue under a will cannot, it seems to me, be otherwise than a claim of inheritance out of the estate."

statement: An oral account stated does not create a new cause of action that can evade the statute of limitations if it is merely an acknowledgment or promise by words only.
supporting_quote: "Now, this new contract is not to be proved by an 'acknowledgment or promise by words only.' That is admitted, it cannot be denied; but it is said that the 'acknowledgment or promise' in the Ordinance refers to cases where there is only one side of the account."

statement: A fidei commissum can be enforced against a purchaser from a fiduciarius who has a partition title, provided the purchaser had no notice of the fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: "Although my decision on question (c) disposes of the case in favour of the respondent, I have thought it desirable to add a few words on the 444 other questions raised in this appeal, (b) raises the question as to whether a valid fidei commissum was created by P 3. It has been contended by Mr. Perera that the learned District Judge came to a wrong conclusion in finding that P 3 created a valid fidei commissum."

statement: A person cannot be allowed to avail himself of his own fraud, and a man cannot set up his own fraud to avoid his own deed.
supporting_quote: "It is a principle of Eoman-Dutch Law that no one can be allowed to avail himself of his own fraud, and of English Law that a man cannot set up his own fraud to avoid his own deed"

statement: The appellants are estopped by the deed of 1870 from making any claim to any share in the residue of the estate of Manuel Fernando and Adriana Swaris.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the word 'inheritance' would include not only property derived in intestacy. A demand to be considered one of the persons entitled to the residue under a will cannot, it seems to me, be otherwise than a claim of inheritance out of the estate but also by will."

statement: The court should follow the decision of the Full Court from 1860, which held that ten years' adverse possession gives a title capable of being vindicated like any other title to land.
supporting_quote: "I think the decree appealed from should be set aside and the case remitted to the Court of requests for the completion of the trial. The plaintiff will have the costs of appeal."

statement: A guardian cannot sell a minor's immovable property without the express sanction of the Court.
supporting_quote: "It is a clear principal of the Roman-Dutch Law that a minor's immovable property cannot be alienated without the decree of a Court of competent jurisdiction."

statement: Before issuing a certificate of conformity, the Court must satisfy itself that an insolvent is entitled to one.
supporting_quote: "The Court must satisfy itself before issuing a certificate of conformity that an insolvent is entitled to one (In re Armitage, 5 S. C. C. 216)."

statement: A plaintiff claiming title by intestate succession must show affirmatively that the intestate estate was less than Rs. 1,000 in value; it is not sufficient that both parties ignore the necessity for administration or even agree that it is not necessary.
supporting_quote: "It is incumbent on a plaintiff in that position to show affirmatively that the intestate estate was less than Rs. 1,000 in value. It is not sufficient that both parties ignore the necessity for administration, or even agree that administration was not necessary."

statement: The Court must insist on administration of an intestate's estate before allowing a suit for recovery of property, unless the estate is under Rs. 1,000 in value.
supporting_quote: "It may be that the plaintiff has established a prescriptive title to the land claimed on the plaint, and in view of that I suggested to the respondent's counsel that, if they were prepared to proceed to trial resting their claim merely on the prescriptive title, it would not be necessary for the respondent to establish either that Punchi Menika's estate did not exceed the sum of Rs. 1,000 or, in the event of his failing to do so, to apply for letters of administration of Punchi Menika's estate."
statute_citation_verbatim: "section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code"

statement: When two or more persons have joined in stipulating for the payment of a certain sum of money, each is ordinarily liable to pay a quota of that money. It is only when the intention of the parties is clearly expressed that each person shall severally pay the whole, that each person becomes bound in solidum.
supporting_quote: When persons have joined in stipulating for the payment of a certain sum of money, each is ordinarily liable to pay a quota of that money, and it is only when the intention of the parties is clearly expressed, that each is severally bound for the payment of the whole, that each person becomes liable in solidum.

statement: A party seeking to cancel a decree entered by mistake must apply to the Supreme Court for an order directing the lower court to investigate and report on the allegation of mistake, rather than bringing a separate action.
supporting_quote: "I think, therefore, that this Court has jurisdiction on application by petition duly supported by affidavit to grant an order upon the Judge of first instance in certain cases of alleged error upon judgment, to inquire into and to ascertain, and then to correct if necessary and right so to do, by restitutio in integrum."

statement: A diga married widower is not entitled to a partition suit in respect of the property of his deceased children, as he only holds a life interest in one moiety and does not 'belong to him in common with other owners' under the Partition Ordinance, No. 10 of 1863, s. 2.
supporting_quote: "All plaintiff has is a life interest in one moiety, and I do not think the Entail and Settlement Ordinance, No. 11 of 1876, could be applied on the ground of analogy. That Ordinance is directed to a specific object which does not include the case of an ordinary life interest. I think, therefore, the appeal must be allowed, and the judgment of the Commissioner set aside, and the action dismissed with costs."
statute_citation_verbatim: Partition Ordinance, No. 10 of 1863, s. 2

statement: A diga married daughter does not forfeit her right to inherit lands which had been acquired by her mother, or to which her mother bad succeeded collaterally, or otherwise than by inheritance from her father.
supporting_quote: "A diga married daughter does not forfeit her right to inherit lands which had been acquired by her mother, or to which her mother bad succeeded collaterally, or otherwise than by inheritance from her father."

statement: Since the enactment of the Civil Procedure Code, all applications for letters of administration must be considered with reference to the terms of that Code and do not leave the Court any discretion where the application is made late.
supporting_quote: "I think, therefore, on the authority of Moysa Fernando v. Alice Fernando (4 N. L. R. 201), the Civil Procedure Code has settled the law with regard to issue of letters of administration, and that it would not be safe for this Court to place too much reliance on the old decisions referred to by the District Judge; and as there is no suggestion that the lapse of time has caused any change of title or affected the rights of the parties, and as it is obvious that the title of the minor respondents cannot possibly have been in any way affected by the delay, I think the District Judge was wrong, and that the petitioner is entitled to be granted the prayer of his petition."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 547 of that Code enacts that no action shall be maintainable to recover any property in Ceylon where the estate exceeds Rs. 1,000 unless letters of administration shall have issued, and section 544 does not provide that before granting such letters the Court shall consider the length of time that has elapsed since the death of the intestate, but only, where there is a conflict of claims, the provisions of section 523.

statement: Under Roman-Dutch law, the omission of property from a will does not necessarily mean it is disposed of by the will. Instead, such property may descend as ab intestato to those nearest in blood to the testator.
supporting_quote: "According to Van Leeuwen the principle stated in Voet (lib, 28, tit. 1, n. 1) that it was not according to law unumquemque qui testandi jus habet etiam pro parte testatum et pro parte intestatum mori posse was never adopted in the Roman-Dutch Law. In that law it appears to be the rule that if a testator excludes part of his property from the operation of his will, it descends as ab intestato, and not to the instituted heirs."

statement: A will is validly attested where a notary public and two witnesses see the testatrix sign, and all four are present together.
supporting_quote: "Since 'attestation' means execution of a deed or will in the presence of witnesses, and 'attesting witness' means a person who has seen a party execute a deed or sign a written agreement, section 3 of the Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 must be construed as dealing only with the authentication and proof of the bare fact of signing by a party."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 3 of the Ordinance No. 7 of 1840

statement: A defendant setting up possession as usufructuary mortgagee for ten years cannot plead it to create a title in someone who is not a party to the action.
supporting_quote: "Can the defendant plead his own possession as creating a title for his lessor, although the possession creates no title for himself ? The Prescription Ordinance contemplates possession by a party getting judgment, his own possession or that of his predecessors in title. It is to be a judgment declaratory of the right of property in a party to the action, not of a stranger."

statement: A primary mortgagee can join a puisne incumbrancer as a defendant in an action to realize the mortgage, even after the passing of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "It may be that in certain cases after the passing of the Code a puisne incumbrancer cannot claim to have notice given to him of an action to realize a primary mortgage; there is nothing, however, in the Civil Procedure Code to prevent a primary mortgagee joining a puisne incumbrancer, should he think it desirable to do so, and I cannot see what the puisne incumbrancers have to complain of in being joined in this action."

statement: No conviction could be sustained under by-law 14 as it is inconsistent with section 232 of the Ordinance No. 7 of 1887, and a lease of the market renders the issuance of stallage licenses unnecessary.
supporting_quote: Both enactments are aimed at making a license necessary for the use of the market. In the second place, I think the effect of section 232 is to substitute the Chairman as the licensing authority in place of the Secretary who is designated in the by-law. Although in a sense the two enactments may be said to be consistent inasmuch as a person may obtain both the Secretary's license and the Chairman's permission, I cannot think that the Legislature intended that the two requirements should co-exist, and that a person in order to use a public market should obtain both the permission of the Chairman and the license of his subordinate officer, the Secretary.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 232 of the Ordinance No. 7 of 1887

statement: An undivided portion of a larger extent of land cannot be the subject of a partition suit unless the co-owners of the whole corpus be made parties to it.
supporting_quote: The Ordinance No. 10 of 1863 appears to provide for the sale or partition of lands held in common, and I can find nothing in the Ordinance which restricts its provision to one single land held in common. It is admitted that ever since the Ordinance No. 10 of 1863 the practice of the Courts has been to allow several lands which are held in common among the same co-owners to be joined in one partition suit. I would affirm the order of the District Judge.

statement: A transfer after the commencement of legal proceedings for partition is void under section 17 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1863.
supporting_quote: " This transfer after commencement of legal proceedings to partition the land is void under section 17 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1863 (see Annamalai Pillai v. Perera, 6 N. L. R. 108). I decree that the deed executed by them in favour of the third defendant was void, and that the two sixth shares of Mahagedarawatta and of the houses thereon are liable to be sold in execution in case D. C., Galle, 6,006, in accordance with section 16 of the Partition Ordinance. The third defendant

statement: The right of pre-emption under the Thesavalamai is still in existence, but the duty to give notice before transferring land has become obsolete.
supporting_quote: "I hold that the right of pre-emption has become obsolete also, and I therefore dismiss the plaintiff's action with costs."

statement: An authority to an agent to borrow money and purchase goods on behalf of his principal does not include an authority to sign promissory notes.
supporting_quote: "an authority to an agent to borrow money and purchase goods on behalf of his principal does not include an authority to sign promissory notes"

statement: When an authority is given to two or more persons to do an act, the act is valid to bind the principal only when all of them concur in doing it, unless express words indicate otherwise.
supporting_quote: "The rule laid down in Story on Agency, section 42, is that 'where an authority is given to two or more persons to do an act, the act is valid to bind the principal only when all of them concur in doing it, for the authority is construed strictly and the power is understood to be joint and not several; '"

statement: The withdrawal of a writ by the Court has the effect of determining the Fiscal's authority and the seizure he may have made under it, even though it is registered.
supporting_quote: "I would hold then that the withdrawal of the writ from the Fiscal's hands by the Court has the effect of determining the Fiscal's authority and the seizure he may have made under it, even though it be registered."

statement: A plaintiff who has a 'right of property' that was never tried or decided against him in an earlier action cannot later assert it as a defense to the same cause of action between the same parties.
supporting_quote: "That clearly is a 'right of property', which would have been a good defence, which therefore ought to have been set up, and which is now conclusively negatived by the decree in the appellant's favour."

statement: A trustee nominated by the District Court under the Property and Trustees' Ordinance, 1871 has the power to appoint a new trustee in his stead if the settlement instrument expressly authorizes such action.
supporting_quote: "The settlor having expressly authorized the trustee nominated by the Court to exercise the power of appointment, it is obvious that such trustee can lawfully exercise that power."

statement: A sale of immovable property over Rs. 1,000 must be advertised in the Government Gazette at least twenty days prior to the sale.
supporting_quote: "It appears to me that the provisions as to publication in the Government Gazette are imperative, and are not to be exercised at the caprice of the execution-creditor"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 256 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A Court should not interfere with a sale held under section 347 of the Code if no injustice has been shown by the party involved, as this view had stood unchallenged for over fifty years and it is important to maintain stable rules of procedure.
supporting_quote: It is especially important for the proper and expeditious conduct of judicial business that the rules of procedure should be stable. Hence it is almost an invariable rule to adhere to former decisions settling the rules of procedure, when they are generally known and acted on, and when they have been established for such a length of time as to make a change injudicious, even though it may have become apparent that they were wrongly decided, or although the Court would have reached a different conclusion if the case were before it for the first time.

statement: A party applying to re-open a preliminary decree must give security for the costs incurred by other parties if they have delayed in ascertaining their proper share and failing to file an answer setting forth their claim.
supporting_quote: In a partition suit, a party applying to re-open the preliminary decree, on the ground of there being a mistake as to the share assigned to him, may be called upon to give security for the costs incurred by the other parties, if he has delayed to ascertain his proper share and to apprise the Court in time of the mistake.

statement: A Crown grant in Ceylon confers absolute dominion on the purchaser, superseding all other title existing at the date of the grant unless such title has been derived from the Crown itself. The remedy for any person claiming to have had better title than the Crown is an action for damages against the Crown.
supporting_quote: "I find that the law in Ceylon is that a Crown grant confers the absolute dominium on the purchaser, superseding all other title existing at the date of the grant, unless such title has been derived from the Crown itself, and that the remedy for any person claiming to have had, at the date of the grant, better title than the Crown, is an action for damages against the Crown"

statement: A defendant cannot use the Statute of Frauds to perpetrate and cover a fraud where he acted as an agent for the plaintiff in purchasing property, but now refuses to reconvey it.
supporting_quote: "To allow him to do so would be to use the Statute of Frauds to perpetrate and cover a fraud which is contrary to the principle enunciated by Lord Justice Turner in Lincoln v. Wright (1) , and which the Court of Chancery in England has followed in many instances Haigh v. Kaye (2) ; In re the Duke of Marlborough, Davis v. Whitehead (3) ."

statement: A house built on land owned in common with others becomes the property of the soil owners, and the builder's sole right is a right to compensation.
supporting_quote: A house becomes the property of the owners of the soil on which it is built, and the builder's sole right is right to compensation (De Silva v. Harmanis, 3 N. L. R. 160).

statement: A mortgagee can sue a party in possession of the mortgaged land, even if that party claims adverse title to the mortgagor.
supporting_quote: "The authorities to which we have been referred by the respondent's counsel have satisfied us that a mortgagee, who seeks a decree rendering the mortgaged property especially bound and executable for the debt, is entitled to sue a party in possession of the land and claiming to be the owner of it, even although he denies the right of the mortgagor to hypothecate it."

statement: For a valid adoption under Kandyan law, it is necessary that the parties be of the same caste and that the adoption should be public and formally declared; it must also clearly appear that the adoption was for the purpose of inheriting the property of the adoptive parents.
supporting_quote: "In order to constitute a valid adoption under the Kandyan Law no particular formalities or ceremonies are required; but it is necessary that the parties should be of the same caste and that the adoption should be public and formally and openly declared and acknowledged; and it must also clearly appear that the adoption was for the purpose of inheriting the property of the adoptive parents."

statement: The Court will grant a lessee relief against a provision in the lease giving the lessor a right to claim cancellation for breach of stipulation, if the breach did not involve a notably grave and damnifying misuse of the property leased.
supporting_quote: "It is true here that the parties agreed that default in payment of taxes should entitle the lessor to cancel the lease and re-enter but as the doctrine of equitable relief peculiar to the English Law has been recognized by the Court in the case reported in 3 N. L. R. 248 and 2 Browne, 397, and as the principle of the Roman Dutch Law, as Withers, J., says in the former case, seems to be that which would be observed in cases of penal stipulation in contracts, my view is that I ought not to decree the cancellation of this contract."

statement: A plaintiff may recover money paid by him for the defendant's use, at the defendant's request, if the payment was made under compulsion or threat of law.
supporting_quote: By English Law a plaintiff may recover money paid by him for the defendant's use, at the defendant's request. It is not enough that the plaintiff's payment benefited the defendant; it must also have been made at his request, express or implied. A request will be implied if the plaintiff has paid under compulsion, or under a threat of compulsion, of law.

statement: An action against an administrator appointed after the filing of a plaint is not barred by prescription if the administrator was added as a party in the same representative character as the original defendants.
supporting_quote: Held, that as he was made a party in the same representative character as that filled by the original defendants, his plea of prescription was not good.

statement: In a case where a lease precedes a mortgage and the lease stipulates that any subsequent mortgage should terminate the lease, it is necessary to join the lessee as a party defendant in the mortgage suit.
supporting_quote: "Where a property has been leased to one party and then mortgaged to another, end the mortgagee desires to realize his mortgage, it is necessary to join the lessee as a party defendant in the mortgage suit, even though the lease stipulated for its determination upon the passing of a mortgage decree."

statement: A purchaser of property which belongs to a third party cannot obtain a sound title if they are aware that the property does not belong to the seller, unless certain conditions are met.
supporting_quote: "Property which belongs to a third party is not saleable, unless the purchaser at least was ignorant of the fact, or the parties, if they were aware, negotiated bond fide (Cens. For. 1 4, 19, 21)."

statement: A sale or mortgage executed during the pendency of a partition suit in respect of a share or interest, to which a person may become entitled after the termination of such suit, is valid and not affected by section 17 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1863.
supporting_quote: A sale or mortgage executed during the pendency of a partition suit in respect of a share or interest, to which a person may become entitled after the partition suit has terminated, appears to me not affected by section 17.

statement: A person cannot acquire title by prescription to property belonging to another, even if they have occupied it for a long time with the owner's consent, unless they take some overt act showing an intention to possess adversely to the owner.
supporting_quote: "Where a person enters into occupation of property belonging to another with the latter's consent and permission, he cannot acquire title by prescription to such property, unless he gets rid of the character in which he commenced to occupy by doing some overt act showing an intention to possess adversely to the owner."

statement: A decree-holder may sue for the balance of a debt even after an agreement to settle all claims, provided that the agreement does not supersede the original decree and the decree-holder has taken no steps by way of execution until after the agreement.
supporting_quote: As to the first of these grounds, the time necessarily occupied in realizing the assigned securities, in my opinion, explains the delay consistently with the continuance in force of the decree.

statement: A co-owner desiring to sell his share of land must give reasonable notice to other co-owners according to the times specified in the first paragraph of section 7 of the Tesavalamai.
supporting_quote: "I think we must hold that reasonable notice must be given. It certainly is desirable that, in order to prevent dispute as to notice and consequent litigation, some definite formality should be prescribed by the Legislature if the right of pre-emption itself is not taken away."

statement: Illegitimate children are not legally incapacitated from taking property given to them by their parents under a will, even if the Tesavalamai does not provide for such donations.
supporting_quote: It is suggested, however, that the persons to whom the properties in this case were devised were prohibited from taking under the will, in view of the provisions of the Roman-Dutch Law, and that as the Tesavalamai did not incapacitate persons, situate as these were, from taking under a will, we must apply the Roman-Dutch Law in this case.

statement: A decree-holder of a different Court can claim concurrence in the proceeds realized under a writ of execution issued by another Court, provided they have obtained their decree and applied for execution prior to the realization of assets.
supporting_quote: "I think that no violence will be done to the provision of section 352 if we read the expression 'for execution of decrees' as meaning 'for satisfaction of decrees,' which would include the case of application for payment of money realized by one Court in satisfaction of decrees of other Courts."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 352 of the Civil Procedure Code, and section 350 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A valid account stated between parties, even without a written acknowledgment, can create an independent cause of action not subject to prescription.
supporting_quote: "Where the plaintiff and the defendant had cross accounts and on a particular day the state of accounts between them was examined by them both in each other's presence, and a balance struck which the defendant admitted to be correct- Held, that there was a ' valid account stated ' between the parties within the meaning of the Prescription Ordinance, notwithstanding the absence of any written acknowledgment on the part of the defendant."
statute_citation_verbatim: "The Prescription Ordinance (No. 22 of 1871), sections 8 13 15"

statement: The jurisdiction of the Court of Requests is determined by the value of the plaintiff's claim, and not the total value of the property in dispute.
supporting_quote: "I think, as counsel for the respondent put it, prima facie the criterion of jurisdiction is the nature and value of the plaintiff's claim."

statement: A Crown grant does not convey an indefeasible title, and a person in uninterrupted possession of land belonging to the Crown for not less than ten years nor more than thirty years acquires a permanent interest in the property under section 8 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840.
supporting_quote: A Crown grant does not convey an indefeasible title. Where a person has been in uninterrupted possession of land belonging to the Crown for not less than ten years nor more than thirty years, such person acquires under section 8 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840 a permanent interest in the property; and he cannot be ejected therefrom, unless the land is required for public purposes or for the use of His Majesty; and the Crown cannot by selling the land to a third party deprive the possessor of the benefit given to him by that section.
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 12 of 1840, s. 8

statement: Execution-creditors who allow their own property to be sold as the property of an execution-debtor under a writ over which they have control are estopped from later claiming that the property was theirs and not the debtor's.
supporting_quote: "It appears to me clear that the appellants, who actually permitted their own property to be seized and sold under their own writ, over which writ they had absolute control, as the property of the first defendant, cannot be allowed now to say against the purchaser, the second defendant, or his vendee, the first defendant, that the property seized and sold under their writ was their property and not the property of the first defendant."
statute_citation_verbatim: "when one person has by his declaration act, or omission intentionally caused or permitted another person to believe a thing to be true and to act upon such belief, neither he nor his representative shall be allowed in any suit or proceeding between himself and such person or his representative to deny the truth of that thing."

statement: Specific devises of real estate pass directly to the devisee, not to the executor.
supporting_quote: "In Cassim v. Marikar[ 2 1 S. C. R. 180.], a decision of the Full Court, and binding on us, it was held that specifically devised property passed direct to the devisee and not to the executor."

statement: The deed No. 7,161 dated January 4, 1873, did not create a valid fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: For these reasons, I think no valid fidei commissum was created by the deed in question, and therefore I would confirm the judgment of this Court under review, with costs.

statement: In the absence of a specified order of succession, the rule of intestate succession applies to determine who succeeds to the property.
supporting_quote: "The opinion is generally received and is undoubtedly correct if the testator have called his heirs (to the inheritance) in general terms and have not expressly summoned the nearest of them or have simply expressed his desire that the goods are not to devolve on any one not related to him, because when the testator does not arrange a definite order of succession, he is considered as leaving this to be settled by the Common Law, according to which fidei commissaries succeed according to the order and rules of intestate succession."

statement: Defendants who had lived in adultery with each other can marry and legitimize their children under Ceylon law, provided the subsequent marriage is legal.
supporting_quote: "The provisions of section 31 thus brought our law into harmony with the English Law as regards the capacity of parents who had committed adultery to marry, and when we consider that our marriage laws affect Europeans to the same extent that they affect certain other sections of the community, it seems abundantly clear that the object of section 31 was to render marriages between persons who had committed adultery legal and valid."

statement: A partition suit is limited to the remedies laid down and provided for in the Partition Ordinance, and does not include a claim for damages.
supporting_quote: "There is no doubt that if this action was brought under the Roman-Dutch Law as it existed before the introduction of any statutory law into the Colony providing for the procedure to be adopted in a partition suit and if this was an action communi dividundo, which is a mixed action, that is, a real action in so far as each co-owner in undivided shares sued for and vindicated thereby his own property or share belonging to him as owner, and personal in so far as it is allowed to owners at the same time to sue lot and obtain in the same proceedings & settlement of their personal claims for damages. The right to recover damages in such an action was recognized by the Roman-Dutch Law. Our Partition Ordinance, however, provides that when any landed property is held in common it is competent for one or more co-owners to compel a partition of such property, or should such partition be impossible to apply for a sale thereof, and provides that one or more owners in any such case may file in the District Court a libel describing the property and stating the extent of his or their share or interest therein, the names and residences of all the co-owners, and the mortgagees and the extent of their respective shares or interest in the land, and also the improvements, if any, which have been on the property by any owner or owners so far as they are known to the person or persons filing the libel and praying for a partition of the property amongst the several owners or a sale thereof as the case may require. Whilst the Ordinance provides for a claim for compensation, it nowhere provides for any claim for damages, nor does it provide for an account being taken in respect of the profit taken by one co-owner to the detriment of another co-owner in the land. It is singularly silent with regard to any claim for damages being raised."

statement: A plaintiff must set out every title by which he claims to be entitled to land in an action, and if he omits to plead any such title, he is debarred from setting up that title in a subsequent action.
supporting_quote: "Where a plaintiff brings an action for land, he must, under section 33 of the Civil Code, set out every title by which he claims to be entitled to it at the time of action. Where he omits to plead any title on which he might have relied in one action, he is debarred from setting up such title in a subsequent action."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 33

statement: The words 'or otherwise' in section 18 of the Ordinance No. 2 of 1877 (section 2 of Ordinance No. 21 of 1900) do not include general criminal offences committed by a notary outside his duties.
supporting_quote: "It limits it to a prosecution in respect of these rules and regulations, and does not refer to prosecution for offences under the general law"
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 21 of 1900, section 18

statement: In the absence of fraud, the remedy of restitutio in integrum is not available in a partition suit on the ground of discovery of fresh evidence after judgment. The only remedy available is an action for damages as provided by the Partition Ordinance.
supporting_quote: The only remedy available is an action for damages as provided for by the Partition Ordinance.

statement: A sale by an owner of shares pending partition proceedings is absolutely void, not merely voidable.
supporting_quote: see Annamalay Pillai v. Perera 2 that a sale in the circumstances in which the substituted plaintiff purchased is absolutely void, and not voidable only, that is to say that the purchaser from a person who has bought at a Fiscal's sale any interest in the land which is the subject of partition derives no title whatever by his purchase. All the previous decisions were reviewed in the case of Annamalay Pillai v. Perera,3 and, in my opinion, the construction placed by Moncreiff and Middleton JJ. on section 17, in view of the language employed in it, was eminently correct. In Dewar Umma v. Ismail Marikar3 Wood Renton J. has construed section 17 in the same way in which it was construed in Annamalay v. Perera 2 by a majority of the Court. The limitation placed by Clarence and Dias JJ. on the words " any owner " in section 17 is not justified, because it will resulti in introducing into the enactment certain words of qualification repugnant to the plain intention of the Legislature, which was to expedite and make easy the settlement of land disputes by means of partition actions. I would, therefore, hold that the sale to substituted plaintiff by Karunaratne, although Karunaratne was no party to the action, was absolutely void, because it was a sale by the owner of certain shares pending partition proceedings. The District Judge was, however, wrong in dismissing the action. The appellant's conveyance having been held to be void, it was open to the District Judge, considering that this was a partition action, to strike his name out, and order that Karunaratne be made Foot Notes: 1 (1906) 9 N.. L. R. 217. 2 (1902) 6 N. L. R. 108; 3 Browne 200. 3 (1906) 3 Balasingham 99. 224 a party in the place of the original plaintiff, re-apportioning the shares by allotting to Karunaratne the eleven-fifteenths he had pur-chased which belonged to the original plaintiff and first defendant, and then entering a fresh interlocutory decree on that footing. Although the original plaintiff has admitted that her interests-have passed to Karunaratne, the District Judge will hold an inquiry into his title as derived both from her and the first defendant as a precautionary measure. The decree

statement: Minors are not bound by section 9 of the Partition Ordinance, and even if they were, the appellants have to face a significant difficulty as no other remedy is open to them except an action for damages.
supporting_quote: "If minors are not bound by the section, it may be argued that the appellants have suffered no damage by the decree. If minors are bound by the section, then the appellants have to face a tether difficulty. Here is an enactment which, in creating new machinery for partition, bars all remedies-after a certain stage in the proceedings but one, which it indicates-an action for damages."

statement: A right of servitude of light and air may be acquired by prescription by mere enjoyment, just as much as any other servitude.
supporting_quote: "A right of servitude of light and air may be acquired by prescription by mere enjoyment, just as much as any other servitude."

statement: A proctor's physical appearance in court is not treated as an appearance under the Indian Code unless he is fully instructed.
supporting_quote: "As far as I can understand, the reasons the Indian Courts gave in the cases cited to us appear to be that when a pleader or vakil appears in court in view of the provision of section 64 of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure, it is necessary that the court should not only be satisfied with the physical appearance of the pleader, but that he is duly instructed and able to answer all material questions relating to the suit"

statement: Where a vendor professed to sell at different dates the same land to two distinct vendees, and the first vendee delivered the deed of sale earlier than the second to the head clerk at the office of the Registrar of Lands for registration in compliance with the terms of section 16 of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891, and where, owing to an office rule, which precluded the day-book clerk from accepting 'any deeds from any member of the department', the registration of the first vendee's title was delayed, and the second vendee's deed was first actually registered, the first vendee is not to be prejudiced by an office rule which precluded his deed from being actually first registered.
supporting_quote: The chief clerk says he refused to accept the plaintiff's deed 'because the rule of this department is that the day book clerk cannot accept any deeds from any member of the department. ' That may be a very salutary rule as regards the members of the department. I do not see, however, how it can affect the rights of outsiders. Both the plaintiff's and defendant's deed reached the registrar's office on the same day. The plaintiff's deed was received first by the registrar of lands. It is true that the defendant's deed owing to a departmental rule was entered first in the day book, but both deeds were entered on the same day in that book. The departmental rule cannot be treated as rendering void the plaintiff's deed, which was received at the registrar's office earlier than the defendant's deed.

statement: The jurisdiction of the Court to entertain an action under section 247 should be determined by the value of the property seized, not solely by the amount of the decree.
supporting_quote: "I do not see why the amount of the writ should alone be taken into consideration as determining the question of jurisdiction. There are two things that must be considered in a matter of this kind, and they are so closely mixed up that they should not be separated I mean that both the value of the land and the amount of the writ are important factors which must decide the question of jurisdiction."

statement: The mere fact that land has appeared to the Government Agent to be forest, chena, waste, or unoccupied and a notice required by the Ordinance in respect thereof given is not of itself sufficient ground of presumption that the land is such as falls within the scope of the Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The mere fact that the land which is the subject of the reference has appeared to the Government Agent to be forest, chena, waste, or unoccupied land and that he has given the notice required by the Ordinance in respect thereof is not of itself sufficient ground of presumption that the land is such as falls within the scope of the Ordinance."

statement: A person has the right to build on land belonging to another and use such building until the owner of the land tenders the value of the building, which is known as the jus superficiarium.
supporting_quote: "According to the Common Law of Ceylon a person has the right to build on land belonging to another, and to use such building until the owner of the land tenders the value of the building. This right, which is known as the jus superficiarium, is acquired and lost in the same manner as any other right to immovable property; it may be acquired by prescription."

statement: The right of pre-emption under the Tesavalamai is limited to adjacent owners who are mortgagees, and not to non-adjacent mortgagees.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, therefore, the right of pre-emption only lies in the adjacent owner who happens to be a mortgagee of the land, and I therefore think that the plaintiffs are not entitled to the right they claim under the Tesavalamai"

statement: Prescription begins to run against an administrator claiming property on behalf of the estate from the date of the grant of letters of administration and not from the date of the death of the intestate.
supporting_quote: "In Ceylon prescription begins to run against an administrator claiming property on behalf of the estate from the date of the grant of letters of administration and not from the date of the death of the intestate."

statement: A distiller is liable for leaving distilled spirits outside the store if such action is not covered by specific exceptions in the Ordinance, even if a renter has possession of the spirits.
supporting_quote: "The arrack was measured on a Saturday evening, and no permit for removal could be obtained until the following Monday. The arrack remained outside the store over the Sunday and was seized on the Monday. I am of opinion that the accused should not have allowed the arrack to be measured on a Saturday evening, or, if he did allow it, he should have locked up the arrack in his store until the permit for removal was brought."

statement: A partition suit cannot be maintained where the land is not held in common and each party has acquired a prescriptive title to a divided portion.
supporting_quote: "It appears to me it would be an abuse of the Partition Ordinance to allow the plaintiff and defendants to use that Ordinance merely to confirm a partition that already had taken place seventeen years before, and which by possession of over ten years had ripened into a prescriptive right in favour of the plaintiff as to his divided portion, and in favour of the defendants, as to their divided portion."

statement: The cause of action survives to the surviving partner when one of several partners dies, and does not need to be joined with the legal representatives of the deceased partner.
supporting_quote: "I think it is clear from the authorities, both English and Indian, which have been cited to us, that although his interest in partnership property passed to his executor, yet the remedy in respect of that property survived to the surviving partner alone, and that it could be brought in his name alone"

statement: The widow's conduct estops her from claiming any share of the property.
supporting_quote: "Held , that she must be taken to have renounced her right to any share in the property, and that her conduct estopped her from claiming any"

statement: A failure to perform a contract is considered a 'wrong' for the prevention or redress of which an action may be brought, and this can establish jurisdiction in the court where the breach occurred.
supporting_quote: "It is clear from the definition of the word "action" that the word "wrong" in the definition is not restricted to "torts. " If the plaintiff had averred an express refusal to fulfil the contract the jurisdiction of the Court of Kandy could not have been disputed, for refusal to fulfil an obligation is specified in the definition as a cause of action."

statement: The presumption omnia rite esse acta applies to official acts, such as a sale under the Paddy Tax Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "A sale under the Paddy Tax Ordinance is distinctly an official act done by the Government Agent in recovering a tax due to the Crown."

statement: An appeal to the Supreme Court is not a re-hearing and should be decided according to the law existing at the date of the commencement of the action.
supporting_quote: "Now I take leave to think that the Supeme Court of Ceylon in its appellate jurisdiction under section 40 of the Courts Ordinance 'in hearing a case in appeal ' deals only with appeals ' strictly so-called,' and does not deal with them by way of re-hearing, but according to the law existing at the time when the action was begun."

statement: A vendor who receives formal notice to warrant and defend his title may either take part in the suit, suffer the purchaser to appoint him procurator in rem suam, or request transfer from defendant to plaintiff under section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: Where a vendor receives formal notice calling on him to warrant and defend his title to a property sold by him, he may either take part in the suit against the trespasser in order to prevent collusion, or he may suffer the purchaser to appoint him procurator in rem suam and take the conduct of the action into his own hands, or if he is made a defendant in the action he may ask, under section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code, that he be transferred from the position of a defendant to that of a plaintiff.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 18

statement: A mortgage decree that orders the defendant to pay a certain sum of money within a certain time and directs that, in default of such payment, the property hypothecated be sold to satisfy the debt is a decree for the payment of money.
supporting_quote: The decree orders the defendant to pay the plaintiff Rs. 282 with interest and costs within one month from date, and in default of payment directs the sale of the hypothecated property.

statement: The District Court within the district of which a minor is resident has jurisdiction to appoint a curator for his estate.
supporting_quote: "I think, however, that it is difficult to gather this opinion altogether from the terms of chapter XL. of the Civil Procedure Code, as he would appear to have thought, section 584 being the only section in that chapter which seems to point to that conclusion. Looking, however, to the terms of the 2nd paragraph of section 71, I am inclined to the opinion that the Court within the district of which the minor is resident is the Court having jurisdiction to appoint a curator to his estate."
statute_citation_verbatim: "By section 71 of the Courts Ordinance, No. 1 of 1889, general jurisdiction over the persons and estates of minors and wards is conferred on the District Courts. By section 71 of the same Ordinance it is enacted that ' every district court shall have the care and custody of the persons and estates of all idiots and lunatics and others of insane and nonsane mind resident within its district, with full power to appoint guardians and curators of all such persons and their estates. '"

statement: The first defendant is not bound by the mortgage decree and consequent Fiscal's sale, as the second defendant did not furnish his address to the Registrar of Lands under section 644 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "It is common ground that the mortgagee did not furnish his address to the Registrar of Lands. It is thus clear that the first defendant is not bound by the mortgage decree, and that the action against him fails."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 644 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The lessor is bound to put the lessee in possession of the property leased; that is an implied term of the contract of lease; and if he fails to do so, he is liable to pay the lessee damages for his breach of the contract.
supporting_quote: It is an implied term of the contract of letting and hiring that the lessor should put the lessee in possession of the property let; and a lessor who fails to implement his contract by so doing is liable in damages for breach of contract.

statement: An executor's sale of property burdened with a fidei commissum is not valid without the leave of the Court or proof of special circumstances, according to the blend of English and Roman-Dutch Law administered in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that it would not be good. The executor, as an instrument in the administration of the estates of deceased persons, was imported into the Ceylon system of law as regards all persons in the opinion of the Judges in Staples v. de Saram( 1 Ram. (1868-1868) 275.) by the Charter of 1833. There appears no reason to doubt the correctness of the opinion of the learned Judges."

statement: The dismissal of a claim on the ground that it was improperly made is not an order falling under sections 244, 245, or 246 of the Civil Procedure Code; and the claimant in such a case is not obliged to bring an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code to establish his right to the property claimed.
supporting_quote: The dismissal of a claim on the ground that it was improperly made is not an order falling under sections 244, 245, or 246 of the Civil Procedure Code; and the claimant in such a case is not obliged to bring an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code to establish his right to the property claimed.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 247

statement: A donation made by a person in favour of his daughter-in-law in contemplation of her marriage with the donor's son is revocable under Kandyan Law.
supporting_quote: "Therefore after the said marriage I nor my heirs, &c, shall raise any objection or dispute to the grant herein made, and the donee, the said Dingiri Menika, and her heirs, &c, shall possess the same after the said marriage."

statement: In a deed of gift, the prohibition against alienation in the habendum is void as repugnant to the terms of an unfettered grant made in the operative clause.
supporting_quote: "Upon a strict construction of the instrument, I am inclined to think that the testatum or operative clause having made an unfettered grant of the property with express contemplation of alienation in the mention of assigns, the prohibition of alienation in the habendum is void as repugnant to the terms of the grant."

statement: A Fiscal's sale does not constitute an alienation by the owner within the meaning of section 17 of 'The Partition Ordinance, 1863'.
supporting_quote: "I agree with my learned brothers, whose judgments I have had the advantage of perusing, that an alienation by the Fiscal being ex necessitate, and involuntary so far as the owner of the share sold is concerned, is not an alienation by the owner within the meaning of section 17 of the Partition Ordinance, and would grant the prayer of the petition of appeal with costs."
statute_citation_verbatim: 'The Partition Ordinance, 1863' (No. 10 of 1863)

statement: A judgment-debtor who has fraudulently conveyed property can be cited as a party defendant in an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code to set aside the fraudulent conveyance.
supporting_quote: "I, therefore, can see no reason under the Civil Procedure Code why a claim to set aside the deed might not be added to the plaint in an action under section 247, or be pleaded in the answer in reconvention"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247

statement: A deed of gift with a valid clause against revocation, considering past assistance and pecuniary consideration, is irrevocable.
supporting_quote: "Here, as there, a pecuniary consideration is disclosed; and in all three cases the terms of the debarring clause are substantially identical."

statement: An objection to non-joinder of parties should be taken at the earliest possible opportunity; otherwise such objection will be considered to have been waived.
supporting_quote: An objection to non-joinder of parties should be taken at the earliest possible opportunity; otherwise such objection will be considered to have been waived.

statement: A lessee can still claim the right to compensation for improvements even if a forfeiture clause in a lease is not enforced, as long as no damage has resulted from the default and the breach was due to accident or mistake.
supporting_quote: "The Court of Equity in England was from an early period accustomed to grant relief against the payment of the whole penalty on money bonds; and the Statutes 4 and 5 Ann. c. 16, ss. 12 and 13, and 8 and 9 Will. III. c. 11 conferred a similar jurisdiction on the Courts of Law."

statement: The plaintiff is entitled to a declaration that he is the manager of the temple and an injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with his management, provided there is no evidence showing he has been removed or voluntarily withdrawn from his office.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion he is entitled to a declaration that he is the manager, and to an injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with his management, and to an order for delivery to him of the articles specified in the plaint."

statement: The Court has the power to order a lease on land to be cancelled and valued separately, with its value deducted from the purchase money and paid to the lessees in cases where the land is too small for partition.
supporting_quote: That the Court should have the power to order the land to be sold free of the lease is only reasonably necessary for effectually carrying out the object of the Partition Ordinance, and I have no hesitation in holding that it has that power.

statement: The appointment of an attorney to act in Ceylon does not remove the disability constituted by absence beyond the seas under section 14 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "I can conceive of only one way by which absence from a place is terminated, namely, by going to that place. It can scarcely be argued that the right to sue for the recovery of the property first accrued to the attorney on his appointment in 1894."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 14 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, s. 14.

statement: Rule 16 of the rules of the Public Service Mutual Provident Association is not ultra vires of the Association.
supporting_quote: "Held, that this rule was not ultra vires of the Association."

statement: Oral evidence is admissible to prove fraud subsequent to the execution of a deed under Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, even though the initial transaction was not fraudulent.
supporting_quote: "It is clear that according to section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 oral evidence is inadmissible in cases relating to land, Nachiar v. Fernando (2) . But where there is fraud the proposition may be stated broadly that oral evidence is admissible."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840

statement: A reissue of a writ is not vitiated by the fact that the judgment-creditor has failed to mention to the Court a payment made by the judgment-debtor before such reissue; and an innocent purchaser under such writ is not affected by such failure.
supporting_quote: "It would be well if practitioners make it a rule never to reissue an old writ. T HIS was an application by the judgment-debtor to set aside a Fiscal's sale of property sold under a mortgage decree. The application, to which the judgment-debtor, the purchaser, and the Fiscal were made parties, was made on the follo"

statement: The shipowner is liable for all natural consequences of the shipper's wrong-doing, whether of a general average character or not.
supporting_quote: "It appears to me that every line of this reasoning applies with equal force whether the cause of the danger which called for the general average act was the negligence of the master or the fault of one of the cargo owners. The shipper in default may have no claim to contribution. But his wrong-doing is not to prejudice the rights of his innocent co-owners, nor does it relieve the shipowner of the duty to protect their interests by an adjustment of general average."

statement: A plaintiff may be entitled to damages even if specific performance of a contract is no longer possible, provided the other conditions stipulated in the agreement were complied with.
supporting_quote: "I think there is no good cause of action alleged against the second and third defendants. They denied that they were aware of the agreement, and no issue was settled on that point, or as to whether they knew that the plaintiff had complied with, or that the seller had failed to comply with, the agreement; and the four months had expired before the transfer and mortgage to them."

statement: Under the Tesawalamai, a wife's inherited property is considered her separate property and does not vest in her husband.
supporting_quote: "On the contrary, the Thesawaleme regards a wife's inherited property as being, like her dowry, her separate property."

statement: An administrator is not entitled to maintain an action for a chose in action belonging to his intestate, but not included in the inventory of that intestate's property or covered by the amount of stamp duty paid on the letters of administration.
supporting_quote: "The question at issue is whether an administrator can sue for a chose in action belonging to his intestate, but not included in the inventory of that intestate's property, or covered by the amount of the stamp duty paid on the letters of administration. It appears to me that the question must be answered in the negative."

statement: The Crown is liable for the negligence of its servants employed in a government hospital, and a husband can claim damages for the loss of his wife due to such negligence.
supporting_quote: The Crown held liable in damages for the negligence of its Servants employed in the Government hospital, which caused, or contributed to, the death of a patient admitted into the hospital. A husband is entitled to damages for the loss of his wife occasioned by the tortious act of a third party.

statement: A deed of gift, even with a reservation of power to revoke in case of misconduct, vests the property immediately in the donees upon acceptance and does not allow revocation without alleging misconduct.
supporting_quote: "I hold accordingly that the judgment under appeal should be set aside, and judgment given declaring the plaintiffs entitled to the shares claimed."

statement: A proviso in a deed of gift that is inconsistent with an absolute gift cannot be given effect to.
supporting_quote: "The proviso is inconsistent with the previous absolute gift. And he does not say what is to happen if she does not so grant and convey it to the children; apparently she might have disposed of it by will to any one she pleased. And if he meant that she should only have a life interest with remainder to the children, I should have expected him to say so; and moreover, if that was his intention, what was the object of requiring her to 'grant and convey?'"

statement: Marriage does not confer majority on a Kandyan minor wife under the applicable laws.
supporting_quote: "It is clear, of course, that if Roman-Dutch Law governs the case, marriage confers emancipation: Deeresekere v. Goonesakere; 1 and also-to put aside at the outset a preliminary argument suggested by Mr. Hector Jayewardene on behalf of the appellant-that section 502 of the Civil Procedure Code throws no light on the problem we have now to solve."
