statement: The first defendant's acquiescence in the partnership deed being drawn up with the second defendant as a partner, subject to his claim to draw as much money from the business as the other partners had drawn, does not amount to such a recognition of the second defendant's right as would estop the first defendant now from asserting that the second defendant has no legal right.
supporting_quote: I do not think that first defendant's acquiescence in the partnership deed being drawn up with the second defendant as a partner, subject to his claim to draw as much money from the business as the other partners had drawn, amounts to such a recognition of the second defendant's right as would estop the first defendant now from asserting that second defendant has no legal right.

statement: Long and uninterrupted possession, ut dominus, of land subsequently claimed to form part of the public highway raises a strong presumption that the land in question is the private property of the possessor.
supporting_quote: "Although it may not be possible for a private owner to prescribe from the public highway by virtue of length of possession, yet long and uninterrupted possession, ut dominus, of land subsequently claimed to form part of the public highway, raises a strong presumption that the land in question is the private property of the possessor."

statement: An action for use and occupation will not lie unless there has been a contractual relationship, either express or implied, between the parties.
supporting_quote: "An action for use and occupation will not lie unless there has been a contractual relationship, either express or-as in the case of a tenancy by sufferance-implied, between the parties"

statement: A grantor cannot validly reserve an absolute unfettered power to revoke a grant of land in perpetuity at any time for any purpose.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, as the two declarations are inconsistent, and as the first is quite clear and the second is doubtful, we must give effect to the first, and hold that there is no absolute unfettered power of revocation at any time."

statement: A judgment-creditor is not required to prove due diligence or explain the delay in applying for a writ of execution if more than one year has elapsed between the date of decree and the application, provided that the debt remains unpaid.
supporting_quote: "Where more than a year has elapsed between the date of decree and the date of application for writ, the judgment-creditor is not required, as a condition precedent to Such application being allowed, to prove the exercise of due diligence, or to explain the delay in making such application. The judgment-creditor need only show that the decree has not been satisfied."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 337 and 347.

statement: A person who obtains money on a mortgage of property, which at the date of such mortgage is under seizure, by concealing from the mortgagee the fact of such seizure, is guilty of cheating.
supporting_quote: "A person who obtains money on a mortgage of property, which at the date of such mortgage is under seizure, by concealing from the mortgagee the fact of such seizure, is guilty of cheating under section 403 of the Penal Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 403 of the Penal Code

statement: A deed of gift can create a fidei commissum, and acceptance may be inferred from circumstances such as possession.
supporting_quote: "Held, also, that it is not essential that the acceptance of a deed of gift should appear on the face of it, but that such acceptance may be inferred from circumstances. Possession by the donee of the property donated leads do the inevitable inference that the deed of donation was accepted."

statement: A notarially executed document containing a condition for the payment of money may be deemed to fall under section 6 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, allowing a plaintiff to sue within ten years.
supporting_quote: 'In my opinion the document we have to deal with in this case, though notarially attested, is not an agreement conditioned for the payment of money. It is an agreement to deliver certain movables, namely, paddy, by a certain date; that being so, the case seems to me to be on all fours with the case cited by Mr. Kadramer.'
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, section 6

statement: The execution-creditor may, in an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code, prove the prescriptive right of the execution-debtor to the property; and for that purpose the execution-debtor may be added as a party plaintiff or party defendant, as the case may be.
supporting_quote: The execution-creditor may, in an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code, prove the prescriptive right of the execution-debtor to the property; and for that purpose the execution-debtor may be added as a party plaintiff or party defendant, as the case may be.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247, Civil Procedure Code

statement: A deed of gift to a minor requires present acceptance by the natural or legal guardian, not an acceptance at some future indefinite time by the minor himself after he has attained majority.
supporting_quote: In the case before us the property which was the subject of the donation never came into the possession either of the donee or of his self-constituted. guardian, but always remained with the donor. The District Judge has expressly found this to be so. He was in error, however, in holding that there was due acceptance. There could not be in law any acceptance, as I have already pointed out, by an uncle as natural guardian of his minor nephew.

statement: In putting documents in evidence in a case the provisions of sections 111-114 of the Civil Procedure Code ought to be observed.
supporting_quote: "In putting documents in evidence in a case the provisions of sections 111-114 of the Civil Procedure Code ought to be observed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 111-114

statement: Intervenors, who are lessees, cannot claim compensation or damages in land acquisition proceedings where the property is subject to a fidei commissum and the intervenors were not authorized by the other claimants.
supporting_quote: "Held , that the intervention was wrongly allowed, and that it was not competent for the lessees to claim compensation or damages in these proceedings."

statement: The Fiscal is not a corporation sole with the right of perpetual succession, and that the successor in office of a Fiscal, in whose favour an obligation is created by bond, has no right to maintain an action on such bond, even where the obligation is created in favour of the said Fiscal and his successors in office.
supporting_quote: Held , by Wendt J., that the Fiscal is not a corporation sole with the right of perpetual succession, and that the successor in office of a Fiscal, in whose favour an obligation is created by bond, has no right to maintain an action on such bond, even where the obligation is created in favour of the said Fiscal and his successors in office.

statement: An unregistered deed bearing date before February 1, 1840, cannot be received in evidence even if both parties rely on it.
supporting_quote: "The provision in section 7 of the Ordinance of 1866, that an unregistered deed bearing date before February 1, 1840, shall not be received in evidence, bars its admission, even although both parties rely on it."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 6 of 1866, section 7.

statement: A donor in a deed of gift may reserve to himself the power to revoke the gift, and such a revocation is valid.
supporting_quote: "It is lawful for the donor in a deed of gift to reserve to himself the power to revoke the gift; and a revocation made in the exercise of such power is valid."

statement: The plaintiff is estopped by her conduct relative to the execution of a notarial deed in which she, as administratrix, conveyed certain lands to the first defendant, thereby intentionally causing the first defendant to believe that the lands were paraveni property of Sundara and acting upon such belief.
supporting_quote: That is to say, he argued that plaintiff by standing by and seeing herself as administratrix execute and deliver the deed to the first defendant, with the recital that the lands were the paraveni property of Sundara, and had therefore devolved ab intestato on the first defendant, had by such conduct intentionally caused the first defendant to believe that the lands were such paraveni property, and to act upon such belief, and that plaintiff was therefore precluded by section 115 from denying the truth of the representation so made by her.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 115 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: Where a vendor expressly covenants to warrant and defend the title in a deed of conveyance, this excludes any implied obligation on the part of the vendor to give good title.
supporting_quote: "Held, that this express covenant in the deed excluded the obligation implied by law on the part of the vendor to give good title to the vendee, and that the plaintiff must be confined to such express stipulation."

statement: The burden of proving title or possession lies with the decree-holder when an obstructor has satisfied the Court that they are a bona fide claimant.
supporting_quote: "But when once the obstructor has satisfied the Court on that point, the application of section 377 (b) has exhausted itself, and the initial and ultimate burden of proving title or possession, as the case may be, is on the decree-holder."

statement: A will that limits the surviving spouse's interest to a mere possessory right, prohibiting alienation of property, does not create a fidei commissum but rather a usufruct.
supporting_quote: "Clause 3 is the only clause which directly gives the surviving testator any interest. It does not appoint him heir of the precedent testator, and does not devise to him the dominium of any property of the estate, but expressly limits his interest to the possession of the produce or income, and, as if further to emphasize the limitation, expressly prohibits him from alienating the movable and immovable property in any manner whatsoever."

statement: A claim by prescription can be waived.
supporting_quote: "I have no doubt that it can. When one party says that he does not rely on a claim by prescription, the other party adduces no evidence to rebut such a claim and therefore the Court must treat the claim as not proved."

statement: The execution sale did not convey the mortgage debt, and the right to recover the mortgaged debt passed only to the original mortgagee's heirs.
supporting_quote: "There was a previous action (C. R., 1,993)about this land. The present plaintiff's vendor sued the purchasers at the Fiscal's sale to be put in possession; he was held to have title, the purchasers at the Fiscal's sale against Salaman being held to have kept the mortgage alive. It may seem hard that the purchasers under writ should fail to prove title, it being held that they had possessed as mortgagees (see C. R., 1,993), and that now they should fail to get the mortgage debt paid to them as they had not purchased the mortgage. But I think the law is clear, and the Fiscal's sale did not convey the mortgage debt."

statement: Intervenors are entitled to intervene in a partition suit before the sale is carried out, even after an order for sale has been made under section 4 of the Partition Ordinance (No. 10 of 1863).
supporting_quote: Held (reversing the order of the District Judge), that they were so entitled.

statement: A partition suit is not a mere proceeding inter partes to be settled by consent, compromise or the opinion of the Court on points submitted in issues. The paramount duty cast upon the District Judge is to ascertain who are the actual owners of the land.
supporting_quote: "A partition suit is not a mere proceeding inter partes to be settled of consent, or by the opinion of the Court upon such points as they choose to submit to it in the shape of issues. It is a matter in which the Court must satisfy itself that the plaintiff has made out his title"

statement: The decision of the Maha Sanga Sabhawa is not binding on the parties if it was improperly made, as evidenced by the exclusion of important evidence.
supporting_quote: "Moreover, the order of February 12, 1904, was attacked by the second defendant as having been improperly made; a good deal of the evidence was directed to that point, and at the close of the evidence the plaintiff's counsel admitted that it is competent for the Court to set aside the award (meaning the order) on grounds of irregularity or misconduct; and I agree with the District Judge that the order was improperly made, because the most important evidence was improperly excluded."

statement: A person who has obtained possession of land in a subordinate character, such as tenant or mortgagee, must show that by an overt act known to the person under whom he possesses, he has got rid of his subordinate status and assumed the character of a purchaser for prescription to commence.
supporting_quote: Where a person who has obtained possession of the land of another in a subordinate character, e.g. as tenant or mortgagee, seeks to utilize that possession as the foundation of a title by prescription, he must show that by an overt act, known to the person under whom he possesses, he has got rid for this proposition, it will be found in such cases as Maduanwala v. the property ut dominus.

statement: An action quia timet is maintainable in Ceylon, provided there is actual or imminent injury and prospective damage of a substantial nature.
supporting_quote: "The existence of such a deed on the register, said that learned Judge, in language that may fitly be applied to the present case, 'would necessarily 1 (1886) 7 S. C. C. 145. 2 (1901) 2 Tambiah 73. 19 prejudice the plaintiff. It would render his share in the land unsale able and valueless, because no one would purchase from him or would lend money to him on that security until his title on the register was cleared."

statement: A Fiscal's conveyance obtained after the institution of an action but before trial can still confer title for the purpose of rei vindicatio proceedings.
supporting_quote: "The facts that the second defendant-respondent had obtained the Fiscal's transfer at the date when he filed answer, and that the plaintiff-respondent sued not on the Fiscal's sale, but on his own transfer from the second defendant, are, I think, immaterial. The latter point is exactly covered by Silva v. Hendrick Appu (ubi sup.) , in which the action was brought by the assignee of the purchaser at the Fiscal's sale."

statement: A dismissal of an action for want of title on the part of the plaintiff to sue does not operate as res judicata.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the plea was bad, inasmuch as the first action was dismissed . for want of title on the part of the plaintiff to sue, and such dismissal did not operate . as res judicata."

statement: Once a writ of execution is received by the Fiscal while property is already under sequestration, it operates as an automatic seizure without further action.
supporting_quote: "I therefore think that where the Fiscal has already seized property upon a mandate of sequestration, and while so having the property in question in custodia legis receives a writ of execution from a judgment-creditor of the person whose goods are under sequestration, the receipt by the Fiscal of such writ operates as a seizure of such goods without further action on the part of the Fiscal."

statement: A party who has been equally negligent as the other cannot take advantage of their own wrong to enrich themselves at the expense of the co-delinquent.
supporting_quote: If the doctrine were carried out under all circumstances, it would practically lead to a repeal of a legislative enactment of great use and importance, and I do not think in admitting it as a part of our law, which has been done in the case of Perera v. Fernando, 1 decided in 1864, we should do so without jealously regarding the facts of each case.

statement: An act of unlawful interference with the possession of property, under circumstances disclosing a real intention to intimidate or annoy the possessor, constitutes criminal trespass.
supporting_quote: "When once an act of unlawful interference with the possession of property, under circumstances disclosing a real intention to intimidate or annoy the possessor, has been established, the offence of criminal trespass has been committed"

statement: The onus of proving the date of Justina's death lies with the party claiming she died before July 1, 1852.
supporting_quote: Such continuance is essential to first defendant's title, and he must prove it.

statement: A judgment-creditor is not the representative in interest of the owner within the meaning of section 92 of the Evidence Ordinance, but may give evidence of a contemporaneous agreement varying the terms of a written contract under section 99 of the Evidence Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "It is true he is seeking to prove that at the date of seizure his judgment-debtor was possessed of certain saleable rights in the goods, but he has not himself acquired any 'interest' in the goods under or through the judgment-debtor. Unless he has, he is in my opinion not a '' representative in interest'' of the judgment-debtor."

statement: A dismissal of an action for failure to establish a cause of action does not create res judicata if the court did not actually adjudicate on the merits of the claim.
supporting_quote: "Although not exactly on all fours, such a case is somewhat analogous to those in which the Court declines jurisdiction altogether, on the ground that the subject-matter is outside the territorial or pecuniary limits of its jurisdiction. It is beside the point to argue that it would at the present day be held, and that in deciding case No. 5, 265 the District Judge ought to have held, that plaintiff had a good cause of action, and that plaintiff ought to have appealed and had the case sent back for trial and determination of his title. Suffice it that the Court held the other way."

statement: A mortgage is not a transfer and does not fall within the purview of section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "A mortgage is not a transfer, and does not fall within the purview of section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code"
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 547

statement: There is no limit to the time within which a first application for execution of a decree may be granted.
supporting_quote: "I think that the order of the District Court should be set aside, and the case sent back for decision on the other objections taken by the respondent to the appellant's application. The respondent should pay the appellant's costs of this appeal."

statement: A judgment in a partition suit operates as res judicata and prevents the parties from raising the question of title again.
supporting_quote: "Now it is trite law that in a partition action the plaintiffs (and each party is practically plaintiff in respect of the interest he claims) must prove not only their common ownership inter se, but also a good title as against all others, because the effect of a decree of partition is to confer an absolute title. Hence a partition suit may fail, in spite of proof of the parties' common ownership inter se, if the Court is not satisfied that the parties collectively have a good title to the land."

statement: A plaintiff can maintain an action on a mortgage bond even after accepting a conveyance that was void due to the properties being under seizure, if he acted in ignorance of this fact.
supporting_quote: "I hold, therefore, that the plaintiff is entitled to maintain his action on the mortgage bond, and that the second defendant was rightly joined as a purchaser in execution of four out of the five lands mortgaged to the plaintiff."

statement: A conveyance of land by a father to his daughter as dowry on her marriage is, prima facie, a conveyance for valuable consideration and gains priority over an anterior deed of sale by prior registration.
supporting_quote: "A conveyance of land by a father to, or for the benefit of, his daughter by way of dowry on her marriage is, prima facie, a conveyance for valuable consideration."

statement: A Court has no jurisdiction to vacate or alter an order after it has been passed, except as provided by section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: A Court has no jurisdiction (except as provided by section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code) to vacate or alter an order after it has been passed.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 189

statement: A transfer to B may vest title in A even without A's name mentioned in the deed, if it is a gift and not a sale.
supporting_quote: "But whether that is so or not the transaction in the present case was a gift, and should be supported as such. I would dismiss the appeal with costs."

statement: A deed of gift of land must be stamped ad valorem.
supporting_quote: "I accordingly hold that this deed required to be stamped ad valorem."

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift is generally revocable unless the circumstances which constitute non-revocability appear most clearly on the face of the deed itself.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the ruling laid down by the Full Court in Bologna v. Punchi Mahatmeya, 1 taken in conjunction with the ruling of the Full Court in Kirimenika v. Ganrala and others, 3 should guide the decisions of this Court in determining whether or not a Kandyan deed of gift is revocable or not."

statement: A grant to a man and his descendants can create a fidei commissum if it shows an intention to tie up the properties for multiple generations, especially with a prohibition against alienation.
supporting_quote: "In 9 S. C. C. 33 a Court of three Judges held that a grant of property 'to A, her children, and their children in perpetuity, which shall not be sold, mortgaged, or gifted to any one, ' was a good fidei commissum."

statement: The court held that there was no valid partition decree allotting the southern seven-eighths of the land to defendants' vendors, and thus plaintiffs were not estopped from asserting their title.
supporting_quote: "In spite of respondents' objection, I think it was open to plaintiffs to take this point. They were not parties to the decree and had no notice of it, and therefore their averring that defendants claimed under a decree and praying that it be set aside as obtained by fraud does not preclude them from taking exception to the contents of the decree when the record was produced and relied upon."

statement: A married woman has the right to appear as a party in an action concerning her separate immovable property, even if section 20 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 was repealed by Ordinance No. 2 of 1889 without substitution.
supporting_quote: "I cannot believe that this was the effect of that repeal, or that it was the intention of the Legislature that it should be so. The Legislature in passing Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 were emancipating women from the thraldom of the Roman-Dutch principle of the community of property on marriage."

statement: A minor's sale of immovables under Kandyan Law is not absolutely void but voidable, and can be avoided only on repayment of the purchase money and probably equitably of the value of improvements.
supporting_quote: I do not think, therefore, we are concluded by the decision of the Pull Court in Muttiah Chetty v. Dingiria et al., and I am strongly of opinion that we should hold, if possible, that the contracts of minors are, as a general rule, not absolutely void under Kandyan Law, but voidable.

statement: A party to a suit should not be allowed to make out a new case on the hearing in review.
supporting_quote: "A party to a suit should not be allowed to make out a new case on the hearing in review."

statement: A minor's immovable property cannot be alienated by him, his parent, or guardian without the authority of the Court.
supporting_quote: 'In my opinion the balance of authority is to the effect that it cannot (see 3 S. C. C. 46 and 6 N. L. R. 367, and the authorities quoted there; see also 3 Browne 12 and 150).'

statement: Where a mortgagee purchases from his mortgagor property mortgaged with him and pays valuable consideration for his purchase, the mortgage is merged in the sale, but the money debt remains all the same, and can be recovered by the mortgagee.
supporting_quote: I think it may be stated as a broad proposition that where a mortgagee purchases from his mortgagor property mortgaged with him and pays valuable consideration for his purchase, the mortgage is merged in the sale, but the money debt remains all the same, and can be recovered by the mortgagee, if necessary, by execution against other property belonging to the mortgagor, because, for obvious reasons, the mortgagee cannot levy execution on property which is already his own.

statement: A person managing a mosque, such as the plaintiff in this case, may have possession sufficient to maintain a possessory action if they control the fabric of the property and manage its affairs on behalf of the congregation.
supporting_quote: "I think that this passage rather understates the position of the muppu as defined in the evidence, but in any event the ratio decidendi was that the muppu's possession was alieno nomine."

statement: The Tesawalamai applies only to Malabar inhabitants of the Province of Jaffna, and not to those who have moved elsewhere.
supporting_quote: "Susan Philips was not herself an 'inhabitant' of that Province. Although she was of Jaffna Tamil descent, her family had long been settled in Puttalam and Chilaw."

statement: The upper proprietor is liable for damages caused by altering natural drainage and discharging water in a more forcible manner than it would naturally occur, even if no negligence is proven.
supporting_quote: "I think the maxim sic utere tuo ut alienum non l�das clearly applies, and the defendants were liable in damages, even if no negligence had been proved."

statement: A claim for the price of newspapers supplied to a person on a verbal agreement falls under section 9 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871 and is prescribed in one year.
supporting_quote: "The papers delivered were goods. The case differs in no way from a claim for the price of boots made and delivered by the maker to the buyer on his verbal order; it falls within section 9, and the ruling of the Commissioner was right."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, ss. 8 and 9

statement: A plaintiff cannot recover damages for negotiating a promissory note under an illegal agreement, as the right to get back the note ceases once it has been unlawfully negotiated.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff cannot succeed against either of the defendants, except by proving that they parted with his note in breach of his agreement with them. The Judge was right in holding the agreement to be immoral and illegal."

statement: The covenant in the deed of transfer amounts to an express and absolute covenant to defend the vendee's title against any disputes whatsoever.
supporting_quote: "I hereby agree on behalf of myself, my heirs, &c., to settle any dispute which may hereafter arise in respect of the title hereby conveyed; and I further hereby declare that I have done nothing before these presents to invalidate the title hereby conveyed."

statement: An auctioneer's authority is determined by the conditions of sale and all the circumstances of the particular transaction.
supporting_quote: "The extent of an auctioneer's authority in regard to any sale must be determined by the conditions of sale and by all the circumstances of that particular transaction."

statement: Acceptance of a deed of gift may be manifested through various means and is determined by the circumstances of each case. In this case, there was sufficient evidence to validate the acceptance.
supporting_quote: It does not follow from the fact that Sinda fraudulently concealed his donation of November 8, 1897, in favour of his children from Mr. Carron at the date of his mortgage to that gentleman in June, 1904, that the deed of 1897 itself was fraudulent; and the circumstances mentioned by the District Judge as to the recital in the deed of gift of the prior mortgage of 1891 in favour of the plaintiff-appellant and the due registration of the deed justify him in coming, as he did, to the conclusion that it was a genuine transfer.

statement: Under the Tesawalamai, a husband can donate more than half of an acquired property as long as he does not dispose of his wife's share immediately. The wife must wait for the dissolution of marriage to seek compensation.
supporting_quote: "But if the husband, who is the absolute manager of the community, ignores the limitation of his powers of donation, and purports to make a gift of the whole of one of the acquired properties, the donation is not ipso facto void so far as it relates to the wife's share, and the wife is not entitled to an immediate rei vindicatio action against the donee for her half share ; she or her heirs must wait till the dissolution of the marriage by death or otherwise for some form of compensation."

statement: A broker who introduces to his principal a person who is able and willing to enter into the contract is entitled to his commission, even if the negotiations should fall through owing to circumstances over which the broker has no control.
supporting_quote: "It has been held in a variety of English cases that where it is agreed that an agent shall be paid a certain commission in the event of his finding a purchaser for the property, it is sufficient, as a general rule, if he procures a complete and binding contract which is accepted by the principal, although the transaction is never completed."

statement: A right of pupillary succession will be forfeited if the pupil deserts his tutor and the temple the incumbency of which he claims.
supporting_quote: "There is ample evidence in the present case justifying the conclusion that such a forfeiture has been incurred by the appellant."

statement: Section 2 of Ordinance No. 9 of 1841 excludes the application of section 8 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840 to any land referred to in section 6, which are lands derived by parties or their predecessors from forest, chena, waste, or uncultivated lands of the Crown.
supporting_quote: "I would hold that the effect of section 2 of Ordinance No. 9 of 1841 is to exclude the application of section 8 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840 to any land referred to in section 6 of that Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 2 of Ordinance No. 9 of 1841

statement: A judgment for the recovery of specific movable property can include an alternative decree for payment of its value, and such a judgment may be executed according to sections 320-322.
supporting_quote: "Per MIDDLETON J.-In an action rei vindicatio for the recovery of specific movable property an alternative decree for payment of its value is not bad."

statement: A party added under section 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure has the right to plead prescription and claim dismissal on that ground, despite an order adding them as a necessary party.
supporting_quote: "As a matter of construction, I think that Mr. H. J. C. Pereira's contention that section 18 of our own Code of Civil Procedure over-rides the right of an added party to plead prescription is untenable."

statement: A mortgage decree, even if not explicitly declared bound and executable, can render property bound and executable for the purposes of a subsequent seizure.
supporting_quote: "It is true it does not completely fulfil the directions in section 201 of the Civil Procedure Code by specifying a day on or before which the money decreed to be due on the mortgage is to be paid, but I think it fulfils the requirements as to which the objection has been taken. The second defendant, therefore, bought the land subject to the mortgage."

statement: A judgment creditor who has seized and registered the seizure of property is not entitled to notice as a puisne incumbrancer under section 643 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Cur. adv. vult. July 28, 1910. Middleton J .- This is a case in which at the argument we were rather led away from the substance of the matter to a critical consideration of its shadow. The question as raised before us was whether a judgment creditor on a money decree, who had seized and registered his seizure of property under section 237 of the Civil Procedure Code, was a puisne incumbrancer under section 643 of the Civil Procedure Code, and as such entitled to notice of proceedings in a hypothecary action by a mortgagee of the same property in order to bind the property by a mortgage decree."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 237 of the Civil Procedure Code; section 643 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A secondary mortgagee is not entitled to notice of a primary mortgagee's action under section 643 of the Civil Procedure Code, and sections 643 and 644 do not apply if neither party provides an address for service.
supporting_quote: The plaintiff did not furnish an address to the Registrar of Lands. Therefore the provisions of section 644 of the Civil Procedure Code do not apply.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 643 and 644 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A Fiscal cannot be made a party to an application under section 282 of the Civil Procedure Code against his will, as his presence is not 'necessary' even though it might be convenient for the determination of the case.
supporting_quote: "It was held by the Supreme Court, in the case of Sinnetampi v. Kandapodi,* that the Fiscal's liability to the execution-creditor and debtor in an action for damages sustained in consequence of a sale irregularly conducted was such a substantial injury within the meaning of the analogous provisions of section 53 of Ordinance No. 4 of 1867 as would give him a right to object to the confirmation of an execution sale on the ground of such irregularity; and there is old authority (see Marshall 171) to the effect that a Fiscal is entitled to notice of proceedings of this kind."

statement: Section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code does not apply to claims for debt secured by mortgage, and section 642 allows a creditor to appoint a representative without proving the estate's value if the mortgaged property is under Rs. 1,000.
supporting_quote: "I think counsel for the appellants is right in arguing that it is not intended to bar claims against an estate for debt, and is not obligatory in such a case as this."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code; section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A decree in a mortgage action for the payment of money due on the mortgage bond and in default thereof for the sale of the mortgaged property, and the realization of any balance of the debt still remaining unpaid after such sale, is a 'decree for the payment of money' within the meaning of section 337, Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "I have no doubt that it is a decree for payment of money. It begins by ordering the defendants to pay the whole debt."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 337.

statement: A Court of Law has no inherent power to modify or set aside its own decrees, except within the limits indicated in the recent case of De Silva v. Ponna-samy Pulle.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that there is any provision in Ordinance No. 10 of 1863 which creates such a power in partition cases."

statement: A Court may correct a clerical error in its decree, even if the same error is present in the judgment upon which the decree was based, especially when the decree has been affirmed by a higher court and the case is now before the Supreme Court.
supporting_quote: "The Civil Procedure Code says nothing about the amendment of a judgment, but section 189 enacts that if any clerical or arithmetical error is found in a decree, the Court shall amend the decree so as to correct the error. It seems to me, therefore, that if a Court is satisfied that there is a clerical error in its decree, it is bound to correct it, and the fact that there is the same clerical error in the judgment upon which the decree is founded cannot make any difference, even though the result is that the decree as amended is at variance with the judgment."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 189, Civil Procedure Code

statement: A lessee who has planted trees on the lessor's land, with the consent, and acquiescence of the lessor, is entitled to the mere cost of the planting at the time of planting, and the lessee has a tacit hypothec for the amount of that cost in the land improved by it, but has no jus retentionis.
supporting_quote: If there was no acquiescence or consent, then the lessee is entitled to nothing.

statement: A gift to a concubine is not ipso jure void under Roman-Dutch Law, and such a gift cannot be taken away on the grounds of immorality.
supporting_quote: "The only ground on which the plaintiff could succeed would be on the ground of immoral consideration, which it would not lie in the mouth of Don Davit to aver, on the principle that he ought not to succeed in a court of law on the basis of his own turpitude."

statement: Under the Dutch system, a sale of land had to be carried out in the presence of the Court. However, under our Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, no sale, purchase, transfer, &c, of land or other immovable property shall be of force or avail in law unless executed before a notary and witnesses.
supporting_quote: "Under the Dutch system it is said the sale of land had to be carried out in the presence of the Court, but under our Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, for the Prevention of Frauds and Perjuries, it is enacted by section 2 that no sale, purchase, transfer, &c, of land or other immovable property shall be of force or avail in law unless executed before a notary and witnesses."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, for the Prevention of Frauds and Perjuries, section 2

statement: A party who has entered into a fraudulent agreement and comes to court with no signs of repentance or repudiation, but instead presents a false story regarding their involvement in the transaction, is not entitled to relief under Roman-Dutch law.
supporting_quote: Are we then here to assist the plaintiff, who has shown no signs of repentance or repudiation, but who came to Court with a false story as regards Marikar Pulle's share in the transaction?

statement: The Crown is estopped from challenging a surveyor's return if it has called upon the plaintiff to pay value for certain lots in accordance with that return.
supporting_quote: "he defendant had by his declarations and acts caused or permitted him to believe. Again, although the evidence is slender on the -point, a portion of the land in question, about 15 acres, has been cleared. This evidence certainly comes from the defendant's side, and I cannot well see how it can be said there is nothing to show that the clearing was the work of the plaintiff"

statement: A custom exists allowing a landowner to enter their neighbor's land for the purpose of screening their fence with olas, which has the force of law and can be considered a servitude.
supporting_quote: "I find, therefore, that there is a universal custom in the Jaffna peninsula which allows the owner of a land desirous of covering this fence with ola leaves to enter the adjoining land, and from that side to put up, heap, and tie the ola to a fence."

statement: A Low-country Sinhalese man who has taken up his permanent residence in the District of Kandy and has married there under Kandyan Marriage Law is not considered a Kandyan for legal purposes.
supporting_quote: "It cannot be maintained that what has been conserved as 'Kandyan Law' amounted to a distinct lex rei sitoe governing absolutely the devolution of land, like, for instance, gavelkind land in Kent. All we know is that a certain section of the community within the Kandyan Provinces, viz., the Kandyan Sinhalese, were allowed to retain their own customary law."

statement: A person who has actual notice of the existence of an instrument cannot get priority over it through the medium of registration, as such an attempt to get priority amounts to fraud within the meaning of the proviso to section 17 of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891.
supporting_quote: "A person who has actual notice of the existence of an instrument cannot get priority over it through the medium of the Registration, Ordinance, inasmuch as such an attempt to get priority amounts to fraud within the meaning of the proviso to section 17 of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 14 of 1891, s. 17

statement: A man who, having a charge or encumbrance upon a property, stands by and allows another to advance money on it, or, for that matter, to buy it under the impression that it is unencumbered, knowing that the latter is going to advance money, is estopped from setting up that interest against the title of the person whom he has deceived.
supporting_quote: "If a purchaser," said Cotton L. J. (S. C. at p. 748) in the argument, and the same line is followed in the judgment, "knows of the existence of a patent, can you bring the case within the rules as to lying by ? Is not the principle this, that if I see a man acting in derogation of my rights without knowing that I have any, I am bound to tell him of them; but if he knows I have rights, and puts an erroneous construction on them, is there any obligation on me to warn him?"

statement: A's possession was 'adverse' within the meaning of section 3 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, as it was unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce or performance of service or duty, and there is no acknowledgment of a right existing in another person.
supporting_quote: "that is to say, a possession unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce or performance of service or duty, or by any other act by the possessor from which an acknowledgment of a right existing in another person would fairly and naturally be inferred."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 3 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: A lessee cannot sue his lessor for breach of implied warranty of title in a Court of Requests or District Court unless the lessor has ousted the lessee from possession.
supporting_quote: "I agree, " he said, "in .the view expressed by Layard C.J. and Moncreiff J. in Fernando v. Fernando, 2 that the claim against the lessor does not affect the alleged trespasser, and cannot be put forward in the action against him."

statement: The use of a word that is similar to another's registered trade mark, even if the overall packaging differs, can be an infringement if it is calculated to deceive ordinary purchasers.
supporting_quote: "Comparing the boxes, packets, labels, wrappings, and stamping of the two soaps, I think that it is clear that the learned Judge was right in holding that the word 'Farina' was put in as a colourable imitation of the word 'Famora,' a part of plaintiffs' trade mark, which would be calculated to deceive the native customer in Ceylon, and so would be an infringement of his trade mark."

statement: The Court has inherent authority to prevent abuse of its process, even in the absence of specific statutory provisions.
supporting_quote: "I am not prepared to accede to the proposition that the Court has not any inherent authority to prevent abuse of its process in cases where the Legislature has not distinctly provided for such contingencies."

statement: Oral evidence of intention to contradict, vary, add to, or subtract from the terms of a written document is not admissible in India under Section 92 of the Indian Evidence Act.
supporting_quote: "Their Lordships do not think that oral evidence of intention was admissible for the purpose of construing the deeds or ascertaining the intention of the parties. By section 92 of the Indian Evidence Act (Act 1 of 1872) no evidence of any oral agreement or statement can be admitted as between the parties to any such instrument, or their representatives, in any suit, for the purpose of contradicting, varying, or adding to, or subtracting from its terms, subject to the exceptions contained in the several provisos."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 92 of the Indian Evidence Act (Act 1 of 1872)

statement: Under clause 4, only the movable properties enumerated were bequeathed to the survivor; and under clause 5, all other property (both movable and immovable) was bequeathed to the named persons.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that much help is to be derived from any of the cases that were cited in the District Court, or in the arguments on the appeal. In Dean v. Crib son 1 the will in dispute consisted of a single clause, in which the only request was a gift by the testatrix of her ' personal property consisting of money and clothes.'"

statement: The terms of clauses VII and VIII vested the dominium in the surviving widow, with a fidei commissum in favor of Edwin Robert.
supporting_quote: "I think that the terms of clauses VII and VIII, of the will vested the dominium in the surviving widow, with a fidei commissium in favour of Edwin Robert;"

statement: Section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 should not be allowed to be used in such a way as to perpetrate and cover fraud.
supporting_quote: "The question, he said " is not one of enforcing an agreement which is not according to law, but whether a defendant is to be allowed to plead the Statute of Frauds in order that he may dishonestly keep the property of another man, of which he got possession by refusing to return it when required.
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840

statement: A married woman's consent to convey property must be evidenced by a written expression of her husband's consent, as required by section 9 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876.
supporting_quote: "I do not see that illiteracy creates any difficulty in the application of this construction of the Ordinance. The mark of the illiterate must be proved in the usual way."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 9 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876

statement: A husband can, since the Ordinance, give to his wife married in community all his interest in any of the common property.
supporting_quote: "The gifts made by the two last-mentioned deeds were therefore valid. But the appellant contends that deed 3,699 only disposed of one-half of the lands mentioned in it, and that the other half remained in the community; that the husband expressly says in the deed that he does not deal with the other half, because it already belonged to his wife; that it is not the law that a husband and wife married in community of property are each entitled to an undivided half of the common property; that although the husband may have intended to make his wife the sole owner, he or the draughtsman of the deed made a mistake, and that he did in fact only make her at most the owner of an undivided half of the lands. The husband made a mistake in supposing that he was entitled to an undivided half and his wife to the other half. And as he was not entitled to an undivided half, either the deed conveyed nothing and had no effect at all, or else it conveyed all the husband's interest; and the Ordinance empowered him to convey all his interest to his wife."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 13 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 enacts that a husband or wife, whether married before or after the commencement of the Ordinance, and notwithstanding the existence of any community of goods between them, may make any gift of any property to the other.

statement: A daughter who marries in diga after her father's death does not forfeit her rights to the paternal inheritance by reason of the marriage.
supporting_quote: "The fact that a daughter marries in diga does not necessarily make her lose her right to the paternal inheritance."

statement: Under the Roman-Dutch Law, a sale of property during litigation is interdicted after litis contestatio has given it the character of res litigiosa.
supporting_quote: "It would seem that the Roman-Dutch jurists considered that litis contestatio occurs in different forms of action at different periods, but at the Cape it has been held to occur on the closing of the pleadings by Villiers C.J. (Nathan, ubi supra)."

statement: The plaintiff's lien on the vessel for repairs is lost because he was deprived of possession by an order of the Court and did not claim a lien until many months later.
supporting_quote: "But he was deprived of possession by an order of the Court, and did not then claim any lien; and he acquiesced the order, and made no claim to have a lien until many months afterwards, when he began this action."

statement: Part payment by a stranger does not have the effect of an acknowledgment of the balance of the debt and a promise to pay it.
supporting_quote: Part payment by a stranger does not have the effect of an acknowledgment of the balance of the debt and a promise to pay it.

statement: A promise to pay a prescribed debt, even if not in writing as required by the Ordinance, can take the case out of the operation of prescription laws and allow an action to be maintained.
supporting_quote: "When the time has expired within which an action to recover a debt is maintainable, and the debtor afterwards promises in writing to pay the debt or makes a payment on account of it, the effect of the promise in writing, or of the payment (from which a promise to pay the balance is inferred), is not to revive a dead claim, but to take the case out of the operation of the enactments which prescribe the time within which an action must be brought."

statement: An innocent purchaser who successfully defends a charge of fraud should not be made to pay the costs of the action.
supporting_quote: It seems to me that it would be reasonable in such cases where there has been an irregularity for which the buyer was not responsible, and of which he was not aware, that the Court should not set the sale aside, except on the terms that the buyer should get back all the money and expenses that he has had to pay. But, however that may be, I think that where the buyer is charged with fraud and defends himself successfully against that charge, it is wrong in principle to make him pay the costs of the action.

statement: Where the servient owner himself acts in a way which affects the exercise of the dominant owner's rights, and the dominant owner takes steps with a view to protecting himself against that conduct on the part of the servient owner and to secure the enjoyment of his servitude, and where no substantial damage has been caused from the protective steps so taken, the legal maxim de minimis non curat lex should be held to apply.
supporting_quote: Where the servient owner himself acts in a way which affects the exercise of the dominant owner's rights, and the dominant owner takes steps with a view to protecting himself against that conduct on the part of the servient owner and to secure the enjoyment of his servitude, and where no substantial damage has been caused from the protective steps so taken, the legal maxim de minimis non curat lex should be held to apply.

statement: A building on the opposite side of a wide public road, or even if a high one at a further distance, would obstruct the light and air to some extent of buildings opposite to or in the shadow of it, but the question is what amount of obstruction is actionable, and what is the proper remedy, compensation, or a mandatory injunction.
supporting_quote: A building on the opposite side of a wide public road, or even if a high one at a further distance, would obstruct the light and air to some extent of buildings opposite to or in the shadow of it, but the question is what amount of obstruction is actionable, and what is the proper remedy, compensation, or a mandatory injunction.

statement: A private person who seeks to recover damages for the obstruction of a public road is bound to prove that in consequence of such obstruction he has suffered special damage.
supporting_quote: "A private person who seeks to recover damages for the obstruction of a public road is bound to prove that in consequence of such obstruction he has suffered special damage."

statement: A deed registered in the wrong folio through the negligence of the grantee is void as against a subsequent correctly registered deed.
supporting_quote: "A deed which was registered in the wrong folio through the negligence of the grantee was held to be void as against a subsequent deed registered in the proper folio."

statement: Where an owner of land who had acquired a right of way by prescription conveyed the land by a notarial instrument to another, the transferee is entitled to assert his right to the servitude acquired by the transferor.
supporting_quote: I can find no authority which would justify me in holding that, under Roman-Dutch law or even under Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, where a right of way has become attached to a land, and that land is made the subject of a valid legal transfer, the transferee is not in a position to assert his right as the owner of the dominant tenement against the owner of the servient tenement.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840

statement: A document signed by a deceased person, witnessed by a notary and two witnesses in the presence of each other, can be admitted to probate if there is sufficient evidence that the formalities were met.
supporting_quote: "I have no doubt from the evidence on the record that the testator signed the deed in the presence of the notary and the two witnesses, who were all present together and conscious of the act being done in the sense required under the English Wills Act"

statement: The Roman-Dutch rule prohibiting requests by a man to a woman with whom he has lived in adultery is not authoritative in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: 'In the Privy Council the judgment proceeded upon somewhat different grounds, and it may be contended that the judgment applies only in cases where a valid marriage had been subsequently contracted between the persons who had lived in adultery. But the language of the last paragraph of the judgment, in my opinion, goes further, and supports the view taken in the Ceylon Courts, that the Roman-Dutch rule with regard to the effects of adultery is not authoritative in Ceylon.'

statement: The appointment of a provisional trustee by the District Committee after the term of office of the former trustee expired was irregular and voided any lease granted by such provisional trustee.
supporting_quote: Held, that the appointment was irregular. A lease granted by a provisional trustee appointed under such circumstances is void.

statement: The Court is not bound to draw the statutory presumption in favour of a person holding a certificate of sale granted under Ordinance No. 19 of 1905 if there is anything which arouses its suspicion, or suggests the probability that there was a departure from the regular and proper course of business in any particular case.
supporting_quote: The Court is not bound to draw the statutory presumption in favour of a person holding a certificate of sale granted under Ordinance No. 19 of 1905 in respect of property sold for nonpayment of Local Board tax, if there is anything which arouses its suspicion, or suggests the probability that there was a departure from the regular and proper course of business in any particular case.

statement: A Fiscal's transfer after the death of a purchaser, in favor of the purchaser’s heirs or legal representatives, is not valid to convey title.
supporting_quote: "This appeal raises the question whether a Fiscal's transfer executed after the death of the purchaser, in favour of the purchaser, 'his heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns,' passes a valid title to the administrator of the purchaser's estate."

statement: A judgment-debtor cannot acquire a title by prescription to property sold in execution against him until the Fiscal's conveyance is executed, as he remains vested with the title until such time.
supporting_quote: "The sale was held under the Fiscal's Ordinance, No. 4 of 1867, which regulated execution sales before the Civil Procedure Code came into operation. Under Ordinance No. 4 of 1867 the judgment-debtor remained vested with the title until the Fiscal's conveyance was executed (see Silva v . Nona Hamine l ). So that in this case, although the sale took place in 1886, the plaintiff and his co-judgment-debtor were not divested of their title till the Fiscal's conveyance was issued in 1910, and they were entitled to be in possession of the property sold."

statement: The Court has a discretion to allow the revocation of a proxy granted by co-executors, and this decision should not be interfered with unless it is shown that the discretion was wrongly exercised.
supporting_quote: "I am not prepared to answer that question in the affirmative in this case. All four executors concurred in the joint proxy given to Messrs. Prins and Swan at the commencement of the proceedings."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 27 of the Civil Procedure Code invests the Court with a real discretion as to whether or not the revocation of a proxy should be allowed.

statement: A person whose claim was dismissed for default of appearance must bring an action under section 247; he should not move to re-open the claim inquiry (by explaining the default) on the ground that the order was made ex parte.
supporting_quote: Where the Legislature has enacted a particular remedy for a grievance in terms which show that it intended that remedy to be the only one open to an aggrieved party, redress cannot be sought by any other form of proceedings.

statement: A mortgagee who has registered his mortgage bond, and also furnished an address to the Registrar, is amply protected. Subsequent encumbrances must either give him notice of their encumbrances, so that they may be joined as defendants, or, if they fail to do so, they are bound by the decree in the action.
supporting_quote: It is clear 'that if the appellant had registered an address as provided by section 644, the respondent and the other lessees would have been bound by the decree, unless they had taken the steps prescribed by section 644 to be joined as defendants.
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 643 and 644 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A manual seizure under section 227 of the Civil Procedure Code must be apparent and effective to show that property is in custodia legis, and sales during such a period are void if the purchaser knew or had reason to know of the seizure.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the ship was not under seizure when sold by the judgment-debtor to Chelliah, or when sold by Chelliah to the plaintiff, and even if it were, the sale ought not to be held void under the circumstances present here, unless it is proved that the purchaser knew or had reason to know of the seizure."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 227 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A plaintiff who has parted with dominium cannot obtain a declaration of title in an action rei vindicatio.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that either section 18 or section 404 is helpful to the plaintiff in the position in which he has placed himself by conveying the property in question to third parties, for no declaration of title can be made in this action in favour of the purchasers so long as the plaintiff is on the record."

statement: For an estoppel by acquiescence to be established, the plaintiffs must have known of their rights and stood by while misleading the defendants.
supporting_quote: "It is essential, in order to create an estoppel by acquiescence, to show that the plaintiffs, knowing that a violation of their rights was in progress, stood by and so misled the first and second defendants."

statement: A co-owner who has planted improvements with the assent of other co-owners on common property should not be required to pay compensation to the other co-owners for these improvements.
supporting_quote: "It is not reasonable, and it is against all authority, that the improving co-owner should be required to pay compensation to the other co-owner for these improvements."

statement: A co-owner who is entitled to compensation for improvements on the common property cannot be excluded from the benefit of jus retentionis.
supporting_quote: "It is well settled that a co-owner is entitled, subject to certain conditions and limitations, to compensation for improvements effected by him on the common holding, and it is difficult to see on what principle an improving co-owner, who is entitled to compensation, can be excluded from the benefit of the jus retentionis."

statement: Where a will and a codicil are both missing but only one is found, it may be inferred that the testator revoked the will by mistake or ignorance, leaving the codicil valid.
supporting_quote: I find on the evidence that the will was in the possession of the testator, and that it was not forthcoming at his death. The presumption is that he destroyed it. I think it is very probable that the deceased did wish to revoke both the will and the codicil, but by mistake or ignorance only destroyed one of these documents. If the will had been in existence, it seems to me very probable that it would have been found as the codicil was found. I find them on the issue that the last will was revoked, but the codicil was not revoked. I see no reason why the codicil should not be admitted to probate. It is an independent document, and its provisions can be carried out apart from those of the will. I make order accordingly, and order letters of administration with the codicil annexed to issue to the. applicant, the eldest son of the deceased. The second respondent

statement: A purchaser from an administrator who sells with the leave of the Court gets a title which cannot be attacked by the creditors of the estate, but in this case, the first defendant is not in that position because he had notice of an outstanding decree and was incumbent on him to see that all the money paid by him was rightly applied.
supporting_quote: "There can be no question that a purchaser from an administrator who sells with the leave of the Court gets a title which cannot be attacked by the creditors of the estate, but the first defendant is not in that position. It may be, too, that a purchaser from heirs who hold a conveyance from an administrator may assume that everything has been rightly done, and is not put upon inquiry as to whether the debts of the estate have been paid. In this case, however, the first defendant, as I have stated, had notice of the outstanding decree, and the question is whether, in these circumstances, it was not incumbent on him to see that all the money paid by him was rightly applied."

statement: Where a security bond hypothecating immovable property was executed without notarial attestation, the informality does not relieve the obligor of his personal obligation under the bond.
supporting_quote: The fact that the bond is not notarially attested does not render the whole bond invalid. See Halsbury's Laws of England, vol. VII., p. 682; Sidambaram Chetty v . Jayawardana.

statement: A mortgage for immovable property by a person who at the date of the mortgage is not the owner becomes valid, not merely as against him but also as against a bona fide purchaser from him without notice of the mortgage, when he subsequently acquires the ownership.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the passages from Voet (bk. 20, tit. 3, s. 6) and from Nathan (2, 1004) which are quoted in the judgment of Grenier J. in S. C. 385-C. R. Galle, 6,074 (14 N. L. R. 65), expressly negative this contention."

statement: A co-owner who builds on common property acquires no title in severalty as against other owners, but has a claim for compensation through a partition action.
supporting_quote: "The right of the builder is limited to a claim for compensation, which he could enforce in a partition action under sections 2 and 5 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1863."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 2 and 5 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1863

statement: The District Judge had jurisdiction to award damages for the period after the action was brought, even if the breach was continuous and neither party repudiated the contract.
supporting_quote: There is, no doubt, considerable force in this contention; but, on the other hand, one party to a contract is not bound to give to the other unlimited time after a day named to do that which the other has contracted to do. There must be some point of time at which delay or neglect amounts to refusal.

statement: For a gift by a father to his minor child, no acceptance is necessary.
supporting_quote: "No acceptance is necessary in the case of a gift by a father to his minor child."

statement: A translation of a deed would not be admissible as secondary evidence to prove the contents of the original deed.
supporting_quote: "A translation of a deed of conveyance would not be admissible as secondary evidence to prove the contents of the original deed. Section 63 of the Evidence Ordinance is exhaustive of the different kinds of secondary evidence that are admissible to prove the contents of a document."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 63 of the Evidence Ordinance, or null

statement: A non-notarial agreement to purchase land and transfer it to the plaintiff is not enforceable in court.
supporting_quote: "In order to be valid it should have been embodied in a notarial document."

statement: A notarial instrument can be modified by a subsequent non-notarially executed writing, provided that the latter does not itself require notarial execution.
supporting_quote: "On this principle the receipt D 1 in the present case does not require notarial execution, inasmuch as it was not given 'for establishing any security, interest, or incumbrance affecting land,' or for any of the other purposes named in section 2. It is therefore admissible in evidence"

statement: Where a will is traced to the custody of a testator and cannot be found at his death, the presumption is that he destroyed it himself; but this presumption may be rebutted by evidence leading to a contrary conclusion, as by a declaration of good will towards the parties benefited by the will, or of an adherence to the will.
supporting_quote: Where a will is traced to the custody of a testator and cannot be found at his death, the presumption is that he destroyed it himself; but this presumption may be rebutted by evidence leading to a contrary conclusion, as by a declaration of good will towards the parties benefited by the will, or of an adherence to the will.

statement: A testator's will can create a fidei commissum by directing that certain lands shall be the inheritance of a devisee and prohibiting any individual within three generations from selling, mortgaging, or gifting such lands.
supporting_quote: "As for the aforementioned lands, neither I, nor my five sons, nor the children of my five sons, that is to say, no individual of the said three generations, may sell, mortgage, or gift any of the same; only the power to enjoy and develop the same is reserved to them."

statement: A seizure of land by the Fiscal amounts to dispossession, and gives a cause of action under section 5 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "I entirely agree with the forcible remarks of the District Judge as to the need for caution on the part of courts of law, in seeing that the conditions which can alone render an action quia timet competent to suitors exist before such actions are entertained. Nor do I think that it is possible, or desirable to attempt, to lay down any general rules as to the classes of cases in which such actions are maintainable. Each case must be decided on its own merits and special facts."

statement: A fidei commissum should not be lightly imposed, and when the intention does not clearly appear, the inheritance should not be burdened with it.
supporting_quote: "A fidei commissum should not be lightly imposed, and when the intention does not clearly appear, the inheritance should not be burdened with it."

statement: The use of the word 'vesting' in a will does not necessarily indicate an intention to impose a condition on the request made by the testator, such as survivorship.
supporting_quote: "Their Lordships are unable to concur in the view that the use by the testators of the word "vesting" indicates an intention to impose such a condition on the request made by them to their son Edwin."

statement: A Fiscal's transfer, being a deed, is subject to the provisions of section 17 of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that in view of the language of section 17 it can. fairly be argued that a Fiscal's transfer does not fall within the purview of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891"
statute_citation_verbatim: Every deed, judgment, order, or other instrument an aforesaid, unless so registered, shall be deemed void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest there to on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent deed, judgment, order, or other instrument which shall have been duly registered as aforesaid. Provided, however, that fraud or collusion in obtaining as last-mentioned deed. judgment, order, or other instrument, or in securing such prior registration, shall defeat the priority of the person claiming there under; and that nothing herein contained shall be deemed to give any greater effect or different construction to any deed judgment, order, or other instrument registered in pursuance hereof, save the priority hereby conferred on it.

statement: The plaintiff's title is superior despite the defendant's prior registered deed due to the plaintiff's vested legal estate from the date of sale, which is anterior to the defendant's deed.
supporting_quote: At the argument it was conceded that the present case was concluded by the ruling of the Full Court in Aserappa v. Weeratunga et al.; 1 and that the decision of the Commissioner of Requests that the paper title was in the defendant cannot be supported.

statement: Courts in Ceylon will enforce the English rule of equity that where property has been purchased by one person with money advanced for the purpose by another, a trust results in favour of the latter, provided there is clear and unequivocal evidence of the advance of purchase money.
supporting_quote: "It is well settled that Courts in Ceylon will enforce the English rule of equity, that where property has been purchased by one person with money advanced for the purpose by another a trust results in favour of the latter. Ibrahim Saibo v. Oriental Bank Corporation (3 N. L. R. 148), Gould v. Inasitamby (9 N. L. R. 177 ) , Ohlmus v. Ohlmus (9 N. L. R. 188 ) ."

statement: Section 282 of the Civil Procedure Code, so far as irregularity of procedure is concerned, is exhaustive; no irregularity of procedure which is not a material irregularity in publishing or conducting a sale is a ground for setting the sale aside.
supporting_quote: Now, in a matter of this sort, it must be remembered that there are two sides to the question. On the one hand there is the interest of the owner of the property, and on the other there is the interest of the purchaser, who appears in this case to have given a fair value for the property, and has received a transfer according to law. It is practically admitted that under section 282 of the Code there is no ground for setting aside this sale, inasmuch as that section only provides for the avoidance of sales on the ground of material irregularity in the publishing or conduct of the sale. Here no such irregularity is alleged to exist. But it is said that we have the power to set aside any sales where there has been an irregularity which affects the essence of the transaction. I am of opinion that section 282, so far as irregularity of procedure is concerned, is exhaustive, and that no irregularity of procedure which is not a material irregularity in publishing or conducting the sale is a ground for setting the sale aside.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 282

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift, unless specifically made irrevocable and for past services, is revocable if the donee fails to fulfill the conditions attached to the gift.
supporting_quote: Where, on the other hand, the donee has failed to carry out the conditions on which the gift was made, he cannot invoke the protection of the renunciation clause, which was intended to take affect only if the stipulations in the deed were complied with.

statement: A misdescription of the lessor's interest does not invalidate a lease where the intention to demise is clear.
supporting_quote: "It is, in my opinion, a case of falsa demonstratio non nocet. The intention of the lessor to demise his share under the deed recited in the lease is plain and unmistakable, and the misdescription of his interest in the property is merely a falsa demonstratio, which does not prejudice the validity of the lease."

statement: The plaintiff's lease, registered after the mortgage bond but before the mortgage decree and Fiscal's conveyance, remains valid against the subsequent registration of the mortgage.
supporting_quote: "The only effect of registration was to give priority to the subsequent deed. The earlier deed is not affected in any way, save that it has to take second place. ... The plaintiff's rights as lessee remained alive, and although it may be that those rights were subordinate to those of the mortgagee, the plaintiff was not bound by the mortgage decree, he being no party to the action."

statement: Under the Muhammadan law, a wife may sue for her maggar even if she is not a party to the kaduttam deed.
supporting_quote: "It is not necessary that she should be a party to the kaduttam deed in order to entitle her to sue for the dower."

statement: In the absence of an express declaration, a novation may be established by implication from the circumstances and conduct of the parties, provided that the inference is so clear as to make it necessary.
supporting_quote: "By our law differing in that respect from the Roman law, novatio may take place, not only by express agreement, but also tacitly or by implication, the consent of the parties to the novatio being implied from the circumstances and the conduct of the parties. In the latter event, however, the inference must be so probable and conclusive as to make it quite clear that the parties intended to recede from the original obligation and to replace it by another-in fact, it must be a necessary inference, the new obligation being inconsistent and incompatible with the continued existence of the original obligation."

statement: A person may mortgage property of which he is not the owner at the date of the mortgage, whether that property consists of movables or immovables. When such a mortgage is effected, the first mortgage is preferential to any subsequent mortgage after the mortgagor had acquired ownership.
supporting_quote: "Under the Roman-Dutch Law a person may mortgage property of which he is not the owner at the date of the mortgage, whether that property consists of movables or immovables. When such a mortgage is effected, the first mortgage is preferential to any subsequent mortgage after the mortgagor had acquired ownership."

statement: A Muhammadan in Ceylon can dispose of the whole of his property by will under Ordinance No. 21 of 1844, section 1.
supporting_quote: "This provision has uniformly been construed to enable Muhammadans in Ceylon to dispose of the whole of their property by will, and the Muhammadan population in Ceylon has freely taken advantage of the privilege."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 21 of 1844, s.1

statement: The court should allow the plaintiff to prove a secret trust as a basis for title, even if it is not a paper title.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that Sir Joseph Hutchinson C.J., in the case of Catherina Hamy v. Babahamy, 1 when he said that the intention of the Partition Ordinance was to give an indefeasible title to the purchaser to whom the land was sold when the sale was affirmed and completed by the certificate of the Court under section 8, intended to say anything more than that the title of the purchaser was indefeasible as regards the estate that passed to him under the decree."

statement: A possessory action can be maintained by a shifting body like the dhobies of Polwatta, provided their possession is ut dominus and has been continued for ten years.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiffs may be looked upon as trustees holding the land in trust for the Dhoby community."

statement: A purchaser from an assignee of an insolvent is considered a legal representative of the insolvent for the purposes of applying to set aside an order of abatement in a partition action.
supporting_quote: "The cause of action appears to me to be the right of the plaintiff to have the land divided between himself and the co-owners, and the cause of action is the same in this suit. No authority has been brought to our notice to show that a purchaser from an assignee is not to legal representative of an insolvent."

statement: A party cannot raise a ground for the first time in appeal unless it might have been put forward in the Court below under some one or other of the issues framed.
supporting_quote: Under our procedure all the contentious matter between the parties to a civil suit is, so to say, focused in the issues of law and fact framed. Whatever is not involved in the issues is to be taken as admitted by one party or the other, and under our procedure it is not open to a party to put forward a ground for the first time in appeal unless it might have been put forward in the Court below under some one or other of the issues framed, and when such a ground that is to say, a ground that might have been put forward in the Court below, is put forward in appeal for the first time, the cautions indicated in the Tasmania 1 may well be observed.

statement: The plaintiffs have acquired title by prescription over the entire disputed land, not just the cultivated portions.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that it is straining the doctrine of constructive possession to hold that Suppen and the plaintiffs had occupation of the whole land. The greater part of it was uncultivable or could not be cultivated without great expense, and the occupation of Suppen and of the plaintiffs was, in my opinion, such occupation as was to be expected, having regard to the nature and condition of the land."

statement: A conveyance purporting to pass a clean title to purchasers for value and without notice acquires priority over subsequent deeds, even if the original grantor had no title at the time of the conveyance.
supporting_quote: "We are not called upon here to inquire what the legal position would be if the subsequent purchaser had derived his title from a Fiscal's conveyance, which, in terms, passes only the right, title, and interest of the judgment-debtor. We are in presence of a conveyance purporting to pass a clean title to purchasers for value and without notice."
