statement: A deed registered in the wrong folio is void as against parties claiming an adverse interest on valuable consideration by virtue of a subsequent duly registered deed.
supporting_quote: "It is clear that a deed which is not registered in the proper place is not 'so registered' for the purpose of section 17."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 17 of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891, every deed, &c, unless ' so registered ' shall be deemed void, &c.

statement: If the plaintiff definitively abandoned the old route, he must be restricted to using the new route.
supporting_quote: "If the plaintiff definitely abandoned the route d d, I think that he must now be restricted to the new route a a."

statement: In Ceylon, the principles of Roman-Dutch law regarding the right of the owner of a servient tenement to change the situation of a prescriptive right of way are not applicable.
supporting_quote: "How far the principles of the Roman-Dutch law to which-I have referred are applicable to a case where the right to pass over a defined track has been acquired by prescription is a question of some difficulty; but so far as the present appeal is concerned, the questions are purely academic."

statement: Before a vendee can recover the purchase money from his vendor, in case he has suffered eviction, he should call upon his vendor to warrant and defend his title.
supporting_quote: "I think, it is good Roman-Dutch law that before a vendee can recover the purchase money from his vendor, in case he has suffered eviction, he should call upon his vendor to warrant and defend his title."

statement: An order deciding an issue is also an appealable order, especially if it goes to the root of the case and would necessitate a second trial.
supporting_quote: "If an order refusing to frame an issue is an appealable order, an order deciding an issue is also an appealable order."

statement: The lower proprietor is obliged only to receive such water as flows in the ordinary course of nature from the upper tenement.
supporting_quote: "He is not bound to receive water which the upper proprietor has discharged into his premises by any artificial means which alters the natural drainage of the land."

statement: A community of persons can hold property or acquire rights in property, and a community of persons can be beneficiaries under a trust deed.
supporting_quote: "A community of persons can hold property or acquire rights in property. In the same way a community of persons can be beneficiaries under a trust deed."

statement: The act of personation by the accused was fraudulent and likely to cause damage or harm to the Chetty, as the Chetty would not have lent money if he knew Isa was substituting for Ligona.
supporting_quote: "I think the case is different to that reported in 11 T. W. R. 24. In that case the intention was manifest, that the real vendor was on her way to carry out the sale when she was taken ill. In the present case, although Ligona now says she ratifies the act of her personator, it is clear to me that the Chetty would not have advanced the money to the accused had he known that Isa was to sign for Ligona; and that if Isa had signed, he would have advanced money to the accused on a deed which it is quite likely might have been repudiated by Ligona and so have caused him damage."

statement: Section 41 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance (No. 8 of 1905) does not preclude a temple, or any duly authorized representative of the temple for that purpose, from acquiring title to any land by prescription.
supporting_quote: Section 41 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance (No. 8 of 1905) does not preclude a temple, or any duly authorized representative of the temple for that purpose, from, acquiring title to any land by prescription.
statute_citation_verbatim: Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, No. 8 of 1905, s. 41

statement: A co-owner has no right to build on the common property without the consent of the other co-owners, and where a co-owner builds with the consent and acquiescence of the other co-owners, he can claim either the cost of the improvement or the difference between the original and the enhanced value of the property, whichever is less.
supporting_quote: "A co-owner has no right to build on the common property without the consent of the other co-owners (see Silva v. Silva1[6N.L. R. 225.] and Voet 10, 3, 7), and where he builds with the consent and acquiescence of the other co-owners, I am not prepared to say that he has any greater right than a mere improver of property that does not belong to himself."

statement: When a purchaser at a Fiscal's sale conveys before he has himself obtained a Fiscal's transfer and then subsequently obtains a transfer, the benefit of the transfer enures to the purchaser.
supporting_quote: "This was clearly understood to be the law before the passing of the present Code, as shown by the following authorities: Selohamy v. Raphiel 3 and Silva v. Tissera. 4"

statement: In the absence of collusion or special circumstances, legatees cannot sue for the recovery of assets which have been legally alienated by the executor.
supporting_quote: "As a general rule, in the absence of collusion or special circumstances the legatees cannot sue for the recovery of assets which have been legally alienated by the executor."

statement: There is nothing in section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code which limits the time within which a decree can be rectified.
supporting_quote: "There is nothing in section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code which limits the time within which a decree can be rectified."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code, s. 189

statement: A party to an action in which a mortgage decree under section 201 of the Civil Procedure Code has been entered cannot bring a separate action to have a sale of land in execution of the decree set aside on the ground of irregularity; such questions must be determined by order of the Court executing the decree.
supporting_quote: "All questions arising between the parties to the action in which the decree was passed, or their legal representatives, and relating to the execution of the decree, shall be determined by order of the Court executing the decree, and not by separate action."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 344

statement: The defendant in an action is not bound to make a claim in reconvention on a distinct and separate cause of action.
supporting_quote: The defendant in an action is not bound to make a claim in reconvention on a distinct and separate cause of action.

statement: An interlocutory decree for partition is a decree within the meaning of section 207, and can only be modified in accordance with the provisions of section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: An interlocutory decree for partition is a decree within the meaning of section 207, and can only be modified in accordance with the provisions of section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 189

statement: A conveyance is not vitiated by a subsequent erroneous addition when the instrument provides an adequate and sufficient definition with convenient certainty of what is intended to pass.
supporting_quote: "This maxim means that as soon as there is an adequate and sufficient definition with convenient certainty of what is intended to pass by a particular instrument, a subsequent erroneous addition will not vitiate it."

statement: A co-owner who is in the position of the defendant cannot claim, on the strength of the tattamaru arrangement, to exclude his co-owner altogether from the property.
supporting_quote: "But a co-owner who is in the position of the defendant in this case cannot claim, on the strength of the tattamaru arrangement, to exclude his co-owner altogether from the property."

statement: A court can dispose of a case on issues of law alone, even if no evidence has been taken, provided that the issue is clear and there are no disputed facts.
supporting_quote: "Section 147 of the Civil Procedure Code expressly enables the courts of first instance to dispose of a case on issues of law alone, and for that purpose to postpone the settlement of the issues of fact until after the issues of law have been determined."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 147 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: Planting agreements can vest title to a one-fourth share of the land in planters who fulfill their obligations, even if no immediate conveyance is made.
supporting_quote: Unless we are forced by law to construe the deeds as contended for the appellants, it would obviously be unjust to deprive the respondents of the share which it was manifestly intended they should have, and which they have undoubtedly possessed for over forty years.

statement: In the case of a sale of shares, where no time is specified for delivery and the contract is silent as to the time for delivery, the seller is bound to deliver within a reasonable time before payment, unless his obligation is otherwise regulated by a binding usage or custom.
supporting_quote: "In considering what is reasonable time, regard must be had to the circumstances of the case. It would be impossible to lay down any hard and fast rule as to what constitutes unreasonable delay in the delivery of shares sold."

statement: A person who knows the value of their property is not entitled to rescission merely by reason that the price at which they have sold it is less than half its true value, unless the sale is grossly disproportionate to its true value.
supporting_quote: "A person who knows the value of his property is not entitled to rescission of the sale merely by reason of the fact that the price at which he has sold the property is less than half its true value. The case is otherwise where the property is sold at a price grossly disproportionate to its true value."

statement: A Crown grant to multiple grantees does not necessarily convey the property in equal shares unless specified.
supporting_quote: "Where, for example, as frequently happens in this country, several persons contribute the purchase money in unequal shares, the vendor or grantor might reasonably refuse to accept the responsibility of setting out the shares of the purchasers in the deed or grant; he might fairly insist on making the grant to the vendees simpliciter without any attempt to define their respective shares; leaving it to them to adjust their shares in accordance with the agreement between themselves."

statement: A fidei commissum was established by the will of Anohamy, and it was not destroyed by the partition decree.
supporting_quote: "I think that, on the authority of the case to which I have referred, the District Judge was right in holding that Don Christian's shares were subject to a fidei commissum."

statement: The proper evidence that a witness cannot be found is that the person whose duty it was to call him has made use of his legal powers under section 131 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: In my opinion the best evidence and the proper evidence that a witness cannot be found is. that the person whose duty it was to call him has made use of his legal powers under section 131 of the Civil Procedure Code.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 131 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: In the absence of probate, title under a will cannot be established in the Courts of this Colony.
supporting_quote: "Apart from authority, I should not have had any difficulty in holding that it is only by proof of probate that title under a will can be established in the Courts of this Colony."

statement: A non-notarial agreement can modify a notarial mortgage bond, but the modification must not affect the security or immovable property involved.
supporting_quote: "Herein lies, to my mind, the distinction between that case and this. The writing in question not only changes the mode of payment of the debt, but increases its burden, with the result that now the plaintiff owes Rs. 1,177.50 instead of a smaller sum. The further effect of this is to make the security bear a larger debt, and consequently, I think; the agreement does affect the lands or immovable property mortgaged by plaintiff."

statement: A vendor who sells without title and subsequently acquires title cannot set it up against a purchaser from him, but this does not apply to subsequent purchasers.
supporting_quote: If the fifth defendant, when he purchased, failed to search the register, or bought the share notwithstanding the registration, he accepted a serious risk, but I fail to see that he is in the same position as a vendor who sells when he has no title to give, and subsequently, when he has obtained title, repudiates the sale and sets up his newly acquired title against his purchaser. The element of fraud involved in the latter transaction is wanting in the purchase by the fifth defendant.

statement: The granting of letters does not result in the imposition of additional stamp duty on the estate.
supporting_quote: (1) That the grant of letters would not involve the estate in double stamp duty. (2) That the appellant was entitled to sue for his share of the estate without obtaining letters. Wood Renton

statement: A person is entitled to sue for their share of an estate without obtaining letters of administration.
supporting_quote: (1) That the grant of letters would not involve the estate in double stamp duty. (2) That the appellant was entitled to sue for his share of the estate without obtaining letters. Wood Renton

statement: On a question of pure law, where the Code is silent, the proper course is to refer to standard text books on the subject rather than resorting to expert opinions.
supporting_quote: "On a question of pure law (as distinguished from questions of usage or practice), where our Code of Muhammadan law is silent, the proper course is to refer to the standard text books on the subject, and not to resort to the opinions of experts."

statement: A prohibition against alienation out of the family by a legatee or donee is sufficient to create a fidei commissum in favor of the members of the family.
supporting_quote: "A prohibition against alienation out of the family of a legatee or donee is itself sufficient to create a fidei commissum in favour of the members of the family."

statement: The intention of the testator should be gathered from the terms of the will and surrounding circumstances, not just general rules for interpreting wills.
supporting_quote: "general rules for the interpretation of wills are unsafe guides; and that the only true criterion is the intention of the testator to be gathered from the terms of the will and from the surrounding circumstances"

statement: A provision creating a fidei commissum must be interpreted in favor of that intention unless the words used can be given an interpretation that supports it.
supporting_quote: "If the intention of a donor or testator to create fidei commissum is clear, and the words used by him can be given an interpretation that supports that intention, I should be slow to embark on a voyage of discovery in search of possible interpretations that defeat that intention."

statement: A married woman paying money under a mistake of law is not recoverable unless there are special circumstances, and in this case, the third defendant was aware of her legal position.
supporting_quote: "Under the Roman-Dutch law there is a conflict of opinion whether money paid under a mistake of law is recoverable, but the tendency in South Africa appears to be to hold that money paid under a mistake of law is not recoverable unless there are special circumstances; that, in other words, there must be a natural equity on the side of him who claims the condictio indebiti. (Morice's English and Roman-Dutch Law 226.) But the case of a married woman paying money in discharge of an obligation concluded by her without her husband's consent appears to stand on a different footing."

statement: A party cannot by representation, any more than by other means, raise against himself an estoppel so as to create a state of things which he is under a legal disability from creating.
supporting_quote: It is a well-settled principle of law that a party cannot by representation, any more than by other means, raise against-himself an estoppel so as to create a state of things which be is under a legal disability from creating.

statement: A daughter who, after having married in bina, subsequently leaves her parents' house and goes to live with her husband in diga, may still retain her rights of inheritance if she keeps up a close connection with the mulgedara.
supporting_quote: "The mere residence of the grandchild,

statement: A tacit hypothec created by a will is void as against a registered conveyance if the probate of the will has not been registered.
supporting_quote: "Held, that as the annuitant had not registered the probate of the will producing the inventory and a proper description of the land, the tacit hypothec created by the will was void by reason of the registration of the defendant's deed."

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift, intended by the donor to operate as a donation and accepted by the donee as such, is revocable unless it contains specific clauses making it irrevocable.
supporting_quote: "That being the law, it must, I think, in all cases be followed, except in a case to the special circumstances of which it is quite manifest that it was not intended to apply in all its rigour."

statement: A lessee can be ejected from leased property before the term expires if they have abused the property, as per Roman-Dutch law.
supporting_quote: "Whether the destruction of the trees is attributable to malicious action on the part of the defendant, or whether it is due merely to negligence on his part. the defendant is liable to be ejected."

statement: A trustee receiving money on behalf of his cestui que trust cannot set up a plea of prescription in bar of the claim of such cestui que trust.
supporting_quote: "I am not prepared to differ from the finding of the learned District Judge on the facts of this case. The only points that remain, therefore, for consideration are whether the respondents' claim is prescribed, and whether or not that part of the judgment under appeal, in which their claim is allowed with interest at 15 per cent., can be maintained. On the first of these points, although I am not sure that I should have come to the Same conclusion myself, I think that we are bound by, and ought to follow, the case of Antho Pulle v. Christoffel Pulle [(1889) 1 N. L. R. 120], in which it was held by Burnside C.J. and Clarence J. that a trustee, receiving money on behalf of his cestui que trust, cannot set up a plea of prescription in bar of the claim of such cestui que trust."

statement: A lessee who has been in possession for less than a year and a day can still bring a possessory action if they take advantage of their predecessor's possession.
supporting_quote: "That decision was approved by Bonser C.J. in D.C. Negombo, No. 2,795, 10 and by Wendt J. in Goonewardene v. Pereira. 6"

statement: The acceptance of a donation of land must be notarially attested and by the donee or someone competent to represent the donee for entering into contracts.
supporting_quote: "In my own opinion, the acceptance of a donation of land must be notarially attested as much as the making of such a donation, and the acceptance must be by the donee himself or some person competent in law to represent the donee for the purpose of entering into contracts."

statement: A fraudulent deed, unlike a deed executed by a person not competent in law to enter into contracts, is valid until it is set aside or cancelled, and when it is cancelled, the cancellation refers back to the date of the deed.
supporting_quote: "A fraudulent deed, unlike a deed executed by a person not competent in law to enter into contracts, is, under the Roman-Dutch law, valid until it is set aside or cancelled, and when it is cancelled, the cancellation refers back to the date of the deed."

statement: A landlord has a tacit hypothec over the proceeds of sale of movable property in the hands of a person who knowingly has had the property sold in execution of a decree in his favour and drawn the money himself.
supporting_quote: The tacit hypothec that a landlord has over the invecta el illata in the house let out attaches, in the case of movable property, to the proceeds sale of such property in the hands of a person who knowingly has had the property sold in execution of a decree in his favour and drawn the money himself.

statement: Under Kandyan law, the father is not the heir of property inherited by his child through the mother in a bina marriage.
supporting_quote: "the father is not the heir of the property of his children born in a bina marriage which they have acquired through their mother: the maternal uncles or next of kin on the mother's side are the heirs to such children. "

statement: A diga married husband has a life interest in the acquired property of his deceased wife if there are children.
supporting_quote: "I think that some operation should be given to the paragraph in Sawers cited before us. That it does not apply to a binna marriage or to paraveni property sufficiently appears from other passages in Sawers and from the authorities referred to by Mr. Justice Pereira. The only other case to which it can be applied is to the acquired property of a woman in diga, and I think the decision in Saduwa v. Siri 2 [8 Bal. 18.] correctly holds that the husband has a life interest in the property acquired by the wife during such a marriage."

statement: Where a land is sold by a person who has already leased it, the vendee succeeds to all the rights of the vendor on the lease without a special assignment of it by the latter to the former.
supporting_quote: "A purchaser from the landlord of the property leased steps into the shoes of the landlord, and receives all his rights and becomes subject to all his obligations, so that he is bound to the tenant, and the tenant is bound to him, in the relation of landlord and tenant."

statement: A lease is considered an incumbrance under the Registration Ordinance (No. 14 of 1891), and therefore, a lessee's rights are not affected by the sale of land under the Partition Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "In any event your appeal cannot succeed. If the lease is an incumbrance, your rights are not affected by the sale,"
statute_citation_verbatim: Under the Registration Ordinance (No. 14 of 1891), section 16, a lease is an incumbrance.

statement: A mortgage of an undivided share during the pendency of a partition action is invalid under section 17 of the Partition Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Nor is the contention tenable that section 17 does not apply, because as a matter of fact the mortgagors purported to mortgage the entire land. The plaintiff himself admits that in reality the mortgage was only of an undivided half of the land."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 17 of the Partition Ordinance

statement: The principle of collation cannot be applied to the Muhammadan law of succession in Sri Lanka.
supporting_quote: "It has been held that a casus omissus in any of the special laws is governed by the Roman-Dutch law. [De Sampayo A.J.-Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 specially excludes Muhammadans from the operation of its provisions.]"

statement: Partition decrees are conclusive by their own inherent virtue and do not depend for their final validity upon anything which the parties may or may not afterwards do.
supporting_quote: "Partition decrees are conclusive by their own inherent virtue, and do not depend for their final validity upon anything which the parties may or may not afterwards do."

statement: When questions as to title arise in a partition suit, whether it be between the original parties to it or an intervenient who seeks to come in after the interlocutory decree and another party, the Court should not refer the parties concerned to a separate action to have such questions in the first instance decided, but the same should be adjudicated upon in the partition suit itself.
supporting_quote: "When questions as to title arise in a partition suit, whether it be between the original parties to it or an intervenient who seeks to come in after the interlocutory decree and another party, the Court should not refer the parties concerned to a separate action to have such questions in the first instance decided, but the same should be adjudicated upon in the partition suit itself."

statement: To establish a prescriptive servitude of way, the evidence must be precise and definite, relating to a defined track rather than mere straying across an open land.
supporting_quote: "The evidence to establish a prescriptive servitude of way must be precise and definite. It must relate to a defined track, and must not consist of proof of mere straying across an open land at any point which is at the moment most convenient."

statement: A promissory note can be assigned otherwise than by endorsement.
supporting_quote: It is well established law that although bills and notes partake largely of the nature of money, yet they retain also their innate character of chattels and choses in actions. As chattels they may be bought and sold, and as choses in action they may be assigned.

statement: If a vendor does not give vacant possession to the purchaser, the purchaser would have an immediate right of action against them for their failure to implement the primary obligation of the contract of sale.
supporting_quote: "If a vendor does not give vacant possession to the purchaser, the purchaser would not be under any obligation to take preliminary steps against the persons who had ousted him, or to give to his vendors notice to warrant and defend the title which they had purported to convey, but would have an immediate right of action against them for their failure to implement the primary obligation of the contract of sale."

statement: A vendor who had become liable to warrant and defend his vendee's title, upon receiving notice from his vendees of an action against them disputing their title to the land, was duty-bound to have himself added as a party to the case or otherwise do all he could to defend his vendee's title.
supporting_quote: Where a vendor of a parcel of land, who by agreement or otherwise had become liable to warrant and defend his vendee's title, received notice from his vendees of an action against them disputing their title to the land, it was his duty to have himself added as a party to the case, or otherwise to do all he could to defend his vendee's title.

statement: A person's cause of action for a prescriptive title does not accrue until their rights are interfered with or placed in jeopardy.
supporting_quote: It cannot, I think, be said that any cause of action accrued until something had accrued which interfered with or placed in jeopardy his rights under that deed, and it is not contended that anything of that nature occurred before the property in question was included in the inventory.

statement: An hypothecary action can be brought against a person who has purchased the property mortgaged at a Fiscal's sale held in execution of a writ against the mortgagor, but who has not yet obtained the usual Fiscal's conveyance in his favour.
supporting_quote: A hypothecary action can be brought against a person who has purchased the property mortgaged at a Fiscal's sale held in execution of a writ against the mortgagor, but who has not yet obtained the usual Fiscal's conveyance in his favour.

statement: A plaintiff who buys property during the pendency of a mortgage action and obtains a Fiscal's transfer before the added defendant does not have an absolute right to a declaration of title against the added defendant, as the added defendant may still obtain a superior title through a subsequent mortgage decree.
supporting_quote: "Now, the result of this action is, in my opinion, almost absurd. Judgment has been given for the plaintiff, and it is admitted that all the added defendant has to do, now that he has obtained his Fiscal's transfer, is to bring another action and obtain a reversal of those proceedings."

statement: When a claim is clearly prescribed on the footing of the averments in a plaint, the claim may be dismissed without evidence being gone into or consideration of the averments in the answer.
supporting_quote: If on the footing of the averments in a plaint the claim made therein is clearly prescribed, the claim is liable to be dismissed without evidence being gone into or consideration of the averments in the answer.

statement: A decision on an incidental issue by a Court in the exercise of its ordinary civil jurisdiction is not conclusive on questions arising on other causes of action.
supporting_quote: What Knight Bruce V.C. himself meant by an 'incidental issue' is clear from the fact that what he held in the case was that the finding of fact in a suit in Ecclesiastical Court for a grant of letters of administration, necessary to the decision and appearing on the face of the order, was not conclusive in proceedings between the same parties in a Court of Equity for distribution.

statement: An undertaking by a party to an action to abide by the ruling of the Court is of no avail, unless the opposite party is himself prepared to acquiesce in the decision.
supporting_quote: "In the first place, an undertaking of this nature, to have a binding effect, should, in my opinion, be given in a more formal and solemn manner than in the shape of a casual answer to a question put by the Court in the course of the examination of a party as a witness. In this connection I may observe that the Commissioner in his judgment says that in spite of the defendant's undertaking his counsel urged the plea of prescription, and that plea the Commissioner has in effect upheld."

statement: In the absence of fraud or an express warranty of title, a vendor's only primary obligations are to give the purchaser 'vacant possession' and to warrant and defend the title after the purchaser is judicially evicted.
supporting_quote: "In the absence of fraud on the part of the vendor, and of an express warranty of title, he is only entitled to get vacant possession."

statement: The register of temple lands prepared under the provisions of 'The Temple Lands Registration Ordinance, 1856,' is binding on the Crown in all questions touching the boundaries and extents of the several lands claimed by the temple concerned.
supporting_quote: "A register of temple lands prepared under the provisions of " The Temple Lands Registration Ordinance, 1856, " is binding on the Crown in ail questions touching the boundaries and extents of the several lands claimed by the temple concerned"
statute_citation_verbatim: The Temple Lands Registration Ordinance, 1856

statement: A mortgagee must comply with the requirements of sections 643 and 644 of the Civil Procedure Code to bind a puisne incumbrancer, and failure to do so means the puisne incumbrancer is not bound by the mortgage decree.
supporting_quote: "It now appears that the respondent is not in a position to furnish this proof, and we have, therefore, to consider whether, in that state of the facts, the learned District Judge, in declaring the appellant entitled to the 24 lachams in question under the dowry deed, was right in making that declaration of title subject to the mortgage in favour of the respondent. In my opinion he was not."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 643 and 644 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A mortgagee is not bound to give notice of his action to a lessee, whose deed was executed before but registered after the execution and registration of the mortgage bond.
supporting_quote: The date of execution is the test of the applicability of section 643, and the section does not extend to instruments which, if they can be described at all as subsequent incumbrances, can only be described as such in a figurative sense on account of the artificial priority which the Registration Ordinance gives to a competing deed.

statement: A cannot maintain an action against B for rectification of the deed of conveyance where A is subsequently allotted another portion in lieu of the portion conveyed by him.
supporting_quote: Where A being allotted a certain portion of land in a decree in a partition suit, conveys that portion to B, and the decree is subsequently varied, and A is allotted another portion in lieu of the portion conveyed by him,- Held, that B cannot maintain an action against A for rectification of the deed of conveyance.

statement: In a partition action, the principle applicable to ordinary actions for declaration of title as to profits-after litis contestatio should hold good.
supporting_quote: "The point taken by the plaintiffs in appeal No. 296 is that the learned District Judge should have ordered the defendant to account to them for a two-thirds share of the profits that accrued to him from possession of the land since litis contestatio in the action and to pay damages. To this claim it appears to me that there are several answers. In the first place, it is not a claim of which the Court could take account in a partition action.. Even as regards the share of profits, it is really a claim in the nature of damages, and in a partition action damages cannot be claimed or awarded."

statement: Where a person obtains a conveyance of property without fraud, but afterwards fraudulently refuses to pay the consideration stipulated for, the grantor is not entitled to claim a cancellation of the conveyance, but his remedy is an action for the recovery of the consideration.
supporting_quote: Where a person obtains a conveyance of property without fraud, but afterwards fraudulently refuses to pay the consideration stipulated for, the grantor is not entitled to claim a cancellation of the conveyance, but his remedy is an action for the recovery of the consideration.

statement: A trustee can maintain an action for a trust fund even after ceasing to be the trustee, provided they were able to do so at the time of instituting the suit.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, however, as the plaintiff was able to maintain the action, at the time he entered the suit, the proceedings to the time he ceased to be trustee are good, and the action should not be dismissed altogether."

statement: An agreement to pool profits from opium sales, where the partners are all licensed individuals and do not involve unlicensed persons in the sale, is not illegal under the Opium Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Since writing the above I have seen the judgment of my brother Ennis, and I may say that I am in entire agreement with him. Of course my decision is that the agreement is ex facie valid. There is nothing in its terms that can be said to contravene any provision of the law"

statement: A deaf and dumb person can be competent to contract if they possess a degree of intelligence, can communicate by signs, and understand the nature of the act.
supporting_quote: "She can understand certain matters of a sort describable by signs, but I am not satisfied that she can be made to understand that a certain document was a sale as distinguished from a lease or a mortgage."

statement: A plaintiff should not be allowed to tax costs in a higher class than the one in which the action was instituted and decided, even if the value of the subject matter increased significantly during the litigation.
supporting_quote: "Now, this action was commenced, proceeded with, and concluded on the basis of the value of the land being Rs. 4,500, and presumably the plaintiff has already incurred all the necessary expenses of the actual litigation. To tax costs now as in a case of a higher class would be to give him expenses to which he has not been put, and to allow him in effect to make an extra profit out of the litigation."

statement: The word 'signature' in section 69 of the Evidence Ordinance must be taken to include a mark.
supporting_quote: "The word " signature " in section 69 of the Evidence Ordinance must be taken to include a mark."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 69 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: A sannas that was not registered but whose genuineness had been upheld by a judicial decree before the enactment of Ordinance No. 6 of 1866 is admissible in evidence.
supporting_quote: "The decree," said Wendt J., "pronounced it genuine. It ceased to be a document in private hands."

statement: A duplicate of a deed over thirty years old produced from the office of the Registrar-General is admissible in evidence without further proof; it must be held to have been produced from proper custody within the meaning of section 90 of the Evidence Ordinance.
supporting_quote: The document in question cannot, in my opinion, be treated as a copy of an original deed. This document, no less than 'the deed which passed to the grantee, was signed by the parties and attested by the notary. It is in all respects an original deed. The question merely is whether, having been produced from the office of the Registrar -General, it is to be deemed to have come from proper custody.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 90 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: The Muhammadan law applies to all followers of Islam, including immigrants from India and Malays, and governs inheritance and succession regardless of the location of immovable property within Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "The fact is that the Muhammadan law is based on religion, and is applicable to all followers of Islam. Even before the Ordinance No. 5 of 1852 the Supreme Court applied it to Moors in Kandy, observing that they were governed by their own laws and customs of inheritance and marriage which are founded on their religion."

statement: The offspring of a Kandyan father by a Low-country Sinhalese woman cannot be said to be Kandyan and must be governed by the general law of the land.
supporting_quote: As regards nationality, the District Judge is apparently using the word in its strictly legal sense. It is only when the word is used in that sense that it can be said that the wife takes the husband's nationality and the child the father's. Thus, every subject of the Crown, be he Sinhalese, Tamil, Chinese, or Hottentot, is British in nationality, that is to say, he is subject to the British flag; but where the word is used in a looser and more popular sense-in the sense of race for instance-the rule relied on by the District Judge has no application at all.

statement: The interest in common property left to the survivor by a joint will is not necessarily limited to a usufruct, but may be an absolute ownership as indicated by the specific wording of the will.
supporting_quote: "I am quite in agreement with Mudaliyar Gunasekara, a Sinhalese scholar of repute, when he says that the correct translation is: 'If one should die and the other survive, the person who lives is directed as far as in us lies to possess the property according to his or her pleasure, and to do whatever he or she likes with it.'"

statement: The phrase 'under the same restrictions as before' in paragraph 12 refers to the restriction against inheritance by the children of a second marriage of any one of the immediate devisees, in addition to the fidei commissum mentioned in paragraph 10.
supporting_quote: "Now, on a comparison of the two paragraphs 10 and 12 it will be seen that there is a great similarity between them. In paragraph 10 the property in the Fourth Cross street is devised to John Anderson Dias and Livertina subject to a fidei commissum; and immediately after the words' 'fidei commissum,'' comes the proviso against the issue of a second marriage that I have already cited. In paragraph 12 the property in Canal row is devised to John Anderson Dias and others, and immediately after the words 'fidei commissum' follow the words' and under the same restrictions as before.'"

statement: The rule of jus accrescendi does not apply where the intention of the testator is to divide the property equally between two groups and allow the lawful issue of deceased institutes to inherit freely, as opposed to taking by substitution.
supporting_quote: "I am therefore of opinion that the finding of the learned District Judge as to the intention of the testators was right; that the intention of the testators was not to preserve the property intact, but to divide the property equally between the two groups, the sisters of the husband and the sisters of the wife surviving at the death of the testators; and that on the death of Maria without issue, her share in the property was freed from the fidei commissum."

statement: A surviving testator has no right to revoke a mutual will if the will disposed of the joint property on the death of the survivor, and if the survivor has accepted some benefit under the will.
supporting_quote: "It is quite true that the clause in the will by which the fidei commissum is constituted prohibits in terms 'mortgaging' alone, but the subsequent provision that the property is to be possessed by the survivor and then by Antoinette, is to devolve thereafter on Antoinette's children and grandchildren, and is to revert to the spouses and the other heirs only in the event of Antoinette dying without issue, is wholly inconsistent with the theory that Christina possessed any general power of sale under the will. The case is, therefore, one of a fiduciaria, who has power to sell only under an exception from a general, although implied, prohibition of any sale of the property in question."

statement: An article annexed to a building is considered a fixture and passes to the purchaser on sale of the building if it was intended by the owner to be a permanent part of the structure, even if its attachment is superficial.
supporting_quote: "Thus, a wooden screen standing on its base and only wedged in between two walls so as to be held firmly by them by lateral pressure, but intended by the owner of the building to bet a permanent partition of the main hall of the building into two rooms, is a fixture that passed to the purchaser on a sale of the building"

statement: A pleader appointed to record evidence should administer the oath to himself and to the interpreter.
supporting_quote: "A pleader appointed to record evidence should administer the oath to himself and to the interpreter."

statement: A judgment on a mortgage bond obtained against a person appointed to represent the estate of the deceased mortgagor under section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be executed by seizure and sale of property of the mortgagor other than those specially mortgaged.
supporting_quote: "I have no doubt that this question should be answered in the negative. The mortgage sections of the Code provide, in the first place, that an action to realize money due on a mortgage should be brought against the mortgagor whether he is still owner of the property or not, or, if the mortgagor is dead, against the executor or administrator of his estate; and in the next place, that in the event of the mortgage property being under the value of Rs. 1, 000, some person may be specially appointed to represent the estate of the deceased mortgagor for all the purposes of the action."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A purchaser in execution of a decree in an action on the bond can maintain an action in the nature of an actio doli against the parties involved to obtain a cancellation of the conveyance.
supporting_quote: Held, that it was competent to a purchaser in execution of a decree in an action on the bond in favour of C to maintain an action in the nature of an actio doli against A, B, and A's children to obtain a cancellation of the conveyance in favour of B and A's children.

statement: The mere massing of the joint estate of husband and wife for the purposes of a joint will does not by itself constitute adiation of inheritance under the will by either spouse.
supporting_quote: "The mere massing of the joint estate of husband and wife for the purposes of a joint will does not by itself constitute adiation of inheritance under the will by either spouse."

statement: An agreement for voluntary separation and a provision as to property are not only not illegal, but valid as between the parties themselves, and are only ineffectual for certain purposes.
supporting_quote: "The result of all the authorities is that an agreement for voluntary separation and a provision as to property are not only not illegal, but valid as between the parties themselves, and are only ineffectual for certain purposes."

statement: For a matter to be compulsorily referred to arbitration, it must relate wholly or in part to matters of mere account of an intricate and complicated character which cannot conveniently be tried in the ordinary way.
supporting_quote: "Under section 5 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1866 it is only when it appears to the satisfaction of the Court that an action relates wholly or in part to matters of mere account of an intricate and complicated character, which cannot conveniently be tried in the ordinary way, that the Court is given the power to order that such matters, either wholly or in part, be referred to arbitration."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 5 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1866

statement: The District Judge should have allowed the issue as to whether the seizing officer had the written authority under the hand of the Government Agent, which is required by section 43 of the Irrigation Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The learned District Judge should have allowed the issue as to whether the seizing officer had the written authority under the hand of the Government Agent, as is required by section 43 of the Irrigation Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 43 of the Irrigation Ordinance, No. 16 of 1906.

statement: The defendant is clearly bound to remove the encroachments, and should be ordered to do so without substantially impairing the use of the house.
supporting_quote: "I think that the defendant should be condemned to remove the encroachments at D, E, F, G, and M, and to surrender possession of H to the plaintiffs, and to pay the plaintiffs costs, in both Courts"

statement: An action for the recall of probate cannot be brought by summary procedure under section 537 of the Civil Procedure Code where an order nisi declaring a will proved has been made absolute, and interested parties must bring an independent action to set aside the judgment if fraud is alleged.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiffs, who were not parties to the testamentary action, sue for the recall of the probate of the will of Ran Etana granted to her husband, the defendant. The ground of action assigned in the plaint is that the will produced in Court 'was not the act and deed of Vithanage Ran Etana.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: "Section 537 of the Civil Procedure Code lays down the procedure for the recall or revocation of probate. Sections 536 and 537 should not be read together. Section 537 is not limited to the grounds of recall specified in section 536, but it was intended to permit applications for recall of probate on any legal ground."

statement: When a vendee sues a trespasser and the action is unsuccessful, he may still sue his vendor for damages.
supporting_quote: "Now, the cases cited were mainly those of lessee against lessor or vendee against vendor, where the lessor in the one case or the vendor in the other had placed his lessee or vendee in full physical possession of the land leased or sold by him. These cases can have no application whatever to the present, because in this case, admittedly, the plaintiff was not put in possession of the land sold to him by the defendants."

statement: A Fiscal's sale can be set aside under section 344 if it was made under an entire mistake, when to the knowledge of the purchaser the exigency of the writ had been fully satisfied.
supporting_quote: "Applying the principle thus recognized, I think that, if a Fiscal's sale can be shown, before it is confirmed, to have been made under an entire mistake, when to the knowledge of the purchaser the exigency of the writ had been fully satisfied, the sale may similarly be set aside under section 344."

statement: A person who conspired with the parties to a deed to bring about its execution cannot be made party to an action for cancellation of that deed when no damages are claimed as sustained by the plaintiff by reason of the fraudulent execution of the deed.
supporting_quote: "In an action for the cancellation of a deed, the parties to the deed need be the only parties to the action. A person who has conspired with the parties to the deed to bring about its execution is not liable to be made a party to such an action when no damages are claimed as sustained by the plaintiff by reason of the fraudulent execution of the deed."

statement: The procedure adopted by the parties on the petitioner's application was summary procedure under chapter XXIV of the Code, which was in order by reason of the provisions of section 595.
supporting_quote: "The procedure adopted by the parties on the petitioner's application was summary procedure under chapter XXIV. of the Code, That, I think. was in order by reason of the provisions of section 595."

statement: The prevention by fraud or force of the execution of a decree must be strictly traceable to an action done within the ten years immediately preceding the date of the application for execution.
supporting_quote: "The prevention by fraud or force of the execution of a decree in order to deprive a judgement-debtor of the benefit of section 337 (a) of the Civil Procedure Code must be strictly traceable to an action done within the ten years immediately preceding the date of the application for execution."

statement: A seizure on a prior writ cannot be availed of for the purpose of the sale of the property, and when a Fiscal having seized property under a writ sends it to the Court for an extension of the time allowed for execution, an application under section 224 is not necessary.
supporting_quote: "That in the case of a writ issued on an order on an application expressly made under section 224 of the Code, it is necessary that in terms of section 226 there should be a proper seizure of the property of the judgment-debtor on the particular writ so issued. A seizure on a prior writ cannot be availed of for the purpose of the sale of the property."

statement: A co-owner has no right whatever to build on the common property without the consent of his co-owners.
supporting_quote: "A co-owner has no right whatever to build on the common property without the consent of his co-owners."

statement: Parties cannot, however, by agreement dispense with the appointment of a commissioner under the Partition Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "A building erected by a co-owner on the common property is itself the common property of all the co-owners, the builder being, in certain circumstances, entitled to compensation."

statement: A lessee does not have the right to compensation for improvements made on land, unless there is a specific agreement with the lessor or the lessee has the bona fide possession of the property.
supporting_quote: "Admittedly, the defendant occupied the land claimed by the plaintiffs as a lessee, not of the plaintiffs, but of one of the fiduciarii on deed D 1 filed of record. It is now well-settled law in the Colony that, in order to be entitled to compensation for improvements, a person should have had, not only possession of the property improved, but bona fide possession of it."

statement: An agreement relating to fructus industriales requires notarial execution unless it is a single growing crop or even a single season, but extends to an indefinite period of future cultivation and establishes a kind of partnership in land.
supporting_quote: As a matter of fact, the agreement between the plaintiff and the defendant was constituted by a non-notarial writing, which was produced by the plaintiff for the purposes of the argument in the Court below; and it is clear from the averments in the plaint as well as the document that the agreement between the parties did not relate merely to a single growing crop or even a single season, but extended to an indefinite period of future cultivation, and that it established in effect a kind of partnership in land.

statement: Under the Roman-Dutch law, a purchaser cannot claim cancellation of a contract due to any defect in title by the seller after the sale has been completed. However, this rule does not apply when no actual sale has occurred and the vendor's title is discovered to be defective before completion.
supporting_quote: "In the present case it is expressly stipulated in the agreement sued upon that the vendors should 'execute a good and valid conveyance of the land free from all encumbrances in favour of the purchaser, ' and that stipulation, according to the authority cited by the appellant's counsel- Lysaght v. Edwards 1 - meant not merely that the seller was to execute a formal conveyance in accordance with legal requirements, but that he should be in a position to make a good title according to his undertaking to sell and transfer the parcel of land referred to in the deed of agreement."

statement: The defendant is not liable for damage caused to a public road if the agricultural operations carried out are in the ordinary course and do not significantly alter natural drainage.
supporting_quote: "In this state of facts, what are the rights of the Crown and the liabilities of the defendant ? At the argument of this appeal some 492 question was raised as to the right of the Attorney-General to o maintain this action. I confess I feel some doubt as to whether a civil action for damages is the proper remedy for injury caused to a public road. But as the case was fought out on other grounds in the District Court, I do not think that we need decide this point."

statement: A decree declaring title to land is not an order of the Court 'affecting' land as contemplated by the Land Registration Ordinance, and thus does not need to be registered under section 16. However, if it were deemed registrable, its unregistered status would not affect the validity of a subsequent registered deed for priority purposes only.
supporting_quote: It will be observed that the other documents, the registration of which is compulsory under section 16, are all documents affecting the devolution of land by transfer, transmission, or charge. They all affect the title to land; but how can a decree which merely declares title affect the title? The title existed presumably before the action in which the decree was had, and the decree declaring title is the expression of the finding of the Court as to the true state of the existing title. It must be presumed to be a right finding, and not one which affects the title, but one which merely settles it.

statement: A plaintiff who has granted a donation to her son cannot revoke the gift on grounds of ingratitude if the defendant's actions, while offensive, do not rise to the level recognized by Roman-Dutch law.
supporting_quote: "Does such conduct on the part of the defendants, as is disclosed by the circumstances just stated, amount to ingratitude within the meaning of the Roman-Dutch law ? To this question there can, in my opinion, be but one answer, - and that is an answer in the negative."

statement: Where the language of a will is not strictly grammatical, one should attach that meaning to it which it is quite clear from the context that the testator attached to it.
supporting_quote: "where the language in a will is not strictly grammatical, one should attach that meaning to it which it is quite clear from the context that the testator attached to it."

statement: The plaintiff cannot establish an agreement by oral evidence to vary a deed of sale, as this would be in contravention of section 92 of the Evidence Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The case against the second defendant may be disposed of at once. That depended on proof that the second defendant took the conveyance from the first defendant with notice of the alleged agreement. The only evidence on the point Is the fact that the plaintiff, even after the transfer to Diego Perera, continued to be in possession of the first three lands., but I do not see how that fact can be said to have informed the second defendant of the agreement."
statute_citation_verbatim: "The deed purports t o be a conveyance on sale, not a mortgage, and it is not alleged that Diego Perera did not use his own money, or that he acted as agent for another, or that he acted fraudulently, or any of the grounds upon which in Ceylon (Somasunderam Chetty v. Todd; 1 Pronchihamy v. Don Davith; 2 D. C. Jaffna, 7,409) oral evidence is admissible to prove a trust not inconsistent with the deed."

statement: A fidei commissum created by a will does not lapse if the legatee dies before the testator, and the property goes to the next in line of the lineage.
supporting_quote: "It appears to be clear Roman-Dutch law that, in the event of the legatee dying before the testator, the legacy does not lapse (Voet 36, 1, 69)."

statement: A deed registered in the wrong folio is void as against parties claiming an adverse interest on valuable consideration by virtue of a subsequent deed which has been duly registered.
supporting_quote: "The main issue in the case may be stated thus. The root of title of Jusenis Fernando and his co-owner Juan Fernando was a Crown grant dated October 5, 1870. This Crown grant was registered in folio 40 of vol. A 27. The plaintiff's deed is registered in the same folio. On the other hand, the seventh added defendant's deed of March 25, 1909, is registered in folio 136 of vol. 196 under the title Baranawedageliadda. It is now the settled law of this Colony (see Mohammadu Soli v. Isa Natchia, 1 Paaris v. Perera, 2 and 263- D. C. F. Chilaw, 741 3 ) that a deed which has been registered in a wrong folio is void as against parties claiming an adverse interest on valuable consideration by virtue of a subsequent deed which has been duly registered."

statement: The plaintiffs have no right either by inheritance or by prescription.
supporting_quote: "I am wholly unable to consent to this proposition. In my opinion the plaintiffs have no right either by inheritance or by prescription."

statement: A woman who becomes a surety with her eyes open and with full knowledge of her rights cannot evade responsibility by not pleading the benefit of the senatus consultum velleianum, especially if she has benefited from the transaction.
supporting_quote: "Moreover. it is clear that the deceased had benefited by the transaction in connection with the bond sued on."

statement: A married woman's immovable property becomes her separate estate, but she has only a prima facie right to the rents of that property, and the husband may step in whenever he pleases and claim it as his own under section 19.
supporting_quote: "Section 9 clearly provides, by necessary implication, that not only the immovable property with which it deals but the rents of that property become the married woman's separate estate. The object of the section was, in my opinion, to confer on married women the kind of interest in property which the Courts of Equity in England, and subsequently the Married Women's Property Act, 1870, recognized."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 9 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, 1876 (No. 15 of 1876)

statement: The original gift to Tikiri Banda remains unaffected by the subsequent deed executed by Mutumenika in favour of the defendants.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the original gift to Tikiri Banda remains unaffected by the subsequent deed executed by Mutumenika in favour of the defendants."

statement: Under the Kandyan law, illegitimate children are not included in a gift unless there is clear indication that the grantor intended to benefit them.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that this argument is sound. In the first place, the deed nowhere refers to the 'heirs' of Setuwa and Hapuwa, and the present question is not as to who are Hapuwa's intestate heirs, but as to who are to be held entitled to Hapuwa's one-third share by virtue of the gift. In the next place, under the Kandyan law, illegitimate children are heirs to a limited extent, for they succeed only to the acquired property of the deceased; and until the decision in Rankiri v. Ukku [ 10 N. L. R. 12. ]judicial opinion was that legitimate children, the widow, and certain collaterals would exclude the illegitimate children even as regards the acquired property."

statement: If a debtor tells the creditor that he has come for the purpose of paying a specified amount, and the creditor says it is too late or insufficient in amount, or otherwise indicates that he will not accept the money, the actual production is thereby dispensed with, and there is a good tender of the amount mentioned by the debtor.
supporting_quote: "If the debtor tells his creditor that he has come for the purpose of paying a specified amount, and the creditor says that it is too late, or is insufficient in amount, or otherwise indicates that he will not accept the money, the actual production is thereby dispensed with, and there is a good tender of the amount mentioned by the debtor"

statement: The claim is based on a written contract of sale, making it subject to section 7 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "What is the foundation of the plaintiff's claim for compensation ? There can be but one answer to this question, namely, 'the written contract of sale between the plaintiff and the defendant.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 7 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: An heir can create a title by registration even after the ancestor has disposed of his property during lifetime, provided the heir sells what would have been his right and title if the prior unregistered deed had not existed.
supporting_quote: "It has been further argued that the effect of the marriage settlement was to prevent the husband from having any right to grant the lease of 1800 at the time it was made, for that the wife's right was effectually conveyed as between her husband and herself by the deed of 1779; that she had no interest in her at the time she, married;. that she could therefore pass no interest to her husband by the marriage; that the husband consequently never had any right, and therefore could convey none to the lessee. Now, it may be admitted, that as against the husband, who was party to the deed of 1779, that deed was valid; it may be admitted also that he could not of right exercise any power over the property inconsistent with that deed; but as by the non-registration of that deed the grantees suffered him, as to the world at large, to have the appearance of right, neither they, nor any claiming under them, are at liberty to set up the deed in opposition to the persons who have been deluded by the appearance of right in the husband."

statement: The finding of illegitimacy is res judicata even if the court also found that the land was already divided.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the question of the legitimacy of the plaintiff is clearly res judicata by reason of the judgment in the former action. I would dismiss the appeal with costs."

statement: A prescriptive right to a projection over another's land does not extend to removing an old encroachment and creating a new one elsewhere.
supporting_quote: "The maxim of the English law- cujus est solum ejus est usque ad coelum et inferos -is as much a maxim also of the Roman-Dutch as of the Roman law (see Voet 8, 2, 18), and the old projection of the defendant's roof was, therefore, no more than an encroachment by the defendant on the plaintiff's land, in respect of which the defendant had acquired prescriptive rights, which certainly did not extend to a right to remove that particular encroachment and encroach on another part of the plaintiff's land."

statement: A court has the discretion to make an order of abatement ex mero motu under section 402 of the Civil Procedure Code, provided it gives due notice to the parties and there are no extenuating circumstances preventing the plaintiff from prosecuting the action.
supporting_quote: "It was urged that under section 402 the Court could act only on the application of the defendant. I can see nothing in the section which prohibits the Court from acting ex mero motu."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 402 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: Christopher Brito's possession of the Dombawinne estate did not amount to an ouster, and his co-owners retained their legal interest in one-eighth of the property.
supporting_quote: A mass of evidence and family correspondence has been adduced in the case, most of it entirely irrelevant, and in strictness inadmissible. It shows that most of the children were in impecunious circumstances, and were frequently, and often successfully, applying to their father for money; but nowhere is there any direct demand by any of the children on their father for their share of the property, nor is there any assertion on his part, either verbal or in witing, that he claimed any legal right to the entire property.

statement: A notarial lease is a written contract or agreement within the contemplation of section 7, and the period of limitation for an action for rent due under such a lease is six years.
supporting_quote: "No doubt, also, section 6 was not discussed there at all; but it is inconceivable that if section 6 had any bearing on the question, the eminent Judges who took part in the decision would not have considered it. It seams to me that the whole question of prescription was fully before the Court, and I think the decision is a binding authority in the present case."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, section 7

statement: Prescriptive title to chena land within the Kandyan Province cannot be set up against the Crown.
supporting_quote: "I hold that prescriptive title to chena land within the Kandyan Province cannot be set up against the Crown."

statement: A lessee is not entitled to compensation for improvements as against the lessor's child, who brings an action to vindicate his share.
supporting_quote: Under the Roman-Dutch law as it exists in Ceylon the mother does not become, on the death of the father of a minor child, the guardian of the latter, otherwise than by appointment made by ('sort under chapter XL, of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: The plaintiff's title to the property is valid and she should be declared entitled to her share, subject to certain conditions.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff is declared entitled to the share claimed, but it must be subject to the rights created by the usufructuary mortgage."

statement: A Crown grant of divel lands conveyed only a one-fifth share of the entire land, subject to payment of produce to the Government.
supporting_quote: "The Commissioner considers that the Crown grant in reality conveyed a one-fifth share of the whole land, and in this opinion I think he is right."

statement: If a donee dies leaving a descendant, the condition under which property is to revert to the donor's estate is defeated.
supporting_quote: "I hold that the property vested in Madalena Silva, and on her mother's death subject only to the entail created in favour of Lenohamy's descendants."

statement: A court should take the view that the language used by the donors has failed to disclose an intention to give a share of the property to Louisa's children on her death.
supporting_quote: "This is essentially a case where a court should take the view that the language used by the donors has failed to disclose an intention to give a share of the property to Louisa's children on her death."

statement: A servitude of emphyteusis can be acquired by prescription under the Prescription Ordinance, even if it involves a payment of one-third of the produce.
supporting_quote: 'I think, however, that the words "a possession unaccompanied by payment of rent or produce" are governed by the following words of the section: 'from which an acknowledgment of a right existing in another person would fairly and naturally be inferred' In the present case I consider that apart from the deed of 1836, which is inadmissible in evidence, it is quite obvious, and has been uncontested throughout the case, that the defendants and their predecessors have throughout and for very many years claimed to hold this land in perpetuity at a rent charge under some deed executed by Gallage Hendrick, and therefore that their claim to this servitude has been adverse to the plaintiffs and their predecessors; and the payment of one-third share of the proceeds of the land is not, under the circumstances, a payment from which an acknowledgment of a right existing in the plaintiffs and their predecessors in title to the land unburdened with the servitude, would fairly or reasonably be inferred.'
statute_citation_verbatim: 'The expression 'immovable property' shall be taken to include an shares and interest in such property, and all rights, easements, and servitudes thereunto belonging or appertaining.' Section 2 of the Prescription Ordinance, 1871.

statement: A lessee is not bound to notify his right of way unless he knows that a violation of his rights is in progress and the other party would be misled by his silence.
supporting_quote: "to create an estoppel by acquiescence it is essential to show that the party against whom it is pleaded, knowing that a violation of his rights was in progress, stood by and so misled the oilier party."

statement: The plaintiff could not enforce a contract for a distillery license that was never applied for or accepted, even if the circular letter held out an inducement to form such a contract.
supporting_quote: With regard to the second point, the contract to grant the distillery license for the purposes mentioned In the circular is a matter altogether apart from an ordinary application for a distiller's 434 license contemplated by the Ordinance and I do not think the Government can be heard to say that the only remedy, in case the Government refused to carry out the contract, was an appeal to itself. In my opinion, however, the appellant never applied for and was never willing to accept the license that he was entitled to under his contract, namely, a license trammelled with the condition that all arrack distilled should be used for the purposes of his own rents.

statement: Evidence of an oral agreement to lease premises as a rice store cannot be admitted under the Evidence Ordinance if the written lease is formal and does not indicate the purpose for which the premises were to be used.
supporting_quote: "The deed, both in the body of it and in the schedule, describes the premises as 'all those houses and grounds bearing assessment Nos. 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18. situated at Bankshall street, &c., ' and there is no provision or expression in the instrument indicating the purpose for which the premises were to be used."

statement: When a court orders the sale of property, the executor no longer has authority to dispose of the property except upon further orders of the Court. The sale by the court takes precedence over subsequent sales by the executor.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that all this can be ignored in considering whether the sale to the defendants prevails over the sale to the plaintiff. In my opinion, when the Court exercised its jurisdiction and took upon itself the sale of the property, the executor had no longer any authority to dispose of the property, except upon further orders of Court, and cannot be allowed to defeat the acts of the Court in regard to the sale."

statement: The donor cannot waive conditions of a fiduciary gift without the consent of the reversioners, especially when the reversioners are legitimate descendants of the donee.
supporting_quote: "In such a case as the present, where the reversioners are the legitimate descendants of the donees, acceptance of the gift by the fiduciary donee its a sufficient acceptance on behalf of the descend-ants, and precludes the donors from revoking it, even if such a consent as the original owners of the land gave to the execution of the second lease could be regarded as a revocation."

statement: A deed of gift does not create a valid fidei commissum if it lacks an adequate designation of the persons to be benefited on the death of the fiduciary.
supporting_quote: "This decision is binding upon us, and I feel that I cannot usefully add anything to the reasoning by which it is supported."

statement: A person seeking relief from prescription on the ground of concealed fraud is entitled to avail himself in all cases, and not only in cases relating to real property, of the fraud, not only of the defendant himself, but of any person through whom he claims.
supporting_quote: "I think that the proposition has been stated too narrowly, and that the person seeking relief from prescription on the ground of concealed fraud is entitled to avail himself in all cases, and not only in cases relating to real property, of the fraud, not only of the defendant himself, but of any person through whom he claims;"

statement: A Kandyan mother has the right to inherit her children's acquired properties in preference to the father, and this rule is generally accepted based on text-writers' statements and judicial recognition.
supporting_quote: "The right of a Kandyan mother to inherit her children's acquired properties in preference to the father rests principally on a statement found in Armour 87 that the mother is heiress to the acquired property of all kinds left by her child. This, however, is supplemented by the passage in Armour 89 that 'if the mother has departed this life previous to the demise of her child, then the father will be entitled to the reversion of the child's acquired property.' Sawyer 17 also appears to lay down the law to the same effect, and later writers have accepted the position. Judicial recognition of the rule is to be found in D. C. Kandy, 21,994, 1 and Ranhami v. Menik Etana; 2"

statement: The children of a Kandyan man and a low-country Sinhalese woman are not necessarily considered Kandyans, as the status depends on specific circumstances and there is no general rule.
supporting_quote: If the law is to be declared in that sense, the task must be accomplished by the Legislature, after taking full account of the different classes of cases for which it will have to provide.

statement: A sale under the Partition Ordinance is subject to existing leases, unless it is expressly declared to be free of them.
supporting_quote: "I entirely agree with Pereira J. in Silva v. Soysa, 2 [(1913) 17 N. L. R. 67.] that there can he no objection to a lessee being made & party to the action, or to his rights being adjudicated upon and a suitable order made with reference to them. Section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code, with the reasonable necessity arising from the object of the Ordinance, is a sufficient authority for such, a course."

statement: A co-owner can sue another co-owner to have their title declared to a certain share of the property owned in common, and for damages sustained by them due to the wrongful enjoyment of their share.
supporting_quote: "There is no objection to one co-owner suing another to have his title declared to a certain share of the property owned in common, and for damages sustained by him by reason of the wrongful enjoyment of his share by the other co-owners."

statement: Prescription which has already commenced to run is not interrupted by the supervening minority of a person who succeeds to the right in dispute, unless specifically provided otherwise.
supporting_quote: "I have little doubt that the Legislature to Ceylon intended to follow the law of England with reference to the effect of disabilities upon the limitation of actions, and the weight of judicial authority, from the case of Muttu v. Menika 3 down to Sinnatamby v. Meera Levvai, 4 descends so unmistakably on this side of the controversy that we should not be justified now in disturbing the settled interpretation of the law upon the ground of a strictly literal construction of section 14 of the Ordinance of 1871."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 14 of the Prescription Ordinance, 1871 (No. 22 of 1871)

statement: Ratification of an unauthorized act by a principal can be established without a notarially attested instrument, as long as the principal ex post facto creates the agent for the purpose of the agreement.
supporting_quote: "All that was necessary was that the first defendant should ex post facto create Casie Chetty his agent for the purpose of the agreement in question."

statement: The donation by a spouse to another is not fraudulent merely because the donor desires to safeguard the property gifted against being made liable for his debts, and the donated property should be subject to the debts of the donor only at the time of the alienation.
supporting_quote: It seems to me that, in the present case, the evidence against the 2nd defendant cannot be put higher than this, that he desired to safeguard the property gifted to his wife against being made liable for his debts, or at any rate for the results of the litigation on which he was about to embark. That is not sufficient to make the alienation fraudulent, in the absence of affirmative proof that he had no other poperty against which his creditors could have recourse.

statement: A customary marriage is valid under the law, independently of registration.
supporting_quote: "Generally speaking, there are three requisites for a valid marriage, namely, competency, intention to marry, and a recognized form of marriage. There is so dispute in this case as to the first two requisites, and it is equally without doubt that under our law the customary form of marriage is good, independently of registration."

statement: Under the Tesawalamai, a father can allocate all of his deceased wife's property as dowry to daughters and exclude sons from it if they are grown up.
supporting_quote: "The father, then, has the right to dispose of the whole of the deceased wife's property in dowry to the daughters, and the sons take nothing unless something remains after the daughters have been dowried."

statement: A judgment against a minor who is unrepresented by a guardian is at most an irregularity, and the judgment will stand as a valid adjudication against the minor until reversed, and will not be open to a collateral attack.
supporting_quote: "A judgment against a minor who is unrepresented by a guardian is at most an irregularity, and the judgment will stand as a valid adjudication against the minor until reversed, and will not be open to a collateral attack."
statute_citation_verbatim: SRC030-s480, SRC030-s502 or null

statement: The burden of proving the good faith of a transaction rests on the party who stands in an active confidence relationship with the donor, unless independent advice is shown.
supporting_quote: "Certainly the ease of Sital Prasad v. Parbhu Lal, 3 on which the plaintiff's counsel relied in this connection, does not support any such proposition.
