In that case there is a specific finding that the party alleged to have used undue influence himself obtained the execution of the impugned deeds."

statement: The period of prescription for an action based on negligence begins from the date of the theft, not the accrual of pecuniary damages.
supporting_quote: "In principle, in actions for damages such as this, the measure of damages is the value of the goods, and not the amount of the writ, and this value is that placed on them by the Fiscal."

statement: Where an instrument requiring to be stamped is executed by several persons, it is not necessary that they should all cancel the stamp.
supporting_quote: "The Commissioner's opinion that when an instrument is executed by several persons they must all cancel the stamp is, I think, also erroneous."

statement: Where the intended fraud is not accomplished, the maxim 'in part delicto potior est conditio defendantis' has no application, and the party who has delivered the property may lawfully reclaim it before the alleged purpose is carried out.
supporting_quote: "The law is that where the intended fraud is not accomplished, the maxim in part delicto potior est conditio defendants has no application, and the party who has delivered the property may lawfully reclaim it before the alleged purpose is carried out. See Mohamadu Marikar v. Ibrahim Naina"

statement: An action for damages consequent on judicial eviction is maintainable against all previous vendors where there is privity of contract between the plaintiff and all defendants due to a covenant to warrant and defend the title.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the action was maintainable against all the defendants, as there was privity of contract between the plaintiff and all the defendants."

statement: A sale having duly taken place in execution of a decree valid at the time cannot afterwards be set aside as against a bona fide purchaser not a party to the decree, on the ground that the decree had been, subsequently to the sale, reversed.
supporting_quote: It was there held that a sale, having duly taken place in execution of a decree valid at the time, cannot afterwards be set aside as against a bona fide purchaser, not a party to the decree, on the ground that the decree had been, subsequently to the sale, reversed.

statement: An action by one co-owner can be maintained without joining all other co-owners if the dispute is between only a few of them and does not prejudice the rights of others.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion sections 17 and 22 of the Code are intended to do away with all technical objections on the score of non-joinder or mis-joinder of parties unless they are taken in due time and for good reason. If, however, it be found that the action cannot proceed for want of parties, section 18 enables the Court even mero motu to add such parties."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 17 and 22 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A Court of Requests has jurisdiction to hear and determine an action for enforcing a contract if the 'contract sought to be enforced was made' within the local limits of its jurisdiction.
supporting_quote: "The omission of paragraph (d) in section 77 of the Courts Ordinance, as amended by Ordinance No. 11 of 1895, was intentional. The cause of action is the non payment- of the wages, and that took place at Kalutara."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 77 of the Courts Ordinance, No. 1 of 1889, as amended by section 4 of the Ordinance No. 12 of 1895, and Section 9 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: An agreement under the Waste Lands Ordinance, even when entered into with a claimant who only claims an undivided share, is conclusive of title as against other co-owners who did not make claims.
supporting_quote: "The Ordinance, when it provided for an agreement with the claimant, meant that a complete settlement of the title might thereby be arrived at, whether there might or might not be possible claims on the part of other persons who have not chosen to come forward."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 4 (1) of the Waste Lands Ordinance, No. 1 of 1897, as amended by the Ordinances of 1899, 1900, and 1903.

statement: A co-owner who improves a house under the mistaken impression that he is sole owner has no right of action against his co-owners, but can retain the property as if he were a bona fide possessor until a proportionate share of the expenditure is refunded to him.
supporting_quote: Voet 10, 3, 3 (Samson's Translation 389), after dealing with the case of a person who knows that there is another co-owner with him, proceeds to say that the position is different if he spent the money on improvements thinking that the property was his alone, and that, though he has no direct action to recover the amount of compensation, he has the right 'to retain the property as if he were the bona fide possessor of another's property until the other's pro rata share of the expense is made good to him.'

statement: A minor's contract under Roman-Dutch law is not void but invalid as far as the minor’s obligation is concerned until ratified by the minor upon attaining majority, while it binds the other party to it.
supporting_quote: "According to the Roman-Dutch law, a minor's contract is such that it does not bind the minor unless he ratified it on attaining majority, while it binds the other party to it."

statement: The Supreme Court is not entitled to go into the merits of the case, or to dispose of them on any assumption that the decisions of the Supreme Court and the District Court are correct when deciding whether an application for a stay of execution pending appeal to the Privy Council should be allowed or refused.
supporting_quote: In deciding whether an application for a stay of execution pending appeal to the Privy Council should be allowed or refused, the Supreme Court is not entitled to go into the merits of the case, or to dispose of them on any assumption that the decisions of the Supreme Court and the District Court are correct.

statement: In partition actions, costs should be borne by the co-owners pro rata.
supporting_quote: "I feel constrained, although with reluctance, to set aside the order from which this appeal is brought, and to direct that the costs of all the parties, including those of the respondents, on whose behalf a statement of objections was filed, should be borne pro rata."

statement: A fidei commissum can be created even if the donor uses expressions inconsistent with it, provided the intention to create one is clear.
supporting_quote: "In considering whether a fidei commissum is created, one has to look at the document as a whole, and if the intention to create a fidei commissum is clear, effect should be given to it, even although the donor or testator may have used in the document expressions that are inconsistent with a fidei commissum."

statement: A bona fide purchaser for value without notice of a trust can be deprived of the property purchased on the ground of any irregularities in the order for sale, or in the procedure by which that order was obtained only if the Court ordering the sale has jurisdiction.
supporting_quote: The defendant is, in my opinion, entitled to shelter himself under the authority of the order of the District Court of Badulla if he can show-for as to this the burden of proof is on him-that he made the purchase in good faith for valuable consideration and without notice of the trust.

statement: A person holding a beneficial interest cannot maintain an action for partition under the Ceylon Partition Ordinance until they have obtained a conveyance from the legal owner.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff has as yet no legal estate; his only right, if any, is a right of action against defendant to compel him to grant conveyance of a half share. "

statement: A vendor is liable for eviction, whether the whole thing has been evicted or only a part, provided it be a part of the thing and homogeneous with it, and a real servitude is a 'homogeneous part.'
supporting_quote: "Before dealing with the other covenants, I may state that under the Roman-Dutch law a vendor is liable for eviction, whether the whole thing has been evicted or only a part, provided it be a part of the thing and homogeneous with it, and a real servitude is a 'homogeneous part.'"

statement: The doctrine of enormis laesio does not apply when the transaction is not a sale and there was no consideration passed or intended to pass.
supporting_quote: There is, therefore, no room for the application of the doctrine of enormis Icesio,1[Voet 18, 5, 16, and Juta's Digest, vol. II. , col. 2583.] as the transaction was not a sale at all.

statement: A plaintiff is estopped from setting up a usufructuary mortgage as against the defendant if he himself was a bidder at the sale and did not disclose the existence of any mortgage, despite requesting the Fiscal to carry out the sale subject to the mortgage.
supporting_quote: The plaintiff wrote to the Fiscal asking the Fiscal to carry out the sale subject to the mortgage, but Fiscal did not carry out the sale subject to the mortgage, nor was the existence of any mortgage disclosed at the sale either by the Fiscal or by the plaintiff. The defendant purchased the property without knowledge of the mortgage. Held, that plaintiff was estopped from setting up the usufructuary mortgage as against the defendant.

statement: A mutual will, unless its wording specifically applies to the estate of the first dying only, can be effective as the separate will of the survivor if no new will is made.
supporting_quote: "Unless the words of the joint will are such as to apply to the estate of the first dying only, I imagine the will would be effective as the separate will of the survivor if the survivor made no new will."

statement: The property brought together by the husband and wife upon marriage, as per section 1 of the Tesawalamai, is presumed to be from acquired property.
supporting_quote: On this ground the learned District Judge has dealt with each of the items in the schedule.

statement: Where a Kandyan dies unmarried, childless, and intestate, his acquired property devolves on his mother in full ownership, to the exclusion of his brothers and sisters.
supporting_quote: "These decisions, with which I entirely agree, will apply much more strongly to a case where there are only half-brothers and half-sisters. Property gifted to a person is 'acquired property' of that person."

statement: A mortgage is indivisible, and a person who pays the debt when the creditor has brought the hypothecary action may have recourse against the others for contribution.
supporting_quote: "The mortgage being indivisible, all those to whom the mortgaged property come are in the position of co-obligors."

statement: The Muhammadan law which prevails in Ceylon is so much and no more of it as has received the sanction of custom in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "It has been frequently pointed out that this Code is not exhaustive {Perera v. Khan, 1 to cite one case among others). Where the Code is silent, and there is no special custom on any point, it has been held that the Roman-Dutch law should be resorted to, as being the law generally applicable in the absence of any special law, which takes the matter out of the operation of that general law. (Case in the District Court of Colombo referred to in the judgment of Lawson D.J. in 1862 in the anonymous case, D. C. Colombo, No. 29,129, 2 Ibrahim Sayibu v. Muhamadu, 3 and Tillekeratne v. Samsedeen. 4"

statement: A father may revoke a gift to his children, even without assigning a just cause, according to Shafei law.
supporting_quote: "With respect to the tradition of the Prophet quoted by Shafei, the meaning of it is that the donor is not himself empowered to retract his gift, as this must be done by decree of the Kazee with the consent of the donor, excepting in the case of a father, who is himself competent to retract a gift to his son when he wants it for the maintenance of the son."

statement: Prescription is a mode of acquisition independent of any documentary title which the possessor may at the same time have, and although the one may be defeated by the operation of the Registration Ordinance, the other remains unaffected.
supporting_quote: "Prescription is a mode of acquisition independent of any documentary title which the possessor may at the same time have, and although the one may be defeated by the operation of the Registration Ordinance, the other remains unaffected."

statement: Payment by cheque is a conditional payment, and when the cheque is honoured, that operates as a payment as from the date of the giving of the cheque.
supporting_quote: "Generally speaking, payment by cheque is a conditional payment, and when the cheque is honoured, that operates as a payment as from the date of the giving of the cheque (Hadley v. Hadley [(1898) L. R. 2 Ch. 680.])."

statement: A person in whose favour a deed of agreement for sale of land was executed by its owner is not by the mere registration of such deed in a position to enforce specific performance against a third party, to whom the land was sold subsequent to such registration.
supporting_quote: "A person in whose favour a deed of agreement for sale of a land was executed by its owner is not by the mere registration of such deed in a position to enforce specific performance against a third party, to whom the land was sold subsequent to such registration."

statement: Where a purchase is made in the name of a stranger, a trust of the legal estate results in favour of the person out of whose pocket the money for the purchase has come.
supporting_quote: It is well-established law in England that where a purchase is made in the name of a stranger, a trust of the legal estate results in favour of the person out of whose pocket the money for the purchase has come (see Lewin on Trusts, 11th ed., p. 178, and the numerous cases there ) cited).

statement: A party who advances money on an informal agreement is entitled to a refund only if the other party refuses or is incapable of completing the transaction, and the consideration for the advance therefore fails.
supporting_quote: "It is necessary, however, to take account of certain local decisions on the subject. I was certainly much impressed at the argument with the number of them, and with the long period of time which they covered. But when the cases are closely examined, it will be found that they are neither individually strong, nor collectively such as to form a cursus curia. None of them contains any discussion of principles or exposition of the law."

statement: Buddhist temples can acquire title to land by prescription, even if they are prohibited from acquiring property without the license of the Governor.
supporting_quote: The prohibition against the acquisition of property by a Buddhist temple without the license of the Governor does not prevent a Buddhist temple from acquiring title by prescription to a land.

statement: A Chetty agent signing on behalf of a firm binds the firm when he prefixes the initials of the firm to his own name, provided he has authority to do so.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion therefore that in the present case Muttiah Chetty, having been authorized by the power of attorney to sign in the name of the firm, he has properly done so by prefixing the vilasam to his name, and that that signature binds the firm on the note."

statement: A subsequent sale by an administratrix with a Court order takes priority over a Fiscal's sale, but the registration of the conveyance is crucial for establishing title.
supporting_quote: "Held , that plaintiff had a superior title. Aserappa v. Weeratunga 1 [ 1 (1911) 14 N. L. R. 417. ] and Tikiri Banda v. Loku Banda 2 [ 2 (1911) 15 N. L. R. 63. ] -followed."

statement: A court has the power to amend a decree that omits terms agreed upon by parties due to clerical error, even if the original parties are deceased and the amendment is sought by their legal representatives or heirs.
supporting_quote: "I do not find any insuperable difficulty in the use of the word 'heirs' to express this idea. The usual meaning of the term no doubt is 'heirs ab intestato, ' but I believe the Tamil equivalent of the term is much wider, and includes relationship by blood, and sometimes even by marriage."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 5, 189, and 408

statement: A judgment-creditor is not conclusively bound by an adverse judgment against his debtor, but can show that the property belongs to his debtor if it was obtained fraudulently and collusively.
supporting_quote: "It appears that estoppels may arise by the voluntary conduct of a party or by operation of law, and it seems to me that the principle that a judgement-creditor is not concluded by estoppels against his debtor applies only to estoppels which arise from conduct, and does not apply to an estoppel' not brought about by the voluntary conduct of the debtor but by an adverse judgment against him."

statement: A mortgagee must sue the executor or administrator of a deceased mortgagor, and if the mortgaged property exceeds Rs. 1,000 in value, an administrator must be appointed.
supporting_quote: "The proviso to section 642 enables the mortgagee to take the less onerous course of applying for the appointment of a special representative where the mortgaged property is less than Rs. 1,000 in value. The proviso no doubt says that the Court 'may' make such an appointment if it appears to the Court necessary or expedient."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A Fiscal has no legal power to stay a sale otherwise than upon an order of Court.
supporting_quote: "The trend of judicial decisions in this Colony distinctly establishes the proposition which is supported by the language of sections 342 and 343 of the Civil Procedure Code, that a Fiscal has no legal power to stay a sale otherwise than upon an order of Court."

statement: A co-owner who has made improvements to a jointly owned property cannot claim half the cost of those improvements from the other co-owner if that co-owner has sold their share, unless there is a partition and the improved portion is not fully compensated.
supporting_quote: "X has still his right to compensation under the Partition Ordinance, in the event of a partition, should he not get the whole ' of the portion of the land which he has improved; and if Y has purported to sell to the purchaser of his interest the improvements effected by X, that is a matter between themselves, in which X is not concerned."

statement: A person claiming to be the owner of a piece of land which had been partitioned by others in a proceeding under Ordinance No. 11 of 1863 cannot claim damages under section 9 of the Ordinance from the parties to the partition action if they acted bona fide and in ignorance of the rights of the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: If any owner or co-owner is aware of the pendency of the partition action and abstains from coming forward he cannot afterwards claim damages.
statute_citation_verbatim: Provided that nothing herein contained shall affect the right of any party prejudiced by such partition or sale to recover damages from the parties by whose act, whether of commission or omission, such damage had accrued.

statement: A vendor can be held liable for breaches of covenants even if the vendee knew about potential defects, as long as the covenants are clear and express.
supporting_quote: "The defendant followed this up by covenanting that he would warrant and defend title against all disputes and objections. These are express covenants, and therefore even knowledge of defects on tie part of Adam Bawa will not affect the liability of the defendant."

statement: The principle of enormis laesio is applicable to a lease as much as to a sale, but for this purpose the difference in value should exist at the time of the lease or sale and not thereafter.
supporting_quote: For this purpose the difference in value should exist at the time of the lease or sale and not thereafter. (Grotius' Introduction 3, 52, 2; Walter Pereira's Laws of Ceylon 657.)

statement: A fidei commissum is not extinguished by a partition under Ordinance No. 10 of 1863; it remains attached to the property allotted in severalty to the fiduciary.
supporting_quote: "A fidei commissum is not extinguished by a partition under Ordinance No. 10 of 1863; it remains attached to the property allotted in severalty to the fiduciary."

statement: An executor who purchases property for himself using his son’s name, without the son having any funds or involvement in the transaction, constitutes a nominee purchase and is voidable by other beneficiaries.
supporting_quote: "In addition to these findings, there must be mentioned the fact that the executor, whose action was challenged, never ventured to give evidence. It is true that he was old and was said to be in ill health, but he attended the Court throughout the trial. No application was made to take his evidence on commission, and no medical evidence tendered to show he was incapable of giving testimony."

statement: An action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code should be brought in the Court within whose local limits the property is situate.
supporting_quote: "What is the cause of action, if any, arising from the seizure of property and the order on a claim in execution? To my mind it is hardly proper in this connection to speak of a cause of action in the ordinary sense. It appears to me that an action under section 247 does not directly arise from any act of the parties, but is a special statutory action provided for the determination of one of two questions arising from the order of Court in the claim proceedings, namely, (1) where the claim is disallowed, whether the claimant has the right which he claims to the property in dispute, and (2) where the claim is upheld, whether the execution-debtor has, as against the claimant a saleable interest in the property seized in execution of the decree in the plaintiff's favour? Both these questions relate to and involve a declaration of title to the property, and I think that subject to the other factors which may affect the jurisdiction of the Court, the action should be brought in the Court within whose local limits the property is situate."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The owner of the dominant tenement cannot increase the volume of sewage or discharge it in a concentrated form to the prejudice of the owner of the servient tenement.
supporting_quote: "This is what has happened in the present Case, and the action is therefore well founded."

statement: Paraveni nilakarayas are the owners of the lands comprised in the panguwa.
supporting_quote: "Here the obvious comparison was between the paraveni nilakarayas of a gabadagama and those of a nindagama, and the Court, which included Dias J., a Judge of eminence and wide experience, impliedly stated it as an accepted proposition that the paraveni nilakaraya, and not the proprietor of the nindagama, was the owner of his holding."

statement: A diga married daughter may re-acquire binna rights if she is re-admitted into her father's family and restored to her natural rights of inheritance, provided the father's family intends or recognizes this result.
supporting_quote: "The point to- be kept in view in all cases, I think, is that the essence of a diga marriage is the severance of the daughter from the father's family and her entry into that of the husband, and her consequent forfeiture of any share in the family property, and the principle underlying the acquisition of binna rights, as I understand it, is that the daughter is re-admitted into the father's family and restored to her natural rights of inheritance."

statement: A purchaser of one of the mortgaged lands is entitled to an assignment of the mortgage bond upon tendering the entire sum due on the bond to the mortgagee.
supporting_quote: Certainly if rights of action are, on the most certain principles of law, to be ceded to guarantors of another's debt and also to sureties, when these are willing to pay the debt in full, against the other persons who at the same time became co-sureties or guarantors, I see no reason why cession of action ought not to be also made to any person whatever who pays the whole debt, and thus also the right of action should be ceded to a purchaser by him whom he pays.

statement: A mortgagee's right to proceeds from the sale of a mortgaged share in an undivided property is limited to the share allotted to the mortgagor under the partition decree, unless the mortgage was of the whole land.
supporting_quote: "The main provision of section 12 of the Partition Ordinance deals with a mortgage of the whole land which is the subject of action. The proviso to the section does not touch the case of a mortgage of an undivided share in the event of a sale in the partition action, and in such a case the right of a mortgagee is confined to the proceeds of the sale."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 12 of the Partition Ordinance

statement: An unsuccessful action by an owner of land against a trespasser in possession does not interrupt the running of prescription.
supporting_quote: "An unsuccessful action by an owner of land against a trespasser in possession does not interrupt the running of prescription."

statement: A surety's liability is limited to paying the principal debtor if they fail to do so, and a general renunciation of suretyship rights must be specific or declared by a lawyer for it to be valid.
supporting_quote: "The 'payment' here referred to is clearly the payment by the company to the plaintiff. Any liability undertaken by a surety must be construed strictly and in a sense least burdensome to the surety, and when the defendant in the first clause agrees that, if there shall be the whole or any part of the said monies due and payable at the expiration of twelve months, he shall, and will pay the same to the plaintiff, the only conclusion is that he undertakes to pay if the company shall not have paid within the period mentioned, and that thus he makes himself liable no more and no less than as surety."

statement: A surviving spouse in the capacity of executor de son tort may validly sell the property of the deceased spouse for the payment of debts.
supporting_quote: A surviving spouse in the capacity of executor de son tort may validly sell the property of the deceased spouse for the payment of debts.

statement: The Government's refusal to grant distillery licenses constitutes a breach of contract if the licenses are for the purpose of supplying arrack both by retail and wholesale as per the terms of sale.
supporting_quote: "It follows that the letter from the Government Agent on July 31, 1912, unconditionally refusing to grant a distillery license to distil under Ordinance No. 10 of 1844, constitutes a breach of the obligation undertaken by the Government in the letter of March 4, 1912, at the time of the sale of the arrack rents of Negombo and Anuradhapura."

statement: A warrant of attorney to confess judgment is given as security for the plaintiff, and allows the plaintiff to get another proctor to act if the named proctor refuses.
supporting_quote: "On the contrary, a warrant of attorney is given as security for the plaintiff, and is delivered to him to use it as he wishes by getting the named proctor or any other proctor of the Court to act under it. The object of it will be effectively defeated if the named proctor refuses to act in the interests of the defendant or for any other reason, unless the warrant is so framed as to enable the plaintiff to get another proctor to act."

statement: From the uninterrupted sole possession of certain co-owners extending over a large number of years, and the conduct of the other co-owners in not asserting any right to possess, a presumption of an ouster by the co-owners in possession and the commencement of an adverse holding can be presumed.
supporting_quote: In the present case, although. Babappu, according to his own evidence, knew that his co-owners had during his minority granted a mining lease in respect of the land, he never, when he attained majority, attempted to assert any right to his share, and, although he purported to sell to Tillekeratne in 1895, his vendee never possessed, nor was the land included in the inventory of his estate on his death in 1901, and his heirs, the present appellants, made no attempt to assert any right to possess until the year 1916. It appears to me that the correct presumption to draw from the long uninterrupted possession of Babappu's co-owners, and the conduct of himself and his vendee, is that Babappu and his vendee knew that Babappu's co-owners were holding adversely to him, and that they had, in fact, ousted him from possession.

statement: A Court of Appeal must form its own view of the facts, even when based on findings of fact from a Judge of first instance.
supporting_quote: "While a Court of Appeal will always attach the greatest possible weight to any finding of fact of a Judge of first instance based upon oral testimony given before that Judge, it is not absolved by the existence of these findings from the duty of forming its own view of the facts"

statement: A deed executed by an attorney for his principal, even when signed in the attorney's own name, can be valid if it is clear that the attorney was acting on behalf of the principal and not for himself.
supporting_quote: "Where is the difference between signing J. B. by M. W. his attorney, which must be admitted to be good, and M. W. for J. B.? In either case the act of sealing and delivering is done in the name of the principal and by his authority."

statement: Under English law, a bank can charge compound interest on current accounts where the customer has acquiesced in such practice and there is an agreement to pay it or if it aligns with trade custom.
supporting_quote: "While under the Roman-Dutch law compound Interest was not allowed, even though it had been expressly stipulated for, under 497 the English law it was allowed where, inter alia, there was an agreement, express or implied. to pay it, or where its allowance was in accordance with a custom of a particular trade or business."

statement: Presentation for ordination, apart from robing, is sufficient to constitute pupillage.
supporting_quote: "It may be added that these functions may validly be performed by delegation, and it would seem that a priest presented for ordination by a priest other than the robing priest in his own name will be the pupil of both. This probably is an instance of pupillage by adoption spoken of by the High Priest in the Matara case."

statement: A District Court is not bound to accept and proceed upon any indictment presented by the Attorney-General without regard to whether it is authorized by law or not.
supporting_quote: "There having been no magisterial inquiry into the offences charged in the indictment, the indictment should, in my opinion, have been quashed."

statement: A borrower does not have a legal duty to disclose their insolvent status when borrowing money, and such non-disclosure does not necessarily constitute cheating under section 398 of the Penal Code.
supporting_quote: "I question very much whether this was the class of cases which the legislator had in mind, and certainly he gives no illustration drawn from this class."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 398 of the Penal Code

statement: In Ceylon, the cause of action for fraud arises when the cheques are received and dealt with by the appellants, not when they discover the fraud later.
supporting_quote: "Their Lordships are, therefore, of opinion that, according to the law of Ceylon, the cause of action accrued., under the circumstances of this case, at the dates when the cheques were received and dealt with by the appellants"

statement: A mortgagee is not required to give notice under section 643 of the Civil Procedure Code if the claimant does not have a valid registrable document.
supporting_quote: It is only a grantee, lessee, mortgagee, or other incumbrancer who claims an interest in land sought to be affected by an action under chapter XLVI. of the Civil Procedure Code on a valid registrable document who is entitled to the notice of action provided for by section 643 of the Code.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 643 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A sale of mortgaged property under section 201 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be set aside for want of title in the mortgagor by summary application to Court.
supporting_quote: "Section 344 of the Civil Procedure Code, which has been invoked, no doubt provides that all questions relating to the execution of the decree should be determined by the Court executing the decree; but I think these questions have regard only to procedure and the conduct of the parties concerned or of the officers entrusted with the duty of carrying out the seizure and sale. In my opinion such a question as the title of the execution-debtor to the property sold is outside the scope of section 344."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 201, 284, and 344

statement: A judgment entered against a minor, though unrepresented by a guardian, is at most an irregularity and not open to a collateral attack.
supporting_quote: a judgment entered against a minor, though unrepresented by a guardian, was at most an irregularity, and that it would stand as a valid adjudication until reversed, and was not open to a collateral attack.

statement: A mortgagee who fails to provide an address for service under section 644 of the Civil Procedure Code and obtains a hypothecary decree against the mortgagor cannot subsequently bring another action against a subsequent grantees or incumbrancers claiming a declaration that the property is chargeable with the mortgage debt.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that the view taken by Lascelles C.J. in Ramanathan Chetty v. Cassim 2 as to the intention of the Legislature in enacting chapter XLVI. of the Code is the correct view. The action under chapter XLVI. was intended to provide one action only 'to realize moneys due or secured upon mortgage,' and to do away with the multiplicity of suits."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 644 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The Court has a discretion to refuse discovery of documents where it can see that no good is reasonably to be expected from ordering it, and whether any good is to be expected can be ascertained by looking at the pleadings.
supporting_quote: "It would appear that the order made on February 5,1920, regarding the filing of an affidavit was made in error, because the motion has endorsement by plaintiff's proctor of receipt of notice for 11th instant (i.e., for to-day). I would, therefore, vacate the order of February 5, 1920, and I would refuse to order affidavit as applied for. Costs of this inquiry to be borne by applicant (defendant)."

statement: An interlocutory appeal does not ipso facto stay proceedings in the action pending the determination of the appeal.
supporting_quote: "On the contrary, to judge from the provisions of chapter LIX. regarding the somewhat analogous case of an appeal from a decree, it would appear that the Code does not contemplate an appeal acting as a stay of proceedings, and, in my opinion, there is no stay of proceedings on an interlocutory appeal, unless an application is made for the purpose and acceded to."

statement: The discretion to issue a commission for the examination of witnesses abroad lies with the Judge, but this decision can be reviewed by the Supreme Court. In deciding whether to issue such a commission, the Judge must weigh the circumstances and determine what is in the interests of justice.
supporting_quote: "It is also in the power of the Supreme Court to review that discretion, and among the cases cited are cases where that discretion has been reviewed."

statement: A partnership in the opium business is illegal when an unlicensed person claims to have been a partner and has actively engaged in furthering its interests.
supporting_quote: "Section 6 of the Opium Ordinance of 1899 (No. 5 of 1899) is sufficient to stamp with illegality and render unenforceable rights arising under a partnership in the opium business, when an unlicensed person claiming, as the appellant does here and under document P 1, to' have been a partner has been engaged as such in furthering its interests"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of the Opium Ordinance of 1899 (No. 5 of 1899)

statement: The sum of Rs. 100 per leaguer mentioned in the deed is a penalty, not liquidated damages.
supporting_quote: Now, applying those principles to the present facts, what is the position? We have to ask ourselves, firstly, Do the circumstances show that the parties intended Rs. 100 as a pre-estimate of the damage, or must it, on the contrary, be regarded as a penalty in terrorem; and secondly, to assist us to determine that question, we have to ask ourselves, Is there an extravagant disproportion between the agreed sum and the amount of damage capable of pre-estimate? In my opinion this sum is a penalty, and not liquidated damages.

statement: A person who is put to his election must have clear proof that he was acquainted with his rights and the necessity of making an election, and he must unequivocally make his election.
supporting_quote: "In order that a person who is put to his election should be concluded by it, two things are necessary. First, a full knowledge of the inconsistent rights and of the necessity of electing between them. Second, an intention to elect manifested either expressly or by acts which imply choice and acquiescence."

statement: Only an administrator de bonis non of the estate of A himself can bring an action on a contract between A and B, even if B is the executor under A's will.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff as administrator of B's estate could not sue on the agreement, and that only an administrator de bonis non of the estate of A himself could bring the action."

statement: A party who is present at a Fiscal's sale but fails to notify their title to the purchaser may be estopped from denying the plaintiff's title if there are circumstances that would have put the purchaser on notice of the potential defect in title.
supporting_quote: "The first defendant, though present at the Fiscal's sale, did not intimate to the purchaser that he was entitled to this land. As to why the first defendant failed to do so, it is not necessary to record any finding. But evidently the first defendant did not wish to disclose the deed in his favour by the second defendant, who was the judgment-debtor."

statement: The interest given to each son was the subject of a separate fidei commissum, and each son had the power to dispose of his interest subject to any right that might accrue to any child upon the birth of such child.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, therefore, the interest given to each son was the subject of a separate fidei commissum, and each son had the power to dispose of his interest subject to any right that might accrue to any child upon the birth of such child."

statement: An executor's remuneration should be a rate rather than a lump sum, and it should bear some relation to the magnitude of the estate.
supporting_quote: "I think it is quite reasonable that the executor's remuneration should bear some relation to the magnitude of the estate. That, I think, was the intention of the Legislature, and it is quite reasonable that, where the estate is a large one, the executor should be remunerated more fully than in the case of a small estate, even though the work involved may be much the same in the two cases."

statement: A shareholder's liability to contribute towards a company’s assets during winding-up proceedings is a statutory obligation, distinct from their previous liability as shareholders, and can be recovered even if the original calls for payment were time-barred.
supporting_quote: "The ordinary liability of a shareholder to contribute his share of capital arises under the articles, but on a winding up it is converted into a statutory liability under section 63. of the Indian Companies Act, 1882. The amount of contribution ordered by the Court can be re-covered, though the claim on the basis of sails originally made by the directors may have been barred by limitation before the winding up."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 61 of the Indian Companies Act, 1882, which corresponds to section 88 of the English Companies Act of 1862 and to section 128 of the Companies (Consolidation) Act, 1908.

statement: A partition decree made by a Court of Requests with reference to immovable property exceeding Rs. 300 in value is not binding on a person claiming an interest in the property who was not a party to the action.
supporting_quote: "It may be taken therefore that, in view of the limitation of the Courts of Requests jurisdiction with respect to value, the decree in a partition action made by a Court of Requests affecting immovable property exceeding Rs. 300 in value is of no legal force."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 44 of the Evidence Ordinance, No. 14 of 1895; Section 2 of the Partition Ordinance, No. 10 of 1863.

statement: The question whether an actual partition or a sale should be ordered should be gone into and determined by the Court as part of the proceedings preliminary to the interlocutory decree, which should, when entered, definitely order a partition or a sale, as the case may be.
supporting_quote: As the necessity for such applications frequently arises under similar circumstances, it may be convenient to settle the practice which should be followed in partition cases. In my opinion the question whether an actual partition or a sale should be ordered should be gone into and determined by the Court as part of the proceedings preliminary to the interlocutory decree, which should, when entered, definitely order a partition or a sale, as the case may be.

statement: A promise made to settle a dispute can be enforceable even if the underlying claim is not legally enforceable, provided it was made in good faith and after negotiation.
supporting_quote: The validity of the claim, or the ultimate success of a suit brought to enforce it, is entirely beside the point. On those facts the plaintiffs were, in their Lordships' opinion, entitled to succeed in the present action.

statement: In a contract for specific performance, there must be consideration and mutuality. The agreement in question lacks both.
supporting_quote: "It is not alleged that this sum was rendered to plaintiff, but he alleges that, as the income of the leasehold interests exceeded that sum, the defendant was bound, in terms of the agreement, to make a conveyance of half his interests. But it is essential in a contract such as this that plaintiff must show some real, substantial consideration proceeding from himself, and that consideration must be ascertained at the time of the execution of contract."

statement: Under the Tesawalamai, an action for pre-emption does not extend to the purchase of a water right alone without offering to buy the adjoining land, as it would be highly inconvenient.
supporting_quote: "I cannot hold, in the absence of proof, that the right of pre-emption extends further than convenience allows, and the extinction of a water right might be highly inconvenient."

statement: The value of the subject-matter of a possessory action for the purpose of jurisdiction when the suit is brought by a lessee is not the value of the unexpired term of the lease, but the value of the land itself.
supporting_quote: "The value of the subject-matter of a possessory action for the purpose of jurisdiction when the suit is brought by a lessee is not the value of the unexpired term of the lease, but the value of the land itself."

statement: A broker to entitle himself to a commission in a negotiation that has fallen through must either prove direct default on the part of the vendor or a binding agreement by the vendee to buy the property.
supporting_quote: "A broker to entitle himself to a commission in a negotiation that has fallen through must either prove &direct default on the part of the vendor or a binding agreement by the vendee to buy the property."

statement: The right to an incumbency is still a legal right, and not purely an ecclesiastical matter.
supporting_quote: "it would seem that the presiding priest or incumbent has the control and administration of the Vihare itself, although the property vests in the trustee, and, therefore, the right to an incumbency is still a legal right, and not purely an ecclesiastical matter."

statement: Prescriptive title cannot be proved against the Crown for chenas situated within the Kandyan Provinces under section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840.
supporting_quote: "I have given reasons for thinking it cannot."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 6 of the Ordinance No. 12 of 1840

statement: A purchaser in execution cannot successfully rely on section 344 of the Civil Procedure Code to set aside a sale if there is no proof of fraud or misrepresentation.
supporting_quote: "The matter, therefore, really turns on the question of fact, which I have indicated. In my opinion the materials in the case do not amount to proof of fraud."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 344 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: An action quia timet is not maintainable where the plaintiff has an immediate remedy in an action for partition.
supporting_quote: But, in the present case, it would seem that the plaintiff has an immediate remedy in an action for partition.

statement: A mortgagee who has not registered an address for service and has failed to make a subsequent grantees or puisne incumbrancer a party in the action cannot bind such parties through a decree, unless there is evidence of their knowledge and acquiescence.
supporting_quote: "The facts that the plaintiff knew of the pendency of the mortgage action but took no steps, and that he bid at the auction sale, were held not sufficient in the circumstances of this case to constitute an estoppel."

statement: A purchaser at an execution sale is not bound by the order on a claim inquiry, even if considered in the same position as the execution debtors.
supporting_quote: "Even if the defendant is considered in the same position as the execution-debtors, it is quite clear that the execution-debtors were not bound by the order on the claim, although, according to the practice of our Courts, execution-debtors are noticed as regards the inquiry into any claim."

statement: In a will contest, the party seeking probate has the burden to prove that the will was executed without suspicion of fraud. If suspicions arise, those suspicions must be addressed and removed by the party propounding the will.
supporting_quote: "All that we need ask, therefore, with regard to the evidence of the alleged substitution, is this : Is there a reasonable suspicion that that substitution took place, and if so, have the propounders by the evidence which we took in the Supreme Court removed that suspicion ?"

statement: A co-owner has the right to build and live on common land, and can eject another co-owner who attempts to occupy a house built for private use without permission.
supporting_quote: "If a co-owner exercises his right and builds a house for his private use on the land, he may eject any other co-owner who attempts to occupy that house without his permission."

statement: A co-owner who mines on common land is entitled to keep the minerals mined, even if they are in actual possession of them and the property in the mines belongs to others.
supporting_quote: "Indeed this act of possession appears to me to be lawful even as regards the Crown, because the Crown has waived its right to mines and minerals in the case of lands alienated before 1901."

statement: An improving co-owner is entitled to compensation on the same principles as those applicable to a bona fide possessor, and the fruits of the improvement itself cannot be set off in calculating the amount of compensation.
supporting_quote: "Moreover, this Court has laid down that an improving co-owner is entitled to compensation on the same principles as those applicable to a bona fide possessor, and it is well known that the fruits of the improvement itself cannot be set off in calculating the amount of compensation."

statement: A cheque tendered and accepted as part payment satisfies the Sale of Goods Ordinance, even if subsequently dishonored.
supporting_quote: "I doubt whether that is right. A man might receive a cheque and might write to the sender: ' I have received your cheque, but I have changed my mind, and I am not going to fulfil my contract.' That would not be an unqualified acceptance of the cheque, but it cannot be disputed that there would have been a part payment to satisfy the section. "

statement: A notary's failure to have a deed executed in duplicate does not affect its operation as a deed.
supporting_quote: "The fact is that Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, like its predecessor Ordinance No. 7 of 1834, apart from the main purpose of requiring written instruments for certain classes of transactions, contained many provisions concerning the duties of notaries, which have since been embodied in separate Ordinances specially relating to notaries. In this connection it is instructive to note the whole of section 15, part of which I have above cited. It is as follows: 'And it is further enacted that every deed or other instrument, except any will, testament, or codicil required by this Ordinance to be executed or acknowledged before or to be attested by a notary, shall be executed, acknowledged, or attested in duplicate, and every such notary shall at the end of each month transmit the duplicates of all deeds or other instruments executed or acknowledged before or attested by him during the month to the Court of the district wherein he shall have been licensed to practise, with a list in duplicate of such deeds of instruments.'"

statement: A proctor's lien is not destroyed by his death, but may be enforced by his legal representative.
supporting_quote: "A proctor's lien is not destroyed by bis death, but may be enforced by his legal representative."

statement: A trustee cannot prescribe against a cestui que trust.
supporting_quote: "It is a well-established principle that a trustee cannot prescribe against a cestui que trust"

statement: The court found that the plaintiffs retained their private property rights over the road and did not dedicate it to public use.
supporting_quote: It is clear from the description and extent given in these two series of deeds, from the year 1862 to the year 1916, that the owners for the time being considered the present road as part of their land, and dealt with it on that footing. So far as these deeds go, the supposed dedication of the road to the public is negatived, and, on the contrary, they disclose an intention to keep the whole land to themselves.

statement: A gift made with the condition that it takes effect after the donor's death is considered a donation inter vivos, not mortis causa.
supporting_quote: "A gifted a property to B 'as a gift that cannot be revoked at any time for any reason whatever, which' is to be owned by him after my death.' Held, that was not a donation mortis causa, but a donation inter vivos"

statement: The proper party to be sued for encroachment on a road reservation is the Local Board, not the Crown.
supporting_quote: "I, therefore, think that the plaintiff has not made out a case for compensation to be paid to him by the defendant corporation, nor for compelling the defendant corporation to convey any portion of the land in dispute to him. The defendant corporation can only deal with a road according to the provisions of the Road Ordinance or the Local Boards Ordinance, 1898."

statement: A bona fide purchaser for value cannot assert the principle that title passes by operation of law against such a purchaser.
supporting_quote: "This principle cannot be asserted against a bona fide purchaser for value. (This question was reserved by Bertram C.J.)"

statement: A will creates a valid fidei commissum in favor of successive generations of the testator's children, grandchildren, and remoter descendants.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the will creates a valid fidei commissum in favour of the children, grandchildren, and remoter decendants of the devisees"

statement: The subsequent acquisition of title by the vendor does not enure to the benefit of the purchaser in a sale where the vendor had no title at the time of the sale.
supporting_quote: The fact that the vendor in this case described the title he conveyed, in 1906 as by inheritance and possession and his subsequent title as by purchase makes no difference in the operation of the deed to convey title.

statement: A person acting on the orders of another may not generally be free from liability for breach of the rule, but in this case, the accused showed sufficient grounds for exemption due to their bona fide belief that they were felling timber on their master's property.
supporting_quote: "The same remark applies to Slema Lebbe, the third accused. At all events, any bona fide claim of title on the part of Mohamadu Usoof ought to benefit them."

statement: For a marriage to be valid under the Kandyan Marriage Ordinance, it must have been contracted according to the laws, institutions, and customs in force in Kandy before the date of the Ordinance No. 13 of 1859.
supporting_quote: "This section, however, requires that the marriage should have been 'according to the laws, institutions, and customs in force in Kandy' before the date of the Ordinance No. 13 of 1859."

statement: A lessee under an informal lease is to be treated as a lessee for a period not exceeding one month and cannot be ejected until the contract of monthly tenancy is terminated by due notice.
supporting_quote: "This being so, the defendant cannot be treated as a trespasser until the contract of the monthly tenancy is terminated by due notice, that is, by a month's notice in terms of the law."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840

statement: The burden of proving that a person is not practicing medicine for gain, as defined by the Medical Registration Ordinance, section 20, lies with the accused.
supporting_quote: "It is clear from section 105 of the Evidence Ordinance, No. 14 of 1895, that it is for the accused to prove the existence of any circumstance on which they rely to bring themselves within the benefit of section 20."
statute_citation_verbatim: Evidence Ordinance, section 105.

statement: A usufructuary mortgagee is not entitled to a share of the proceeds from mining activities unless such rights are expressly stipulated in the mortgage bond.
supporting_quote: I do not think the law allows a lessee or usufructuary mortgagee the right to dig for minerals or share in the proceeds, unless it is expressly so stipulated in the lease or mortgage bond.

statement: The usufructuary has the right to exploit the property for minerals and is obligated to secure a share of the proceeds to the minor.
supporting_quote: "This is clear enough, and the amount agreed upon as the ground share, which was presumably considered reasonable by the plaintiff, and is usual, must be regarded as the 'pretium deductis impensis'. For it is certain that the mineral could not have been extracted by the defendant or in her name on any other terms. Neither she nor the minor were capable of working the mine on any other terms and gain a larger share of the profit. And the usufructuary has a perfect right to exploit the property in this way. She is, therefore, bound to secure to the minor the half share of the principal sum or price."

statement: A surety who acquiesces in the sale of mortgaged lands is not discharged from his obligation on the bond.
supporting_quote: In a local case reported at page 193 of Morgan's Digest, it has been laid down that a surety who after notice does not object to the sale of the mortgaged lands is not thereby discharged. In the present case, not only did the third defendant not object, but his conduct was such that it must be presumed that he really consented to the sales of the lands.

statement: The reservation does not change the status of possession, as the donors possessed as owners and not under the donee.
supporting_quote: "The character of the donor's possession did not change. They possessed as owners and not under the donee."

statement: Dowry or kaikuli is held in trust by a husband for the wife and cannot be withheld on the ground that it has been spent for the sustenance of the marriage.
supporting_quote: "Dowry or kaikuli is held in trust by a husband for the wife, and cannot be withheld on the ground that it has been spent for the sustenance of the marriage."

statement: Lands subject to service tenures cannot be sold or partitioned under the provisions of the Partition Ordinance, unless it may be in cases where the proprietor of the nindagama and the paraveni nilakaraya are all consenting parties to the proceedings.
supporting_quote: It has been held by this Court in several cases that the paraveni nilakarayas of a panguwa of a nindagama cannot maintain an action for the partition of the lands in the panguwa. These cases were considered, and had their culmination in the Full Bench decision in the case of Appuhamy v. Menike.2 [ 2 (1917) 19 N. L. R. 361. ] The reasons for the decision appear to be two; one, that the right of a paraveni nilakaraya falls short of the ownership required by the Partition Ordinance; and, next, that the services are indivisible.

statement: Respondents were entitled to intervene and establish a trust in an action for partition.
supporting_quote: Held, that the respondents were entitled to establish the trust in this action.

statement: A partner's share in a partnership is not governed by the formalities relevant to the transfer of goods, but rather is more akin to a chose in action that does not require a written assignment.
supporting_quote: "what is meant by the share of a partner is his proportion of the partnership assets after they have been all realized and converted into money, and all the partnership debts and liabilities have been paid and discharged, " so that a partner is not the owner in the ordinary sense of a share in the individual assets and an assignment by him of his share is not governed by the formalities relevant to the transfer of goods.

statement: Where people have been in possession of land for a considerable length of time, it may be presumed that the original permissive possession has changed to adverse possession.
supporting_quote: "It does seem to me that this is a case in which that presumption ought justly to be drawn. Here is a family which for sixty years have been in possession, quite possibly, as the District Judge suggests, originating by permission. It does not seem to me just that they should be disturbed through a stranger, for purposes of his own, buying in an outstanding paper title."

statement: To impeach a will on the ground of undue influence, it must be proved that the influence exercised amounted to coercion, i.e., compelled the testator to do something he did not want to do.
supporting_quote: "To impeach a will on the ground of undue influence, it must be proved . that the influence exercised amounted to coercion, i.e., compelled the testator to do something he did not want to do."

statement: An assignee of a bond can recover the full amount of an assigned instrument though it be more than he paid for the assignment, except perhaps where the assignment is in the nature of a speculative or litigious transaction.
supporting_quote: The assignee of a bond can recover the full amount of an assigned instrument though it be more than he paid for the assignment, except, perhaps where the assignment is in the nature of a speculative or litigious transaction.

statement: The term 'assurance' includes a conveyance and cannot be restricted to a hypothecation.
supporting_quote: I think he is mistaken in his interpretation, for the word 'assurance' has been held to mean something which operates as a transfer of property ( re Ray 1 [ 1 65 L. J. 1 Ch. 320. ] ), and it has also been held that a document of title can properly be called an 'assurance' ( re Roberts Evans v. Thomas 2 [ 2 57 L. T. 79. ] ).

statement: Where there have been mutual dealings between parties and a balance has been struck by consent between them, the plaintiff is entitled to sue on an account stated, and this notwithstanding the absence of any written acknowledgment of the debt on the part of the defendant.
supporting_quote: "Where there have been mutual dealings between parties and a balance has been struck by consent between them, the plaintiff is entitled to sue on an account stated, and this notwithstanding the absence of any written acknowledgment of the debt on the part of the defendant."

statement: There is no preference among heirs, partners or co-owners, and adjacent landowners who have a right of mortgage in the Tesawalamai.
supporting_quote: "There is no preference among these classes; they are all equally entitled. Nor is there anything in the Tesawalamai to support the notion that a person coming under any two of the classes has a right of pre-emption preferential to a person who comes under one class only."

statement: A purchaser who knew that the vendor had a disputed title and bought the land on speculation is not entitled to recover any more than the price actually paid; he is not entitled to recover damages.
supporting_quote: "For when one knowingly and deliberately buys what does not belong to the seller, he is not to be presumed to have meant to make a gift of the price, but rather to have entertained the hope of acquiring the ownership when the Vendor should acquire it." (Berwick's translation 540.)

statement: In the absence of an appeal by the lessee against a judgment in an ejectment action, it does not bar his subsequent claim for damages against his lessors for failure to warrant and defend.
supporting_quote: "Held , that in the circumstances the fact that plaintiff had not appealed in case No. 16,109 was not a bar to his present claim."

statement: Where a suit is pending, a reference to arbitration can only be made by the Court itself in that suit.
supporting_quote: "This does not imply that the award is wholly useless, and effect may not be given to it in some other way. The award appears to be binding on the parties as regards the method of distribution of the estate in the testamentary suit and other matters connected therewith"

statement: It is to the party at whose instance a sale takes place that the purchaser must look for repayment, not only of the purchase money, but of the expenses and charges if the sale becomes abortive.
supporting_quote: "It is to the party at whose instance a sale takes place that the purchaser must look for repayment, not only of the purchase money, but of the expenses and charges if the sale becomes abortive."

statement: The burden of proof of undue influence lies on those who allege it, and the propounders are not required to produce specific witnesses or evidence as long as their evidence is sufficient to remove suspicion.
supporting_quote: "It would have been no doubt more satisfactory if the petitioner himself had given evidence of the condition of the testator and of the circumstances under which the will was prepared, and also if the two doctors, who have been the regular medical attendants of the testator during recent years, had been called, but there is no rule of law to the effect that a person propounding a will to which suspicion attached should himself give evidence, or should produce any particular witnesses or class of evidence so long as the evidence is sufficient to remove the suspicion attaching to it."

statement: A person may prescribe by virtue of intermittent cultivation appropriate to chenas, and the plaintiff can rely on section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 2 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "Nor do I think that what he says is weakened by a subsequent expression in his judgment, where he says : 'Even if we assume that the evidence is true.' Accepting this evidence, we, then, must ask ourselves what is the effect of it. The learned Judge thinks that there is good reason to believe that the land was originally chena, and that if the Crown were to intervene and claim this land, there would be no answer to the claim of the Crown, inasmuch as there is no prescription against the Crown in the Kandyan Provinces. That may very well be. But the Crown is not a party in this case. We are trying a claim by one individual against another. The plaintiff, as plaintiff, is entitled to rely upon the second part of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 2 of 1871."
statute_citation_verbatim: "the second part of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 2 of 1871"

statement: An express trust can only arise between the cestui que trust and his trustee. A constructive trust is one which arises when a stranger to a trust already constituted is held by the Court to be bound in good faith and in conscience by the trust in consequence of his conduct and behaviour.
supporting_quote: An express trust can only arise between the cestui que trust and his trustee. A constructive trust is one which arises when a stranger to a trust already constituted is held by the Court to be bound in good faith and in conscience by the trust in consequence of his conduct and behaviour.

statement: When a sale is made under one of several writs, the proceeds should be distributed according to the priority of the mortgages involved.
supporting_quote: As a matter of fact, the Fiscal purported to sell, and did sell, the three-fourths share of all the defendants under the writ issued by the plaintiff only; that is to say, he sold the shares of the first, second, sixth, and seventh defendants as primary mortgagors, and the share of the fourth defendant as secondary mortgagor. This must be taken to be the only sale which took place.

statement: A purchaser who defaults in payment of the balance of purchase money and subsequently applies to set aside a sale under section 284 of the Civil Procedure Code is not entitled to return of the deposit forfeited under section 262.
supporting_quote: I regret that I do not see that the Court can afford her any relief. Section 284 only allows her to apply to set aside a sale. But by her own default under section 262 the sale seems to me to have been set aside already. There is, consequently, no sale in existence to set aside.

statement: A person interested in the property, even if not a holder of a decree from the same court, can apply to set aside an execution sale under section 282 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "The respondent had himself seized the property in execution, and, if the sale under the plaintiff's writ were irregular and liable to be set aside, he would be entitled to bring the property to sale under his own writ. Moreover, if the sale under the plaintiff's writ had not been irregular and the property had realized its proper value, a larger balance of proceeds, after payment in full of the plaintiff's decree, would be available for satisfaction of the respondent's claim."

statement: To establish an estoppel, the action taken by the party seeking to establish the estoppel must be directly connected with the false impression caused by the representation or conduct of the party sought to be estopped.
supporting_quote: "To establish an estoppel, it must be proved that the action taken by the party seeking to establish the estoppel was directly connected with the false impression caused by the representation or conduct of the party sought to be estopped."

statement: For the purposes of section 338 of the Civil Procedure Code, 'estate below the value of Rs. 1,000' means a net estate after the deduction of secured debts.
supporting_quote: "I think that the expression 'estate below the value of Rs. 1,000' in section 338 of the Civil Procedure Code has the same meaning as in the Stamp Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 338 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The Court has no discretion to add a party after judgment under Section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Section 18 contemplates the adding of parties before judgment. It allows the plaintiff or defendant to apply on or before the hearing 'to add a party'; but it says that the Court may 'at any time' order any party to be added. This means before final judgment."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: The plaintiff's Fiscal's transfer is prior in date as well as registration, and his title should prevail over that of the defendant.
supporting_quote: "I think his title should prevail over that of the defendant."

statement: Copies of an order nisi for service on respondents must be stamped and in the English language, not translated.
supporting_quote: "Every copy of an order nisi for service on respondents must be stamped, and must be in the English language."

statement: The court should not order the disclosure of profits before determining liability.
supporting_quote: "The Court is always unwilling, before the right to relief is established, to make an order for discovery which may be injurious to the defendant, and will only be useful to the plaintiff if he succeeds in establishing his title to relief."

statement: Under the Partition Ordinance, any improvement must be valued according to the expenditure in respect of the improvement, or even less, if the improvement is less in value.
supporting_quote: "It is well understood that, even under the Partition Ordinance, any improvement must be valued according to the expenditure in respect of the improvement, or even less, if the improvement is less in value."

statement: An agreement for the use of a paddy field with a promise to deliver a certain quantity of paddy or its value is not maintainable in the absence of a notarially executed agreement.
supporting_quote: "It is quite clear that in this case the consideration was not a share of the crop, but a certain quantity of paddy or its value independently of what the crop might be. This case is entirely within the ratio decidendi of the case of De Silva v. Thelenis."

statement: An agreement to share profits from a business venture involving the sale of toddy without proper government authorization is void in law.
supporting_quote: "Thus, it is perfectly clear that the defendant and the plaintiff attempted to enjoy the privileges conferred on the licensees without the consent of the proper authority, and entered into this agreement in respect of them."

statement: The first defendant's conduct, by accepting a mortgage bond from his brother in 1910 that the latter was entitled to a share of all plantations, estops him from disputing the plaintiff’s right to one-third of both soil and plantations.
supporting_quote: "It is a principle of natural equity that when A allows another to hold himself out as the owner of A's property and a third person purchases it for value from the apparent owner in the belief that he is the real owner, A shall not be permitted to recover, unless he can prove that the purchaser had direct notice of the real title, or that there existed circumstances which ought to have put him on inquiry which, if pursued, would have led to a discovery of it."

statement: The market rate for paddy should be used to determine damages when the defendant fails to deliver the stipulated amount of paddy.
supporting_quote: "Under the decree the defendant may, if he does not wish to pay in cash, discharge his obligation by delivering the paddy in kind, and I do not think he is entitled to any further relief so far as the stipulations in the deed are concerned."

statement: A document executed by a person, even if somewhat in the nature of a deed, can be given effect as a testamentary disposition where it is clear that the testator intended it to take effect after their death.
supporting_quote: "Where a document executed by a person was somewhat in the nature of a deed, but where it was clear that he intended that it should take effect as a testamentary disposition, the Court gave effect to the document as a last will."

statement: An authority to execute an instrument, which under the law must be notarially executed, can be given orally.
supporting_quote: "As to the facts, it appears that the plaintiff some years ago received from her late husband a transfer of the property in dispute. Before she had received that transfer she had given her husband a power of attorney authorizing him to transact business in her name, the object being that as she was a Muhammadan woman she need not be troubled to subject herself to the publicity which the execution of notarial documents involves."

statement: A conveyance made pendente lite is ineffectual as against a mortgagee who has obtained judgment, even if the original mortgage purported to deal with land that had ceased to exist.
supporting_quote: "Therefore, there is no question that this conveyance was a conveyance pendente lite, and ineffectual as against the second defendant."

statement: A fluctuating and uncertain body of people, such as the inhabitants of a district or a section of the inhabitants of a district, cannot by prescription acquire a right of fishery against any individual member of the community. Still less could such a fluctuating and uncertain body acquire a prescriptive right against the public itself.
supporting_quote: A fluctuating and uncertain body of people, such as the inhabitants of a district or a section of the inhabitants of a district, cannot by prescription acquire a right of fishery against any individual member of the community. (See the judgment of Lord Selborne L.C. in Neill v. Duke of Devonshire. 1 [(1882) 8 A. C. 154.]) Still less could such a fluctuating and uncertain body acquire a prescriptive right against the public itself.

statement: The plaintiff's action to recover a motor car or its value from the person in possession is valid, even if that person purchased it fraudulently.
supporting_quote: "This is the nature of the present action, and I think the learned District Judge has rightly decided it."

statement: A fiduciary is not entitled to receive back the sum paid by him in a sale of property subject to fidei commissum, and a sale should be ordered if it is reasonable from the point of view of the fiduciary and there is no prospect of loss to the fidei commissary.
supporting_quote: I do not think that he is entitled in the case of the sale to receive back any part of the purchase price, because the money which he contributed to the purchase of the present property has now become subject to the fidei ammiesum. The Judge has refused to make the order on the ground that the property may go up in price when the 335 fidei commissaries came in for their rights, but that may be said with regard to any trust property for which authority for sale is desired.

statement: Decrees in waste lands cases do not necessarily wipe out titles of vendees who transferred their rights prior to the decree.
supporting_quote: "In reality the decree in favour of the claimants in the waste lands case must be held to enure to the benefit of those to whom they transferred their rights previously."

statement: A will clause prohibiting voluntary alienation of property does not prevent a forced sale, such as one by the Fiscal in execution.
supporting_quote: "But a forced sale, like a sale by the Fiscal in execution, is not affected by the provision in question."

statement: The surviving fiduciary is not a necessary party to an action for declaration of title and possession where the agreement was entered into with the predecessor in title, and the claimant does not derive title through any of the parties to that agreement.
supporting_quote: "The learned Judge has declared the plaintiffs entitled to a half share in the property and to possession of the half share."

statement: A deed of conveyance that prohibits the sale or mortgage to outsiders but does not clearly designate beneficiaries does not create a fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: "The document, it is to be observed, is not a sale, but a conveyance, and whether by way of gift or on sale it is impossible to say. It must, therefore, be read strictly, and the Roman-Dutch rule of law in connection with such claims is that there is no fidei commissum, unless the persons to be benefited are clearly designated."

statement: A judgment-debtor's right of indemnity against a third party does not entitle a judgment-creditor to sell the property of that third party under a judgment against his debtor.
supporting_quote: The fact that a judgment-debtor has a right of indemnity against a third party does not entitle a judgment-creditor to sell the property of that third party under a judgment against his debtor.

statement: A notary's authority to practice is tied to the judicial district specified in their warrant, and any changes to that district must be addressed through a new application or amendment.
supporting_quote: "If a notary in the situation of the appellant wishes to preserve the area of his original practice, it seems to me that his proper course is to apply to the Governor under section 11 of the Ordinance to 'change the area specified in his warrant, and to grant him a new warrant.'"

statement: The Court should exercise great care when ordering substituted service under the Partition Ordinance, especially in partition actions involving multiple owners.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, in view of the serious consequences of a partition decree, the Court ought to exercise very great care with reference to the alternatives prescribed by this section."

statement: A trust, express or constructive, will not be extinguished by a decree for partition and will attach to the divided portion which on the partition may be assigned to the trustee.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion trusts of all description attaching to property partitioned remain attached to the lot awarded in severalty to the trustee"

statement: A vendor has the right to intervene in a partition action for the purpose of warranting and defending the title he has conveyed.
supporting_quote: "In practice a vendor of any of the parties to an action is allowed to intervene in a partition action for the purpose of warranting and defending the title he has conveyed. There is nothing I can see against the practice."

statement: The cause of action for the return of money entrusted for safekeeping arises from the date of refusal to return after demand, not from the date of deposit.
supporting_quote: "The period of prescription is to be reckoned, according to the Ordinance, from the date the cause of action arises on a deposit. The cause of action would be the refusal to return that deposit. That refusal could only arise when a demand has been made."

statement: Identity of name is not essential for registration under the Land Registration Ordinance.
