supporting_quote: "I quite understand the inconvenience that persons interested may experience when they wish to search the register with a view to finding out previous transactions unless the same name is carried forward, but the point is whether under the Ordinance identity of name is an essential detail. As far as I know, there is no case in which the contention on the defendant's behalf was upheld, and on principle I do not think the contention is sound."

statement: The servitude, which had become extinct by merger, did not revive on the subsequent separation of the two lands.
supporting_quote: Held , that the servitude (right of way), which had become extinct by merger, did not revive on the subsequent separation of the two lands.

statement: Property acquired before marriage, such as money saved out of earnings, belongs to the husband or wife for their separate estate and is not considered part of the diathetam even if invested during marriage.
supporting_quote: "I think, therefore, that the money which the husband had saved out of his earnings before his marriage belonged to him for his separate estate, whether it is strictly called mudusom or not. The circumstance that it was invested during marriage does not change its character."

statement: Under the Tesawalamai, property inherited by a daughter from her mother (who had dowry property) would devolve on the mother's nearest relatives, which in this case were the children of Theivanipillai's sisters.
supporting_quote: "Thus, the plaintiff became entitled to one-sixth share. The question was fully argued on both sides, and a mass of authorities has been cited, but the only case in point is the one I have just referred to."

statement: The acceptance of security tendered by an appellant under section 756 of the Civil Procedure Code is a judicial act and should be evidenced by an order of Court.
supporting_quote: The acceptance of security tendered by an appellant under section 756 of the Civil Procedure Code is a judicial act and should be evidenced by an order of Court.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 756 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: Good faith by a contractor is essential to support a claim for payment for the work actually done under a contract which has not been fully executed.
supporting_quote: The case of Hauman v. Nortie [ S. A. R. App. Div. 293 ] indicates that good faith by a contractor is essential to support a claim for payment for the work actually done under a contract which has not been fully executed.

statement: A Buddhist priest cannot be ejected from a Buddhist vihara except for some personal cause, irrespective of the rights of property.
supporting_quote: "A Buddhist priest cannot be ejected from a Buddhist vihare except for some personal cause, irrespective of the rights of property."

statement: The succession to the incumbency of a temple is governed by the rule of pupillary succession, not by particular appointment by specific families on each occasion of a vacancy.
supporting_quote: "In view of these circumstances, I think the finding of the District Judge that the succession to, the incumbency was according to the rule of pupillary succession, and not by particular appointment by these families on each occasion of a vacancy, is reasonable."

statement: Choses in action vest successively in successive trustees for the time being under the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, 1905.
supporting_quote: "I think there can be no doubt that it was the intention of the Ordinance that choses in action should vest successively in the trustee for the time being holding office under the Ordinance in the same manner as other trust property."

statement: Where a claimant fails to appear and adduce evidence on the day fixed for inquiry, an order dismissing the claim is equivalent to an order after investigation under section 245 of the Civil Procedure Code and is conclusive against the claimant unless they bring an action under section 247.
supporting_quote: "In view of the circumstances, in which the order dismissing the plaintiff's vendor Ibrahim Saibo's claim in action D. C. Batticaloa, 4,391, was made, I think the order concluded Ibrahim Saibo and necessarily also the plaintiff. I would dismiss the appeal, with costs."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 245 of our Code

statement: When the time for the performance of an obligation is fixed, the breach may well be considered as occurring when the performance does not take place within the time so fixed. However, if there is no fixed date but only an obligation to do any act within a reasonable interval after a given date, there cannot be said to be a breach unless there has been a refusal either on demand or otherwise to perform the obligation, or unless the person liable has in some way disabled himself from performing the contract.
supporting_quote: When the time for the performance of an obligation is fixed so that there can be a definite starting point for the running of the period of prescription, the breach may well, in ordinary circumstances, be considered as occurring when the performance does not take place within the time so fixed. But when there is no fixed date for the performance, but there is only an obligation to do any act within a reasonable interval after a given date, there cannot be said to be a breach, unless there has been a refusal either on demand or otherwise to perform the obligation, or unless the person liable has in some way disabled himself from performing the contract.

statement: No appeal lies from a decree for cancellation and refund of money paid in an action for damage or demand, except upon a point of law or with the leave of Court.
supporting_quote: "Held, that no appeal lay, except upon a point of law or with the leave of Court."

statement: The Court has a discretion to include additional land in a partition suit, but it requires a very strong case to do so, especially when the added defendants are not co-owners and merely seek protection of their equitable interests.
supporting_quote: "It is a still stronger proceeding where the persons asking for such an enlargement are not co-owners, but simply persons admitted for the protection of their equitable interests. I do not say that, even under these circumstances, the Court might not give effect to the prayer of such persons in appropriate cases. Certainly the Court would have a discretion in the matter, but it would require a very strong case to induce a Court so to proceed."

statement: For purposes of jurisdiction, the leasehold interest and not the whole land must be valued in an action by lessees against lessors and a co-owner of the lessors.
supporting_quote: "The value of the lessee's interest in the land leased is Rs. 240. It is a lease for six years, and they have paid Rs. 120, three years' rent in advance."

statement: The District Court of Kegalla had jurisdiction over the case as the cause of action arose within its jurisdiction.
supporting_quote: Held , that the District Court of Kegalla had jurisdiction, as the cause of action arose within its jurisdiction.

statement: An action for cancellation of a deed of gift by a husband on the ground that it was a fraud on the community does not lie with the administrator of the estate of the wife.
supporting_quote: "Such an action might have been open to the wife herself as a personal action, or possibly to her heirs after her death as a personal action."

statement: A donee can lawfully enter into a deed of partition and convey his share to another donee, thereby releasing the share from any restraint in favor of other donees.
supporting_quote: "The direction about the mortgage and sale is intended for the benefit of the donees to enable any of them if so minded to purchase before others any share which might be sold. It is competent, therefore, for each of them to waive his right so as to release the share of each from any restraint in favour of the others."

statement: An action for damages consequent upon a breach of contract does not allow an appeal except upon a matter of law, or with the leave of the Court.
supporting_quote: Held, that no appeal lay except upon a matter of law, or with the leave of the Court.

statement: A donor may expressly reserve a power of revocation and exercise it himself, even if the gift is not an irrevocable remuneratory donation.
supporting_quote: "I do not see any principle disentitling a donor to do so. Since a gift is purely voluntary, and as it is in the power of the donor to give the property absolutely or a limited interest therein, I think that it is not contrary to law if he makes a transitory gift, such as a gift to be terminated by his own act."

statement: The property given as a dowry under the deed of gift is subject to a fidei commissum condition, and on the death of Tyagarajah (the donor's son), his heirs became entitled to the property.
supporting_quote: "On the death of Tyagarajah (the donor's son) the property devolved on his children. "

statement: A mutual mistake can be rectified by the court even without a formal claim for rectification, based on equity and justice.
supporting_quote: "It is clear that if he went to Court as plaintiff, the defendant could have claimed relied by way of injunction against the plaintiff from interfering with his possession, and to have his sale deed rectified. Does the fact that the defendant is resisting the plaintiff's claim disable him from setting up the plea which could have availed him as plaintiff ? We think not."

statement: Parol evidence is inadmissible to establish a trust where the agreement resembles a mortgage or pledge rather than a true trust.
supporting_quote: "The object of the (first) agreement was to create something much more resembling a mortgage or pledge than a trust. The arrangement differed absolutely in nature and essence from that entered into, where one man with his own proper moneys buys landed property, and gets the conveyance of that property made to another."

statement: An oral agreement to waive rent for a period can be admitted as evidence if it was entered into after the lessee was unable to carry out the terms of the original lease.
supporting_quote: "The agreement entered into at the time the defendant agreed to take possession was not a variation of the terms of the original lease, but was a new agreement entered into after the plaintiff had been found unable to carry out the terms of the lease. This is a verbal lease, and so long as possession is held under it, its terms must be carried out."

statement: A bond given to the Secretary of the Court cannot be considered as a bond given to the Crown, and does not come within section 20 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840.
supporting_quote: A bond given to the Secretary of the Court cannot be considered as a bond given to the Crown, and does not come within section 20 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840.
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, section 20

statement: Oral evidence can be led to prove the existence of a trust, even if there is no specific provision in local law for such trusts.
supporting_quote: "It was also urged that prior to the Trusts Ordinance, No. 9 of 1917, there was no case of a trust on all fours with the present case. It is, however, unnecessary to consider whether there were any previous cases, because this matter has now to be dealt with on the basis of the Trusts Ordinance, 1917, and on the basis of the Evidence Ordinance."

statement: Under the Roman-Dutch law, a vested interest in remainder can be alienated and such an alienation is effective to put the transferee in loco procuratoris.
supporting_quote: "It may, therefore, be that a transfer of a contingent interest is effective to put the transferee in loco procuratoris."

statement: If a will is made by a testator and is shown to have been in his possession but not forthcoming at the time of death, it is presumed to have been destroyed with intent to revoke.
supporting_quote: It is an accepted principle of the law that if a will is made by a testator, and is shown to have been in his possession and is not forth-coming at his death, it is presumed to have been destroyed animo revocandi.

statement: The obligations imposed on the executor by the will are not purely personal but attached to the properties devised, creating a trust.
supporting_quote: "The present case does not seem to me a case of a legacy, subject either to a conditio or modus .... The properties accorded to the executor by the testator arc not accorded to him as a free gift, but only subject to the liberalities accorded to Ms wife and children. Until these are satisfied, the administration of the estate is not concluded.'"

statement: A Kandyan from giving a limited interest to one person and providing that at the termination of that interest the property should vest in another person is not prevented by Kandyan law.
supporting_quote: There is no principle of Kandyan law which prevents a Kandyan from giving a limited interest to one person, and providing that at the termination of that interest the property should vest in another person.

statement: An express prohibition against alienation is not necessary to create a fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: "It is well-settled law that an express prohibition against alienation is not necessary to create a fidei commissum. To take a simple example. A grant of land to A, subject to the 'condition that upon his death it shall devolve upon B and C, creates a valid fidei commissum in favour of B and C, although there is no express prohibition."

statement: A person in the position of the plaintiff is not without remedy against a forcible or illegal entry, and can maintain an action for damages.
supporting_quote: But a person in the position of the plaintiff is not without remedy against a forcible or illegal entry. He is not a trespasser, but was let into possession by the defendants as their tenant, and as such could only be ejected by due process of law. If, as is alleged, the plaintiff was forcibly ousted, he is clearly entitled to some damages.

statement: Collusion involves parties acting together for a common and indirect end, even if not involving conscious moral dishonesty or deprivation of legal rights.
supporting_quote: "It may involve no conscious moral dishonesty. Even where it does involve such a conscious moral dishonesty, it may, nevertheless, be questioned whether it amounts to fraud if the object in view does not involve any deprivation of a man's legal rights."

statement: A mortgagor who pays the assignor (mortgagee) in ignorance of an assignment, without notice, is wholly discharged from their obligation. However, a payment made after receiving notice from the assignee not to pay the original mortgagee is not dischargeable.
supporting_quote: The above principle does not apply to the case of payment by a purchaser from the mortgagor. The purchaser must take measures to satisfy himself that the person he pays is entitled to receive the money. Otherwise he pays at his peril.

statement: A hypothecation of the sum deposited can be established by including a manuscript provision in the bond.
supporting_quote: "and for better securing the payment of the said sum of Rs. 27-50 I do hereby deposit in cash Rs. 27-50 as per Kachcheri receipt dated July 12, 1921, bearing No. 422."

statement: The interest of a mother in the acquired property of her husband is not defined with exactitude in Kandyan law; but it seems clear that it was regarded as nothing more than a usufruct.
supporting_quote: "The interest of a mother in the acquired property of her husband is not denned with exactitude in Kandyan law ; but it seems clear from a number of incidental references that it was regarded as nothing more than a usufruct."

statement: A bond executed before a Justice of the Peace for security of costs does not comply with the requirements of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 or the amending Ordinance Ho. 17 of 1852.
supporting_quote: It does not therefore comply with the requirements of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 or the amending Ordinance Ho. 17 of 1852 as regards the manner in which it was executed.
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 or the amending Ordinance Ho. 17 of 1852

statement: A curator must strictly observe the sanction given by the Court to deal with a minor's property and cannot lease it to another person without such authority.
supporting_quote: "The curator or any person in that position must strictly observe the sanction given by the Court to deal with the minor's property."

statement: When two parties have agreed for the conveyance of a definite corpus from one to the other, the vendor cannot derogate from his own grant by setting up the plea that he was not in fact entitled to so much as he granted, but that he has another interest in the property which he has never conveyed, and which he retains to himself. The heir of the vendor must be in the same position.
supporting_quote: "When two parties have agreed for the conveyance of a definite corpus from one to the other, the vendor cannot derogate from his own grant by setting up the plea that he was not in fact entitled to so much as he granted, but that he has another interest in the property which he has never conveyed, and which he retains to himself. The heir of the vendor must be in the same position."

statement: A sale in execution under a decree upon a primary mortgage shifts the right created by other mortgages from the land to the proceeds of sale left over after the satisfaction of the claim of the primary mortgagee.
supporting_quote: "It follows, therefore, that the title to a land sold in execution of the decree upon a primary mortgage passes to the purchaser free of any encumbrance created by a secondary mortgage or any such encumbrance."

statement: In strict law, an order of Court is not necessary to cut down overhanging branches if the person whose land is overhung with branches could clip the branches without trespassing on his neighbour's land.
supporting_quote: "It appears to me that an action for an order of the Court would not he necessary if the person whose land is overhung with branches should clip the branches without trespassing on his neighbour's land."

statement: Where two parties have acquired the whole interest of a shareholder in certain proportions, and their deeds describe the interest of such a shareholder as an undivided interest, and it transpires that a specific portion of the land has, in fact, been held by the person through whom they both claim as his portion for the prescriptive period, this specific portion must be divided in the same proportions as those described in their deeds.
supporting_quote: Where, however, two parties have acquired the whole interest of a shareholder in certain proportions, and their deeds describe the interest of such a shareholder as an undivided interest, and it transpires that a specific portion of the land has, in fact, been held by the person through whom they both claim as his portion for the prescriptive period, and the question then arises as to the proportion in which that specific portion has to be divided, it seems to ma that justice requires that, as between those parties, this specific portion must be divided in the same proportions as those described in their deeds.

statement: When members of a family make an informal but definite partition of their lands, and each party enters into possession of his share, then the possession of the several shareholders becomes adverse from the date of their doing so, and title by prescription can be acquired.
supporting_quote: "When members of a family make an informal but definite partition of their lands, and each party enters into possession of his share, then the possession of the several shareholders becomes adverse from the date of their doing so, and title by prescription can be acquired."

statement: Section 289 of the Civil Procedure Code does not override the provisions of section 238; a bona fide private alienee is statim securus if the seizure has not been registered.
supporting_quote: "If the seizure is not registered, the necessary implication of section 238 is that a bona fide private alienee is statim securus. Section 289, as regards relation back, must be read in the light of section 238, and its operation should not be extended to a case where the seizure has not been registered."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 289 of the Civil Procedure Code or null

statement: An erroneous decision on a pure question of law does not prevent the court from deciding the same question arising between the same parties in a subsequent suit according to law.
supporting_quote: "A decision which is erroneous cannot have the force of res adjudicata in a subsequent proceeding for a different relief. Or when the cause of action is different, but the matter has already been in controversy, then the estoppel ought to be limited to matters distinctly put in issue and determined previously, and should further be restricted to questions of fact or of mixed law and fact .... section 537 .... But as regards the law, an erroneous decision does not prevent the Court from deciding the same question arising between the same parties in a subsequent suit according to law."

statement: A court should not enforce a sale against a purchaser misled by its duly accredited agents, especially when the sale was under the direction of the court and created through misrepresentations or misleading conduct.
supporting_quote: "It would be disastrous, it would be shocking, if the Court were to enforce against a purchaser misled by its duly accredited agents a bargain so illusory and so unconscientious as this."

statement: The re-acquisition of binna rights is not a one-sided process; the father's family must intend, or at least recognize, the results.
supporting_quote: "The re-acquisition ,of binna rights " is not a one-sided process; the father's family must intend, or at least recognize, the results"

statement: A forfeiture of binna rights can be waived, and the connection with the mulgedera is evidence of such waiver.
supporting_quote: "The instances given in the text books on Kandyan Law of the cases in which binna rights can be regained are illustrations of a principle and not categories exhaustive in themselves. The underlying principle is that the forfeiture by a marriage in diga of the rights of the diga married daughter to a share of the inheritance, may be set aside by her readmission into the family"

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift is irrevocable if it expressly renounces the donor's right to revoke and does not depend on any contingency.
supporting_quote: "Where, on the other hand, the donee has failed to carry out the conditions on which the gift was made, he cannot invoke the protection of the renunciation clause, which was intended to take effect only if the stipulations in the deed were complied with. The principle laid down by Armour involves an examination of the deed in order to ascertain the true intention of the parties."

statement: A lease is not an alienation within the meaning of section 17 of the Partition Ordinance, 1863.
supporting_quote: It has been held that a lease is not an alienation within the meaning of section 17 of the Partition Ordinance {Kirihamy v. Mudianse [ 1 ]).
statute_citation_verbatim: Partition Ordinance, s. 17

statement: The court held that the plaintiffs failed to prove the existence of certain bequeathed items at Abdul Karim's death, and thus their claim for those items was not supported by evidence.
supporting_quote: "It is very difficult to accept first plaintiff's uncorroborated statement that, on his father's death the widow was left with cash to the value of Rs. 20,000. The evidence given by defendant as to the maintenance of the widow by Abdul Karim and the education of the children is much more likely."

statement: A mortgagee who does not register their action under sections 27 (a) (1) of the Land Registration Ordinance, 1891, as amended by Ordinance No. 29 of 1917, loses their rights against a puisne incumbrancer.
supporting_quote: "In order to protect the mortgagee there is provision in sections 643 and 644 for the registration of addresses, and I think it is now pretty well settled that a mortgagee, who does not avail himself of this protection, loses his rights against a puisne incumbrancer not joined in his mortgage action."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 27 (a) (1) of the Land Registration Ordinance, 1891, as amended by Ordinance No. 29 of 1917

statement: The identity of the subject-matter of a sale, even if mistakenly stated in the deed, does not necessarily affect the validity of the conveyance if the vendor has a valid title to the thing sold.
supporting_quote: "The identity of the subject-matter of the sale would not be the same so as to enable us to hold practically that a conveyance of Blackacre, which she did not possess, must be deemed to a conveyance of Whiteacre, which she did."

statement: Under a decree against a special representative appointed under section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code, only the mortgaged property could be sold, and the sale of other than mortgaged property is invalid as against the heirs of the deceased mortgagor.
supporting_quote: Only the mortgaged property could be sold, and the sale of other than mortgaged property is invalid as against the heirs of the deceased mortgagor.

statement: A bond is indivisible, and prescription does not run on the entire amount as long as the plaintiff has possession for interest.
supporting_quote: 'The learned Judge held that the bond was one and indivisible, and that, therefore, prescription did not run.'

statement: One must presume after lapse of years that everything had been done that should have been done.
supporting_quote: "One must presume after lapse of years that everything had been done that should have been done."

statement: The defendants cannot be held liable for damages under section 9 of the Partition Ordinance as their failure to inform the Court about a settlement in a testamentary case does not constitute an 'act of omission' with intent to cause prejudice.
supporting_quote: "I doubt it. The plaintiffs singularly failed to establish their allegation that the defendants "fraudulently made the Court to understand that they were the sole heirs of the Adigar." As the District Judge rightly found, the preliminary decree was quite correct, and the plaintiffs had no cause to complain of it. As regards the final decree, even if the Court was informed of the settlement, there would have been a practical difficulty in introducing it into the partition case. Don Manuel Appuhamy was not a party to the settlement, and was not bound by it, nor were two out of the four children of Punchi Banda. They must get their full snares under any circumstances. Is the share, which the plaintiffs got under the settlement, to come out of the defendants' shares alone ? Or is the plaintiffs' one-third share to be proportionately reduced ?"
statute_citation_verbatim: "nothing herein contained shall affect the right of any party prejudiced by such partition or sale to recover damages from the parties by whose act, whether of commission or omission, such damages had accrued."

statement: In the case of concealed fraud, an action is available from the time of the discovery of the fraud, or from the time the party defrauded might by due diligence have come to know of it.
supporting_quote: "It is a well-known principle of English equity that in the case of concealed fraud of this description, an action is available from the time of the discovery of the fraud, or from the time the party defrauded might by due diligence have come to know of it."

statement: A person who enters into possession of land under an agreement with the owners to sell the same to him cannot acquire title by prescription after the lapse of ten years, especially if his possession is not adverse to the true owners.
supporting_quote: "On the facts reported I confess that I find it difficult to see how an intending purchaser who is given possession with an agreement that the vendors would convey the land to him when they had perfected their own title can be regarded as a licensee under the vendor."

statement: A proctor who acts contrary to the instructions of his client in entering into a settlement can be directed by the Supreme Court to set aside the consent judgment without sending the case to the District Judge for further investigation.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that in this case it would be necessary to remit the matter for inquiry to the District Judge. If it had been seriously contended that both parties contracted on the supposition that the lease expired on April 11, 1920, that might be a mutter for inquiry by the District Judge. But, from the evidence before us, it would hardly seem worth while to investigate that question."

statement: A deed is registered in the right folio if it can be connected to earlier registrations through sufficient cross-references, even if there are differences in the extent or description of the land.
supporting_quote: "In its own language what the Ordinance requires is that every deed relating to lands should be registered 'so as to facilitate reference to all existing alienations or incumbrances affecting the same land.'"

statement: Side entries in folio numbers can establish a sufficient connection between deeds for the purpose of facilitating reference to all existing alienations or encumbrances affecting the land, thereby allowing prior registration.
supporting_quote: "The side entries in folio 45/236 and folio 96/100 would, on a proper search, have disclosed to the plaintiff the prior registration of D 2. It may be that the writing of the side entries by the registering officer was not a usual method of registering, but, at most, it would be a sole and gratuitous fault or mistake of the registering officer. But as I am of the opinion that the two side entries provide a sufficient connecting link between the volumes and folios in which the two competing deeds are registered ' to facilitate reference to all existing alienations or encumbrances affecting ' the land in claim within sections 15 and 16 of the Land Registration Ordinance of 1891. I would allow the appeal with costs, and set aside the decree of the District Court, and dismiss plaintiff's action, with costs."

statement: A refusal to pay, except upon terms that the plaintiff should give a guarantee against any loss sustained on the consignment, is not within the terms of the contract and can be considered a refusal to be bound by the contract.
supporting_quote: "Clearly such a stipulation is not within the terms of the contract, and a refusal to pay on that ground was a refusal to be bound by the contract, and would be a good ground for refusal to make further deliveries."

statement: An owner of a dominant tenement does not lose their servitude over a servient tenement by acquiring an interest in that servient tenement.
supporting_quote: "The principle involved is that of the extinction of servitudes by confusio. A servitude is extinguished when the servient and dominant land meet in the same hand, but there is no such confusio unless the interest of the proprietor in both tenements is identical."

statement: The ande cultivator is a person who cultivates land under someone in possession, and the owner or usufructuary mortgagee of the land can claim damages for silting caused to their field.
supporting_quote: "The ande cultivator is, after all, only a cultivator under a man in possession. No doubt Ordinance No. 21 of 1887 legalized the ande cultivation system without notarial documents being required, but the possession of the cultivator was not improved so far as the law is concerned."

statement: Any irregularities during the trial of this case have not prejudiced the substantial rights of either party.
supporting_quote: "It may be that the plaintiff should have sought first to set aside the deed to the defendant, or adopted some other procedure to realize his claim against the estate, of M, but I am satisfied that any irregularities there may have been during the trial of this case have not prejudiced the substantial rights of either party, as it seems to me clear, on the admissions of the defendant and the attitude he has taken up, that the property acquired by him on D 1 could, by a proper procedure, have been made liable for the payment of the debt. "

statement: The Supreme Court has the power to grant relief for an omission in connection with a bond under section 756 of the Civil Procedure Code, even if there is no reference to section 757 in the amending Ordinance No. 42 of 1921.
supporting_quote: I think this is taking a too narrow view of the remedial legislation enacted by the Ordinance No. 42 of 1921. Section 756 provides for security tendered being 'accepted.' When the rest of the section is read with the expression 'accepted,' it appears clear that 'acceptance' really implies 'completion' of the security within the time limit, namely, twenty days. It cannot be completed unless the bond provided for in section 756 is executed. Therefore, when the new Ordinance gives this Court power in the case of any mistake, omission, or defect on the part of an appellant in complying with the provisions of section 756 to grant relief, it must be taken to have intended to apply the provisions to any omission or defect in connection with the bond.

statement: A person who takes possession of land and executes improvements thereon on expectation of a formal title, which in good faith he believes himself certain to obtain, may be considered a bona fide possessor.
supporting_quote: "I have not found any definition of a mala fide possessor, but I think a man who takes possession in the mistaken belief that he has a title or that he is certain of obtaining one, whether his mistake be a mistake of fact or of law, cannot be said to do so mala fide."

statement: A lessee who is displaced due to the prior registration of a mortgage claim cannot withhold rent from their lessor from the moment of notice of sale, as a tenant is not discharged from legal obligations to their landlord by a lawful act on the part of the landlord.
supporting_quote: "The answer appears to be, subject to any special condition in the conditions of sale, from the date of the execution of the transfer. There is nothing in the Code to correspond with section 298, which would make the purchaser's title relate back to the date of the actual sale. The lessee was consequently bound to pay the lessor his rent up to that date; in the present case up to February 11, 1920."

statement: A deed transferring property for the use of a specified sect of Buddhist priests, with trustees to sell the property and apply proceeds to benefit an institution, does not violate section 41 of Ordinance No. 8 of 1905.
supporting_quote: "The object of the section it not to control gifts of money, but to control the permanent tying up of land. The interest conferred in this case is not in the land, bat in the proceeds of its sale."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 41 of Ordinance No. 8 of 1905

statement: The term 'forest' in the Waste Lands Ordinance, 1897 should not be interpreted as meaning 'virgin primeval forest'. Land considered 'waste lands' primarily denotes open country with few or no trees and is described as lying open, desolate, unoccupied, uncultivated.
supporting_quote: "The term 'forest' in the Waste Lands Ordinance, 1897 (and in Ordinance No, 12 of 1840), must not be interpreted as meaning 'virgin primeval forest.' The expression 'waste lands' primarily denotes open country in which there are few or no trees-land which 'lies open, desolate, unoccupied, uncultivated.'"

statement: The presumption of Crown ownership over chena lands in the Kandyan Province, including those within royal villages or Gabadagamas, cannot be rebutted by prescription and is governed by Section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840.
supporting_quote: "The provisions of section 6 of the Ordinance No12 of 1840 therefore apply to them, and the Crown is presumed to be the owner of them unless that presumption is rebutted in any of the ways mentioned in that section. The only attempt to rebut the presumption consisted of the contention that D 1 and D 2 constituted a grant by the Crown of the lands in dispute. This is a contention born of despair. It is unsound, and will not bear examination."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840

statement: A Court has no jurisdiction to confirm a sale after the decree that authorized it has been set aside.
supporting_quote: "The true principle appears to me to be that the confirmation of the sale is a step in the execution of the decree which the Court has no jurisdiction to take if the decree no longer exists."

statement: The hindrance or obstruction should be at the time of giving of possession, or shortly thereafter.
supporting_quote: "The hindrance or obstruction should be at the time of giving of possession, or shortly thereafter."

statement: A court may add a party to an action at any time before judgment is pronounced, provided the addition would enable it to effectively adjudicate all questions involved.
supporting_quote: "The language of section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code that the Court 'may at any time order that the name of any person whose presence before the Court may be necessary in order to enable the Court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all the questions involved in the action' is wide enough to cover this case and to allow the addition of a fresh party at any time before the decision of the action, that is, before the judgment is pronounced."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The court may allow fresh issues to be formulated after the case has commenced if such a course appears to be in the interests of justice, even if these issues do not arise on the pleadings.
supporting_quote: "No doubt it is a matter within the discretion of the Judge whether he will allow fresh issues to be formulated after the case has commenced, but he should do so when such a course appears to be in the interests of justice, and it is certainly not a valid objection to such a course being taken that they do not arise on the pleadings."

statement: The Court held that the mortgage decree effectively ordered the sale of lot (1g) as it was included in lots (1a) and (1b), which were sold under the mortgage.
supporting_quote: "I think it must be held that since lots (1a) and (1 b) cover lot (1 g), the mortgage decree in effect ordered the sale of lot (1 g)."

statement: The defendant is not entitled to the house built on land co-owned by Ummini and Umayathai, as Umayathai was deceased when the construction began.
supporting_quote: "We thus conclude, as ^ appears from the death certificate, that Umayathai died in April, Singho 1901, over a year before the date of the agreement between the defendant and Ummini. Consequently, she could not, by any act of hers, recognize the building of the boutique which was being erected by the defendant."

statement: A part-owner of a land is entitled to use it for taking carts to his house which is on the land, provided, by doing so, he does not interfere with the enjoyment of the land by his co-owners.
supporting_quote: It seems to me that the plaintiff has misconceived his action, and that the issues tried did not cover the actual facts of the case. It seems to me an elementary principle that the part-owner of a land is entitled to use it for taking carts to his house which is on the land, provided, by doing ,so, he does not interfere with the enjoyment of the land by his co-owners.

statement: Money paid, but not due, can only be recovered back if it is made under a mistake or if an unequivocal protest or objection was lodged at the time of payment.
supporting_quote: It may also be recovered if, at the time when the payment was made, an unequivocal protest or objection has been lodged. See the law as stated and supported by the South African authorities in Maasdorp, vol. HI., page 396.

statement: A compromise entered into without the leave of the Court is voidable against all parties other than the minor in a testamentary case involving a minor.
supporting_quote: "The section of the Code applicable to the matter in section 600, which enacts that no next friend or guardian for the action shall, without the leave of the Court, enter into any agreement or compromise on behalf of a minor with reference to the action in which he acts as next friend or guardian, and that any such agreement or compromise entered into without the leave of the Court shall be voidable against all parties other than the minor."

statement: In the absence of specific evidence, a deed is prima facie evidence that several grantees acquired title in equal shares.
supporting_quote: "This inference may of course be rebutted by specific evidence as to the intention of the purchasers."

statement: In cases where a mistake is alleged in the deeds, all parties to the alleged mistake should be made parties to the cause for justice to be done.
supporting_quote: For the purpose of regularizing the situation, the defendant is asking that the plaintiffs' deeds should be cancelled in so far as they purport to convey the 64-acre block. It is difficult to see how this can be done, unless both the parties to the deeds sought to be cancelled are before the Court.

statement: The Court has no power to dismiss an action for non-payment of costs.
supporting_quote: "There is nothing in the law empowering the Court to dismiss an action for nonpayment of costs."

statement: A donation made in contemplation of marriage must be returned in case the marriage does not take place.
supporting_quote: "A donation made in contemplation of marriage must be returned in case the marriage does not take place."

statement: The action is not maintainable by the plaintiffs as liquidators due to prescription.
supporting_quote: "I think that the defendant's plea of prescription must be upheld, and this appeal allowed, with costs, in both Courts."

statement: The debts and incumbrances mentioned in section 17 (1) (b) of the Ordinance include only those incurred or created within Ceylon, as there is no reference to debts incurred elsewhere.
supporting_quote: "That being so the words 'debts and incumbrances' must be interpreted to mean such debts and in-cumbrances as have been 'incurred or created' within the Island, as there is no reference to debts incurred elsewhere."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 17 (1) (6) of the Ordinance.

statement: A person's omission to disclose information cannot be presumed to be intentional for the purpose of estoppel unless a reasonable man would take the omission to be true and believe it was meant that he should act upon it.
supporting_quote: "The action taken upon the belief must be directly connected with the false impression caused by the representation or conduct," and he proceeded to cite a number of cases, in each of which it was deemed essential that the representation or conduct complained of should have been intended to bring about the result whereby the loss had arisen, or that it was meant that the representation should be acted upon.

statement: A partition decree is conclusive against all persons, and a person whose title was concealed through fraudulent collusion cannot have the decree set aside; their only remedy is an action for damages.
supporting_quote: "It is as well settled as any point of law can be that a partition decree is conclusive against all persons whomsoever, and that a person owning an interest in the land partitioned, whose title even by fraudulent collusion between the parties had been concealed from the Court in the partition proceedings, is not entitled on that ground to have the decree set aside, his only remedy being an action for damages."

statement: Where a person has obtained possession of property subject to a trust or condition and fraudulently claims to hold it free from such trust or condition, they cannot be allowed the advantage of the Statute of Frauds.
supporting_quote: It has been established by a chain of authorities, which cannot now be C.J. disputed, both in England and in this country, that where a person has obtained possession of a property of another, subject to a trust or condition, and fraudulently claims to hold it free from such trust or condition, he cannot be allowed to claim the advantage of the Statute of Frauds.

statement: A lease executed by an heir and administrator, acting as such, is subject to the administrator's right to sell for the purpose of the estate, allowing a creditor to seize and sell the property in execution.
supporting_quote: Held, that the lease was subject to the administrator's right to sell for the purpose of the estate, and consequently that a creditor of the estate may seize and sell the same in execution.

statement: When a property is sold under the Partition Ordinance, subsequent transactions should be registered in the original folio of registration to maintain priority over other registrations.
supporting_quote: 'For certain purposes the question of identity may be as important in the one case as in the other. It is true that there is no express provision with regard to a sale of the land by decree, but I think that the language of section 24 of the Registration Ordinance is wide enough to include the case of a certificate of sale under the Partition Ordinance, for it enacts that ' when any property which shall have been once registered shall be subsequently sold, encumbered, or otherwise affected or dealt with, the deed or instrument purporting to transfer or otherwise deal with or affect such property shall state the volume and folio of the register in which such property has been previously registered.'

statement: A will clause creating a fidei commissum can still be effective even after an internal distribution among heirs, provided the deed does not alter the original conditions of the will.
supporting_quote: "However imperfect the words of the deed may be as a matter of conveyance, it clearly was intended to effect a division of the various lands of the testatrix among the heirs, but such a deed would not, in my opinion, put an end to the fidei commissum originally created by the will"

statement: The eleventh clause of the will does not create a valid fidei commissum in favor of the family.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the provision in the eleventh clause is insufficient to create a fidei commissum in favour of the family of the kind discussed in Robert v. Abeywardena (supra)."

statement: The court held that the deed created a fidei commissum, with the husband as the fidei commissarii and the three children’s heir as co-owner.
supporting_quote: "Now, if that is the interpretation to the deed, what is the effect of it ? 'All three children predeceased their father. The one-fourth share, therefore, vested in the father, ceased to be burdened by the fidei commissum, and he retained an absolute right in that one-fourth undivided share."

statement: A deed of gift prohibiting immediate donees from alienating property, and providing that after their death the property shall devolve on their children, grandchildren, or lawful heirs, creates a fidei commissum where the first objects of the donor's munificence were the children and grandchildren.
supporting_quote: "A deed of gift after prohibiting the immediate donees (his three children) from alienating the property provided that after their death it should devolve on their children, grandchildren, or their lawful heirs. Held, that the deed created a fidei commissum"

statement: A debtor who transfers all his property to defeat creditors, even if the transfer is executed in multiple documents on consecutive days, can be considered insolvent for the purposes of fraudulently alienating assets.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the fact of the three deeds being executed in three consecutive days and not on one and the same day makes no real difference. They must be taken as one and the same act of alienation, and to hold that before the execution of the last of the three deeds Ismail Lebbe was not insolvent, as he had some property left, would be to give effect to a mere subterfuge."

statement: Where a person transfers property to another without consideration with the object of defrauding creditors, it is open to the heirs of the transferor to sue the transferee for recovery of the property.
supporting_quote: Held, that it is open to the heirs of A to sue B for the same.

statement: In the absence of a nominee, the credit balance and contributory call shall be paid to the widow; if there be no widow, to the children; and if there be no children, to the next of kin or legal heirs.
supporting_quote: "In the absence of a nominee the credit balance and contributory call shall be paid to the widow; if there be no widow, to the children; and if there be no children, to the next of kin or legal heirs."

statement: The Kandyan law governs the matrimonial rights of a Kandyan Sinhalese woman who marries a low-country Sinhalese, and not Ordinance No. 15 of 1876.
supporting_quote: "Where a Kandyan Sinhalese woman marries a low-country Sinhalese, her matrimonial rights are governed by the Kandyan law and not by Ordinance No. 15 of 1876."

statement: A wife should be given notice when a mortgage bond is put in suit by the mortgagee, even if the property was conveyed to her under section 13 of the Matrimonial Rights Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Even assuming that the conveyance were a voluntary conveyance, still it would be subject to the husband's debts, and Somiel should have had notice when the debt was claimed and the bond put in suit."

statement: An incumbent is succeeded by his pupil and not by his fellow-pupils, with the senior pupil having the right to succeed in most cases.
supporting_quote: "As a rule, the senior pupil has the right to succeed the incumbent, and this has been recognized and enforced by our Courts"

statement: Execution upon a decree for the recovery of money due on a mortgage can be levied not only on the mortgaged property but also on other property belonging to the deceased mortgagor's estate, even if such property was not mortgaged and is in possession of his sole heir.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that it is not correct to say that the action contemplated in chapter XLVI. is a pure hypothecary action. If by those words it is meant to describe the action mentioned in section 642 as the mortgagee's action in rem, the description will be opposed to the plain meaning of the words of the action which disclose that the action should in every case be the combination of the action in personam and in rem, because it requires the mortgagor to be made a party although he is not in possession. But if, on the other hand, by those words were meant that the action was confined to the object of realizing the mortgaged property after the death of the mortgagor, What necessity is there to make his representative a party to the action if the property is in the possession of third parties."

statement: A person interested in the matter, but not a party to the action, may apply for a stay of execution proceedings under section 343 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: There is nothing in the section to prevent a person interested in the matter being heard. On the contrary, it is declared that all persons interested in the matter of the execution should be made parties. If such persons, though not themselves parties, may be made parties for the purpose of the application, there seems every reason why they should be allowed to make the application, if necessary, themselves.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 343

statement: A person who has a claim for unliquidated damages only cannot be regarded as a creditor to whom a Paulian action is available.
supporting_quote: "A person who has such a claim against another cannot be regarded as a creditor. A creditor connotes the existence of a debt and a debtor. It cannot be said that the claim for damages is a debt, or that the person against whom the claim is made is a debtor."

statement: A court has the power to allow a transferee to intervene in an action to revoke a deed of gift where their presence is necessary for the court to effectively adjudicate on all questions involved.
supporting_quote: "I think the Court has power under section 18 to add these appellants as defendants to the action. The appellants are persons who ought to have been joined as defendants when the action was instituted, and section 18 empowers the Court at any time to order such persons to be joined as plaintiffs or defendants."

statement: An unsuccessful claimant cannot maintain an action under section 247 if he had no right to the property at the date of the seizure.
supporting_quote: Holding that to be the true meaning of this case one must go further and say that in a case where a person cannot be a claimant because he had no interest in the property, he cannot be bound by the last paragraph of section 247 which would make an order rejecting his claim res adjudicata against him.

statement: The rights of parties to an action must be determined as at the date of the institution of the action, not from the date when a party is added.
supporting_quote: "There is ample authority for the principle that the rights of parties to an action must be determined as at the date of the institution of the action. In this instance the added-defendant came into the action some time after the Fiscal's transfer had been obtained."

statement: Where a mortgage bond is put in suit, after the death of the mortgagor, for the purpose of obtaining a money decree only, it is not necessary to make the legal representative of the mortgagor a party defendant in terms of section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: Where a mortgage bond is put in suit, after The death of the mortgagor, for the purpose of obtaining a money decree only, it is not necessary to make the legal representative of the mortgagor a party defendant in terms of section 642 of the Civil Procedure Code.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code No.2 of 1889 s.642

statement: For a conviction of criminal trespass to be valid, the re-entry must not only have been made in assertion of a right known to the law but also with intent to annoy the complainant. If these conditions are not met, the charge fails.
supporting_quote: "As Straight J. said in In re Govind Prassad [ 2 (1879) 2 All. 465.]: ' Re-entry into or remaining upon land from which a person has been ejected by civil process or of which possession has been given to another, for the purpose of asserting rights he may have solely or jointly with others, is not criminal trespass, unless the intent to commit an offence or to intimidate insult, or annoy is conclusively proved.'"

statement: A person who has taken a conveyance pendente lite is not exempted from the provisions of section 326 if they obstruct execution, as sections 327 and 328 do not apply to such cases.
supporting_quote: "It is quite plain that the paragraph has reference to the two sections which are in pari materia, namely, sections 327 and 328. This becomes quite manifest if we refer to the corresponding provisions of the old Indian Code of Civil Procedure, namely, section 333. That runs, 'Nothing in section 321 or 332 applies, &c,' and sections 331 and 332 are the sections which correspond with our sections 327 and 328."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 326, 327, 328 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: Proceedings by way of restitutio in integrum will not be entertained to set aside a judgment given in pursuance of a warrant of attorney to confess judgment, except in the case of fraud or a fundamental departure from the terms of section 31 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: Proceedings by way of restitutio in integrum will not be entertained to set aside a judgment given in pursuance of a warrant of attorney to confess judgment, except in the case of fraud or a fundamental departure from the terms of section 31 of the Civil Procedure Code.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 31

statement: A security bond given by a surety can be enforced in the same action as the original judgment, provided that the surety is first notified to show cause why the bond should not be forfeited.
supporting_quote: "The Supreme Court held Ukku that when a person has bound himself as a surety for the performance by a party to a legal proceeding of a judgment or order in such proceeding, he may be proceeded against in the same proceeding for the forfeiture of his bond and the recovery of the amount thereof, but he must, in the first instance, be noticed to show cause why the bond should not be forfeited and the amount should not be recovered from him."

statement: The right claimed by the plaintiff Village Committee is not vested in them under section 39 of the Village Communities Ordinance as it does not meet the criteria for immovable property.
supporting_quote: "Now a right to water cattle is an incorporeal right and would therefore not properly fall under the description of immovable property in a context such as this."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 39 of the Village Communities Ordinance

statement: Costs in a partition action are not a first charge on the land to be partitioned or on the divided portions after partition, but they are payable by the individuals taking part in the partition action.
supporting_quote: They, do not appear to be a charge on the land to be partitioned or on the divided portions after partition, but to be sums payable by the individuals taking part in the partition action, so that when a writ issues for costs, the property belonging to the individual liable to pay may be seized and sold in execution in the ordinary way without there being any charge on the land.

statement: A decree by a Court of Requests affecting immovable property exceeding Rs. 300 in value is not binding on a person claiming an interest in the property, if that person was not a party to the action and the Court did not have competent jurisdiction.
supporting_quote: "It is a recognized principle of law that a decree purporting to be made by a Court of limited jurisdiction with regard to a matter outside its jurisdiction is a nullity (see Attorney-General v. Lord Hotham3 [ 3 (1827) 3 Russell 415. ]). The jurisdiction of a Court may be limited either in respect of area, or in respect of value, or in respect of subject-matter, or in respect of a combination of all or any of these matters. It does not seem to me that the authorities justify any distinction being drawn between these various sorts of limitations. It may be taken therefore, that, in view of the limitation of the Courts of Requests jurisdiction with respect to value, the decree in a partition action made by a Court of Requests affecting immovable property exceeding Rs. 300 in value is of no legal force."

statement: The court held that the omission to distribute handbills was not a sufficient ground for setting aside the sale, as no direction from the Court regarding this form of advertisement was given.
supporting_quote: "It has been found, as a fact, that the commissioner did advertise the sale in the three newspapers and also by means of posters. The only omission was as regards the handbills."

statement: A final decree under the Partition Ordinance is only binding and conclusive if it was 'given as hereinbefore provided', which includes essential steps such as investigation into titles, declaration of rights, and direction to partition specific land.
supporting_quote: "It has been held in several cases that when a decree under the Partition Ordinance is pleaded as a basis of title, it is open to the party against whom it is pleaded to show that it is not a decree 'given as hereinbefore provided, ' and so, has not the conclusive effect given to decrees under section 9."

statement: A trustee, acting at the request of a cestui que trust in depositing funds with a bank, should not be held responsible for the loss if the bank fails.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me, therefore, that on the analogy of the pledge of a tangible chattel, the Government Agent ought not to be held responsible for the disappearance of the fund deposited at the defendant's request in the Bank of Colombo."

statement: The phrase 'their death' should be construed as 'their death respectively,' meaning the property will devolve upon their children after each individual's death, not only after both have died.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion there is such an alternative interpretation. What is more, I consider it the more natural interpretation. The phrase 'their death,' in my opinion, ought to be construed as though it read 'their death respectively,' or 'the death of the said Elaris Moraes and Patrick Joseph Obrain Moraes, respectively,' and the phrase 'their children' should be construed as though it read 'their respective children.'"

statement: The interpretation of a fidei commissum deed should consider the natural intention of the donors, and in the absence of clear words to the contrary, survivorship is implied for interests passing to grandchildren.
supporting_quote: "There are, I think, certain slight but definite indications in the words of the document pointing to survivorship. The deed prohibits the spouses or 'either of them' from alienating the properties or any of them, or any part thereof. They are to possess them and take and enjoy the rents, profits, and income thereof during their natural life. Such words seem hardly consistent with a share in the properties passing elsewhere on the death of either of the spouses."

statement: A transfer of property by an insolvent to a daughter, made in fulfillment of a promise made before her marriage, can be considered a fraudulent preference if the transfer is made after ten years and the other party has not been put under pressure.
supporting_quote: "Where a person, in insolvent circumstances transferred property to his daughter ten years after her marriage to fulfil a promise made to settle property on her before her marriage. Held , that the transfer amounted to a fraudulent preference within the meaning of section 58 of the Insolvency Ordinance."

statement: The creditors are entitled to any profits earned by the business for a specified period, and the assignee is entitled under that document to an account of the profits of the business carried on under the partnership deed from February 21, 1916, to December 31, 1916.
supporting_quote: I am entirely unable to follow this reasoning. The assignee, as representing the insolvent, is entitled under this document to any profits earned by the business for a specified period. In my opinion he is entitled under that document to an account of the profits of the business carried on under the partnership deed from February 21, 1916, to December 31, 1916, and the case should be sent back to the learned District Judge to enable that account to be rendered, and to enable the plaintiff, if he so desires, to surcharge and falsify, and judgment should be ultimately entered up on the footing of that account.

statement: The defendant was liable as a principal debtor and not merely as surety based on the proper construction of the deed.
supporting_quote: "This question must be answered by consideration of the deed as a whole. It was not seriously disputed at the hearing before this Board by counsel for the respondent that the covenant contained in clause 1 was an absolute promise to pay the full amount that would be due and owing on the expiration of twelve months from the date of the deed, and indeed it would be difficult to frame a clause more clearly imposing such a liability."

statement: The de facto trustee of a Hindu temple is not entitled as such to obtain possession of its temporalities, and disputes between persons vested with legal title to endowments should be settled through a vesting order under section 112 of the Trusts Ordinance.
supporting_quote: The de facto trustee of a Hindu temple is not entitled as such to obtain possession, of its temporalities. Our law does not recognize the personality of religious foundations.
statute_citation_verbatim: Trusts Ordinance, ss. 101,102, and 112

statement: The court held that the plaintiffs were entitled to a declaration that the temple and its lands were subject to a charitable trust under the Trusts Ordinance, and also to an order settling a scheme for management in accordance with existing religious law and custom.
supporting_quote: "Held , further, that the plaintiffs were entitled to a declaration that the temple and the lands, with which it was endowed, were subject to a charitable trust within the meaning of the Trusts Ordinance, and also to an order settling a scheme for the management of the temple in accordance with existing religious law and custom"
statute_citation_verbatim: Trusts Ordinance, No. 9 of 1917, section 102

statement: The Land Registration Amendment Ordinance, No. 29 of 1917 applies to a lis pendens initiated but not concluded before the passing of the Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "That question is whether section 3 of the Land Registration Amendment Ordinance, No. 29 of 1917, as amended by Ordinance No. 21 of the following year, which declares that 'a lis pendens shall not bind a purchaser unless and until it is registered,' applies to a lis pendens initiated but not concluded before the passing of the Ordinance."

statement: A mortgage decree is a document affecting land and must be registered. An unregistered decree does not bind a grantee who has not given valuable consideration for his grant.
supporting_quote: "That a mortgage decree must be registered was held in the cases of Salman v. Gabo [ 1 1 Leembruggen's Rep. 27.], Madan Lebbe v. Nagamma, [ 2 (1902) 6 N. L. R. 21.] and Adappa Chetty v. Babi (supra)."

statement: A mortgagee's rights under a mortgage bond can be extinguished if the principal obligation is discharged, and an endorsement on the bond by the assignee of 'Bond cancelled and discharged' effectively releases the security to the original mortgagor.
supporting_quote: "Now, in the present case, the plaintiff's rights under the mortgage were hypothecated to Mr. Fellows for the purpose of securing the payment to Mr. Fellows of another debt. It is clear that if the debt had been fully discharged on the principle enunciated by Pothier, the accessory security ought to be discharged also. We need not inquire whether in fact the principal debt was discharged, because Mr. Fellows, by endorsing on the deed 'Bond cancelled and discharged' is effect acknowledged for the purposes of this security the extinction of that debt."

statement: A husband can claim double the value of maggar from his wife if she refuses to reconcile, provided a khula divorce has been granted or is pending.
supporting_quote: "In this case the learned Commissioner seems to think that owing to the failure of the husband to follow all the provisions of sections 80-85 and fulfil the conditions therein, he is disentitled to exact double the value of the maggar under section 86. At the present time it is impossible to follow the provisions of these sections, for it is not possible to convene a meeting of 'priests,' 'commandants,' and 'officers of companies,' as required by those sections, to settle the difference of Muslim spouses."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 80-86

statement: The Partition Ordinance reserves the right of a party to claim damages if they act bona fide and in ignorance of the rights of third parties, or if their action causes damage even without fraudulent intent.
supporting_quote: "It is unnecessary to consider whether the act of the first defendant was fraudulent or wilful. It is sufficient that he caused the damage, and that it was done knowing that the present plaintiff had preferred a claim to the land."

statement: The Court has no jurisdiction to amend a decree after the Supreme Court has fixed a date for depositing money, unless acting in revision.
supporting_quote: Held, that the Court had no jurisdiction to make the order. But acting in revision the Supreme Court fixed a date for the deposit of the money.

statement: A claim to recover the balance consideration on a deed of sale is prescribed in six years.
supporting_quote: "It does not fall within the principle of the case of Thomassie v. Kanavathipillai (supra), for, although that was an action to recover the consideration for a land sold to the defendant, the claim did not arise on the deed of sale, as the deed stated that the full purchase money had been received by the vendor. In fact, the deed of sale negatived the claim, and it could not be said to be based on or to have arisen from the deed. This was pointed out in Dawburn v. Ryall (supra) and Mohideen v. Bandara. [ 1 (1919) 4 C. W. R. 188.] The present claim is for the balance consideration due on the deed of sale. By a deed of sale the vendor transfers the land, and the vendee agrees to pay the price. The action to recover the unpaid balance of the price grows directly out of the deed of sale, it is dependent on it, and derives its vital force from it. It is, therefore, a claim arising from an agreement in writing: see Dawburn v. Ryall (supra). In the latter case the vendee sued the vendor to recover compensation for a deficiency in the extent of the land sold to him by a notarial conveyance, and it was held by a Bench of three Judges that the claim was based on a written agreement, and that the action would be prescribed after the expiration of six years under section 7 of the Prescription Ordinance. I therefore hold that the plaintiff's claim is based on an agreement or contract in writing, and would be prescribed within six years.

statement: A decision on every point in issue, or matter in controversy in a case is a res judicata, and the identity of cause of action is immaterial.
supporting_quote: "As I pointed out in my judgment in the latter case, a decision on every point in issue, or matter in controversy in a case, is a res judicata, and the identity of cause of action is immaterial."

statement: Under the Roman-Dutch law, a cause of action for lateral support arises only when damage has occurred and not merely due to apprehension of future damage.
supporting_quote: "The underlying principle being that a landowner may lawfully dig upon his own ground to any depth he pleases, provided he causes no damage to his neighbour. In The Darley Main Colliery Co. v. Mitchell 1 Lord Halsbury said: 'It is clear no action would lie for excavation. It is not, therefore, a cause of action; that case Bonomi v. Backhouse (supra) established that it is the damage and not excavation which is the cause of action.'"

statement: In an action for divorce brought by a husband, the nature of damages awarded against a co-respondent is compensatory, not punitive.
supporting_quote: "The nature of damages awarded against a co-respondent is compensatory, not punitive."

statement: A joint and several proxy authorizes the surviving partner to continue representing the client after the death of one partner, provided the client consents.
supporting_quote: "When the clients gave the authority to Mr. Solomon Fernando and to Mr. Llewellyn Solomon Fernando, carrying on business under the name, style, and firm of 'Fernando & Fernando' jointly and severally to appear and act for them, they relied I think on the personal skill of whichever of the two partners might act in a particular case. The form of proxy contemplates action by one of the partners independently of the other."

statement: An order staying sale does not cancel the sale, and a subsequent purchaser can still claim validity of the sale unless the sale is vitiated by specific reasons such as fraud or mistake.
supporting_quote: "When the sales referred to in Privy Council case were held, the decree was still in force and had not been modified or set aside. Here at the time of the sale the order to stay sale had already been made, and that order was in the hands of the officer responsible to the Court, and with whom alone the Court had any dealings in law, namely, the Deputy Fiscal, in ample time for him to communicate with his Arachchi. The case of Velappa v. Ramachandra (supra) can be distinguished from this case, because here there was an order from the Court taking away the authority of the Fiscal to sell."

statement: The long-continued exclusive possession by one co-owner, without any claim from the other co-owners, does not necessarily result in adverse possession if there are reasonable circumstances that explain the lack of such claims.
supporting_quote: "It is a question of fact where ever long-continued exclusive possession by one co-owner is proved to have existed, whether it is not just and reasonable in all the circumstances of the case that the parties should be treated as though it had been proved that that separate and exclusive possession had become adverse at some date more than ten years before action brought."

statement: In contracts for the sale of land, Courts of Equity will give relief when there has been a delay in payment, but time must be essential in the agreement and clearly stipulated.
supporting_quote: "What I have to determine in this case is whether time was essential in the agreement of the parties of July 8, 1925, and confirmed by the Court on July 9, 1925. The test is 'that it must be clearly and expressly stipulated and must also have been wholly contemplated and intended by the parties that it shall be so; it is not enough that a time is merely mentioned during which or before which something shall be done.'"

statement: A grant of administration is registerable under the provisions of the Ordinance, and a duly registered deed affecting land belonging to a deceased person's estate gets priority over any claim based on an unregistered grant.
supporting_quote: "The only difference is that in that case the 'instrument' which had not been registered was a probate of a will, whereas in this case the instrument is a grant of administration. But this difference does not matter. A grant of administration is expressly mentioned in section 16 of the Ordinance alongside with a probate of a will among 'instruments' which are registerable."

statement: Under the Muhammadan law, a necessary element to constitute the validity of a deed of gift is delivery of possession, actual or constructive. Delivery of the deed amounts to constructive delivery of possession for this purpose and where such gift is to a minor child acceptance by the father appearing on the face of the deed constitutes a delivery of the deed.
supporting_quote: Under the Muhammadan law a necessary element to constitute the validity of a deed of gift is delivery of possession, actual or constructive. Delivery of the deed amounts to constructive delivery of possession for this purpose and where such gift is to a minor child acceptance by the father appearing on the face of the deed constitutes a delivery of the deed.

statement: A donatio propter nuptias deed passes an absolute title to the donees, and registration of marriage is not a condition precedent for transfer of title.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that the deed No. 5,111 (D 1) contains nothing detracting from the grant of an absolute title made by its operative words."

statement: A Kandyan woman's right to an inheritance, which is a temporary joint interest, is forfeited upon marriage out in diga and does not affect a third party who has acquired the property for valuable consideration.
supporting_quote: "The right that a Kandyan woman has to an inheritance is a 'temporary joint interest.' See Sawyer, p. 1. On her marriage out in diga she loses that temporary interest."

statement: A deed of gift under Kandyan law is generally revocable unless the donor clearly renounces this right.
supporting_quote: "The general rule is that deeds of gift under the Kandyan law are revocable. To cite only two Full Bench decisions: Bologna v. Punchi Mahatmaya1 [ 1Ram. (1863-68) 195. "

statement: An administrator cannot bind the estate by an onerous covenant without express consent of the Court, and such a covenant to warrant and defend title must be approved by the Court.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that an administrator can bind the estate by such an onerous covenant without getting the express consent of the Court for the insertion of such a clause"

statement: The share of rents given to a deceased beneficiary does not automatically accrue to the surviving beneficiaries but instead falls into the residue as per the will's provisions.
supporting_quote: "I would accordingly hold that upon the death of Jennie Joseph the surviving beneficiaries did not become entitled to her share of the rents. There remains to be considered the question whether the share of rents in dispute falls within the provisions of the eighth clause of the will, or is payable to the heirs of the intestate estate."

statement: The father of a child born from a binna marriage has a right to inherit the property of that child, which is superior to the rights of more distant maternal relatives.
supporting_quote: As a matter of construction I should have held that it (that is, Armour's opinion) was applicable only to cases where the claimants on the maternal line stood in a more remote degree of relationship to the propositus than that of great-aunt.

statement: The Land Commissioner is entitled to appeal to the Privy Council as of right if the matter in dispute on the appeal amounts to or is of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards, or where the appeal involves directly, or indirectly some claim or question to or respecting property or some civil right amounting or of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards.
supporting_quote: "1. Subject to the provisions of these rules, an appeal shall lie- (a) as of right, from any final judgment of the Court where the matter in dispute on the appeal amounts to or is of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards, or where the 300 appeal involves directly, or indirectly some claim or question to or respecting property or some civil right amounting or of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards;"
statute_citation_verbatim: 1. Subject to the provisions of these rules, an appeal shall lie- (a) as of right, from any final judgment of the Court where the matter in dispute on the appeal amounts to or is of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards, or where the 300 appeal involves directly, or indirectly some claim or question to or respecting property or some civil right amounting or of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards;

statement: A certificate issued under section 146 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance is conclusive evidence of the title of the Council to the property and cannot be impugned on the ground of a fundamental infirmity.
supporting_quote: "When land is purchased by the Municipal Council, a certificate issued under section 146 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance is conclusive evidence of the title of the Council to the property. Such a certificate cannot be impugned on the ground of a fundamental infirmity attaching to it."
