statute_citation_verbatim: Municipal Councils Ordinance-Purchase of land by Council-Certificate of title-Conclusive evidence-Ordinance No. 6 of 1910, s. 146.

statement: The plaintiff cannot sue tenants for commuted dues without joining the co-owners as parties to the action.
supporting_quote: "The material importance of this point is that the owner of only a share of a nindagama cannot sue tenants for commuted dues without joining the co-owners us parties to the action, and the plaintiff, therefore, is at once out of Court."

statement: Section 12 of the Partition Ordinance, No. 10 of 1863 preserves the rights of mortgagees regardless of whether they have mortgaged an entire land or an undivided share.
supporting_quote: "The substantive part of that enactment is quite clear. It is: 'Nothing in this Ordinance contained shall affect the right of any mortgagee.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 12 of the Partition Ordinance, No. 10 of 1863

statement: The memorandum of December 11, 1914, does not obligate the respondent to account for one-third share of profits earned by the business after December 31, 1916.
supporting_quote: "Does it, as contended by the appellant, mean that the respondent is to account to him for one-third share of the profits of the business referred to so long as it may be carried on by himself, or does it mean, as contended by the respondent, that the period of accounting came to an end on December 31, 1916, the date when the original term fixed by the deed of January 30, 1914, came to an end."

statement: A lease is void as against a subsequent mortgagee who registered his mortgage prior to the lease, even if the registration of the mortgage and the lease are in different books.
supporting_quote: "To escape from this situation Mr. Drieberg for the defendants, appellants, addressed three arguments to us. He argued that as the decree was obtained upon four bonds, and one of them was unconnected with the land in dispute and other lands than the one in dispute were also sold under the same decree, that it was not clear that the sale to the plaintiff was under the mortgage created by the bond subsequent in date to the lease. This argument is not sound. The decree was for a lump sum which included the sum due on that bond. Accordingly, the sale of the share in dispute under the decree must be deemed to have been upon the mortgage created by that bond."

statement: A donor is entitled to reserve a life-interest in favor of a third party, and such reservation should be stamped under item 30 (a) rather than item 30 (c).
supporting_quote: "A donor is entitled in the same instrument without any other stamp duty than is necessary for a conveyance to distribute the various rights which make up the ownership to various persons as she pleases. Item 30 (c) steps in only when she reserves anything to herself."

statement: A party not being a party to the proceedings cannot intervene and seek to vacate orders for sequestration.
supporting_quote: "Now. for the respondent to come into this action in that way, it seemed to me that he must have been acting, as I think he only could act, under some procedure laid down by the Courts Ordinance or Civil Procedure Code or some other Ordinance."

statement: The doctrine of part performance cannot be applied to contracts governed by the Ceylon Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, as such contracts are deemed void ab initio and not merely voidable.
supporting_quote: "Now a contract which is to be of no force and effect is void. No emphatic adjectives and no redundant repetition could express a conclusion of nullity more effectually than do the simple words which the Legislature has employed."
statute_citation_verbatim: No sale .... shall be of force or avail in law.

statement: An inclusive fee charged for professional services rendered by a veterinary hospital, which includes diet and medicine, is considered a book debt within the meaning of section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "I do not suggest that professional skill is not required in a veterinary hospital, but in this case the veterinary surgeon admits he cannot say what part of the sum charged represents his own professional services. An inclusive fee has been charged for the benefit of the business carried on by the partnership, into which the fees for professional services have become merged. That inclusive fee, it is admitted, includes diet and medicine."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prescription Ordinance, 1871, s. 9

statement: The Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance does not provide for the appointment of a person to act as Diyawadana Nilame during the temporary absence from the Island of the holder of the office.
supporting_quote: "The Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance contains no provision for the appointment of a person to act as Diyawadana Nilame, during, the temporary absence from the Island of the holder of the office."

statement: A lease for a term of years can be considered an alienation under the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, and if granted by an incumbent with proper authority, it is valid.
supporting_quote: "Reading sections 27 and 42 together, I think it a reasonable inference that it was intended to include a lease within the term 'alienation' as used in that section."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 42 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance.

statement: Prescription begins to run against a claim by a purchaser who has suffered legal eviction from the date of eviction, and not from the date of sale.
supporting_quote: "Where a purchaser of property who has suffered legal eviction sued his vendor for recovery of purchase price and damages. Held , that prescription began to run against such a claim from the date of eviction, and not from the date of sale."

statement: A mortgage executed pending a seizure is null and void.
supporting_quote: "that the plaintiff's mortgage, having been executed pending such seizure, was null and void"

statement: A deed conveying an interest in land during the pendency of a partition action is void under section 17 of the Partition Ordinance if it was not obtained after an order of abatement.
supporting_quote: "The failure to take steps to set it aside within a reasonable time gives rise to the inference that the order was well founded and no reason for setting it aside existed. I am content to rest my decision in this case on the ground indicated above, and uphold the title of the plaintiff."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 17 of the Partition Ordinance, 1863.

statement: A co-owner who plants is not entitled to the entirety of a plantation or other improvement made by him on common land, but may be entitled to compensation for improvements.
supporting_quote: "The partition Ordinance provides for a co-owner being allowed credit for any improvement made by him, but there is no law which declares a co-owner entitled to the entirety of a plantation or other improvement made by him on the common land, unless of course he has acquired it by prescription."

statement: A confession recorded by a Magistrate without complying with the requirements of sections 134 and 302 of the Criminal Procedure Code is inadmissible in evidence.
supporting_quote: "Where a Police Magistrate records the confession of an accused person, without complying with any of the requirements of sections 134 and 302 of the Criminal Procedure Code,- Held , the confession was inadmissible in evidence."
statute_citation_verbatim: Criminal Procedure Code, ss. 134, 302-404 or null

statement: A plaintiff seeking rectification of a deed can maintain an action for partition even if the deed has not been formally rectified, provided that the mistake in the description is discovered after the institution of the action.
supporting_quote: "As Lord Sterdale M. E. said in the latter case :- 'After rectification the written agreement .... is to be read as if it has been originally drawn on its rectified from ( Johnson v. Bragge 5 ) and it is that written document, and that alone, of which specific performance is decreed.'"

statement: Under Muslim law, a donation cannot be revoked after the death of the donee.
supporting_quote: "Under the Muslim law a donation cannot be revoked after the death of the donee."

statement: The word 'same' in section 19(2) of the Estate Duty Ordinance, 1919 refers to property passing on the death of a deceased person and not to any subsequent alienation or derivative title.
supporting_quote: "I therefore hold that the word 'same' refers to the property passing on the death of the deceased and that the section with reference to the persons in class (c) should read: 'By every person in whom the property passing on the death of the deceased is vested by alienation or other derivative title.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: 19. (2) Estate duty, so far as not paid by the executor, shall be paid by the person to whom any property passes for any beneficial interest in possession, and also to the extent of the property actually received or disposed of by him, by every trustee, guardian, or other person in whom any interest in the property so passing or the management thereof is vested, and every person in whom the same is vested by alienation or other derivative title shall be accountable for the estate duty on the property.

statement: A tenant can plead that he has been evicted by a title paramount, which occurred during the tenancy and before rent became due, to avoid paying rent.
supporting_quote: "It is equally good law, however, that he may prove that since the tenancy commenced the landlord's title has expired and that he has been evicted by title paramount."

statement: Prescription does not begin to run against a fideicommissary until after the death of the fiduciary, and the principle that prescription, when it once begins to run, is not interrupted by the death of the owner does not apply in such cases.
supporting_quote: "It has been held by our Courts that prescription does not begin to run against a fideicommissary until after the death of the fiduciary"

statement: A valid fidei commissum is created where the language of a document clearly indicates an intention that property shall remain in the family for the benefit of the members of the family and shall not be alienated outside the family.
supporting_quote: "Now the words 'I do ordain that the said four donees during their life time shall not mortgage, sell, or transfer to any outsider except among themselves the said donated lands' do not create a fidei commissum in favour of the members of a family."

statement: A company carrying on business through an agent in Ceylon is considered to be resident within the Island for the purpose of prescription.
supporting_quote: "For as Cotton L. J. said in Erichsen Cash,1 whenever a foreigner either by himself or through a representative in this country "habitually does and contracts to do a thing capable of producing profit, and for the purpose of producing profits he carries on a trade or business.""

statement: A donor can renounce the right to revoke a Kandyan deed of gift, making it irrevocable, provided such agreement is not subversive of the essential requisites of a contract.
supporting_quote: "In view of the law as laid down in the decided cases, it cannot be said that an agreement renouncing the right to revoke is subversive of the essential character of a gift under the Kandyan law."

statement: The intention of the testators as to the devolution of their immovable property in the event of Seypatchy being the survivor is clearly that she was only to have the enjoyment for life, and not an absolute vested interest.
supporting_quote: "Nowhere in this will, which contains such elaborate provisions, is there any clause which suggests that it was the intention of the testators that upon the happening of any event the immovable property was to vest absolutely in Seypatchy. On the other hand, there is every indication in the third clause of the intention of the testators that their immovable property was to pass to their legatees and those in whose favour that property was burdened with fidei commissa in the hands of the legatees."

statement: The maternal uncles, and failing them, the next of kin on the mother's side, are the heirs.
supporting_quote: "According to Sawer, the maternal uncles, and failing them, the next of kin on the mother's side, are the heirs."

statement: A gift or sale by a father of his inherited property to his illegitimate son constitutes such property the acquired property of the son.
supporting_quote: "It has been repeatedly held that a gift or sale by a father of his inherited property to his soil constitutes such property the acquired property of the son."

statement: A landlord's hypothec over property brought on leased premises has preference over a subsequent mortgage or judgment lien, provided the landlord retains possession of the property until after judicial sale.
supporting_quote: "All these therefore will severally have preference in the res singulares bound to them by law or usage or of which they have the right of retention until reimbursement of expenditure on them, before other creditors whether hypothecarii or chirographarii, however protected by an anterior express conventional or by a legal hypothec whether general or special" (with a few exceptions mentioned).

statement: A title acquired under a partition decree is good and conclusive against all persons whomsoever, regardless of any prior sale or agreement to sell.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that sections 16 and 17 of the Registration Ordinance apply to partition decrees to the same extent as to other judgments or orders of Court. Partition decrees are conclusive by their own inherent virtue, and do not depend for their final validity upon anything which the parties may or may not afterwards do. They are not, like other decrees affecting land, merely declaratory of the existing rights of the parties inter se. They create a new title in the parties absolutely good against all other persons whomsoever."

statement: A deed of sale executed before the final decree in a partition action is void and does not create any valid agreement to convey.
supporting_quote: "If alienations and hypothecations pending partition proceedings are to be treated as agreements to alienate or hypothecate, section 17 would become practically a dead letter. Further, such a contention, so far as I am aware, has never been entertained if it was ever submitted-by our Courts, although numerous deeds which have become inoperative by virtue of section 17 might have been saved if that contention was sound."

statement: A notice as required by the proviso to section 5 of the Partition Ordinance must be given for a partition decree to have its conclusive character, and failure to give such public notice can lead to setting aside the final decree.
supporting_quote: "The failure to give such notice to the public deprives a partition decree of its conclusive character. A PPEAL from an order of the District Judge of Galle refusing -the appellant to intervene in an action for the partition of a land called Galpotte-elamanana."
statute_citation_verbatim: "Provided that the Commissioner shall, thirty days at least before making such partition, affix on some conspicuous part of the land a written notice of the day on which they propose to make the same, and give further notice thereof by beat of tom-tom in the village or place where such land is situated, and in such other manner as shall appear best calculated for giving the greatest publicity thereto."

statement: A commissioner appointed under the Partition Ordinance is a statutory public servant within the meaning of section 183 of the Penal Code.
supporting_quote: "I have come to the conclusion that a commissioner appointed under the Partition Ordinance comes within the seventh class of persons mentioned in section 19 of the Penal Code, and as such is a statutory public servant."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 19 of the Ceylon Penal Code, class 7

statement: Prescription for a claim of damages arising from seduction begins to run from the date of defloration.
supporting_quote: Real injuries include seducing a virgin (48.5.1.). The foundation of the Roman-Dutch law action for seduction of a virgin arises from the injury to herself. I am therefore of opinion that the section governing the claim is section 10 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, which enacts that no action shall be maintainable for any loss, injury, or damages unless the same shall be commenced within two years from the time when the cause of action shall have arisen.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 10 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: A trustee of a Buddhist temple may maintain an action quia timet to set aside a deed by which a priest, claiming by virtue of pupillary succession, transferred land belonging to the temple even though the trustee's enjoyment of the land has not been interfered with.
supporting_quote: "The trustee of a Buddhist temple may maintain an action quia timet to set aside a deed by which a priest, claiming by virtue of pupillary succession, transferred land belonging to the temple even though the trustee's enjoyment of the land has not been interfered with."

statement: The registration of a deed affecting an entire estate, including unregistered lands within that estate, does not require separate registration of each land under the Lands Registration Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "As it is the registration of a deal respecting the whole, so it is a registration of a deed respecting each part of the whole. Nothing that has been adduced in argument satisfies me that the requirements of section 16 of the Ordinance have not been complied with."

statement: A plaintiff who has registered their business name under the Business Names Registration Ordinance can maintain an action for arrears of rent, even if they are an assignee of the original plaintiff.
supporting_quote: "The added plaintiff being an assignee of the plaintiff could be in no better position and could not maintain the action."

statement: A person who enters into possession of land subject to a fidei commissum and puts up buildings thereon, on an agreement with the fiduciary to pay rent for occupation and receive compensation when required by the fiduciary, is not entitled after the interest of the fiduciary has ceased to claim compensation from the fideicommissary and retain the property until payment.
supporting_quote: "a person who enters into possession of land which is subject to a fidei commissum and puts up buildings thereon, on an agreement with the fiduciary to pay rent for the occupation of the premises and to receive compensation for the buildings whenever the premises are required by the fiduciary, is not entitled, after the interest of the fiduciary has ceased, to claim compensation from the fideicommissary and to retain the property until the payment of such compensation."

statement: Consenting to judgment on a warrant of attorney for a larger sum than is mentioned in the warrant does not render the judgment a nullity but only an irregularity that is capable of amendment.
supporting_quote: It is only an irregularity that is capable of amendment. Where judgment was entered for a sum in excess of the amount given in the warrant and it appeared that that sum was justly due, the Supreme Court refused to entertain application for restitutio in integrum to amend the decree.

statement: The Court can only exercise its powers to modify charitable trusts under section 100 of the Trusts Ordinance to carry out the intentions of the founders, provided those intentions are not inconsistent with existing laws.
supporting_quote: "It is not its duty to direct charity property to be employed in such manner as it thinks will be the most beneficial for public purposes, but to carry into effect the intentions expressed by the founders, so far as those intentions are not inconsistent with any existing law."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 100 of the Trusts Ordinance 1917

statement: Heirs holding property of an intestate are trustees for the legal representative, who stands in the position of a creditor or general body of creditors, and must hold the property to satisfy just demands.
supporting_quote: "A certain interest vests in the legal representative also. Now section 96 of the Trusts Ordinance, 1917, declares that- 'In any case not coming within the scope of any of the preceding sections where there is no trust, but the person having possession of property has not the whole beneficial interest therein, he must hold the property for the benefit of the persons having such interest, or the residue thereof (as the case may be), to the extent necessary to satisfy their just demands. '"
statute_citation_verbatim: "A certain interest vests in the legal representative also. Now section 96 of the Trusts Ordinance, 1917, declares that- 'In any case not coming within the scope of any of the preceding sections where there is no trust, but the person having possession of property has not the whole beneficial interest therein, he must hold the property for the benefit of the persons having such interest, or the residue thereof (as the case may be), to the extent necessary to satisfy their just demands. '"

statement: A contract of sale, such as the one in D1, is generally considered assignable unless there is a clear intention to avoid any possibility of assignment.
supporting_quote: "Generally speaking, the question of whether one of two contracting parties can by cession of his interest establish a cessionary in his place without the consent of the other contracting party depends upon whether or not the contract is so personal in its character that it can make any reasonable or substantial difference to the other party whether the cedent or the cessionary is entitled to enforce it. Subject to certain exceptions founded upon the above principle rights of action may by our law be freely ceded."

statement: The District Committee has no power to appoint a priest as a provisional trustee under section 34 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Per DALTON J.-The District Committee has no power to appoint a priest as a provisional trustee under section 34 of the Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 34 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, 1905

statement: In an action against a person appointed under the provisions of section 642, the plaintiff can levy execution against other property of the estate if the amount of the decree is not realized by the sale of the mortgaged property.
supporting_quote: "I am in complete agreement with the reasons given, by Schneider J. for his opinion that in an action against a person appointed under the provisions of section 642 the plaintiff can levy execution against other property of the estate if the amount of the decree is not realized by the sale of the mortgaged property."

statement: A purchaser from the purchaser at a Fiscal's sale is not entitled to ask for a conveyance in their own name, but must make the application through the original purchaser.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that the provisions in the Code were intended for cases of that kind. In my opinion the appellant hits no right to ask the Court for mi order that the Fiscal should convey the property to her."

statement: An appeal can be taken from an order adjudicating on the satisfaction of a decree, even if it is not a final judgment in the traditional sense.
supporting_quote: "Section 80 is the section which confers the right of appeal in Courts of Requests cases. According to its provisions any person ' dissatisfied with any final judgment or any order having the effect of a final judgment may (excepting where such right is expressly disallowed) appeal against any such judgment or order for any error in law or in fact.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 80 of the Courts Ordinance, No. 1 of 1889

statement: A fidei commissary who joins a mortgage on property and sells it, thereby renounces their right to succeed to the property upon the death of the fiduciary.
supporting_quote: "By joining in the mortgage Lenohamy must be regarded as having renounced her spes successionis so as to enable Lucyhamy to grant a full and effective mortgage of the property."

statement: The plaintiff is entitled to the possession of lots A, B, C, and D against the respondent.
supporting_quote: "I am, therefore, of opinion that as regards the lots A, B, C, and D the plaintiff has proved his right to possession against the respondent"

statement: An order disallowing a claim under section 241 of the Civil Procedure Code is not conclusive as to the title of the claimant if no action under section 247 is brought, unless it involves an investigation in open Court with opportunity for the claimant to be heard.
supporting_quote: What is contemplated is a proceeding in Court of a summary nature directed to the investigation of the claim preferred. This is in no sense such proceeding, nor is it possible to suggest that this is such an investigation as is required before an order disallowing a claim can fairly be said to be an order made under section 245, and as such conclusive as to the title of the claimant if no action under section 247 is brought.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 241, 244, 245, and 246

statement: A contract that is an existing enforceable contract within the meaning of section 93 of the Trusts Ordinance can be specifically enforced, even if it affects immovable property not required by law to be registered.
supporting_quote: "The contract was an existing enforceable contract within the meaning of section 93 of the Trusts Ordinance and that the plaintiff was bound to hold the property for the benefit of the company to the extent necessary to give effect to the contract."
statute_citation_verbatim: T HE CONTRACT WAS AN EXISTING ENFORCEABLE CONTRACT WITHIN THE MEANING OF SECTION 93 OF THE TRUSTS ORDINANCE AND THAT THE PLAINTIFF WAS BOUND TO HOLD THE PROPERTY FOR THE BENEFIT OF THE COMPANY TO THE EXTENT NECESSARY TO GIVE EFFECT TO THE CONTRACT.

statement: A deed of gift that renounces the donor's right to revoke and is expressed as absolute and irrevocable does not require a clause of disinherison if it covers all the donor’s property.
supporting_quote: "If the grant related to a part only of the landed property of the donor, it must be taken to have the effect of an absolute and irrevocable grant. Is the law different where the grant extends to all the donor's landed property? The principles upon which, the judgments referred to proceed apply generally, and are in no way affected by such considerations."

statement: A donatio mortis causa requires the presence of at least five witnesses or the formality of a notary and two witnesses, as per common law requirements.
supporting_quote: "It is undoubtedly a very hard case, but I am unable, for the reasons set out above, to say that this is not a donatio mortis causa. There is no doubt in my mind upon the point. Under those circumstances such donations in the words of Voet (XXXIX. 6, 4) require the presence of at least five witnesses or the formality of a notary and two witnesses."

statement: A partition decree is conclusive against all persons, even those with a concealed interest in the land, and bars any subsequent claim to that interest.
supporting_quote: The effect of such a decree is to determine all pre-existing right or title and every claim to any right or title to the subject of partition. The decree in the partition case relied on by the defendant is binding and conclusive against the plaintiff as effectively as if he himself had been a party to the case.

statement: In Ceylon, equitable interests in land can be transferred by parol evidence due to the absence of specific statutory provisions similar to those found in England's Statute of Frauds.
supporting_quote: "Since 1871, however, there has been local legislation 'bringing the law more into conformity with the English law of trusts, culminating in 1917 in Ordinance No. 9 of 1917, which specially provides in section 118, after a long series of provisions based entirely on English law, for the application of English law in a matter for which no specific provision is made."

statement: A sale of land cannot be set aside on the ground of laesio enormis where a part of the consideration for the sale was a promise by the vendee to support the vendor. In such a claim, the price must be certain and fixed.
supporting_quote: A sale of land cannot be set aside on the ground of laesio enormis, where a part of the consideration for the sale was a promise by the vendee to support the vendor. In a claim for relief on such ground the price must be certain and fixed.

statement: Where a person buys a lottery ticket in the name of another minor, no beneficial interest in the prize passes to the minor.
supporting_quote: "As regards the intention of the appellant at the time of the purchase of the ticket it is obvious that a man in his position could not have had any intention to make a gift of such a sum to his son or even a gift of a chance of obtaining it. It is also clear that in purchasing the ticket he did not act under a mandate or in any sense as an agent for his son. By what process therefore did the beneficial interest pass to the son?"

statement: A payment of interest in advance cannot be regarded as a payment made on the date the interest became due for the purpose of interrupting prescription.
supporting_quote: "The payment of interest in advance cannot be regarded as a payment made on the date the interest became due for the purpose of interrupting prescription."

statement: A Councillor who acts as such after becoming interested in a contract with the Municipal Council is liable to prosecution under section 33 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance, 1910.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion however that section 33 was intended to penalize a Councillor who acts as Councillor after he became concerned or interested otherwise than as shareholder in a Joint Stock Company in any contract or work made with or done for the Council. I accordingly hold that the accused by entering into the contract P'21 became liable to prosecution under the provisions of section 33."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 33 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance, 1910.

statement: A partition decree, even if the Commissioner of Lands fails to give thirty days' notice to the public as required by section 5 of the Partition Ordinance, is not conclusively binding on all parties and third parties unless such notice was given.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the language which the Legislature has thought fit to use in providing for this notice, a general consideration of the provisions of the Ordinance, and the effect given to a final decree under section 9 strongly indicate that this is intended to be a notice to the public and is an imperative provision of the Ordinance."

statement: Where a partition action involves the question of a right of pre-emption under section 14 of the Ordinance, that right should be exercised before the interlocutory decree for partition or sale is entered.
supporting_quote: It seems to us that if an action under the Ordinance involves the question of the right of pre-emption under section 14, that the right should be exercised before the interlocutory decree for partition or sale of the land is entered.

statement: A police officer is entitled to the protection of section 79 of the Police Ordinance if he acts in good faith and within the scope of his duties.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that on the true construction of this section its operation is limited as the learned Judge has found. I think that by the words 'intended to be done' it extends protection to any act which a police officer does in the reasonable and bona fide belief that he is acting within the scope of his authority"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 79 of the Police Ordinance

statement: Where the Thesawalamai is silent, recourse to Roman-Dutch law should be made for pre-emption rights.
supporting_quote: "As regards pre-emption in Thesawalamai, where the Thesawalamai is silent the Roman-Dutch law is applicable."

statement: An administrator, to whom letters of administration have not been issued, has no authority to sell the property of the estate, even with the sanction of Court.
supporting_quote: "All the proceedings in the case are of an extraordinary nature. No notice of sale was given to the widow. The conditions of sale are irregular, as no provision is made for confirmation or otherwise by Court of the sale."

statement: Section 24 of the Ordinance only applies to the volume and folio in which a deed containing an accurate description of the land has been previously registered, not to subsequent deeds.
supporting_quote: "I am therefore of opinion that the rule laid down in Silva v. Appu (supra) is subject to the qualification contended for by the appellant, and that section 24 of the Ordinance only applies to the volume and folio in which a deed containing an accurate description of the land has been previously registered."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 24 of the Land Registration Ordinance, 1891

statement: An order admitting a claim under section 4(1) of the Waste Lands Ordinance does not confer absolute title on the claimant unless it is made in pursuance of an agreement with the Settlement Officer.
supporting_quote: "For this reason I am of opinion that the order 6 D 5 does not confer absolute title on the respondent."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 4 (1) of the Waste Lands Ordinance

statement: In an appeal to the Privy Council, the appellant is entitled to give security for the respondent's costs by the mortgage and hypothecation of immovable property.
supporting_quote: "In an appeal to the Privy Council the appellant is entitled to give security for the respondent's costs by the mortgage and hypothecation of immovable property."

statement: A person claiming damages under section 9 of the Ordinance must show that the defendant had been guilty of a breach of legal duty towards them, and this can be based on any act giving rise to damage, whether wilful or accidental.
supporting_quote: "I think it is clear that no action lies under section 9 except upon proof of the breach of a legal duty. The proviso to section 9 does not create fresh remedies but merely keeps alive such remedies as exist. If a person claims damages under that proviso, he must show that the person against whom he claims them had been guilty of a breach of legal duty towards him."

statement: A Buddhist priest can be deprived of, or can free himself from, the character, or status, or quality of a priest.
supporting_quote: "With respect to the 2nd defendant, all that it is necessary to say is that he claims the right of succession to Rewata by deed, said to have been executed after Rewata had been found guilty by the ecclesiastical tribunal, which deed however he does not produce. I agree with the learned Judge's conclusion as to the value of that deed."

statement: For section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code to apply, it must be clearly established that the parties intended for an agreement or compromise to be embodied in a decree.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion the judgment cannot be supported. It is fundamentally necessary before section 408 can be applied that it should be clearly established that what is put forward as an agreement or compromise of an action by the parties was intended by them to be such."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A person can intervene in proceedings under the Land Acquisition Ordinance and be heard, even if their claim is made after the land has been vested in the Crown.
supporting_quote: Why, therefore, he should not be entitled to put forward his claim whilst the money is still in Court, and before it reaches the 1st defendant's hands, it is difficult to understand. The 7th defendant has been properly joined as a party, under the provisions of section 32 of the Ordinance, after notice to all the other parties, including the 1st defendant.

statement: A curator of a minor's estate appointed under section 582 of the Civil Procedure Code has no power to grant a lease of property without the sanction of court.
supporting_quote: "A curator of a minor's estate appointed under section 582 of the Civil Procedure Code has no power to grant a lease of property without the sanction of court."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 582

statement: A decree declaring a right to property does not necessarily imply a right to immediate possession of that property.
supporting_quote: For instance, an action may well be instituted for a declaration of right to property, the right to the possession and enjoyment of which for life or for a specified period is admittedly in the defendant. There are several other cases in which a declaration of a right to property may be sought and granted without any intention to affect the possession or enjoyment thereof.

statement: A conveyance by way of sale may be made subject to the life interest of the vendor under the law of Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "Under the law of Ceylon a conveyance by way of sale may be made subject to the life interest of the vendor."

statement: The benefit of 'absence beyond the seas' under section 14 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871 does not require previous presence in Ceylon and can be claimed by a person who has never been in the Island.
supporting_quote: "I do not think it is possible to uphold it without doing considerable violence to the plain language of section 15."

statement: A usufructuary mortgagee is liable for acts of omission and ordinary negligence in an action pignorantitia.
supporting_quote: The agreement is that the mortgagee should 'hold and possess' the property. Full possession is with the mortgagee (Lee, 1st ed., p. 179), and he can claim to possess every bit of the property as against the mortgagor till the bond is discharged.

statement: Section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840 still has the force of law for all purposes in proceedings under the Waste Lands Ordinance, and cannot be rebutted by any means other than those provided in section 6.
supporting_quote: "It does not seem necessary to say more than this. There is how-DALTON J ever one point I would wish to refer to in respect of the argument- put before us. It is admitted that section 6 either confers upon Special the Crown or declaratory of a very valuable right. I do not Officer think sufficient importance has been laid upon the word 'deem' in that section. Whether it be the creation of a new right or the statutory declaration of an existing right as would seem to be the case, that right cannot be taken away by inference in a later statute, unless the terms used make the inference irresistible."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of Ordinance No. 12 of 1840

statement: Evidence of the parties' intention is admissible when a document's language applies partly to one set of existing facts and partly to another, but does not apply correctly to either.
supporting_quote: When the language used applies partly to one set of existing facts and partly to another set of existing facts, but the whole of it does not apply correctly to either, evidence may be given to show to which of the two it was meant to apply.
statute_citation_verbatim: Evidence Ordinance, 1895, s. 97

statement: A deed does not create a valid fidei commissum unless it can be fairly gathered from the language used that the donor intended to benefit a particular class by prohibiting alienation of property.
supporting_quote: "It is impossible to presume an intention to create a fidei commissum, unless it can fairly be gathered from the language used that the donor intended that Fidelis Boteju should only have a life estate in the property which, on his death, was to pass to a person or class of persons clearly designated."

statement: A deed of gift does not create a valid fidei commissum if it grants property to donees subject to a prohibition against alienation but without designating persons to benefit from the prohibition after the donees.
supporting_quote: "Therefore full power is hereby granted unto the five donees and their heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns to own all the right and power, which I, the donor, and my heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns have and hold in and to the same and to possess the same undisturbedly for ever subject to the aforesaid conditions and stipulations."

statement: A devise to a husband is subject to a fidei commissum residui in favour of the brother where the will grants the husband full right of donating, transferring, or otherwise alienating the property with the properties devolving on the brother upon the death of the husband.
supporting_quote: The language implies an intention that the devise to the husband should be subject to a fidei commissum residui. It is urged, however, that the direction that on the death of her husband 'the properties' shall devolve on her brother implies all her property and excludes the notion of the residue alone passing. The language is extremely inartistic, but I do not think that these words create any insuperable difficulty. Had the .words 'the residue'- or equivalent words been used the matter would necessarily have been too clear for argument. The language of the will renders the point raised by counsel for the respondent arguable, but it is not sufficient to prevent effect being given to what appears to be the intention of the testator that what is to devolve on her brother is the property or so much of it as is left undisposed of at the death of her husband.

statement: A husband is not the 'duly authorized agent' of his wife merely by being her husband, and a receipt given by him for rent to which she is solely entitled does not discharge the obligation to pay rent.
supporting_quote: "There are circumstances in which a husband may be regarded as the agent of his wife by implication. But he is not so merely by reason of the fact that he is the husband and the fact that the third defendant joined in the lease did not under the circumstances make him a 'duly authorized agent' of the plaintiff to give receipts for money to which she is solely entitled."

statement: A mortgage bond executed by a wife without the written consent of her husband is invalid for non-compliance with section 9 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876, but may be ratified by the husband to support a claim for money lent on the bond.
supporting_quote: "The first of these points depends upon the correct interpretation of section 9 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876. That section after giving a wife a separate estate in her immovable property proceeds as follows: - 'Such woman shall .... have as full power of disposing of and dealing with such property by any lawful act inter vivos with the written consent of her husband, but not otherwise, or by last will without such consent as if she were unmarried.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: "section 9 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1876"

statement: A mutual will which disposes of the joint property of the survivor, with the property being consolidated into one mass for the purpose of a joint disposition of it, becomes irrevocable by the survivor if he has accepted some benefit under it.
supporting_quote: "When these two conditions are not present the mutual will operates as the will of the first dying and the survivor will be free to make another disposition by will."

statement: A landlord is not entitled to claim an increased rent unless the original contract provides for such a variation of its terms.
supporting_quote: "The relations between the parties are governed by the agreement between them. The tenant agrees to pay and the plaintiffs agree to accept a certain rent. The latter have no more right to enhance it than the former has to reduce it."

statement: Where property, which formed the subject of a specific devise under a will, was subsequently disposed of by the testator during his lifetime by deed of gift, such disposition operates as a revocation pro tanto of the devise.
supporting_quote: Where property, which formed the subject of a specific devise under a will, was subsequently disposed of by the testator during his life time by deed of gift,- Held , that such disposition operated as a revocation pro tanto of the devise

statement: The doctrine of lis pendens is applicable to movable property under the Roman-Dutch law.
supporting_quote: "The Roman-Dutch law text books, however, draw no distinction between movable and immovable property, and there is express authority that the principle applies equally to movable property ( Voet XLIV. 6, 1: Nathan's Common Law of South Africa, Vol 4, s. 2173 )."

statement: An order requiring the manager of a lunatic's estate to pay a fixed sum into Court as the income of the estate without regard to a statement of accounts is irregular.
supporting_quote: "An order requiring the manager of the estate of a lunatic to pay a fixed sum into Court as the income of the estate without regard to a statement of accounts, showing the receipts and disbursements, is irregular."

statement: A fraudulent minor who states he is of full age, is bound by his contract and the minor must be at the time of the contract held to have been a major in the eye of the law.
supporting_quote: "Even regarding this action as a merely vindicatory one, a fraudulent minor who states he is of full age, is bound by his contract, and the minor must be at the time of the contract held to have been a major in the eye of the law ( juris interpretation)."

statement: A mortgagee of movables without delivery is entitled to a preferent right over the proceeds when sold under an unsecured creditor's writ, unless the mortgage has not been registered within fourteen days.
supporting_quote: "The law as amended by Ordinances Nos. 8 of 1871 and 21 of 1871 now requires that a mortgage of movables without delivery gives the pledgee or mortgagee no right or priority in respect of such property unless it is created by writing signed by the person effecting the same and unless such writing shall within fourteen days be duly registered. The mortgage by virtue of which the respondent claims a preference to the fund in Court conforms in all respects to these requirements. He is therefore entitled to the preference he seeks."

statement: Where, at a sale held under a mortgage decree, there was a condition that the bids were subject to the acceptance of Court, but this condition was not incorporated in the contract entered into between the auctioneer and the purchaser, the Court had no power to refuse confirmation of the sale where the purchaser had complied with the conditions embodied in the contract.
supporting_quote: Where, at a sale held under a mortgage decree, there was a condition that the bids were subject to the acceptance of Court, but this condition was not incorporated in the contract entered into between the auctioneer and the purchaser,- Held , that the Court had no power to refuse confirmation of the sale where the purchaser had complied with the conditions embodied in the contract.

statement: A gift by husband to wife is allowed, and the third defendant got a good title subject only to the claims of those who were her husband's creditors at the time of the gift.
supporting_quote: "As I have pointed out, however, these questions do not arise if the Rs. 23,568-18 paid by Wijeyesekere was on account of the consideration for the transfer. All the evidence in the case points to this and I believe the evidence of the Messrs. de Saram and the forth defendant as to the part taken by the plaintiff and that the plaintiff was well aware of the real nature of the transaction, namely, that the third defendant became owner of the land and that there was nothing due on the bond."

statement: A deed conveying land to a donee with certain conditions, including the right of the donor to receive rent in lieu of rent, does not pass title if those conditions are not met.
supporting_quote: "The part of the deed which I have recited leaves no room for doubt, but that the defendant was only in the position of a person entitled to occupation of the premises, provided and only so long as he paid a rent of Rs. 40 to Nei Zulaikkha."

statement: Where, in a partition action, the Court approved of the scheme of partition proposed and made order allotting the shares in severalty in accordance with the scheme, but no final decree was entered, such order allotting the shares constitutes the final judgment in the action.
supporting_quote: Held , that the order allotting the shares constituted the final judgment in the, action and that a conveyance made after such judgment, but before the final decree was entered up, was valid.

statement: A fraudulent deed is not annulled by an action such as a Paulian action, but it is only declared void so far as necessary to make the property available for execution.
supporting_quote: "A fraudulent deed is not annulled by that action, but it is only declared void so far as it is necessary to make the property available for execution."

statement: A usufruct may be acquired by proof of prescriptive possession.
supporting_quote: "A usufruct may be acquired by proof of prescriptive possession."

statement: A mortgage decree is a registrable instrument and one which should be registered, as supported by judicial decisions.
supporting_quote: "The proposition that a mortgage decree is a Registrable instrument and one which should be registered is supported by a large volume of judicial decision"

statement: It would not be safe to arm the purchaser with a Fiscal's conveyance, which would place him in a position of great advantage, given the dispute between parties regarding title to the land.
supporting_quote: "In view of this dispute between the parties, I think it would not be safe to arm the purchaser with a Fiscal's conveyance, which would place him in a position of great advantage. "

statement: A plaintiff can be a holder for value of a promissory note even if the endorsement was made by her husband, provided she received valuable consideration and acted in good faith.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff is thus a holder for value of the note now in question. The plaintiff is a Muhammadan woman and as such is entitled to her separate property."

statement: A person seeking to admit a sannas into evidence under the proviso of section 7 of the Ordinance must show that non-registration was due to a cause utterly beyond their control, and this requires proving both the cause for non-registration and that it was beyond their control.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that, having regard to what I conceive to be the ordinary meaning of the words 'provided it shall be established .... that the same was not registered from other causes utterly beyond the control of the person producing it in evidence, ' the cause itself for non-registration must be established"

statement: A way of necessity cannot be claimed beyond the actual necessity of the case, and even if a cartway is considered necessary, it may have been lost by prescription due to lack of action.
supporting_quote: "Under the Roman-Dutch law a way of necessity cannot be claimed beyond the actual necessity of the case. Here there is no proof that a cartway is a necessity, as the plaintiffs are shown to have have been content during the last fifty years with carrying their produce on their shoulders along the footpath."

statement: Where a contract cannot be completely performed, the party in default may be ordered to specifically perform his part of the contract as far as possible.
supporting_quote: I do not agree with the argument advanced on appeal that where a contract cannot be completely performed the only remedy is damages. The party in default can be ordered to perform his part of the contract so far as that is possible.

statement: The mere possibility of deception by passing-off is not a good ground for refusing registration of the mark.
supporting_quote: "The remedy in such a case is an action for damages against the trader, and the mere possibility of deception by passing-oil is not a good ground for refusing registration of the mark."

statement: The benefit given to L. M. M. was not limited to his minority or any other period than the duration of his life.
supporting_quote: "For myself I have great difficulty in confining this provision to the 90 minority of the beneficiary or to any other period than the duration of his life."

statement: A debtor has the right to pay his debt and redeem a mortgage bond securing the debt, which can be exercised through an agent without needing privity of contract between the first mortgagee and the new creditor.
supporting_quote: "The debtor, in the present case, seeks to pay the debt and redeem the earlier bond through his duly constituted agent, the plaintiff. No privity of contract between the first mortgagee and the plaintiff need exist to enable the latter to act as the debtor's agent."

statement: A deed of release should be considered as one instrument when it involves the release of property from multiple mortgages in a single transaction, even if those mortgages relate to different loans.
supporting_quote: "I do not think we should be justified in saying that there are here two separate transactions, and that, therefore, the deed refers to distinct matters. There was in fact only one transaction, one complete release for one complete consideration, and I think the deed should be stamped as one instrument of release."

statement: A daughter dowried by her brother is debarred from the inheritance under the Tesawalamai, even if the dowry was given out of property belonging to the brother and his wife.
supporting_quote: "The important point is that the Code puts an obligation on the mother to dowry daughters. It does not say, nor can one assume, that the mother has to dowry a daughter from her own share, leaving intact that daughter's share inherited from her father. The admitted principle of the Tesawalamai is 'that if a daughter is dowried she loses her rights to her parents' inheritance, and section 9 is intended to carry this principle into effect after the father has died.'"

statement: In a Tesawalamai intestacy, females succeed to the property of an unmarried sister.
supporting_quote: "One general rule of the Tesawalamai is that males succeed to males and females to females"

statement: The settlement of 1930 between Bandara Menika and Somawathie, despite the uncertainty around proving adoption for inheritance purposes under Kandyan law at that time, was likely motivated by a desire to avoid protracted litigation rather than fraud or personal gain.
supporting_quote: For then only can the plaintiff invoke the well-settled principle of law which, has been incorporated in Section 90 of the Trusts Ordinance in the following terms : "When a person bound in a fiduciary capacity to protect the interests of another person, by availing himself of his character, gains for himself any pecuniary advantage, .... he must hold for the benefit of such other person the advantage so gained."

statement: The mere fact that a fresh offer of an enhanced sum is made after the close of the sale by auction is not of itself enough to justify the Court in refusing to confirm the sale.
supporting_quote: In my opinion the mere fact that a fresh offer of an enhanced sum is made after the close of the sale by auction is not of itself enough to justify the Court in refusing to confirm the sale, and I think therefore that the Court was not entitled to refuse to confirm the sale on that ground.

statement: Part payment can stop the running of prescription under section 13 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871 if it is from which an acknowledgment of the debt can be implied.
supporting_quote: "It has been held by this Court in the following cases, Sawanna Pana Lana Sathappa Chetty v. Kawana Payana Muttu Ramen Chetty,[1 5 S. C. C. 62.] Bacho Appu v. Ramblan [2 (1912) 14 N. L. R. 1] and Arunasalam v. Ramasamy [3 (1915) 17 N. L. R. 156.] that part payment has the effect under section 13 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871 of breaking the prescriptive period, i.e., a part payment from which an acknowledgment of the debt can be implied."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 13 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: The Deputy Fiscal had the lawful right to assign the security bond on behalf of the Fiscal.
supporting_quote: "I see no reason why the District Judge's finding on this point should be disturbed. The main ground of argument was under issue (3), under which issue Mr. Tisseverasinghe raised a number of interesting law points. In the first place, he contended that the assignment was not properly stamped, and that the Deputy Fiscal had no right to assign the bond on behalf of the Fiscal by a mere endorsement, and he quoted in support a case reported in 3 Appeal Court Reports 46. The short answer to this case is that the law has since been amended, making the Fiscal a corporation sole (see section 83A of Ordinance No. 4 of 1867, amended by Ordinance No. 24 of 1908)."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 83A of Ordinance No. 4 of 1867, amended by Ordinance No. 24 of 1908

statement: A broker is entitled to commission only after a binding agreement is concluded, unless the seller's negligence justifies the broker’s claim.
supporting_quote: "Held , that the plaintiff was not entitled to his commission till the purchase was concluded by a binding contract."

statement: A deed conveying title to immovable property executed by a minor is voidable and not void because he has a title to convey, and it is only the minor who can plead that the deed is void owing to his minority. A deed executed by a person who has no title to convey is void against all the world.
supporting_quote: "A deed conveying title to immovable property executed by a 1929. minor is voidable and not void because he has a title to convey, and it is only the minor who can plead that the deed is void owing to his minority. A deed executed by a person who has no title to convey is void against all the world."

statement: A trustee is authorized to make payments for the purposes enumerated in section 20 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, No. 8 of 1905, and such payments cannot be regarded as improper or made ultra vires merely because the sanction and approval of the District Committee was not obtained.
supporting_quote: "That the section empowers a trustee to make such payments is emphasized by section 21 (b) which imposes the duty on trustees of keeping accounts ' of the disbursements made by them ' for the purposes defined in section 20. The learned Judge has drawn the inference that, the sanction of the District Committee is a condition precedent to the payments being lawfully made from the fact that in two of the forms appended to the rules made by the District Committee under section 12 of the Ordinance there occur the words ' date of sanction and No. of authority given by the District Committee.' However desirable it may be for trustees to make only such payments as the District Committee approve of, the mere occurrence of these words in these forms cannot in my opinion fetter or derogate from the express powers of expenditure which are vested in trustees under section 20."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 20 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, No. 8 of 1905.

statement: An agreement under section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code must be notified to the Court by motion made in presence of, or on notice to, all parties concerned. The court is not obliged to enter a decree based on an agreement that was not properly presented.
supporting_quote: "The agreement, compromise, or satisfaction shall be notified to Court by motion made in presence of, or on notice to, all parties concerned. This ruling was approved of by Jayewardene J. in Suppiah v. Abdulla [2 (1984) 26 N. L. R. 79.]"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The appellant is entitled to share in the sum brought into Court, but not necessarily the entire amount.
supporting_quote: "I accordingly hold that the appellant is entitled to share in the sum brought into Court. The next question is whether the appellant is entitled to the entire sum in Court as his share of the assets realized by the sale."

statement: A testator's intention to include after-acquired property in a will can be inferred from the codicil, especially when the original will or codicil contains provisions that have become obsolete due to changes in the testator’s financial situation.
supporting_quote: "What is more likely is that he intended to extend that clause so as to make it applicable as if it were made at the date of the codicil. This same clause also disposed of 'all cash in deposit to my credit in my No. 2 account.' Clearly the effect of the codicil is not to restrict this request to the Rs. 1,250 which was in deposit in 1913, but to make it apply to the Rs. 6,920 in deposit at the time of his death."

statement: A trial on indictment in the District Court must proceed on evidence given in Court. It is irregular to read the depositions of the witnesses in the Police Court and to tender them for cross-examination.
supporting_quote: It is irregular to read the depositions of the witnesses in the Police Court and to tender them for cross-examination.

statement: Equity does not allow the Statute of Frauds to be used as an instrument for fraud, and this principle cannot be applied to a case where the absence of the writing is due merely to non-performance of an informal contract to execute one.
supporting_quote: "This principle cannot be applied to such a case as this. It does operate in certain classes of cases. 'It is a fraud on the part of a person to whom land is conveyed as a trustee and who knows it is so conveyed, to deny the trust and claim the land himself.'"

statement: An executor or creditor who has notice of Court-ordered property sales and appears in related proceedings cannot override such orders by subsequently selling the property to another party.
supporting_quote: " When the Court exercised its jurisdiction and took upon itself the sale of the property, the executor had no longer any authority to dispose of the property, except upon further orders of Court, and cannot be allowed to defeat the acts of the Court in regard to the sale, for that would be not only directly to defy the Court, whose jurisdiction had been exercised at bis own instance, but to set himself above the Court." 460 There an executor who had applied to Court for and obtained an order for the sale of immovable property upon -which the property was sold to A was held to have no right to sell the property to B pending the conveyance to A, and in an action rei vindicatio by A against B, A was held entitled to succeed although B's conveyance was earlier in date. The same principle applies to a creditor who has notice of the proceedings and who has appeared in the administration case. The

statement: A testator's intention to settle property on their real descendants, as far as possible, can be inferred from a clause that prohibits alienation and provides for the property to escheat to the Crown only upon the extinction of all generations of descendants.
supporting_quote: "It is difficult to believe that the language of the testators was used with no other intention than that of appointing the condition upon which the property was to escheat to the Crown regardless of the circumstance that during the lives of successive generations of their descendants the property may by alienation have passed into the hands of strangers."

statement: The prohibition on alienation to an outsider is personal and only applies to the immediate devisees, not their lawful issue.
supporting_quote: "But prohibitions which are not nude, but binding, appear to fall under one of two general classes, to wit, (i) personal, (ii) real prohibitions- (i) 'A prohibition is personal when. a testator interdicts certain persons, by name or as a class from making alienation; for example, if he says, ' I prohibit Titus or my heir or legatee from alienating the land. ' When a prohibition is in this way imposed upon a person, it applies only to the person prohibited, and does not go beyond him.'"

statement: A trustee cannot delegate his powers except within certain well recognized limits.
supporting_quote: "I accept it then as settled law that although a trustee cannot delegate to others the confidence reposed in himself, nevertheless he may in the administration of the trust avail himself of the agency of third parties, such as bankers, brokers, and others."

statement: The burden of proof is on the creditor to prove the execution of a mortgage bond, and the sum due thereunder, even if the debtor has admitted the amount owed.
supporting_quote: "Where a creditor on a bond asks for a hypothecary decree against property title to which has passed to a third party by a subsequent transfer by the mortgage debtor, he has to prove the fact of the mortgage, that it was executed to secure the repayment of money due to him, that the debt was not repaid, and that a definite sum of money is due to him on the bond."

statement: The test of jurisdiction for a declaration that land is free from servitude is the depreciation in value caused to the land by recognition of the right of way.
supporting_quote: The test of jurisdiction was the depreciation in value caused to the land by a recognition of the right of way.

statement: In the absence of a direct gift from a binna married mother, property inherited by a child is considered acquired property and not paraveni (ancestral) property.
supporting_quote: Express authority for this will be found in the case of Ukkuhamy v. Bala Ettana, [1 (1908) 11 N. L. R. 226.] where the claim of the mother, the father being dead, to the acquired property of her child was upheld against that of the child's full brothers and sisters.

statement: The devisees must be deemed to have elected to take the property in its original character if they have been treating it as such for many years, even without a formal deed.
supporting_quote: "But where, as in this case, these heirs, first defendant, and Marigida Perera, from whom the second, third, and fourth defendants derive title, have for many years treated the property as vested in John Theodore Stewart's children and grandchildren, we ought not I think to disturb the construction they have placed on John Stewart's title."

statement: An action for a declaration of title on property included in the estates of deceased persons requires compliance with section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: The plaintiffs cannot, however, be allowed the advantage of a final determination unless and until the provisions of section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code are complied with.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The defendant acted without reasonable and probable cause by applying to the Magistrate for process, issuing a warrant, and petitioning the Attorney-General despite the Magistrate's dismissal of the charge.
supporting_quote: "In stating the offence in the petition he says: 'He granted a cheque for Rs. 2,000 which was dishonoured.' He also suggests that the Magistrate discharged the accused without any inquiry. This was not the case."

statement: A deed of gift by Muslim parents to their minor children, reserving a life-interest and the right to mortgage or transfer the land, is invalid if there is no acceptance on behalf of the minor donees.
supporting_quote: "Where Muslim parents conveyed to their minor child by a deed, styled a deed of settlement, a land reserving to themselves a life-interest and the right to mortgage or transfer the land, and there was no acceptance on behalf of the minor,- Held , that the deed was inoperative to pass title to the donee."

statement: An amendment to a decree for sale in a partition suit, which allocates an unallotted share to specific parties, is conclusive and not subject to further intervention by other claimants.
supporting_quote: "This is in no sense a variation of the decree, it is nothing more than a decree, passed on a later date, that the appellants are entitled to that share. I am not aware of any direct authority on this point, but it seems to me that there is good reason for giving to this amendment the same conclusive effect that the rest of the decree has; and if this is so the learned District Judge could not entertain the application of the respondents after the appellants had been finally and conclusively declared the owners of this share on January 24."

statement: A provision in a decree for sale that requires a co-owner who buys at the sale to give another co-owner an option to purchase within a certain time is not binding on a co-owner who has not consented to it.
supporting_quote: Held, that such a condition should not be embodied in the decree and that it is not binding on a co-owner, who has not consented to it.

statement: The order of partition confirmed by the Court does not have the same effect as a judgment entered in pursuance of it, and cannot be used to convey title without registration.
supporting_quote: It appears to me that there are good reasons for holding that it cannot have this effect. The title acquired under, the judgment alloting divided shares to parties is an indefeasible one; it terminates the old title of common ownership and creates anew title which has to be registered as such under section 27 of the Land Registration Ordinance, No. 14 of 1891, and which the Court by its judgement confers on the parties.

statement: The prescriptive title maturing in favor of the plaintiff since 1909 in respect of lot B was not extinguished by the conveyance in favor of the Crown.
supporting_quote: "Held further, that the prescriptive title maturing in favour of the plaintiff since 1909 in respect of lot B was not extinguished by the conveyance in favour of the Crown."

statement: The relationship between the defendant firm and the plaintiff company is that of agent and principal, not vendor and purchaser.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion it is quite clear that the relationship was that of agent and principal. The words of the opening paragraph are very specific, and there is nothing in the remainder of the indent to indicate any intention of the parties to alter or modify the relationship which those words so clearly established."

statement: A Court has no power to reopen proceedings in order to entertain a claim to a share of the estate on the ground that the claimant is an heir after a final account has been filed and the estate declared closed.
supporting_quote: I can see nothing in the Code which entitles the Court to reopen such proceedings for the purpose of examining fresh claims nor do any of the cases cited support such a contention.

statement: The plaintiff failed to prove the necessary facts for a constructive trust and thus his case fails.
supporting_quote: "Holding as I do that the plaintiff has failed to prove his two props to establish the constructive trust, his whole case fails."

statement: A right of way acquired by prescription is over the definite track used in process of acquiring it.
supporting_quote: "User of a definite track is the only way in which a right of way over the land of another can be acquired by prescription"

statement: A claim for money due to the Kandy Municipality for the supply of electric current and for the hire of electric lamps is prescribed in one year.
supporting_quote: "A claim for money due to the Kandy Municipality for the supply of electric current and for the hire of electric lamps is prescribed in one year."

statement: A Buddhist priest can appoint a successor to the incumbency of a temple through a will, even if the priest has previously dismissed another senior pupil.
supporting_quote: "This document did not in express terms appoint the respondent incumbent. The grantor conveyed to his pupil the temple and all the movable and immovable property belonging thereto which had been conveyed to him for 'upkeep' by his teacher Ratnasara High Priest, deceased ; he next conveyed for the upkeep of the said premises all property to which he was entitled and in his charge and upkeep ; he then conveyed all other sangika movable property wherever situated to which he was entitled and to which he shall become entitled."

statement: An order for delivery of possession under section 287 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be made in favour of a purchaser of property sold under a mortgage decree except as against a defendant in the mortgage action.
supporting_quote: An order for delivery of possession under section 287 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be made in favour of a purchaser of property sold under a mortgage decree except as against a defendant in the mortgage action.

statement: The decree holder is not a necessary party to an application by the judgment-debtor to set aside a sale under section 282 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: I entirely agree with the learned Judge in that case that a judgment-creditor has the greatest interest in an application to set aside a sale in execution and would be greatly affected by the result of the inquiry. I would therefore find no difficulty in following that decision if our section was in entire agreement with the section of the Indian Code. But that is not the case.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 282

statement: The plaintiffs are not entitled to ask for a reconveyance of the land on payment of the purchase money or for an accounting till the land has been sold by the defendant.
supporting_quote: "Held further , that the plaintiffs were not entitled to ask for a reconveyance of the land on payment of the purchase money or for an accounting till the land had been sold by the defendant."

statement: A person who obtains a benefit by voluntary donation must prove the transaction was righteous and that the donor voluntarily and deliberately did the act, knowing its nature and effect. If the donor is old and ill, and the transaction appears to be under pressure or misapprehension, the deed should be set aside unless the donee can show independent legal advice.
supporting_quote: "Whenever a person obtains, by voluntary donation, a benefit from another, he is bound, if the transaction be questioned, to prove that the transaction was righteous, and that the donor voluntarily and deliberately did the act, knowing its nature and effect."

statement: A reversioner, remainderman, or fideicommissary cannot bring a partition case when the life-interest is outstanding in the tenant for life or fiduciary.
supporting_quote: But the main ground on which the decision has gone against the plaintiffs is the plea raised by the defendants that deed No. 130 was in effect not the gift it purported to be, but that it was a transfer of the legal estate only, for the due fulfilment of a promise to pay Rs. 5,000 as cash dowry on the marriage of the first and second plaintiffs and on the express understanding that the legal title conveyed thereby was to be retransferred on the payment of the Rs. 5,000.

statement: A person who files an inventory and takes steps to pay estate duty, while claiming to be entitled to probate, may be considered an executor de son tort if the surrounding circumstances indicate an intention to exercise executorial functions.
supporting_quote: Here the inventory was made by a person who said he was entitled to probate, however mistaken he may have been on that point. He told the Court that no one would object to his claim for probate, and that claim, which could only be on the footing that he was executor, was actually allowed by the Court.

statement: A deed of gift does not create a valid fidei commissum where there is no clear designation of the persons in whose favour the prohibition against alienation was made.
supporting_quote: I do not think it can be said that it is clear from the deed what the donors intended to bring about. I feel quite unable to say that any clear intention to create a fidei commissum is disclosed.

statement: An administrator's bond given as security for the performance of duties, not payment of a certain sum, is not chargeable under item 15(b) but falls under item 15(i).
supporting_quote: It seems to me clear that this bond is in quite a different class from bonds given as security for the payment of a definite and certain sum of money.

statement: An action to set aside a transfer made by an insolvent in fraud of creditors can be brought by a proved creditor during insolvency proceedings.
supporting_quote: "Clearly the plaintiff has an interest in seeing that all assets which are available or can be made available for creditors should be got in, and the transfer which is impeached is alleged to have been made with the intention and to have had the effect of putting the property in question out of the reach of the general body of creditors. It would certainly seem that the plaintiff has a prima facie right to bring this action"

statement: The institution of an action against one of several debtors in solido interrupts the course of prescription against all remaining co-principal debtors.
supporting_quote: "Again it is beyond doubt that, just as is the case generally, so also here, the obligations of correal debtors and creditors can be cancelled by prescription .... For if even one of correal creditors by stipulation has timeously made a legal claim against the debtor, or conversely one of several correal debtors has been called to account by the creditor, the prescription is considered as having been interrupted not only with reference to him who makes the claim or against whom it is made, but also with regard to all the remaining correal debtors or creditors."

statement: A Kandyan woman given out in diga, even if her marriage is subsequently registered as binna, forfeits her rights to inherit from her paternal estate.
supporting_quote: "Where a Kandyan woman was given out in diga but her marriage was subsequently registered as binna. Held, that the diga association operated to forfeit her rights in the parental estate, despite the binna registration."

statement: Section 31 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance, 1910 does not provide a procedure for removing from office a councillor who at the time of election or subsequent thereto has become disqualified by reason of being interested in a contract with the Council. Instead, it provides a procedure for rectifying the list of persons entitled to be elected by erasing therefrom the name of any councillor who has ceased to possess the qualifications required or who have become subject to disabilities which would disentitle them from having their names placed on such a list.
supporting_quote: "Section 31 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance does not provide a procedure for removing from office a councillor who at the time of election or subsequent thereto has become disqualified from continuing as such by reason of the fact that he is interested in a contract or work made or done with the Council.
