The section must be construed as providing a procedure for rectifying the list of persons entitled to be elected by erasing there from the name of any councillor, who has ceased to possess the qualifications which persons whose names are on such lists were required to possess, or who have become subject to any disability which would deprive a person of the right to have his name placed therein, and who upon the erasure of his names ceases to be a councillor."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 31 of the Municipal Councils Ordinance, 1910

statement: The Commissioner is bound to make a valuation of the property before notice of sale is given, and the form and contents and mode of giving notice must be sanctioned by Court.
supporting_quote: These words indicate that the form and contents and mode of giving the notice must be ordered by the Court, and that a sale may be set aside if the Commissioner does not act in accordance with the directions of the Court.

statement: A person who has knowledge of an intended sale by a co-owner of his share and does not offer to exercise his right of pre-emption cannot thereafter bring an action for pre-emption.
supporting_quote: It will be noticed that the first issue was in the alternative whether the plaintiff got notice or whether he was aware of the intended sale of the property. The plaintiff himself has not given evidence denying that he knew of the intended sale nor has his mother been called. Nor has any reason been given for the failure to call her to contradict the evidence given on behalf of the first defendant that the plaintiff's mother knew that the second defendant was intending to sell the land and that the second defendant went and asked her to buy, and that she told the second defendant that she was not prepared to buy nor to pay more than Rs. 550 for a lachcham.

statement: A Court may presume from lapse of time, in conjunction with other circumstances, that the possession of a usufructuary mortgagee has become adverse.
supporting_quote: "A Court may presume from lapse of time, in conjunction with other circumstances, that the possession of a usufructuary mortgagee has become adverse."

statement: An application for probate will not be refused on the ground that it is stale, where the delay has been satisfactorily explained.
supporting_quote: "An application for probate will not be refused on the ground that it is stale, where the delay has been satisfactorily explained."

statement: An action against the heirs must be taken to have begun on the date the administrator was made a defendant, not the original filing of the plaint.
supporting_quote: If the action as originally framed is to be regarded as being against the estate it was wrongly brought, because it was clearly brought in conflict with the provisions in section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code which provides that where a deceased person has left property exceeding in value the sum of Rs. 1,000 no action shall be maintainable for the recovery of any property included in the estate unless probate has been granted or letters of administration have been issued.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 547 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A promissory note given as additional security for a mortgage debt, which was discharged after the note was endorsed for valuable consideration to the plaintiff without notice of the circumstances, remains enforceable by the endorsee.
supporting_quote: "This is, therefore, a case in which the plaintiff is the holder of a promissory note for which he has given consideration but in regard to which it has been shown that the principal obligation for which it was to be secured had been discharged at the time it was endorsed to the plaintiff. The learned District Judge treated it as a promissory note which had been discharged by payment and held that the plaintiff was not entitled to recover."

statement: A duly registered notice of seizure takes priority over an unregistered deed, even if the deed was executed before the notice.
supporting_quote: I would therefore hold that the first defendant's duly registered seizure is entitled to priority over plaintiff's deed which is not registered in the proper folio.

statement: A mortgage decree requires registration, and a deed executed and registered prior to the mortgage decree takes precedence over a subsequent Fiscal's transfer based on that unregistered mortgage decree.
supporting_quote: "As pointed out by the Supreme. Court in Saravanamuttu v. Solamuttu [1 26 N. L.R. 385.] and Adappa Chetty v. Babi ,[2 25 N. L. R. 284.] a mortgage decree requires registration."

statement: The appellant has title to the first land in the schedule to the plaint, subject to a lease by Leisahamy of her interest in 4 acres and 16 perches in favour of Herat Mudiyanselage Loku Menika.
supporting_quote: The appellant, therefore, has title to the first land in the schedule to. the plaint. Any uncertainty regarding the precise boundary between this portion and that on the east of it, conveyed by P .14, is a matter which concerns himself and the person who now owns the 2 acres given to Chelliah on that deed.

statement: In an action for a declaration of a right of way over several contiguous lands, it is necessary to join the owners of all servient tenements over which the right of way is claimed.
supporting_quote: Where an action is brought to" vindicate a right of way over several contiguous lands it is necessary to join the owners of all the servient tenements over which the right of way is claimed.

statement: An owner of land, who by his own act deprives himself of access to a road, is not entitled to claim a way of necessity to the road over the land of another.
supporting_quote: "I have no hesitation in holding that the owner of a land, who by his own act deprives himself of access to a road, is not entitled to claim a way of necessity over the land of another."

statement: A bank with a mortgage over shares has the right to be given preference in the proceeds of sale by an assignee in insolvency, provided they prove their claims and that the mortgage is valid.
supporting_quote: "The Eastern Bank in particular did not put its case before the Court at all. The order appealed from must be set aside. Any appellant who is able to satisfy the Court that shares in his possession belonging to the insolvent are validly held by him as security for the amount of his claim or any portion of it will be entitled to proceed as has been indicated and obtain an order that upon the sale of the shares by the assignee he should be given preference in the proceeds for so much of his claim as is charged upon and secured by such shares;"

statement: A transaction involving advances made by a tea estate proprietor to another for the purchase of green tea leaf falls under section 8 of the Prescription Ordinance, not section 9, and thus has a three-year prescriptive period.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, the appeal must succeed. The facts show that in terms of an agreement which was not reduced to writing plaintiff from time to time advanced sums of money to defendant to enable the latter to purchase tea for the plaintiff. This is a matter which seems to me to fall within section 8 of the Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prescription of Actions Ordinance, 1871, section 9

statement: The first appellant cannot maintain an action for the recovery of possession of temple land and its rents and profits as trustees were appointed under the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance, and only they can bring such actions.
supporting_quote: An issue was framed on this point. It is an action by the plaintiff, claiming to be the chief incumbent, to recover possession of temple land, and it must be taken, for the temple. Under section 20 of the Ordinance this land with its rents and profits vested in the trustees, and it is only the trustees who can bring an action for the recovery of possession of property vested in them-see section 30.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 20 of the Ordinance No. 8 of 1905

statement: The obligees are entitled to sue for the aggregate sum of money lent by them, or either of them.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiffs are entitled to sue for the aggregate sum of money lent by them, or either of them, and to recover such sum as may be found to be due"

statement: A co-debtor who has discharged a debt secured by a mortgage does not create a real charge on the property in favor of the paying co-debtor for a proportionate share of the contribution due from other co-debtors.
supporting_quote: Where one of the several co-debtors of a debt, secured by a mortgage, has discharged the debt, the property does not become burdened with a real charge in favour of the debtor who has paid the debt, for a proportionate share of the contribution due from the others.

statement: An instrument transferring shares is chargeable with duty based on the consideration specified in the instrument, even if that consideration differs significantly from the market value of the shares.
supporting_quote: "The transfer of these shares was to the Company for the price specified in the instrument of conveyance. Whatever arrangements or understanding there may have been between Ramage Dawson and the signatories or any of them prior to the incorporation, there is no evidence upon which it can be found that the Company gave any consideration for the transfer of these shares other than or in addition to the pecuniary consideration mentioned in the instrument."

statement: The plaintiffs are entitled to a five-twelfths share of the land, and the thirteenth defendant is also entitled to share as claimed by him.
supporting_quote: "Appeal allowed with costs. The case is to go back to the learned District Judge with the declaration that Mendiris was entitled to a five-twelfths share of the land and not to any less fraction, also with the declaration that the thirteenth defendant is entitled to share as claimed by him; likewise an order that the learned District Judge do allot shares on such basis."

statement: A lessee who has been put into vacant possession of the property demised cannot, in the absence of an express covenant by the lessor in the lease empowering him to do so, bring his lessor into Court against the latter's will as a defendant to an action brought by him against third parties, not claiming title under the lessor, who have ousted him from possession.
supporting_quote: A lessee who has been put into vacant possession of the property demised cannot, in the absence of an express covenant by the lessor in the lease empowering him to do so, bring his lessor into Court against the latter's will as a defendant to an action brought by him against third parties, not claiming title under the lessor, who have ousted him from possession.

statement: A Muslim gift must be supplemented by delivery of possession, and the absence of evidence for such delivery does not invalidate a gift if the donor has transferred all rights he can.
supporting_quote: "There is nothing in the Muhammadan law to prevent the gift of a right of property. The donor must, so far as it is possible for him, transfer to the donee that which he gives, namely, such right as he himself has, but this does not imply that, where the right to property forms the subject of a gift, the gift will be invalid unless the donor transfers what he himself does not possess, namely, the possession of the corpus of the property. He must evidence the reality of the gift by divesting himself, so far as he can, of the whole of what he gives."

statement: A deed of gift does not create a valid fidei commissum if it does not indicate the persons who are to benefit from the prohibition on alienation.
supporting_quote: "And I the said donor have hereby granted and set over unto the said donee as a gift all the aforesaid high and low lands with all the things thereto belonging or used or enjoyed therewith together with all right, title, and interest thereto and all the deeds and writings relating thereto and have also hereby ordered that the same shall not be sold, mortgaged, or in any manner alienated by him the said .donee or by his heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns and the same shall not be leased out more than two years but to be held and possessed by them for ever after the death of me, the said Menuhamy, the ex Korala."

statement: Where the land acquired is subject to a fidei commissum and the sole claimant is the fiduciarius, it is not necessary to make a reference to Court under section 11. It is sufficient to deposit the compensation in Court under section 37 to abide the further orders of the Court.
supporting_quote: It is sufficient to deposit the compensation in Court under section 37 to abide the further orders of the Court.

statement: A fidei commissum created for the descendants of devisees extends to at least the fourth generation, unless the will explicitly restricts it otherwise.
supporting_quote: "The word 'descendants' may in its narrowest sense be used to denote 'children' and 'children' only, but the usual sense in which it is used implies descent in its successive steps, and I have not the least doubt that is the way in which the notary used it in this will."

statement: A mere prohibition of alienation does not create a fidei commissum, unless the deed designates the persons in whose favour the property is to go over and to whom the estate shall pass in the event of its being alienated.
supporting_quote: The deed would seem to provide (although even this is not absolutely clear) that on the death of Punchi Ukku without disposing of the property to any of the other three donees the property goes to Baby her adopted daughter; this, however, will not help the plaintiff whose claim is made through Mohammadu Lebbe, for in such an event the other three donees could not on any construction of the deed be the fideicommissaries.

statement: A deed of gift inter vivos with a condition that the gift shall take effect after the donor's death does not automatically pass dominium to the donee during the donor's lifetime, but reserves a life interest in the donor. The title passed by the donor thereafter is unimpeachable if they are declared the legal owner.
supporting_quote: "The premises having been granted the condition must in my opinion be interpreted as implying that it is only to take effect in possession after the donor's death. It reserves to the donor a life interest."

statement: A fidei commissum is valid under Roman-Dutch law if the donor's intention to create such a gift is clear, and the deed must be interpreted according to Muslim customs and practices.
supporting_quote: "The question of the validity of the deed was raised in the answer but not in the issues. It may be therefore presumed to have been waived. The deed must be interpreted according to the usages and customs of the Muslims in Ceylon."

statement: The District Court lacked jurisdiction to enter a decree under section 721 of the Code directing the appellant to pay an amount claimed by the respondent, as the affidavit filed by the administrator raised doubts about the validity and legality of the claim.
supporting_quote: "I think that in these circumstances the Court was debarred from acting under this section and compelling payment of a disputed claim or trying the question in dispute."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 721 of the Code

statement: The court has the discretion to refuse a certificate of discharge for an insolvent who has committed specific offenses under section 151 of the Insolvency Act, even if not all elements are strictly met.
supporting_quote: "So far as these latter charges are concerned under section 124, charges 6 (a), 6 (b) ,6 (d), and 2 contain the particulars required according to the ruling in the case of Marikar v. Arunachalam Chetty [1 18 N. L. R. 75.]"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 151 of 7 of 1853

statement: A creditor who has executed a composition deed is entitled to repudiate it if he discovers that other creditors have been induced to execute the deed by means of a secret bargain for a payment in excess of the composition.
supporting_quote: "The essence of composition arrangement between a debtor and his creditors is equality between the creditors and consequently a creditor who has executed a composition deed is entitled to repudiate it if he afterwards discovers that other creditors have been induced to execute the deed by means of a secret bargain for a payment to them in excess of the composition"

statement: A mala fide possessor is not entitled to compensation for useful improvements.
supporting_quote: "Whatever their position may be after their purchases of 1920 and 1921 I cannot see how it is possible to treat the possession prior thereto as other than mala fide. The plantation may be a useful but cannot be considered a necessary improvement, and it is settled law in Ceylon that a mala fide possessor is not entitled to compensation for useful improvements."

statement: A binna-married daughter does not forfeit her share in the paternal inheritance by leaving the mulgedera after her father's death.
supporting_quote: "Under the Kandyan Law a binna-married daughter does not forfeit her share in the paternal inheritance by leaving the mulgedera after her father's death."

statement: Heirs are only liable for the extent of property that has passed into their hands after administration is completed by executors.
supporting_quote: "The liability of the heirs depends upon proof that administration has been completed by the executors and that property belonging to the estate has passed into their hands and is limited to the extent of such property."

statement: Section 11 of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927 does not affect a land title acquired for valuable consideration before the Ordinance came into operation.
supporting_quote: "Section 11 of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927, does not affect a land, title to which has been acquired before the Ordinance came into operation."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 11 of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927

statement: A court is not required to give notice of confirmation of a sale held by an auctioneer in pursuance of a hypothecary decree under the provisions of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927.
supporting_quote: Where property is sold by an auctioneer in pursuance of a hypothecary decree entered under the provisions of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927, the Court is not bound to give notice of confirmation of sale to the judgment-debtor.
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, s. 12 (1)

statement: A mortgagee's acceptance of interest paid in advance does not necessarily waive the right to repayment on demand, unless explicitly stated or implied by clear terms in the bond.
supporting_quote: "No local case was cited in support of this argument for the appellant of an implied waiver, and the South African authorities cited in illustration do not support it either."

statement: Even after a mutual will of spouses married in community of property, the survivor retains dominium over half of the common estate unless they take some benefit under the will.
supporting_quote: "The act of the survivor in taking benefit under the will does not of itself pass the dominium in his half share to those to whom it has been bequeathed."

statement: Where property is sold in lots under the Partition Ordinance, the value of the improvements cannot be increased or decreased according as the lots realized more or less than the appraised value. The appraised value of the improvements must first be deducted before the proceeds of sale are distributed among the soil-owners.
supporting_quote: Where property is sold in lots under the Partition Ordinance, the value of the improvements cannot be increased or decreased according as the lots realized more or less than the appraised value. The appraised value of the improvements must first be deducted before the proceeds of sale are distributed among the soil-owners.

statement: The plaintiff's mortgage rights are limited to the share in severalty allotted by the partition decree, and the plaintiff can only claim an equivalent share of lot A3.
supporting_quote: "Having purchased an undivided 2/3 share of the whole land, when the execution debtor was entitled to lot A3 he is only entitled to an equivalent share, namely 2/3 of A 3 (Bernard v. Fernando1[1 (1913) 16 N. L. R. 638.])."

statement: A Civil Court's order under Section 835 of the Civil Procedure Code to send an offence for investigation to a Police Court is not appealable to the Supreme Court.
supporting_quote: "Where a Civil Court, in exercise of the powers vested in it under section 835 of the Civil Procedure Code, sends for investigation by a Police Court a charge of an offence disclosed in the course of proceedings before such Court - Held, that the order was not appealable to the Supreme Court."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 835

statement: The cause of action for the recovery of movable property arises on the defendant's refusal to return the jewellery upon an offer by the plaintiff to redeem it within a few months.
supporting_quote: According to the defence the money was lent on the condition that the jewellery be redeemed within, a few months. On October 24, 1928, plaintiff asked defendant to return the jewellery, at the same time tendering the sum of Rs. 30 lent to him with the interest. According to the evidence, repeated requests were also made after that, but defendant failed to return the articles. The obligation on the part of the defendant to return the jewellery, on its being redeemed by the plaintiff, was to be performed, according to the defence ' within a few months' of the original transaction.

statement: A judgment entered by consent creates an effective estoppel by res judicata.
supporting_quote: "A judgment entered by consent creates an effective estoppel by res judicata."

statement: A plaintiff is not necessarily required to join all owners of intervening lands as parties in an action for a servitude, but the court may add them at its discretion.
supporting_quote: "I would answer the first question in the negative and. the second in the affirmative, as to the third, following the principle enunciated in Thornhill v. Weeks (supra) it will be in the discretion of the Court to add any party."

statement: A conveyance made to satisfy a statutory requirement of ownership, even if it lacks consideration and the transferee continues in possession, does not create a trust that would exempt the property from execution by a creditor.
supporting_quote: It is not easy to see in this transaction Mr. Goonewardene as the trustee and the first respondent as the beneficiary; going no further than the definition of a trust in the Ordinance itself, can it be said that this transfer was accepted by Mr. Goonewardene for the benefit of the first respondent or that the ownership was nominally vested in the first respondent ? It is sufficient to say that the very object of the transfer was that Mr. Goonewardene should exercise the rights of ownership and he, in fact, did so, for as owner he had himself entered on the list of those qualified for membership.

statement: A letter of acknowledgment can be used to avoid prescription only if it is accompanied by a promise and signed by the party chargeable or an authorized agent, as per section 13 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "no acknowledgment by words only shall be deemed evidence of a new or continuing contract, whereby to take the case out of the operation of the enactments contained in the said section, or any of them, or to deprive any party of the benefit thereof, unless such acknowledgment shall be made or contained in some writing to be signed by the party chargeable or by some agent duly authorized to enter into such contract on his behalf"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 13 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: A court has the power to alter directions given regarding the execution of a hypothecary decree, and this does not render a sale invalid if conducted by a different auctioneer.
supporting_quote: "Where a Court has entered a hypothecary decree, it has power to alter the directions given regarding the execution of the decree. In such a case a sale is not bad for the reason that a different auctioneer was subsequently appointed to carry it out."

statement: A trustee appointed under the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance is not a corporation and cannot prevent a creditor from proceeding against him personally.
supporting_quote: "The mere use of the words ' as trustee' in a contract is not sufficient to execute personal liability. A trustee appointed under the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance is not a corporation."

statement: A corporation can have a dual residence, but for the purposes of section 25(b) of the Civil Procedure Code, it is not considered resident within the jurisdiction of the District Court of Colombo if its primary operations and registration are outside that jurisdiction.
supporting_quote: "The word 'Resident' has a variety of meanings just as much as the word 'residence' which Erle C.J. said has a variety of meanings according to the statute in which it is used."

statement: The Registration of Documents Ordinance, No. 23 of 1927, does not provide a means for a creditor who has not obtained a judgment to obtain the same relief as in a Paulian action.
supporting_quote: Was it then intended by section 32 to afford to a creditor who has not obtained a judgment a means of obtaining what can otherwise only be obtained in a Paulian action?

statement: A court has the discretion to allow a mortgagee to bid and purchase property without setting an upset price, provided no irregularities in the sale are present.
supporting_quote: "There is no provision of the law that a limit as to price is required to be placed upon the mortgagee if he is to be allowed to bid and purchase."

statement: A co-owner who objects to the building of a structure on common property is entitled to ask for an injunction against the co-owner proposing to build, and does not have to bring a partition action.
supporting_quote: Any co-owner who is dissatisfied with this incident of common ownership is free to bring a partition action. It is not correct that the co-owner who objects to the building must resort to a partition action. He is entitled in law to prevent building and to ask for an injunction against a co-owner who proposes to build.

statement: A party cannot obtain relief in equity by setting up and proving the illegality of a transaction, especially when both parties were aware of it or should have been.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff must fail. The appeal must be allowed and the decree of the lower Court set aside, judgment being entered for defendant with costs in the lower Court, and costs of this appeal."

statement: A person who was not a party to the action can still apply to set aside a decree entered irregularly and be allowed to intervene, as long as it is shown that the decree does not bind them.
supporting_quote: "The appellant, who was not a party to the partition action and did not know of it until after the final decree, applied in the District Court that the decree be set aside and that he should be allowed to intervene and prove his claim to an interest in the land."

statement: A District Court does not have the inherent power to vary its own order, and such variation can only be done through an appeal to a higher court.
supporting_quote: "It is a very important principle as on it depends the finality of judicial decisions. If a Judge can review his own decision, there is no limit to the number of times upon which he might do so or upon which he may be invited by the parties so to do."
statute_citation_verbatim: "Nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the Court."

statement: A deceased 'co-parcener' under Mitakshara law is not 'competent to dispose' of a fractional share in the joint property until an intention to separate and its communication have occurred, and such competency must exist at the moment immediately preceding death.
supporting_quote: "I concede that, upon the communication of his unilateral decision to separate himself in status and title from the undivided family, a 'co-parcener' immediately becomes 'competent to dispose' of the definite share which he thus acquires for the first time. A. I. R. 1916 P. C. 104"

statement: The property of an intestate vests in the administrator for purposes of administration, and this gives the administrator the representative status of those who have been found to be lawful heirs.
supporting_quote: "The property of an intestate vests in the administrator for purposes of administration. The administrator is the representative in law of those who have been found in administration proceedings to be the lawful heirs of the intestate"

statement: There was no purchase by Hanscomb of the good-will from Henderson for consideration so as to bring it within the exception provided by section 9 (1) of the Estate Duty Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Held, that there was no purchase by Hanscomb of the good-will from Henderson for consideration so as to bring it within the exception provided by section 9 (1) of the Estate Duty Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 8 of 1919, s. 9 (1)

statement: Appolonia and Thecla obtained title to the property upon Marthinu's death, and the deed did not create a fidei commissum binding on them.
supporting_quote: "Their rights having been disposed of, as set out above, it is not contested that appellant is entitled to draw the sum in Court."

statement: The conveyance by the Fiscal for a mortgage sale does not require a plan if no special order from the Court is obtained, as per Ordinance No. 21 of 1927.
supporting_quote: If this be the correct interpretation of this Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, then the order appealed from was right. To enable the plaintiff-appellants to obtain the conveyance which they are entitled to demand, no plan is necessary and therefore no entry upon the land of the respondent is necessary either.
statute_citation_verbatim: Under section 12 (5) of Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, unless the Court otherwise orders the form of conveyance where the sale is by the Fiscal, is to be that provided in the Ordinance.

statement: Compensation for land depreciation due to the laying down of street lines is not payable under the law as interpreted by this court.
supporting_quote: "I have attempted to look at the question from a point of view as favourable as possible to the defendant, consistently with the law, but I find it impossible to accept Mr. Perera's argument."

statement: A creditor who was not a proving creditor in the insolvency proceedings cannot question the propriety of the insolvency proceedings and is bound by the deed of composition, unless the composition is voidable at the option of the creditor.
supporting_quote: "It would appear that the procedure laid down in section 140 of the Insolvency Ordinance was not followed but it is impossible to concede to the plaintiff in District Court case of Colombo No. 48,533 the right to question the propriety of the insolvency proceedings. He was not a proving creditor and in those proceedings had no status at all. He cannot in this appeal raise any question regarding the correctness or otherwise of orders made in the insolvency proceedings which for the purposes of this appeal are not even before us."

statement: A woman who becomes the wife of a man of inferior caste forfeits her rights in Kandyan customary law.
supporting_quote: "The only trace of civil disabilities attached to such relationships is the forfeiture of rights in the case of a woman who becomes the wife of a man of inferior caste-vide Perera's Armour, Chapter IV., section 8, p. 55."

statement: A mortgagee is entitled to compensation for the portion of land acquired under the Land Acquisition Ordinance, provided their debt has not been satisfied or waived.
supporting_quote: "On the facts as now established the respondent, whose debt has not been satisfied or waived, is entitled to the compensation up to the amount of that debt."

statement: A lessee who has assigned his lease with the written consent of his lessor is not liable for rent after the completion of the assignment.
supporting_quote: "In the case before us, in my opinion, the assignees stepped into the place of the original lessee, the present appellant, and the learned Judge was wrong in his interpretation of the law. The first defendant (appellant) was not liable for the amount claimed, and the action as against him must be dismissed."

statement: The defendant, who was aware of the fraudulent intention to deprive the minor of his property and induced B not to register the deed, held the estate as a constructive trustee for John Rajapakse.
supporting_quote: "I accordingly hold that the defendant was a trustee of the property for John Rajapakse, and that the Crown grants and Final Order on which he rests his title from the Grown were obtained by him as such trustee and do not give him a title which can prevail over the deed of gift."

statement: An application to draw out money from an estate cannot be refused on the ground of insolvency, subject to the rights of other parties entitled to concurrence.
supporting_quote: Held, that the application cannot be refused on the ground that the estate is insolvent; it must be allowed subject to the right of any other parties who are entitled ; to concurrence.

statement: Where there are several lands mortgaged, the plaintiff should be allowed to purchase any one of them at a price which bears the same relation to his aggregate claim as the appraised value of that land bears to the total appraised value of the lands.
supporting_quote: The decree makes proper provision for the sale of all lands together, in which case the plaintiff cannot purchase these lands for less than the full amount of his claim and interest. Provision, however, has to be made as I said for the sale of these lands separately, and we direct that in such cases the plaintiff, if he desires to purchase any one of these lands, can only do so for a price which bears the same relation to the 390 whole of his aggregate claim as the appraised value of that land bears to the total appraised value of all the lands, and he will be entitled to credit for the amount of that purchase price.

statement: A married Muslim woman under the age of twenty-one, who enters into a contract with her husband's assistance, must seek relief from such contract through restitution and must prove damage, loss, or prejudice.
supporting_quote: Where a Muslim woman married and under the age of twenty-one entered into a contract with the assistance of her husband,- Held , that relief from the contract must be sought by way of restitution. To obtain such relief there must be proof of damage, loss, or prejudice.

statement: A person who is entitled to the dominion only of an undivided share of land, with usufruct vested in another, is not entitled to bring a partition action.
supporting_quote: "No case has been cited to us in which the exact point arising here has arisen before. The first matter for consideration here is the nature of the first defendant's life-interest. Is it a life-interest created by way of fidei commissum or by way of usufruct ?"

statement: An order refusing intervention in a partition action is a final judgment within the meaning of rule 1 (a) of the Privy Council (Appeals) Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "It is true an interlocutory decree in the partition proceedings may follow upon the judgment, but 244 it is nevertheless a judgment which has finally decided the rights of the parties on the principal question at issue between them. That is the test that has to be applied in considering this question as laid down by this Court in Ralahamy v. Dinohamy 1[27 N. L. R. 410.] and other cases."

statement: A wife seeking to set aside a fraudulent assignment of mortgage bonds cannot do so as the assets represented by the mortgage bonds are not available for execution under maintenance orders.
supporting_quote: "It will be seen that the words used are 'by distress and sale' and not by seizure and sale as is found in the Civil Procedure Code. It is argued that 'distress' can only be levied on property that is corporeal in its nature, on something that can pass by delivery."

statement: An option to obtain a retransfer of land on the payment of a certain sum passes to heirs and is enforceable, even if no time limit is specified in the agreement.
supporting_quote: The remedy of the vendor on such an agreement is dealt with, and it is stated that his right passes to his heirs and is also assignable. Van Leeuwen (Censura Forensis, Pt. I., bk. IV., ch. 20) is to the same effect.

statement: A mortgage bond securing future advances is unenforceable to the extent that loans made under it are illegal and void.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that for the reasons I have mentioned, as well as those given by My Lord the Acting Chief Justice arising from the facts set out by him that every single loan transaction made or purported to have been made by the plaintiffs is illegal and void and cannot be enforced either by itself or under cover of the bond."

statement: A note that has been paid and returned to the maker cannot be re-issued, and a holder in due course can take it as a negotiable instrument.
supporting_quote: If there is no such statutory provision in Ceylon, that defence is not available here. Further, if this means that there is no defence to such an action, where the note has been paid but has not come back into the maker's hands before it was indorsed to plaintiff, that would, it is urged, be an additional reason to show that Jayawardena v. Rahaiman Lebbe (supra) was wrongly decided.

statement: A registrar of births, deaths, and marriages is not a public servant within the meaning of the Public Servants' (Liabilities) Ordinance, No. 2 of 1899.
supporting_quote: "The respondent here urges he is 'a person employed in the service of the Government of the Colony '. In construing the word 'employed ', however, it is not always easy to see what test has to be applied. It has been held for instance that a person who works for a daily wage, such as a tide-waiter at the Customs, a railway department labourer or a public works labourer, although they are certainly employed in the service of the Government and are paid out of Government funds, are not public servants within the meaning of the Ordinance (Palaniappa Chetty v. Fernando 1[1 A. C R. 27.])."
statute_citation_verbatim: Public Servants' (Liabilities) Ordinance, No. 2 of 1899

statement: A registered notice of seizure does not create an interest on valuable consideration, and thus cannot be given priority over a prior deed that is also registered.
supporting_quote: "Even accepting the correctness of the argument that a registered notice of seizure, as a document affecting land, is therefore a document creating an interest in land (with which argument, I would add, I do not feel able to agree) I am quite unable to see how that interest can be said to be created and claimed on valuable consideration. In that event it is impossible to bring a registered seizure within the provisions of section 7(1)."

statement: Property acquired by a wife during the subsistence of marriage for valuable consideration out of her separate estate is considered Thediathetam and not liable to be sold in execution of the husband's debts.
supporting_quote: "The land in this case was purchased in the name of the wife with her dowry money. The marriage was after 1911 and the Thesawalamai Ordinance, No. 1 of 1911, applies. That Ordinance amends the previous law. Sections 21 and 22 govern this case. This property comes under 21 (a), i.e., property acquired for valuable consideration during the subsistence of the marriage."
statute_citation_verbatim: "Property acquired for valuable consideration by either husband or wife during the subsistence of marriage"

statement: A deed of gift of the stock-in-trade and good will of a business is a bill of sale within the meaning of section 17 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "A deed of gift of the stock-in-trade and good will of a business is a bill of sale within the meaning of section 17 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: SRC022-s17

statement: A claim for money lent, which is prescribed in three years, does not become a book debt within the meaning of section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance merely because the transaction is entered in the books kept by the lender in the ordinary course of business.
supporting_quote: A claim for money lent, which is prescribed in three years, does not become a book debt within the meaning of section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance merely because the transaction is entered in the books kept by the lender in the ordinary course of business.
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 22 of 1871, ss. 8 and 9

statement: Each child's share of the property passes to them upon reaching majority, not when the youngest child reaches that age.
supporting_quote: "The words 'when they come of age' as used here mean when each one of them comes of age."

statement: A Buddhist temple is not a juristic person under Ceylon law.
supporting_quote: "It is not necessary therefore for the purpose of this case to deal with the question whether in Ceylon a Buddhist temple is a juristic person."

statement: An action to recover purchase money, even when based on a written agreement, is not maintainable if not commenced within three years from the time after the cause of action has arisen.
supporting_quote: "The action, therefore, falls within either section 7 or section 10 of the Prescription Ordinance and is not maintainable if not commenced within three years from the time after the cause of action shall have arisen."

statement: A person who applies for administration of an intestate’s estate and agrees to go to trial on issues involving her status is not entitled to challenge the jurisdiction of the Court after a decision is given, if there was no property of the deceased to be administered.
supporting_quote: Where a person claiming to be the wife of an intestate applied for administration to the District Court and agreed to go to trial on issues-involving questions of her status,- Held , that the party was not entitled afterwards to challenge the jurisdiction of the Court to give the decision invited by her, on the ground that there was no property of the deceased to be administered.

statement: The agreement between the husband and wife to secure a monthly payment was enforceable in law and not contrary to public policy.
supporting_quote: "There is nothing in the agreement or in the circumstances under which it was entered into which would justify one in holding that it had any improper object or purpose or that it was contrary to public policy or unenforceable at law."

statement: An order for the payment of compensation, made for the purpose of equalizing shares in a partition action, does not create such a charge over the portion of land allotted to the person liable to pay the compensation as to attach to it in the hands of a transferee for value.
supporting_quote: "There is no doubt as to the competency of a Commissioner, in carrying out a partition decreed by the Court; to award owelty in adjusting the values of the divided portions, but there is nothing in the Partition Ordinance, so far as I can see, to support the argument that a charge is thereby created over any of the divided portions."

statement: A person holding a general power of attorney from the assignee of an insolvent estate is not entitled to bring an action which an assignee may have brought. Where the attorney, who instituted the action, was himself a creditor of the estate and the relief claimed was on behalf of the general body of creditors, the Court should have permitted the plaintiff to ask for that relief in the alternative capacity, provided the facts in regard to that capacity had been pleaded.
supporting_quote: "Where the attorney, who instituted the action, was himself a creditor of the estate and the relief claimed was on behalf of the general body of creditors, the Court should have permitted the plaintiff to ask for that relief in the alternative capacity, provided the facts in regard to that capacity had been pleaded."

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift does not necessarily renounce the right to revoke by using the words 'for ever'.
supporting_quote: "Therefore I do hereby invest the said donees, Wimalahamy, Ram Menika, Mutu Menika, Siyatu Banda, and Punchappuhamy and their heirs, executors, administrators, and assigns with the full power and authority that they be owners from this date and possess the said premises hereby donated and all the right, title, and interest of me the said donor in and to the same for ever without any interruption whatsoever or deal with the same in whatsoever manner they may desire".

statement: A tenant who disclaims to hold of his landlord and puts him at defiance is not entitled to have the action dismissed for want of a valid notice to quit.
supporting_quote: "The appeal is allowed, the costs of appeal following the event of the further trial. Appeal allowed."

statement: To obtain an order under section 12 of Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, the petitioner must show that the respondent is a person bound by the decree.
supporting_quote: "It is essential, therefore, for the petitioner to show that the respondent was a person bound by the decree before he can be granted an order directing that she be removed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, s. 12.

statement: A reissued writ does not terminate the authority of a previous seizure and a fresh seizure is not necessary after the death of an execution-debtor if the property was under attachment at the time of death.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff sought to meet this by arguing that the seizure on March 11, 1924, terminated when the Fiscal returned the writ on June 6,1924, and that the reissue of the writ with fresh stamps was a fresh mandate to the Fiscal, that the seizure under the first issue of writ had ceased to be effective, that a fresh seizure was necessary and as this would be after the death of Kiri Menika the appointment of a legal representative was necessary. But these are all matters on which there is clear authority."

statement: A plaintiff is a necessary party where his instrument is duly registered and where, if the mortgage is duly registered, he has also registered an address for service.
supporting_quote: The plaintiff is a necessary party where his instrument is duly registered and where, if the mortgage is duly registered, he has also registered an address for service.

statement: A person who during the pendency of a hypothecary action purchases the property under mortgage, in execution of a money decree, may intervene under the provisions of section 6, sub-section (3), of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927, but such intervention may be permitted only before the distribution of proceeds of sale under the mortgage decree.
supporting_quote: "A person who during the pendency of a hypothecary action purchases the property under mortgage, in execution of a money decree, may intervene under the provisions of section 6, sub-section (3), of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927, but such intervention may be permitted only before the distribution of proceeds of sale under the mortgage decree."
statute_citation_verbatim: Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927, s. 6 (3)

statement: There was a failure of consideration on the mortgage bond due to de Vos' misappropriation of funds and his inability to discharge the prior mortgage.
supporting_quote: "Held , that under the circumstances there was a failure of consideration on the mortgage bond."

statement: The plaintiffs have a valid title to the land based on a Crown grant, and their possession of the land is continuous and uninterrupted.
supporting_quote: "There can be no question, therefore, that the plaintiffs and their predecessors in title have been in possession of this land and that that possession is ascribable to a grant of the entirety of this land from the Crown which apparently was vested with good title to the premises at the time of the grant."

statement: In a partition action, where the defendant was served with summons but failed to appear on the appointed day for trial, the court is required to proceed ex parte and investigate the title of the respective parties as far as practicable. The decree entered in such circumstances does not bind the absent defendant who can later move to set aside the decree.
supporting_quote: "Where, in a partition action, the defendant on service of summons was absent on the day appointed for his appearance, he is not entitled to receive notice of the day of trial. In such circumstances the Court is required to proceed to hear the evidence and investigate the title of the respective parties in so far as may be practicable by an ex parte proceeding."

statement: The Partition Ordinance does not contemplate partitioning more than one land in a single proceeding unless those lands are held in common by the same set of co-owners in the same proportions.
supporting_quote: "It is not contemplated by the provisions of the Partition Ordinance that any more than one land will be partitioned in one proceeding. An exception may be made in cases in which more than one allotment of land are held in common by the same set of co-owners in the same proportions."

statement: A decree entered in accordance with the provisions of the Partition Ordinance does not conclusively establish title against those who were not parties to the action if there was no proper investigation into title.
supporting_quote: "In D. C. Colombo, No. 46,980, the inquiry was certainly a perfunctory one, and having regard to the fact that the parties to the action were related to one another, the possibility of collusion cannot be excluded, for it is certainly remarkable that apparently none of the parties to this action had any knowledge of the fact that the premises in question had been sold for non-payment of rates before the action was instituted. In my opinion as there was no proper investigation into the title in this action, the decree does not affect the title of persons who were not parties to the action, and therefore the title vested in the Municipal Council must prevail."

statement: The Court may grant relief under section 756 of the Civil Procedure Code if there is a mistake, omission, or defect in complying with its provisions and the respondent has not been materially prejudiced.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that the respondent has been materially prejudiced here, as the security was deposited and the only question left was as to its sufficiency."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 756

statement: A judgment-creditor who purchases property at an execution sale may challenge earlier fraudulent transfers by the debtor, but should first attempt to have those transfers set aside before buying.
supporting_quote: "The proper course for the plaintiff to have adopted was to have seized and registered his seizure of lot 2. He should have had the first defendant examined under section 219 of the Civil Procedure Code and if he disclosed other property which was not claimed by others the plaintiff should have sold it and he would have then known whether lot 2 was needed to satisfy his claim."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 219 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: Service on a person holding a power of attorney from a party is insufficient.
supporting_quote: "It was conceded that the plaintiff who will be respondent upon the appeal to the Privy Council, had appointed an attorney in Ceylon with full powers to act for her, but it was argued that under the rule 5A of the Appellate Procedure Order service of the notice could not be effected upon her attorney."

statement: An action for damages for breach of warranty of goods delivered upon an unwritten contract of sale is not barred by the three-year limitation period under section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 22 of 1871.
supporting_quote: "A claim for damages for breach of warranty of goods delivered upon an unwritten contract of sale is not an action 'for or in respect of goods sold and delivered' within the meaning of section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 22 of 1871, and is not barred until after the lapse of three years after the cause of action shall have arisen."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 22 of 1871

statement: The test to be applied in ascertaining the value of the interest which the appeal involves is that referred to by Lord Selborne in Allan v. Pratt, where the judgment is to be looked at as it affects the interests of the party who is prejudiced by it and seeks to relieve himself from it by appeal.
supporting_quote: "the judgment is to be looked at as it affects the interests of the party who is prejudiced by it, and who seeks to relieve himself from it by appeal"

statement: A notice of seizure issued by the Fiscal on a mandate of sequestration does not create an interest in land within the meaning of section 6 (1) of Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, and is void as against a subsequent mortgage registered prior to its registration.
supporting_quote: "A notice of seizure cannot be said to create an interest in land. It is a notice prohibiting the owner of the property from transferring, alienating, or charging the property and all other persons from receiving the same by purchase, gift or otherwise"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 6 (1) of Ordinance No. 21 of 1927

statement: A co-owner cannot grant a servitude over a portion of the property owned in common without the concurrence of his other co-owners.
supporting_quote: "One of two co-owners cannot properly against the will of the other impose a servitude on an estate which is held in common in undivided shares."

statement: The right to use a threshing-floor is a servitude recognized in law.
supporting_quote: "The right to use a threshing-floor is a servitude recognized in law."

statement: The consideration for the deed was Rs. 42,500, which is the appraised value of the property.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that we are entitled to take into account not only the operative clause but also the recitals for this purpose. I do not think the affidavits add anything material to what is contained in the deed in question. Now, it is of great importance that the District Judge's order of May 21, 1934, confirming the sale has been annexed to the deed in question and forms part of that deed. That order shows that before the confirmation of the sale the Proctor for the plaintiffs quite properly pointed out to Court that it had been discovered that the primary mortgage had been discharged, although the discharge had not been registered. The Proctor went further and expressed his willingness to give credit for the appraised value of Soranawallie estate, viz., Rs. 42,500."

statement: Jus tertii as a defense is not available in cases filed for declaration of title and ejectment based on the provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Therefore this court finds that : (i) Jus tertii as a defence was not available to 1B to 4th Defendant-Appellants in view of the answers given by Court to issues (vii) and (viii)"

statement: A local manager or attorney has the power to sign a statement required for business registration under the Ordinance, even if the individual resides outside the Colony.
supporting_quote: "I regret I am unable to agree with the learned Judge as to his construction of sections 5 and 19 of the Ordinance on this point. Whether or not, as Mr. Hayley has argued, even in the absence of section 19 from the Ordinance, the local manager or attorney would have power to sign the statement it is not necessary to decide. I would hold therefore that there has been no failure to comply with the provisions of the Ordinance in this respect and would hold that this ground of appeal also must succeed."

statement: A person who lodges a caveat against the registration of an instrument affecting land, in which he has no Registrable interest, is liable in damages without proof of malice.
supporting_quote: "A person who lodges a caveat against the registration of an instrument affecting land, in which he has no Registrable interest, is liable in damages without proof of malice."

statement: A failure by the Fiscal to demand payment from the judgment-debtor renders a sale under a writ null and void.
supporting_quote: "If therefore the Fiscal has failed in this duty and this has been established to the satisfaction of the Court, I am of opinion that the sale held under the writ is null and void."

statement: A surety who renounces all benefits to which a surety is legally entitled can still be sued by the creditor after the principal debtor's property has been excused, unless there is an express agreement to the contrary.
supporting_quote: "Persons who have become 'security' for a debt for which a pledge or mortgage has been given may not be sued before the mortgaged property has been excussed, but only after such excussion for any balance that may remain due to the creditor .... unless it were expressly otherwise agreed upon".

statement: In the absence of an agreement, interest is not recoverable prior to the date of action in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "No judgment has been cited before us in which there has been the slightest departure from what appears to be the uniform rule that in the absence of agreement or of any positive rule of law interest is not recoverable in respect of the period prior to the date of action."

statement: A plaintiff may sue for interest without being barred from later suing for the principal, if the bond or mortgage provides for separate covenants for payment of interest and principal.
supporting_quote: "If we look at the mortgage bond, it clearly contains separate covenants as regards payment of interest and of principal. It provides that the mortgagors ' shall pay the interest of the said debt, every month, within the fifth of that month, commencing from the fifth of the current month May, 1921'. It then goes on to provide that the mortgagors and their heirs shall pay the principal amount, Rs. 5,000 and the interest due therefor to the mortgagee and his heirs whenever demanded: It is quite clear that here we have two independent covenants; and it leaves it open to the mortgagee to call in his mortgage money whenever he likes, or to leave it under mortgage with the mortgagors ; but the right to get the interest every month is specifically provided for and requires no demand whatsoever, for the interest is payable independently of demand on the fifth of every month."

statement: Under the Roman-Dutch law, a woman cannot recover property gifted by her to her paramour.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that the principle adopted by the Cape Supreme Court that it will not lend its power and authority to the enforcement of contracts made for illegal or immoral consideration is the correct view of the law. That Court, while admitting that there was a conflict of opinion arising from the Roman-Dutch law authorities, inclined to the view that a concubine or prostitute would not be able to sue for anything promised her in consideration of illicit intercourse; but that if the thing promised had been transferred, it could not be taken from the concubine or prostitute"

statement: Section 7(2)(b) of the Mortgage Ordinance, No. 21 of 1927 applies whether an application for letters of administration has been made or not, provided there is likely to be undue delay in the grant of representation.
supporting_quote: "The only point the Court has to decide is whether there is likely to be undue delay in the grant of the letters."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 21 of 1927, s. 7 (2) (b)

statement: A payment by one of several joint debtors operates as a payment to take the debt out of the Prescription Ordinance, as against all jointly liable with him.

statement: A tenant is entitled to remission of rent where the leased premises are closed due to a vis major or casus fortuitus, provided that the loss of enjoyment of the property is directly and immediately caused by such event.

statement: The Court has the power to fix the period within which money due under a mortgage decree is to be paid, or order such payment by instalments, either at the time of entering judgment or subsequently through section 12 of the Mortgage Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "In a mortgage action the Court, in entering judgment in favour of the plaintiff for the money due on the bond, has power to fix the period within which the money is to be paid or order such payment to be made by instalments. statement: A sale under the Partition Ordinance must be conducted according to specific procedures, including making a just valuation and setting an upset price.

statement: A Court has power to vacate the final decree entered in a partition action upon proof that summons had not been served upon a party to the action.

statement: A dowry deed, even though it may be a conveyance for value, is still considered a gift and must be stamped under Article 30 of the Schedule.

statement: This court may grant relief under section 756 of the Civil Procedure Code, even if formal notice was not given as required, if the Supreme Court deems it just and the respondent has not been materially prejudiced.

statement: An irregularity in the power of attorney does not vitiate proceedings unless it affects the merits of the case or the jurisdiction of the court.

statement: A warrant of attorney to confess judgment must be strictly construed and can only be used by the person or their heirs, executors, administrators, or assigns as specified in the warrant.

statement: A person who builds partly on his own land and partly on his neighbour's land has no right to claim compensation for the value of the building or a portion of it from the owner of the land encroached upon. statement: The charge for making and serving copies of a plaint should be based on the scale in the third schedule to the Civil Procedure Code, unless the process used significantly deviates from manual methods.

statement: An acquisition by gift from the father can no more be reasonably regarded as ancestral property than an acquisition from a stranger, and such an acquisition should then be presumed to be the son's self-acquired property, unless the gift is merely a mode of partition of the patrimony.

statement: An endorsement on a bond is not admissible as evidence against the pecuniary interest of the person making it unless it can be shown that it was made before the claim became barred by the law of limitation.

statement: A register kept by a Vel-Vidane for his own information and not in pursuance of an official duty imposed on him is not a public document within the meaning of section 74 of the Evidence Ordinance.

statement: The court has discretion to give preference to the more deserving party when two partition actions are pending.

statement: A public right claimed from time immemorial must be exercised of right and cannot originate by permission or usurpation of an act of pure neighborliness.

statement: A document produced for letters of administration with a copy of a will annexed must be proved in accordance with the Evidence Ordinance, specifically that it is a copy compared to the original.

statement: An action for damages arising from the breach of a lease agreement is barred by a previous judgment in an action to recover arrears of rent and cancel the lease, if the plaintiff could have included all claims within the first suit.

supporting_quote: "In my view the added first defendant's deed was duly registered so far as the plaintiff is concerned and this view is amply supported by authority. The case of Mudalihamy v. Punchibanda[ 1 5 Ceylon Law Recorder 73.] was very similar to this."

statement: A partition action should not be dismissed merely because the precept or order for the service of a summons was issued before the action was duly registered as a lis pendens in the correct folio.
supporting_quote: There is no provision in the Registration of Documents Ordinance that the action should be dismissed if the requirements of section 12 (1) are not complied with
statute_citation_verbatim: Registration of Documents Ordinance, No. 23 of 1927, s. 12 (1)

statement: The principle of the Roman-Dutch law that a debt is extinguished when the title of the creditor and debtor becomes united in the same person by operation of law does not apply in Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "The principle of the Roman-Dutch law that a debt is extinguished when the title of the creditor and debtor becomes united in the same person by operation of law does not apply in Ceylon."

statement: A minor who fraudulently represents himself to be of full age is bound by his contract under both Muslim and Roman-Dutch law.
supporting_quote: "Where, therefore, a Muslim minor enters into a contract with the consent of his natural guardian the contract is valid. The disability arose because he was under the patria potestas but when the father gave his consent then the contract was vaild."

statement: Prescription does not begin to run against a minor when the cause of action first arose, but rather from the date of execution of the instrument.
supporting_quote: The mortgage bond in this case did not provide for payment within any definite time. Therefore to use the common phrase, prescription began to run against Pootatamby from the date of the execution of the bond, and section 15 of the Ordinance does not avail the present plaintiff for the reason that that section is intended to serve a person who is under a disability at the time the cause of action first arose.

statement: The purchaser's remedy for obtaining possession from a party bound by the decree entered in his favor, who is not a necessary party to the mortgage action but has failed to register her address, can be treated as an order made under section 12(1) of the Mortgage Ordinance.
supporting_quote: In my opinion the order made by the District Judge is an order that he could have made under section 12 (1) of the Mortgage Ordinance.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 12 (1) of the Mortgage Ordinance

statement: A party with regard to whose title an order has been made prior to the date when the Interlocutory decree is entered, may appeal against the Interlocutory decree when that decree is in fact entered by the District Court.
supporting_quote: "It is clear from this decision that a party with regard to whose title an order has been made prior to the date when the Interlocutory decree is entered, may appeal against the Interlocutory decree when that decree is in fact entered by the District Court."

statement: In a partition action after interlocutory decree, the plaintiff is not bound to prove his title against each successive intervenient.
supporting_quote: "It would be monstrous to hold and there is no enactment and so far as I am aware, there is no decision which compels us to hold that in all partition actions, the plaintiff must prove his title afresh against every successive intervenient"

statement: The beneficial interest in the property passed to the heirs of P. Ibrahim Saibo through conveyances, and not by virtue of the partnership agreements.
supporting_quote: "With regard to issues 12A and 12B, I would hold that the heirs of P. Ibrahim Saibo did not become liable to convey their shares to the principal partners, or to the seventh to sixteenth defendants."

statement: An action to recover a sum due upon a hypothecation or mortgage is subject to the statute of limitations, even if the plaintiff has already obtained a judgment against an administrator.
supporting_quote: "The question is whether the present action is one for the recovery of any sum due upon any hypothecation or mortgage of any property. On the face of it, it certainly is such an action."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of Ordinance No. 22 of 1871

statement: The cause of action for a dowry gift promise arises when the defendant refuses to fulfill his promise, not at the time of marriage.
supporting_quote: "Now apart from the fact that the plaintiffs alleged that the defendant had confirmed his promise at the marriage in writing., it is quite clear from the evidence of the plaintiffs (the defendant did not give any evidence at all) that the defendant verbally renewed his promise from time to time till October, 1935, when he definitely refused to fulfil it. This refusal gave rise to the cause of action."

statement: An unregistered overseer is not a public officer who is bound by the General Orders of the Government, and an action may be brought to recover land purchased in breach of such orders.
supporting_quote: "An unregistered overseer is not a public officer who is bound by the General Orders of the Government. An action may be brought by a public officer to recover land purchased by him in the name of another in breach of the General Order which prohibits the acquisition of land without the sanction of Government."

statement: The Commissioner of Stamps has no power to go beyond the value expressed in the deed when determining stamp duty for a conveyance of a right to possess property, unless there is evidence that the stated value is an under-valuation.
supporting_quote: "Moreover, if the Commis�sioner so desires he has the power, under section 29 (2), for the purposes of arriving at his determination, to call for an affidavit or other evidence, which in this case he has not done. The Commissioner apparently based his determination upon a 'Government valuation of the lands affected by the deed ' which is set out as Rs. 40,750. and this sum, says Counsel for the appellant, is the value, not of the right to possess, but of the unencumbered land which is something which the deed does not give."

statement: A husband retains the right to mortgage property that forms part of the thediathetam under the thesawalamai, post-Ordinance No. 1 of 1911, and a wife is not a necessary party to a hypothecary action against her husband for such property.
supporting_quote: and that ruling binds us- that under the thesawalamai the husband has the same right to mortgage property which forms part of the thediathetam property, after the passing of Ordinance No. 1 of 1911, as he had before this Ordinance was enacted, and that the wife is not a necessary party to a hypothecary action against the husband on a mortgage effected by him in respect of thediathetam property, in order to make her interest in the property bound by the decree (Sangarapillai v. Devaraja Mudaliyar[1 38 N. L. R.I]. In that case, however, the wife was alive at the time of the decree and thereafter. In fact, it was she who took the point that she was not bound by the decree entered against her husband. In an earlier case (Ambalavanar v, Kurunathan[. 2 37 N. L. R. 286]. Poyser and Koch JJ. held that where after the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance of 1911 a husband mortgaged thediathetam property, and the mortgagee after the death of the wife put the bond in suit, without making the minor heirs of the wife who were in possession parties to the action, the heirs were not bound by the hypothecary decree

statement: The Supreme Court may order notice to be served on a party who was not made a party to the appeal if it is satisfied that the party would be affected by the appeal, under section 770 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: Where a person who was a party to an action in the lower Court is not made party to the appeal, the Supreme Court would in the exercise of its discretion under section 770 of the Civil Procedure Code order notice to be served on such party if the Court is satisfied that it was not quite clear to the appellant that the party in question would be affected by the appeal.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 770

statement: A vendor can sell property of another provided they do not act fraudulently, give vacant possession, and warrant against eviction.
supporting_quote: Now although a vendor's paper title may not account for all the shares that go to make a unit he may be able to make out a good prescriptive title. In this case, there is evidence to show that the vendor has been in possession of this land for long over the prescriptive period.

statement: Structures constituting a mill, once installed and intended to remain permanently fixed, become part of the land and pass with it upon sale.
supporting_quote: "The various structures which constituted the mill became part of the land on which they stood and that they passed to the second defendant by virtue of the bill of sale."

statement: An interlocutory appeal does not lie against the admission or rejection of evidence only, and such a rejection does not operate as an adjudication on the points raised in the appeal.
supporting_quote: "I do not think however, and no authority has been cited to us to show that we are precluded from dealing with this point in the final appeal No. 286. The interlocutory appeal, in my opinion, being an appeal against the rejection of evidence merely, was in any event wrongly constituted."

statement: A necessary party must be made a respondent to the appeal, and if not, it is a fatal irregularity.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the added plaintiffs were necessary parties to the appeal and that the failure to make them respondents to the appeal was a fatal irregularity."

statement: An account stated can give rise to a mutual agreement that the sum of Rs. 1,853.12 was due from defendant to plaintiff, creating an implied promise on the part of the defendant to pay this amount.
supporting_quote: "The only question is whether the defendant agreed to pay this amount. It was urged that the ledger account was not balanced at the time the defendant was alleged to have agreed to pay the amount due and that therefore there was no account stated. There is I think no room for this contention for the defendant admitted receiving the letter P 5 dated January 20, 1936, before he met the plaintiff about the dispute."

statement: An executor is entitled to claim the benefit of the Prescription Ordinance in Ceylon, even when he is not an express trustee under the will.
supporting_quote: This decision is in keeping with section 111 of our Trusts Ordinance, No. 9 of 1917, which mentions the cases where the Prescription Ordinance is inapplicable in respect of trusts, and adds in clause (5) �This section shall not apply to constructive trusts, except in so far as such trusts are treated as express trusts by the law of England�.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 111 of our Trusts Ordinance, No. 9 of 1917

statement: A Buddhist temple incumbent has the right to nominate his successor from among his pupils, and such nomination does not necessarily require a will or deed.
supporting_quote: "The incumbent of a Buddhist temple is entitled to nominate his successor from among his pupils. There is no requirement that such nomination should be by will or deed only."

statement: An incumbent of a temple cannot maintain an action for declaration of title to property belonging to the temple unless trustees have been appointed under Ordinance No. 19 of 1931.
supporting_quote: It seems clear, therefore, that the plaintiff as incumbent pure and simple cannot maintain this action.

statement: If a judgment-debtor has changed their place of residence and this change is not communicated to the Court, it suffices for the Fiscal's Officer to go to the place of residence mentioned in the plaint or answer.
supporting_quote: "I am, therefore, of opinion that, in the absence of any information given to the Court of a change of residence, it would be sufficient compliance with the terms of the section if the Fiscal's Officer went to the place of residence mentioned by the debtor in the plaint or answer."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 226 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: An unsuccessful claimant under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot maintain an action if they have parted with their rights to the property in dispute before the seizure.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff who has not even a shadow of a title, as he has divested himself to whatever title he had, cannot possibly establish a title superior to that of the judgment-debtor"
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code--Section 247

statement: A Court has power to order that the proceedings in an action in Ceylon be stayed pending the decision of a concurrent action in a Court outside Ceylon, where the matters in dispute are substantially the same. However, the Court will not exercise this power if there is no material on which the Court could form an opinion as to the law and legal procedure in the foreign court or if it cannot be justified that by proceeding with the action the plaintiff cannot obtain any advantage from it which he would not obtain in the foreign Court.
supporting_quote: "A Court has power to order that the proceedings in an action in Ceylon be stayed pending the decision of a concurrent action in a Court outside Ceylon, where the matters in dispute in the transactions are substantially the same. But the Court will not exercise this power where (a) there is no material on which the Court could form an opinion as to the law and legal procedure in the Court outside Ceylon, and (b) there is no material before the Court justifying the finding that by proceeding with the action the plaintiff cannot obtain any advantage from it which he would not obtain in the foreign Court."

statement: The contract between the plaintiffs and defendant was not a wagering contract, and thus the bond executed by the defendant to pay for the loss is enforceable.
supporting_quote: "Held , that the contract was not a wagering contract and that the bond was enforceable."

statement: Where land is divided into an eastern and western half by agreement, a conveyance for an undivided share of the eastern half conveys rights to that entire corpus, even if described as 'undivided' in the deed.
supporting_quote: "Admittedly what was possessed by the co-owners of that half was a divided eastern half, but, in possessing that half by arrangement, the co-owners, Sedris and Abilinu, who obtained that half under the deed in their favour. in 1924, were allowed to possess an extra portion over the western boundary of that half, so that the eastern half came to be regarded as a certain corpus which included the whole of the actual eastern half."

statement: A trust has been created in favor of the respondent, and the claim can be brought under section 6 of the Prescription Ordinance with a ten-year period.
