supporting_quote: "Now, as the legal ownership has to be vested in the person who is designated the owner, language, however forcible and full, may be invoked to vest that ownership without affecting the intention to create a trust in favour of another, and this will explain the use of the words 'absolutely forever'. This done, there must be words to indicate a beneficial enjoyment of the whole or part of that property by another. It would appear that the words 'out of the said lands and premises' satisfies this requirement."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 6 of the Prescription Ordinance

statement: The court held that the partnership could not be established without a written agreement, and that only a one-sixth share passed to each son for estate duty purposes.
supporting_quote: "Held , that the partnership could not be established in the absence of a written agreement. Pate v. Pate (18 N. L. R. 289) and Idroos v. Sheriff (27 N. L. R. 231) followed."

statement: The court held that the jus retentionis is a legal implication of the declaration in the decree that the improver was entitled to compensation, and not explicitly reserving it.
supporting_quote: "Moreover in this case the improver was authorized by the soil owner to continue in possession, and he or rather his representatives, were in possession of the buildings at the time the question of compensation arose in these proceedings inasmuch as the school was being conducted in them. They were persons interested in the allotment of the compensation tendered"

statement: Executors are not liable to pay interest on a legacy until there is a demand, and lack of funds may be pleaded as an excuse for mora in which case the estate will not be liable to pay interest.
supporting_quote: The principles that appear to be deducible from the various authorities on Roman-Dutch law examined by me and relevant to the present case are- (a) Where the obligation to pay a legacy is suspended until an uncertain date or an uncertain condition (e.g., marriage of the legatee), the executors cannot be put in mora except by demand. (b) That such demand, if extra-judicial should be more or less of a formal nature. (c) That interest runs only from date of mora. (d) That in certain circumstances lack of funds may be pleaded as an excuse by the executors for their mora in which case the estate will not be liable to pay interest.

statement: When a sale is conducted by an auctioneer acting on orders of the Court and subject to conditions approved by the Court, the question that arises in setting aside the sale or refusing to confirm it is whether the Judge is exercising his discretion properly and judicially.
supporting_quote: I do not think he is limited to the grounds upon which sales held by the Fiscal are set aside. In this instance in the view taken by the Judge of what actually happened on the occasion of this sale, it is impossible for us to say that he has exercised his discretion in a wrong or improper manner and, therefore, we ought not to interfere with his order.

statement: The court ruled that the plaintiffs have not established a right of way over or the right to use the piece of land described as a bus park, and thus their action fails.
supporting_quote: I do not think this contention is sound. It seems to me to confuse a public stand which is part of a highway and a public stand which is not part of a highway.

statement: The right to a retransfer of immovable property under a deed is movable property, and the seizure and sale were correctly made according to the Roman-Dutch law.
supporting_quote: "On this point there is the authority of van der Keessel Select Theses, Book 2, chap. 1, sec. 14, para. 178-179 . The -translation of this is to be found in Lorensz's van der Keessel at. p. 59."

statement: The beneficial interest in property purchased by a partnership remains with the surviving partners upon the death or retirement of a partner, and becomes an asset of any new partnership formed.
supporting_quote: On the death or retirement of a partner the beneficial interest in the property remained to the surviving partners, and on the formation of a new partnership such beneficial interest became an asset of the. new partnership for the purpose of its business.

statement: When the effect of a statute is merely to limit the time within which an action may be brought and not to extinguish the right, the court will not take the statute into account unless it is specially pleaded by way of defence.
supporting_quote: "It is settled law that when, as in the case of sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the Prescription Ordinance, the effect of the statute is merely to limit the time in which an action may be brought and not to extinguish the right, the court will not take the statute into account unless it is specially pleaded by way of defence."

statement: The claim for a conveyance under the terms of P1 was not prescribed as prescription began to run from the date on which the demand for the conveyance was refused.
supporting_quote: "Held , that prescription commenced to run against the plaintiff from the date on which his demand for a conveyance was refused. Ismail v. Ismail (22 N. L. R. 476 ) followed."

statement: An action for declaration of a status is barred unless it is brought within three years from the time when the cause of action arose.
supporting_quote: "It was contended for the defendants, who have appealed from this order, that the action was one for declaration of a status which was barred in three years and that the District Judge was wrong in deciding the issue on the footing that the period of prescription was ten years."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 11 of the Prescription Ordinance, No. 22 of 1871

statement: The Archbishop of Colombo is entitled to maintain an action for the recovery of income from property belonging to a church, even if he does not claim beneficial interest in the property.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that if the plaintiff, who is called the manager of the temple, has control of the fabric of the temple and of the property belonging to it, he has such possession as would enable him or even entitle him to maintain an action, even though he makes no pretence of claiming the beneficial interest of the temple Or its property, but is only the trustees for the congregation who worship there".

statement: A buyer who purchases a defined parcel of land with all reasonable and necessary access to the road is not entitled to claim an additional right of way to a specific portion of it, even if that portion was previously separate.
supporting_quote: "Even if lots X and Y consisted of two parcels, it is quite open to an owner to amalgamate them and sell them as one parcel by reference to a plan made for the purpose or by description, and a buyer who purchases the lots as one parcel is not entitled to say, ‘I must have another way of access to a portion of it, which by reason of the configuration of the land I can use as a separate portion’."

statement: An action for use and occupation does not lie against a person who was given possession of land in pursuance of an agreement to purchase the land which was not completed through no default on his part.
supporting_quote: An action for use and occupation does not lie against a person who was given possession of land in pursuance of an agreement to purchase the land which was not completed through no default on his part.

statement: An application to sell mortgaged property under a mortgage decree is not governed by section 337 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Now, on an order to sell mortgaged property the Commissioner has an unfettered power to sell the mortgaged property. He need not make any demand for the payment of money nor is it necessary for him to observe the requirements of sections 237 and 256."

statement: A warrant of attorney to confess judgment must adhere strictly to the form prescribed in section 31 of the Civil Procedure Code and cannot include additional provisions.
supporting_quote: "I think that this argument is sound. The District Judge was of opinion that the use of the word 'may' in section 31 enabled a creditor to obtain a warrant in a form other than the one given in the Code. If the position had been that the Code was merely recognizing the validity of warrants of attorney, which otherwise by implication might be held to have been repealed by the Code, then of course it may be argued that the form of the warrant was of no consequence, but if that were the position, the language used in section 31 is inapt. I think that the section merely says that a warrant of attorney may or may not be given, but if given, it should be in the form 12 in the Schedule."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 31 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A warrant of attorney to confess judgment is invalid if the proctor attesting it was not expressly named by and attending at the request of the person executing the document.
supporting_quote: "One important requirement in this section is that the proctor must attend 'on behalf of the defendant'. There are authorities under the similar enactment in 1 & 2 Victoria, c. 110, relating to warrants of attorney and cognovits."

statement: The failure of the Fiscal to demand payment under section 226 of the Code does not render the seizure and sale a nullity, nor is it grounds for a separate action.
supporting_quote: "On a consideration of all these authorities, I am of opinion that the fact that no demand was made by the Fiscal under section 226 of the Code does not deprive the Court of jurisdiction and render the seizure and sale thereafter a nullity, and that it is not open to any person to seek to attack the seizure and sale on that ground in a separate action."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 226 of the Code

statement: An improver who purchases a lot at a price below the assessed value of his improvements is not entitled to the full value of those improvements but must contribute proportionately to other improvers' claims.
supporting_quote: "The Court should provide in the conditions of sale that, in the event of the sale realizing less than the appraised value, the purchaser shall pay the improvers in full or that an improver shall not buy at less than the appraised value of the improvements."

statement: When a court has to decide a question of res judicata in respect of the shares allotted to the parties in a previous partition action, the decree alone need be considered. However, if the decree contains an arithmetical error, it may be construed with reference to the judgment.
supporting_quote: "Where a Court has to decide a question of res judicata in respect of the shares allotted to the parties in a previous partition action the decree alone need be considered. But where the decree contains an arithmetical error, it may be construed with reference to the judgment."

statement: Where a person executed three deeds of gift on the same day and certain lands donated by one deed were included in another, the earlier deed must prevail.
supporting_quote: Where a person executed three deeds of gift in favour of three sons on the same day and where certain lands donated by one deed were included in another,- Held, that the earlier deed must prevail and that there was a presumption that the Notary did his duty properly and that he numbered them in the order in which they were executed.

statement: The deed conveyed a bare dominium of the land to the trustees of the mosque with a right of usufruct to a one-fourth share, and as there was no grant to the children or an acceptance of the gift by them, they would inherit as on an intestacy and a lease by them would be binding on their heirs.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the deed conveyed a bare dominium of the land to the trustees of the mosque with a right of usufruct to a one-fourth share. Held, further, that as there was no grant to the children or an acceptance of the gift by them they would inherit as on an intestacy and a lease by them would be binding on their heirs."

statement: The burden of proving the testator's mental competency at the time of making a will shifts to the objector if there is nothing intrinsically unnatural in the document and it has been duly executed.
supporting_quote: If, after proof of due execution, there is nothing intrinsically unnatural in the document, the burden is shifted to the objector to show that there was undue influence or fraud or that the deceased was not of a sound disposing mind when he made the will.

statement: A spouse can acquire the other spouse's property for valuable consideration, and such acquisition is considered tediatetam property.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion, in view of the language used, that it is not possible for us to say that it does not cover the case of one spouse acquiring property from the other for valuable consideration"

statement: A deed creating a fidei commissum must clearly designate the parties to be benefited, and cannot use vague or general terms like 'heirs descending from her, and authorized persons such as executors, administrators, and assigns'.
supporting_quote: "Since that date there has been a welter of decisions on fidei commissa , some of which have gone the length of saying that once an intention to create a fidei commissum is apparent, words like assigns, executors and administrators should be treated as �surplusage� or notarial flourish and struck out or ignored. I can see no justification for taking such liberties with words chosen by parties or their agents."

statement: A lessor under a hire-purchase agreement is entitled to retake possession of the property if the hirer defaults, provided no more force than necessary is used.
supporting_quote: "The evidence of the plaintiff's husband indicates that no force was employed in the seizure of the lorry. It is impossible, therefore,. to support the judgment of the learned District Judge."

statement: An individual does not cease to exercise a profession and commence an employment when they transition from being an assistant to a partner in the same firm, provided their professional qualifications remain applicable.
supporting_quote: The position of the assessee would have been similar if he had entered into agreements with a large number of clients to attend to their work. He has not done that. On the contrary, he has accepted a post resting on a contract.

statement: A deed of gift can create one fidei commissum by which the property is to devolve on the donees and their children, grandchildren, &c., so long as there are any such in existence.
supporting_quote: "In my view, the terms of the deed of gift in the case before us indicate more strongly the intention of the donor to create one fidei commissum by which the property was to devolve on the donees and their children, grandchildren, &c., so long as there were any such in existence."

statement: Misrepresentation that is honest and not reckless does not entitle the party making it to be liable for damages, even if material to the contract.
supporting_quote: ". . . . But if a man makes a representation in the honest belief that it is true, and there is reasonable ground for such belief, a fraudulent intent will not be imputed to him, although the representation may turn out to be false. In other words, it may be laid down that misrepresentation not amounting to fraud, that is, misrepresentation which is honest and not reckless, will not render the party making it liable to the legal consequences of fraud, although he may be liable for misrepresentation"

statement: A mortgage of an undivided share is protected by section 12 of the Partition Ordinance, even if not disclosed in a partition action.
supporting_quote: "I think it follows from these sections that any mortgage, which has not been excluded in consequence of a finding in the partition case, must be regarded as having force and effect in spite of the partition or sale."

statement: A mortgagor can redeem the mortgage bond at any time during the period for which interest has been paid in advance, provided they do not waive their right to claim overpaid interest.
supporting_quote: "Payment of interest in advance on a mortgage bond does not fetter the mortgagor's right of redemption during the period for which the payment in advance is made. Where a mortgagor who has paid interest in advance exercises his right of redemption during the period for which the payment in advance is made and, while paying the capital in full, makes it clear that he does not waive his right to claim the interest overpaid. Held, that he is entitled by means of the condictio sine causa to recover such interest."

statement: A decision is res judicata between co-defendants when a plaintiff cannot obtain the relief he claims without an adjudication between the defendants, and such an adjudication is made not only between the plaintiff and the defendants but also between the defendants.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion formed after a careful examination of the authorities on the subject, the principle that a decision is not res judicata between co-defendants is subject to two exceptions : (a) When a plaintiff cannot obtain the relief he claims without an adjudication between the defendants and such an adjudication is made, not only between plaintiff and the defendants, but also between the defendants."

statement: The bond tendered as security for respondents' costs is invalid if it does not conform with the requirements of section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 or Ordinance No. 17 of 1852.
supporting_quote: "I accordingly hold that the bond in this case is invalid, as it does not conform with the requirements of section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840, or of Ordinance No. 17 of 1852."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 or Ordinance No. 17 of 1852

statement: A judgment which would amount to res judicata between plaintiff and defendant is not necessarily so between defendants inter se.
supporting_quote: It must be conceded that a judgment which would amount to res judicata between plaintiff and defendant is not necessarily so between defendants inter se.

statement: A conveyance of immovable property by a trustee to the person beneficially entitled to it falls under item 23 (4) of Schedule A, Part I. of the Stamp Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "So far as the transferors are concerned, there is no right, interest, profit or benefit accruing to them, and in regard to the transferees there is not apparent or conceivable any forbearance given or shown, or any detriment or loss suffered, or any responsibility undertaken by them. Once the directors of the Portmore Tea Company resolved that the Company be wound up voluntarily, and appointed a liquidator for the purpose, the resulting position was that this Company held its assets in order that the debts and liabilities of the Company might be paid and thereafter distribution made of what remained in specie or in kind among the contributories of the Company. In other words, it might justifiably be said that the Portmore Tea Company held its remaining assets in trust for those beneficially entitled to them."

statement: The property involved, which was money due under an insurance policy, is considered 'pudgalika' property acquired by the deceased for his exclusive personal use and thus falls under Section 23 of the Buddhist Temporalities Ordinance of 1931.
supporting_quote: "I do not think we can accept the interpretation contended for by the appellants. The next point urged for the appellants is that this was not property acquired by the deceased for his exclusive personal use. It was contended that the word 'use' was equivalent to 'user', and that the property referred to was such as was needed for his personal enjoyment, or to put it in another way, that it was property which the priest himself used or intended to use for himself."
statute_citation_verbatim: "23. All pudgalika property that is acquired by any individual bhikkhu for his exclusive personal use, shall, if not alienated by such bhikkhu during his lifetime, be deemed to be the property of the temple to which such bhikkhu belonged unless such property had been inherited by such bhikkhu"

statement: Section 615 of the Civil Procedure Code does not provide a husband with the right to apply for modification of an order for monthly payment of alimony when such an order is secured by the hypothecation of property.
supporting_quote: "Section 615 of the Civil Procedure Code gives no right to a husband to apply for the modification of an order for the monthly payment of alimony when the order is accompanied by a direction that the payment should be secured by the hypothecation of property."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 615

statement: The reopening of a transaction is barred by section 3 of the Money Lending Ordinance if an account was stated six years before the date of the action.
supporting_quote: "Where an account was stated six years before the date of the action, the reopening of that transaction is barred by section 3 of the Money Lending Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 3 of the Money Lending Ordinance (Chapter 67)

statement: Acceptance of rent after the institution of an action to enforce a forfeiture does not amount to a waiver of the right to claim a forfeiture.
supporting_quote: "Where an action is brought to enforce a forfeiture of a lease for failure to pay rent, acceptance of rent after the institution of the action does not amount to a waiver of the right to claim a forfeiture."

statement: An assignment of a mortgage bond does not discharge the bond, allowing the plaintiff to sue on it.
supporting_quote: Held, that the assignment of the bond did not operate as a discharge of the bond and that the plaintiff was entitled to sue on the bond.

statement: For a deed of gift between Muslims to be valid under the Muslim law, there must be an immediate transfer of dominium and possession must pass to the donee.
supporting_quote: "In the case of Muslims, where the deed of gift manifests an intention to make an immediate transfer of the dominium, the Muslim law is applicable. In such a case, if possession is not given by the donor to the donee, one of the conditions essential under the Muslim law has not been complied with, and the deed of gift is invalid."

statement: Where a power of attorney contains recitals that indicate the purpose for which it was given, and this purpose is the management of a specific business, with the cessation of that business, the authority granted under the power of attorney is automatically cancelled.
supporting_quote: "The phraseology of the recitals indicated, therefore, that the purpose for which the power was given was the management of the plaintiff's business as a timber merchant and restrained the generality of the operative part. With the closing down of that business the authority of the second defendant to act under the power of attorney was automatically cancelled."

statement: A prescriptive right of way cannot be established over a new route unless there is either ten years user or a notarially executed agreement, and the old route must be abandoned.
supporting_quote: 'The question as to whether the prescriptive rights of the plaintiffs with regard to the old route attached after the deviation to the new route has been argued before me by reference to Voet and a number of decisions of this Court. It would be idle to pretend that I have not found considerable difficulty in reconciling those decisions.'

statement: A document purporting to be a 'true copy' of a copy of the original power of attorney copied by a registering officer in a book kept under the Indian Registration Act, 1908 is not in itself sufficient to establish the fact of execution of the original power of attorney when it does not come under section 85 or section 78(6) of the Evidence Ordinance and when it is inadmissible under section 82.
supporting_quote: "A document purporting to be a 'true copy' of a copy of the original power of attorney copied by a registering officer in a book kept under the Indian Registration Act, 1908 is not in itself sufficient to establish the fact of execution of the original power of attorney when it does not come under section 85 or section 78 (6) of the Evidence Ordinance and when it is inadmissible under section 82."

statement: A Court has no power to enlarge the period given by section 84 of the Civil Procedure Code within which a plaintiff is bound to show cause against a decree nisi entered against him being made absolute.
supporting_quote: "A Court has no power to enlarge the period given by section 84 of the Civil Procedure Code within which a plaintiff is bound to show cause against a decree nisi entered against him being made absolute."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 84.

statement: A court may refuse to grant a conveyance where no specific provision of the law empowers it, and such action is based on equity, justice, and good conscience.
supporting_quote: It is the power and duty of the Court in cases where no specific rule exists, to act according to equity, justice, and good conscience, though in the exercise of such power it must be careful to see that its decision is based on sound general principles and is not in conflict with them or the intentions of the Legislature.

statement: A mortgage executed while the registration of a seizure is in force, is void as against the Fiscal's transferee if such mortgage is merely a renewal in whole or in part and not in excess of a mortgage existing prior to registration.
supporting_quote: "The provisions of section 238 do not, in my opinion, operate to give a purchaser a title free of a mortgage executed while the registration of a seizure is in force, if such mortgage is merely a renewal, in whole or in part and not in excess, of a mortgage existing prior to the registration."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 238.

statement: Where a deed has been admitted in evidence without objection at the trial, no objection that it has not been duly proved could be entertained in appeal.
supporting_quote: It is to be noted that no objection was taken to this docu�ment at the trial, and that the objection was taken for the first time in appeal.

statement: A defendant is not entitled to bring in the vendors of land as parties defendants in an action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code solely to obtain a rectification of the deed on which he relies, even if the error was discovered only after the institution of the case.
supporting_quote: "In this case if the motion of the defendant is allowed he in reality, becomes the plaintiff in a distinct cause of action against the new parties and the resulting position is the same as if two plaintiffs have joined in respect of distinct causes of action, and what is more against two different defendants."

statement: The court held that gifts made to heirs, which were intended as dowry or additional dowry, are not subject to collation under the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (Cap. 48) Section 33.
supporting_quote: "I value all the donations at half the face value on the deeds. . . . and hold second, fourth, sixth, and seventh respondents to be entitled to the balance, if any, to make up their shares of the estate. . . . Those respondents are to state in writing within three weeks of the delivery of this order whether they will be satisfied with what they have already received or claim a share of the estate on the terms I lay down"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 33 of Chapter 48

statement: A deed of gift to a concubine is not necessarily invalid under Roman-Dutch law, and the revocation of such a gift must be supported by evidence that it was made for immoral consideration.
supporting_quote: "The principle adopted by the Cape Supreme Court is that it will not lend its power and authority to the enforcement of contracts made for illegal or immoral consideration. Hence a concubine or prostitute would not be able to sue for anything promised her in consideration of illicit intercourse."

statement: A court's decision, even if erroneous or irregular, does not render it incompetent to deliver a decree.
supporting_quote: "The competency or jurisdiction of the Court cannot possibly depend on whether a point which it decides has been raised or argued by a party or Counsel. An express decision upon the construction of sections 17 and 20 and an implied decision must stand on the same footing."

statement: A fidei commissum was created by the will, with a half share going to Pitchammal's husband and the other half to her relatives in the paternal line.
supporting_quote: "I hold for the reasons given by me that by the last will the testator has given legal effect to his intention that the property in the first instance should devolve on Pitchammal subject to a fidei commissum in favour of her children and that Pitchammal should have no power to alienate the property."

statement: A deed of gift creates a fidei commissum residui and possibly a fidei commissum simple if the words 'to deal with the same at will and pleasure' are interpreted to mean that the donee is given the right not only to possess but also to deal with the lands otherwise to the extent of the estate donated.
supporting_quote: "Any apparent repugnancy is eliminated when these words are interpreted to mean that the donee is given the right not only to possess the lands but also the right to deal with them otherwise to the extent of the estate donated to him (in this case the estate of a fidei commissarius)."

statement: The Thesawalamai paragraph 11 has been repealed by the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (Cap. 48), and the father's natural rights to custody should be recognized.
supporting_quote: "With all respect I would submit that guardianship of the children is only incidentally referred to and that it was not intended to be dealt with at all."

statement: The defendant-respondent's claim for compensation for improvements on the land is valid, and the learned Commissioner’s assessment of Rs. 2 per tree may need adjustment based on the provisions of the Definition of Boundaries Ordinance.
supporting_quote: I hold, therefore, that the learned Commissioner was right on his finding of fact, which the evidence supported, to award the defendant-respondent compensation for his trees. The plaintiff's appeal on this point, therefore, fails. There remains, however, still one further matter for consideration. If the defendant-respondent is entitled to compensation for his improvements to this chena land has the learned Commissioner applied a correct assessment in awarding a sum of Rs. 2, per tree?

statement: A deed of gift executed by Muslims, where the deed manifests an intention to make an immediate transfer of dominium, should be construed according to Muslim law.
supporting_quote: "constrained to hold that in the case of Muslims, where the deed of gift manifests an intention to make an immediate transfer of the dominium, the Muslim law is applicable"

statement: A party to a partition action cannot acquire a prescriptive title to a divided portion of the land during the pendency of the action to enable him to give a valid title to such divided portion to a purchaser.
supporting_quote: "A party to a partition action cannot acquire a prescriptive title to a divided portion of the land during the pendency of the action to enable him to give a valid title to such divided portion to a purchaser."

statement: A certificate of no claim is a registrable instrument and should be considered in determining the priority of land titles.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, a certificate of no claim is a registrable instrument. Section 6 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance says that in Chapter III. of that Ordinance instrument means instrument affecting land, unless the context otherwise requires. Section 8 enumerates instruments that shall be deemed to affect land, and among the enumerated classes are" deeds or other instruments for establishing or transferring any security, interest or encumbrance affecting any land (other than a lease at will, or for any period not exceeding one month)"."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance and Section 8 of the Encroachments upon Crown Lands Ordinance (Cap. 231)

statement: A deed dealing with a divided lot of a larger land falls under proviso (a) of section 15(1) when there are earlier registrations affecting the larger land, and must be registered in a separate folio connecting it with the entry relating to the whole area by cross-references.
supporting_quote: "Now section 14 (7) shows how the registrar is to obtain the information with regard to earlier registrations. It provides that 'any instrument (except a will) presented for registration (shall contain) a reference to the volume and folio in which some earlier instrument relating to the same land is registered if such reference is known to the notary'."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 14 and 15 and Regulation 14

statement: A trustee who has acted honestly but not reasonably is not entitled to relief under section 31 of the Trusts Ordinance.
supporting_quote: A trustee, who has acted honestly but not reasonably is not entitled to rehef under section 31 of the Trusts Ordinance.
statute_citation_verbatim: Trusts Ordinance (Cap. 72), ss. 15 and 31

statement: A plaintiff is not entitled to maintain an action quia timet against a defendant who has merely purchased the right and title of a judgment-debtor at a Fiscal's sale, without obtaining a Fiscal's transfer.
supporting_quote: "I do not think the act of the defendant in buying at the Fiscal's sale amounted either to a 'denial' of the plaintiffs' rights or the 'infliction of an affirmative injury' on them."

statement: The sale of premises includes the air space above the land conveyed, unless otherwise specified in the conveyance.
supporting_quote: "Can it be said that there is anything to the contrary in the conveyances in this case ? Counsel for the respondent argues that the references to the premises as bearing assessments numbers 212 and 216, respectively, taken in conjunction with the description of the whole premises as being in accordance with plan D 1 must be so regarded. But I think it is a very strong point in favour of the plaintiff that the actual conveyances of the particular blocks in question were made in accordance with plan P 3, and in that plan the reference to the first floor is (I think, deliberately) omitted."

statement: Section 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure should be interpreted liberally, but only in matters directly arising from the contract itself and quite subsidiary to it.
supporting_quote: "I do not see that a different principle applies in this case. If the intervention be allowed, then quite a separate matter will become the main subject of inquiry, in fact the sole matter of inquiry."

statement: An application for execution of a decree more than ten years after the date of the decree is barred by section 337, unless it can be shown that the application is merely to carry out a subsisting seizure.
supporting_quote: "In view of the rules enunciated in these cases, the crucial question for consideration, in the present instance, is whether this application 'is a step in the former proceedings or an entirely new step' or, in other words, whether the application can be made referable to an existent seizure."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 337 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A decree-holder who attempts to purchase property in execution of a mortgage decree through a nominee without obtaining the previous sanction of the Court is not entitled to equitable relief.
supporting_quote: "It is clear from this section that the condition, which entitles a purchaser to bid for and purchase the property in execution, is the obtaining of 'previous sanction' by the Court. No other section has been cited, nor have I found any other section which empowers a decree-holder to purchase."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 272.

statement: A co-owner cannot establish a prescriptive title against another co-owner unless there is evidence of an ouster or something equivalent to an ouster, and the possession must be exclusive for more than ten years before the institution of the action.
supporting_quote: "His possession was in law the possession of his co-owners. It was not possible for him to put an end to that possession by any secret intention in his mind. Nothing short of ouster or something equivalent to ouster could bring about that result."

statement: When there is a conflict between the recitals and the operative part of a conveyance, the terms of the operative part should decide the question.
supporting_quote: "It is a well settled principle of construction of an instrument that the recitals are subordinate to the operative part, and consequently when the operative part is clear it is treated as expressing the intention of the parties and it prevails over any suggestion of a contrary intention afforded by the recitals."

statement: A purchaser at a sale in execution of undivided interests pending partition proceedings is entitled to the share allotted to the judgment debtor, even if the Fiscal's conveyance is for an undivided share.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, the facts in this case cannot be distinguished from those in Markar v. Siman (supra). I am, therefore, of opinion that the appellant is entitled to the relief which he claims."

statement: A minor cannot adiate an inheritance and is not liable to be sued for the debts of an ancestor, but this does not preclude suing devisees directly if they are in possession of the property.
supporting_quote: "the second defendant is a minor and is joined as a defendant on the footing of his being an heir, but a minor cannot adiate an inheritance and is not liable to be sued for the debts of an ancestor."

statement: A co-debtor cannot as a rule be made liable in solidum unless there is a special agreement to that effect.
supporting_quote: "In the absence of evidence of such intention, the parties, even in the earlier civil law, were not correi but were each entitled or liable only in respect of his rateable share. in the Roman-Dutch Law, following herein the -latest Roman Law, a co-debtor cannot as a rule be made liable in solidum unless there is a special agreement to that effect."

statement: A judge may form the opinion that a transfer of property was made with intent to defeat or delay creditors, even if no specific evidence is presented in court.
supporting_quote: "The simple position therefore is whether the admitted facts disclose acts of insolvency. A man is presumed to intend the natural consequences of his acts. The admitted acts are capable of more than one construction and no argument was addressed to the Judge to show that his view of them was wrong."

statement: Where a strip of land within the boundaries of a larger plot is prohibited from building, its value as a building site should be assessed based on potential alternative uses, with any restrictions affecting its value being considered.
supporting_quote: No doubt it must be borne in mind that the strip in question in fact forms part of a large land, but the physical infirmities or legal restrictions attaching to the strip in question must be taken into account in determining the value of the strip. This case must accordingly be decided on the basis that there was a prohibition against erecting buildings on the strip in question.

statement: A legacy paid under the last will of a deceased person does not form part of the statutory income of a beneficiary within the meaning of section 11(11) of the Income Tax Ordinance and is not liable to tax in the hands of the legatee.
supporting_quote: "This sum cannot be caught up under section 11 (11) far two reasons: (1) It is 'a capital sum. (2) The wife of the assessee, i.e. the person receiving the legacy, is not a beneficiary of the estate of a deceased person."
statute_citation_verbatim: Income Tax Ordinance (Cap. 188), s. 11 (1I).

statement: A person governed by the Tesawalamai must affirmatively establish that they are an inhabitant of Jaffna, and this determination is based on the facts of each case.
supporting_quote: "As the Tesawalamai is a custom in derogation of the common law, any person who alleges that it is applicable to him must affirmatively establish the fact"

statement: The second and third defendants are entitled to concurrence, and share rateably in the proceeds from realizing the security.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the second and third defendants were entitled to concurrence and, in case of deficiency, to share rateably in the proceeds to be obtained when the security was realized."

statement: A deed of gift between Muslims can be valid under the general law even if it does not conform to Mohamedan law, provided that the terms of the deed are consistent with a transaction known and recognized by the general law.
supporting_quote: "But if there are terms in it inconsistent with Mohamedan law, but known to and recognized by the general law, the inference is that it was not intended that there should be a valid gift as understood in the Mohamedan law. but that the donor intended to produce the particular transaction known to and recognized by the general law, and if he has produced it, effect will be given to the deed under that law."

statement: Courts have the discretion to allow parties to compromise their disputes after a full investigation of title, provided that the Court is satisfied that all parties entitled to interests in the land are before it and are solely entitled to it.
supporting_quote: "A number of decisions of this Court have emphasized the duty of the Court to investigate title fully and not treat a partition action as an action. inter partes. The emphasis is always on the necessity to investigate title."

statement: The court should disregard the existence of mortgages when distributing proceeds from a sale under the Partition Ordinance, as this would lead to manifest injustice.
supporting_quote: "to interpret the words 'shares' in the narrow sense contended for would offend against the scheme of the Partition Ordinance and would lead to manifest injustice"

statement: The defendants cannot raise the issue of damages on appeal as they failed to file a cross-appeal or give notice under section 772(1) of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "The respondents have neither cross-appealed nor have they given the appellants notice that they take any objection to that part of the appeal which dismissed their claim in reconvention. Mr. Weerasooria has invited our attention to the case of Rabat v. de Silva[ 8 N. L. R. 82.] which he maintains is an authority for the proposition that notice of objection is not required. In this case the District Judge held that the fifth and sixth defendants could not succeed to the estate of Vincent Perera on the ground that they were his children as the result of his adulterous intercourse with the third defendant. The plaintiffs' claim was dismissed on other grounds. The plaintiffs appealed and the Court held that the fifth and sixth defendants, notwithstanding they had not appealed nor filed objections under section 772 (1) of the Civil Procedure Code, could challenge the District Judge's decision as to their paternity and contend that they were not adulterous bastards and support the decree appealed from by claiming the shares devised to them on that ground. In coming to this conclusion, Middleton J. subjected section 772 (1) to a minute examination. He stated that the section divides itself into two parts, comprising support of and objection to the decree. No notice is required except upon an objection to the decree."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 772(1) of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The cause of action to recover money from a guardian who has received funds on behalf of minors accrued when the guardian failed to pay the amount within a reasonable time after receiving it.
supporting_quote: "A. A. Goonewardene could and should have paid the money into Court immediately after he received it. The breach of the agreement to pay the money to the minors, therefore, occurred about January 31, 1935, and the cause of action to recover the money from A. A. Goonewardene accrued to the plaintiff about that time."

statement: An agreement by a borrower to pay money and allow the lender to possess land in lieu of interest, even if non-notarial, can be used to prove an action to recover money and prevent prescription from running.
supporting_quote: In an. action to recover money lent, an agreement by the borrower to pay the money and to allow the lender to possess a land in lieu of interest may be proved in order to prevent the running of prescription, although the agreement is non-notarial, Nagamuthu v. Sittambarampillai (33 N. L. R. 151), followed.

statement: The defendants cannot acquire prescriptive title against the plaintiffs due to insufficient evidence of possession and the limitation period not being met.
supporting_quote: "There is another difficulty in the way of the defendants -setting up prescriptive title against the appellants. Even assuming that the defendants commenced their adverse possession from October, 1923, they had only five years' possession in 1928, when Philippu executed deed P 2, reserving a life-interest in his favour. Could they rely on that possession or on the adverse possession from 1928, till Philippu's death in 1932, in support of their prescriptive title?"

statement: Where one co-owner conveys the entire premises held in common and the grantee enters into possession under the Conveyance claiming title to the whole premises, such possession is adverse to the co-tenants of the granter.
supporting_quote: The learned writer seems to be of the view that when one of several tenants in common conveys the entire premises held in common and the grantee enters into possession under the conveyance claiming title to the whole premises, such possession is adverse to the co-tenants of the granter and consequently at the expiration of the period of limitation they will be barred.

statement: In computing the period of thirty days within which an application for leave to appeal should be made under Rule 2 of Schedule 1 of the Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance, the days included in a vacation of the Supreme Court should not be reckoned.
supporting_quote: "For the same reasons that are given in the judgment of Poyser J., in Pathmanathan v. The 'Imperial Bank of India, I am of opinion that section 8 of the Supreme Court (Vacation) Ordinance can be invoked in this case"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 8 of the Supreme Court (Vacation) Ordinance (Cap. 1O)

statement: The court should exercise discretion to grant leave to appeal when the matter in dispute is of great general importance, public importance, or otherwise a substantial matter.
supporting_quote: "I do not think it can be said that the question in this case falls within the condition of great general importance or of public importance. The most that can be said in regard to it is that it concerns a question of intestate succession arising in Kandyan law in certain circumstances that are more of uncommon than common occurrence. Nor, is it, otherwise, a matter of such a substantial character as would justify us to give a leave."

statement: Where a mortgagee pays rates due to a local authority, on behalf of a mortgage, in respect of the mortgaged premises, an implied promise by the mortgagor to pay the mortgagee cannot be inferred in the absence of evidence that such payment was made under compulsion.
supporting_quote: Where a mortgagee pays rates due to a local authority, on behalf of a mortgage, in respect of the mortgaged premises, an implied promise by the mortgagor to pay the mortgagee cannot be inferred in the absence of evidence that such payment was made under compulsion.

statement: Under Roman Dutch Law, a fideicommissary is treated as privy to the fiduciary for the purpose of res judicata.
supporting_quote: "I think, on all these authorities, it can be held that under the Roman Dutch Law a fideicommissary is treated as a privy of the fiduciary, or a person claiming under him for the purpose of the law of res judicata"

statement: A subsequent suit for the same relief after proper notice to all parties is not barred under Order 23 Rule 1(3) of the Civil Procedure Code, if the first series of acts or transactions forming the basis of the first suit was incomplete and the second series is complete.
supporting_quote: "So, in the present case, the reliefs claimed in both suits are the same, namely, the recovery of a sum of money due on a mortgage bond. In the Madras case the following view was taken : - ' Without attempting an exhaustive definition of all that may be included in the term ' subject-matter' it should be held that where the cause of action and the relief claimed on the second suit are not the same as the cause of action and the relief claimed in the first suit, the second suit cannot be considered to have been brought in respect of the same subject-matter as the first suit within the meaning of Order 23 Rule 1(3). '"

statement: The right to thresh paddy on another's land is a servitude which can be acquired by prescriptive user.
supporting_quote: The right to thresh paddy on another's land is a servitude which can be acquired by prescriptive user. See Tikiri Appu . v. Dingirirala 1[36 N.L.R.267].

statement: A surety can revoke a continuing guarantee for goods to be supplied or money to be advanced by giving notice, unless the guarantee stipulates otherwise.
supporting_quote: "In the case of such continuing guarantees as the present, it has long been understood that they are liable, in the absence of anything in the guarantee to the contrary, to be withdrawn on notice."

statement: A power of distribution once executed cannot be revoked unless a power of revocation is reserved by the instrument executing the power.
supporting_quote: There can be no doubt, and it was virtually conceded in the argument, that a redistribution can follow a distribution. But the point is whether the trustee had put it beyond his power to redistribute what he had already distributed. I think he had. Redistribution implies, and is also conditioned by, a power to revoke. If in making a distribution the power to revoke is reserved, a redistribution can take place; but if such power is not reserved, the conveyance is irrevocable and the powers of redistribution which could otherwise have been exercised cannot be exercised.

statement: A buyer's refusal to pay for delivered goods, indicating an intention not to be bound by the contract terms, can constitute a repudiation of the agreement.
supporting_quote: 'In regard to the 200 cases purchased by the respondent to which he refers in P 11 dated September 29, it is true that he had not then told the appellant in so many words that he would not pay for the instalments till delivery had been made in full, but it is obvious that that was what he had intended to convey.'

statement: In a case involving a hypothecary decree, directing that the mortgaged property be sold by a named auctioneer, no order for sale with notice to the judgment-debtor under Section 347 of the Civil Procedure Code is necessary.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that, in a case involving a hypothecary decree, directing that the mortgaged property be sold by a named auctioneer, no order for sale with notice to the judgment-debtor under-section 347 of the Civil Procedure Code is necessary."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 347 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The decision in an interpleader action is binding on all parties, and the plaintiff cannot re-agitate matters already decided.
supporting_quote: "In the opinion of their Lordships it is settled, first, that the admission of a fact fundamental to the decision arrived at cannot be withdrawn and a fresh litigation started, with a view of obtaining another judgment upon a different assumption of fact; secondly, the same principle applies not only to an erroneous admission of a fundamental fact, but to an erroneous assumption as to the legal quality of that fact .... If this were permitted litigation would have no end, except when legal ingenuity is exhausted ....... Thirdly, the same principle-namely, that of setting to rest rights of litigants, applies to the case where a point, fundamental to the decision, taken or assumed by the plaintiff and traversable by the defendant, has not been traversed."

statement: The executing Court has jurisdiction to consider the legal effect of a bargain between a judgment-creditor and a judgment-debtor that affects the execution, discharge or satisfaction of the decree under section 344 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "This view rests upon the authority of the Privy Council in a case to which I shall presently refer. Section 47 corresponds with section 344 of our Code. Even, therefore, if the Judge was right in holding that there had been no adjustment which could be recorded under section 349 of the Civil Procedure Code, it was still necessary for him to consider under section 344 of the Civil Procedure Code whether the plaintiff's right to execution was controlled and if so to what extent and in what manner, by X 10 or by A, if A had superseded X 10."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 344 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A decree of dismissal entered without adjudication on the merits does not constitute a registrable instrument under the Registration of Documents Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "But, that is not an end of the matter for, apart from res judicata properly so termed, there are certain statutory bars which preclude the bringing of an action when an earlier action relating to the same matter has been dismissed without a decision, determination, or adjudication of any question of law or fact."

statement: A co-owner has the right to preempt any share sold by other co-owners to a stranger without notice.
supporting_quote: "the 2nd appellant would have the right to pre-empt any share sold by the other co-owners to a stranger without notice to her"

statement: A court may hear parties who claim a completed sale, even if not given formal leave to intervene.
supporting_quote: "In this view of the matter, ordinarily the case would have had to go back for the Ceylon Theatres, Ltd. to be made added parties and to be heard on the question indicated, but in this instance it seems clear from the proceedings that the trial Court while professing not to give the Ceylon Theatres, Ltd. and Roche any hearing on the question before it, was in effect hearing them and that the order appealed from was made with full knowledge of the relevant facts."

statement: A deed of gift to minors by their mother, their father being a lunatic, may be accepted on their behalf by their maternal uncle.
supporting_quote: "A deed of gift to minors by their mother, their father being a lunatic, may be accepted on their behalf by their maternal uncle."

statement: The plaintiffs are declared entitled to an undivided 1/12th and 1/72nd of the field, as well as leasehold rights under P 6.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiffs are accordingly declared entitled to an undivided l/12th and l/72nd of this field. They are also declared entitled to open pits and excavate for gems. They are also entitled to the leasehold rights under P 6."

statement: A deed of revocation executed by the donor in 1904, which ceased to have any legal effect upon its execution, did not get overridden by a subsequent registered transfer made in 1916.
supporting_quote: "When Mudalihamy revoked P2 in 1904, that deed ceased to have any legal effect That result was brought about by the mere fact of revocation and not by reason of any fact of registration."

statement: A lessee who loses possession of leased land due to a partition action and is not under an obligation to intervene in the partition action can claim damages from the lessor for the unexpired portion of the lease, provided that the compensation received does not adequately cover the loss.
supporting_quote: Where the undivided share of a land which was partitioned had been leased and the portion leased had been allotted to a co-owner other than the lessor, who was given compensation.- Held , that the lease was not bound to intervene in the partition action and that he was entitled to claim damages from the lessor.

statement: Section 718 of the Civil Procedure Code can be applied to cases where an administrator claims property as his own, which a party to the testamentary suit alleges belongs to the estate.
supporting_quote: "With great respect, I- would, therefore, say that de Zoysa v. de Zoysa (supra) was wrongly decided on this point, and that the second order of the District Judge was correct."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 718 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A mortgage on property that was subsequently set aside due to the mortgagor's consent and action, rather than laesio enormis or other vendor-initiated rescission, remains valid.
supporting_quote: "In this connection I would invite attention to the distinction drawn between contracts that are void and those that are voidable in the 18th edition of Anson's Law of Contract, pp. 4 & 5. As the transaction between the 1st and 3rd defendants was not void, but merely voidable, Nagarajah obtained a good title."

statement: A court may reserve a right of mortgage to the plaintiff even if the sale was fraudulent and collusive, provided it avoids the fraud and places the parties in statu quo.
supporting_quote: Civil Courts interfere in cases of fraud from a civil and not a criminal point of view. It is not their function to punish the wrong doer. Their function is to avoid the fraud and thereafter, as far as it is possible to do so, to place the wrong doer and the person or persons he has wronged or attempted to wrong in statu quo.

statement: A panguwa, free from any liability on the part of nilakarayas to render services or pay commuted dues for over ten years, can be partitioned under the Service Tenures Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Inasmuch as the land is no longer subject to a liability to perform indivisible services I am of opinion that the learned Judge was right in coming to the conclusion that it could be the subject of a partition action under the Ordinance."

statement: A person who expends money or labour in improving property, intending to do so for his own benefit, thinking either that the property belongs to himself, or that he has the right to occupy it for some substantial period, whereas in fact he has no such right or title to the property and in consequence the improvements are acquired by the owner of the property, is entitled to claim from the latter the amount by which the property has been enhanced in value.
supporting_quote: Wille in Principles of South African Law (1937 edition), page 353 sets out the right to improvements to property as follows : - "A person who expends money or labour in improving property, intending to do so for his own benefit, thinking either that the property belongs to himself, or that he has the right to occupy it for some substantial period, whereas in fact he has no such right or title to the property and in consequence the improvements are . acquired by the owner of the property, is entitled to claim from the latter the amount by which the property has been enhanced in value.

statement: In a transaction involving pawn or pledge, it is not necessary for the pawnee or pledgee to tender the pawn or pledge as a condition precedent to recovering the amount lent.
supporting_quote: "It is not the necessary condition of the right of a pawnee or pledgee to recover the amount lent by him that he should tender the pawn or pledge."

statement: A person who enters into occupation of property belonging to another with the latter's permission cannot acquire title to such property by prescription unless he gets rid of his character of licensee by doing some overt act showing an intention to possess adversely.
supporting_quote: Where a person enters into occupation of property belonging to another with the latter's permission he cannot acquire title to such property by prescription unless he gets rid of his character of licensee by doing some overt act showing an intention to possess adversely.

statement: An agreement to give produce in lieu of interest on a property sale is not obnoxious to the terms of section 2 of Ordinance No. 7 of 1840.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the agreement was not obnoxious to the terms of section 2 of the Ordinance for the Prevention of Frauds, No. 7 of 1840."
statute_citation_verbatim: Ordinance No. 7 of 1840 (Cap. 57) s. 2.

statement: An agreement for the transfer of lands in consideration of marriage is valid even if it is not notarially attested.
supporting_quote: "Held, that the agreement was valid, although it was not notarially attested."

statement: The defendants are under a legal obligation to make monthly payments of Rs. 666.67 to the plaintiffs out of the net income of the Nagrak estate, unless funds have been earmarked for necessary expenses.
supporting_quote: "It is further ordered and decreed that the defendants do pay to the plaintiffs out of the nett income of the said Nagrak estate a sum of Rs. 2,000 forthwith, that they do also out of the said nett income make monthly payments to the plaintiffs at the rate of Rs. 666.67 per mensem (the said Rs. 666.67 or part thereof, if not available in respect of any month being carried forward and remaining due and payable to the plaintiffs according to the tenor of this decree)"

statement: A vendor cannot represent title of which he has divested himself and there is not even a legal fiction to that effect.
supporting_quote: "A vendor cannot represent title of which he has divested himself and there is not even a legal fiction to that effect."

statement: A plaintiff is barred from maintaining a fresh action for the same matter or in respect of the same part if they withdraw their suit against some defendants without obtaining permission.
supporting_quote: Section 406 (2) of the Civil Procedure Code enacts that 'if the plaintiff withdraw from the action, or abandon part of his claim, without such permission (the permission of the Court referred to in sub-section (1)) .... he shall be precluded from bringing a fresh action for the same matter or in respect of the same part'.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 406(2)

statement: A person cannot enrich himself at the expense of another, and a party who was himself a party to an illegal consideration is precluded from obtaining assistance of the law to recover it.
supporting_quote: "It is a maxim of law, established, not for the benefit of plaintiffs or defendants, but is founded on the principles of public policy, which will not assist a plaintiff who has paid over money or handed over property in pursuance of an illegal or immoral contract, to recover it back"

statement: An application for execution of a mortgage decree is not barred by section 337 of the Civil Procedure Code if it is made after an earlier application and the first application did not constitute an application under Chapter 22 of the Code.
supporting_quote: It could be so regarded only if the application of September, 1941, was also an application under Chapter 22 of the Code. I do not think that the application of September, 1941, was such application.

statement: The defendant is estopped from asserting that the delivery period ended on a certain date when he led the plaintiff to believe by letter and conduct that the contract was still subsisting, especially since the plaintiff acted on this belief at serious expense.
supporting_quote: Inasmuch as the defendant led the plaintiff to-believe by letter, as well as conduct, that the contract was still subsisting, and inasmuch as the plaintiff acted on that belief at serious expense to himself, it would be unjust to allow the defendant to assert that the delivery period ended on November 15.

statement: A valid tender of the sum within the period is essential to plaintiff's cause of action in an agreement for re-transfer of land.
supporting_quote: "Held, (in an action by plaintiff for a re-transfer), that valid tender of the sum within the period is essential to plaintiff's cause of action."

statement: The maxim of falsa demonstratio non nocet is not applicable in this case.
supporting_quote: I do not think that this is a case to which the maxim of falsa demonstratio is applicable. That maxim when stated fully reads, Falsa demonstratio non nocet cum de corpore constat.

statement: A donee who is in possession of property gifted to him may avail himself of the exceptio doli when he is sued by the donor or any person claiming under him.
supporting_quote: "A donee, who is in possession of property gifted to him may avail himself of the exceptio doli when he is sued by the donor or by any person claiming tinder him."

statement: A voluntary statement made to induce the represented to act upon it is sufficient for estoppel, regardless of whether there was an intention to deceive.
supporting_quote: "The contention which from time to time has been advanced on behalf of a representor that his honesty and innocence of intention ought to exempt him from liability to estoppel, as it does from liability to an action for damages, is based on a hopeless confusion between a cause of action based on fraud and a rule of evidence, and has always been rejected, for the obvious reason that, in the case of estoppel by representation, as, indeed, also in the case of proceedings for rescission of contract on the ground of misrepresentation, the only material suggestion is, not the state of the representor's morals, but the effect of the representation on the mind and will of the representee. Accordingly, it has always been held that it is no answer to a case of-estoppel to establish, or rather, perhaps, that it is not incumbent on the representee to negative, the fact that the representation was made in innocent inadvertence or forgetfulness, or that the representor in making it, had no intention to defraud or injure the representee, or any other sinister design. If, as has already been explained, it appears that the representation was made ' wilfully ', in the sense of ' voluntarily ', that is, with the actual or implied intention of inducing the representee to act upon it, it is wholly irrelevant whether it was, or was not, made ' wilfully ' in any ethical sense."

statement: Courts can apply equitable principles to establish a trust even when the transaction is documented, and may fasten on an individual who obtained title under such a document a personal obligation if it appears that they acted fraudulently.
supporting_quote: "It has been pointed out that both these decisions may be regarded as obiter dicta, but even so, I do not think that it is open to us to minimize the weight of these pronouncements. It is, however. I think, competent for me to point out that in neither of these cases was the question whether parol evidence was admissible to prove u trust considered."

statement: A fidei commissum can be created even where the language of the will is open to criticism, provided there is doubt as to who are the recipients of the bounty.
supporting_quote: "When the intention to substitute another (or fidei commissary) for the first taker (or fiduciary) is expressed, or is to be gathered by necessary implication from the language of the will, a fidei commissum is constituted. Where these requisites appear, it matters not that the language employed is open to criticism"

statement: Where an application for probate is unsuccessfully opposed by blood relations of the testator, the costs of the proceedings may be directed to be paid out of the estate if the circumstances merit such an order.
supporting_quote: I would therefore, in dismissing the appeal, vary the order of the District Judge regarding costs and direct that all the costs of the proceedings in the Court below as well as in this Court subsequent to the Supreme Court judgment, dated February 18, 1944, be paid out of the estate.

statement: A fidei commissum can be created even when the language of the will is not entirely clear, as long as it presents some difficulties but does not leave the intention to create one in doubt.
supporting_quote: "I am unable to agree that the different views expressed in these decisions all of which agreed in holding in favour of a fidei commissum should compel us to a conclusion against the existence of a fidei commissum on the ground that the language of the last will leaves us in doubt whether & fidei commissum has been created. It has to be admitted that the will presents some difficulties, but I do not think these difficulties afford sufficient ground for saying that the language employed in the last will is so involved in doubt that a Court is compelled to hold that the testator has failed to create a valid fidei commissum."

statement: A deed of gift creates a valid fidei commissum extending to four generations if the donor intended it and certain conditions are met.
supporting_quote: "The learned District Judge dismissed the plaintiff's action holding that P 1 had not been accepted and that it did not create a valid fidei commissum. It is well settled law that no donation is complete and valid unless it is accepted by the donee."

statement: The defendant's action under section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code was not taken with reasonable and probable cause, as evidenced by Emily de Silva's alleged statement that P 1 was a fraudulent alienation.
supporting_quote: "I see no reason for rejecting the evidence of the defendant on this point. No doubt these points were before the District Judge, but the only comment he makes on it is that 'Had the lawyers known all the facts which are now known to this Court, and upon which another District Judge and the Supreme Court in the Paulian action held against the defendant, they would have given different advice- to the defendant. Those facts, had they been fully disclosed to the lawyers or had they been impartially reviewed by the defendant himself, would have shown him that P 1 was a good deed which could not be attacked, and that there was no reasonable or probable cause for taking steps by seizure and a 247 action to have it set aside '."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 247 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The Court should not allow a creditor who has been guilty of conspiratorial silence regarding matters within his knowledge to re-open proceedings, especially after a delay of one year.
supporting_quote: "I think the Court was within its rights in refusing an application by a creditor, who had not only delayed one year, but had also been guilty of conspiratorial silence regarding matters within his knowledge."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 133 of the Insolvency Ordinance

statement: A person who writes out a will for the testator cannot insert therein any benefit for himself and, should he do so, cannot take such benefit unless the testator either odds a clause in his own handwriting to the effect that he dictated the will and acknowledges its correctness, or in some other manner clearly confirms the disposition.
supporting_quote: It matters not, in the least degree, that evidence was led to show that the petitioner copied the will from a Notary's Manual at the request of the Notary who later attested the will. He cannot take under the will unless there is satisfactory proof of a confirmation by the testatrix of the will in the manner indicated in the passage cited from Steyn's Treatise.

statement: A party cannot be deprived of property sold at a mortgage sale if they purchased it bona fide for value and without notice of any trust or irregularities.
supporting_quote: "The same principle was also formulated in the Privy Council case of Rewa Mahton v. Ram Kishen Singh [4 I . L. R. 14 Calc. 19.]"

statement: A person may mortgage property of which he is not the owner at the time, and when the rights of such a mortgagee come into competition with those of a later mortgagee who took his mortgage after acquisition of title by the mortgagor, the first mortgagee is preferred.
supporting_quote: But, as was held in the case of Goonetilleke v. Jayasekera [1 14 N.L.R. p.65. ], under the Roman-Dutch Law, a person may mortgage property of which he is not the owner at the time and when the rights of such a mortgagee come into competition with those of a later mortgagee, who took his mortgage after acquisition of title by the mortgagor, the first mortgagee is preferred "because the right of pledge was confirmed from the moment of the mortgagor's acquisition of ownership".

statement: The plaintiff must prove that a definite sum of money is due on the mortgage bond before succeeding against a third party in possession of the mortgaged premises.
supporting_quote: "It accordingly appears to me to be clear that if the plaintiff has proved (as he appears to have substantially done) his mortgage, his mortgagor's title at the time of the mortgage, and that the mortgage debt is still unpaid, he is entitled to a decree in his favour declaring the property liable to be sold to satisfy that debt."

statement: A transferee of mortgaged property, whose transfer was not registered and who was therefore not a party to the mortgage action, is entitled to surplus proceeds after satisfaction of the mortgage in suit.
supporting_quote: 'Held , that the transferee was entitled to the surplus proceeds.'

statement: A person who is ousted and regains possession without delay has continuous possession, but if the interruption is final, then prescriptive possession cannot be established.
supporting_quote: If the person ousted regained possession in a few days his possession would be continuous and not otherwise. The interrupter may be punished criminally and he may be condemned in damages for the wrong, but the interruption would remain.

statement: A co-owner's possession of the entirety of a property is not adverse without proof of ouster or something equivalent to ouster.
supporting_quote: Where a person obtains a transfer of the entirety of a property from a co-owner, his possession is that of a co-owner, and it does not become adverse without proof of ouster or something equivalent to ouster.

statement: A broker is entitled to sell goods purchased on the principal's instructions, in a certain contingency, without intervention of a court.
supporting_quote: "When an agent is employed to enter into any contract or do any other lawful act involving personal liability and is expressly or impliedly authorised to discharge such liability on behalf of the principal, the authority becomes irrevocable as soon as the liability is incurred by the agent."

statement: The defendant Company has established their claim by virtue of prescription.
supporting_quote: "The latter have established their claim by virtue of prescription."

statement: A party can lead oral evidence to prove the true nature of a transaction, even if it contradicts a statement in a written contract, particularly when seeking equity.
supporting_quote: "The principle of English equity was that he who sought equity must do it. In this case the plaintiff comes into Court repudiating a statement with regard to the payment of the consideration, and if he is allowed to put that forward, he ought also to suffer the person whom he attacks to show the real nature of the transaction."

statement: A defendant can claim rescission of the sale only for the lands where vacant possession was not given, even if multiple lands were sold in one conveyance.
supporting_quote: "I think, moreover,, that we should adopt in this case the principle underlying the opinion expressed by Voet that 'if a number of things have been sold together for one (lump) price, the obligation for eviction is multiplied according to the number of the things, and as many actions are given as there are things evicted which were included in the single sale, . . . . '"

statement: In cases involving service tenures, the liability for commuted dues is indivisible and owed jointly and severally by all nilakarayas.
supporting_quote: "the services in their nature were indivisible and therefore the obligation to pay the commuted dues must be regarded as an indivisible obligation"

statement: A right of cart way by necessity can be claimed no further than the actual necessity of the case demands.
supporting_quote: "A right of cart way by necessity can be claimed no further than the actual necessity of the case demands."

statement: A plaintiff can assert a servitude of drawing water from a well even if their land is separated by a public road or intervening land, provided the intervening land has a similar servitude.
supporting_quote: "For which reason it became the custom that water could lawfully be led by right of servitude through the adjoining estates of more than one person, and that one and the same servitudes of passage, driving, and way, could be constituted over several farms of several owners; and the right of drawing water was not stopped by the fact that there existed an intervening public road or place."

statement: A building in respect of which a servitude of light and air is enjoyed cannot claim the same servitude after demolishing an old building and erecting a new one closer to the common boundary.
supporting_quote: "Where a building in respect of which a survitude of light and air is enjoyed is demolished and a new building is erected closer to the common boundary, the same servitude cannot be claimed in respect of the new building."

statement: A person having the right of pre-emption is entitled to exercise the right by offering to buy the land at the price actually paid for it by a purchaser, and not at the market value.
supporting_quote: "Under the Thesawalamai a person having the right of pre-emption of a land is entitled to exercise the right by offering to buy the land at the price-actually paid for it by a purchaser. In such a case he is not entitled to assert the right by offering to buy the land at the market value."

statement: A husband governed by the Thesawalamai cannot donate more than half of the thediathetam property, and if he does so, his wife's share is not irretrievably lost but she can claim her half share against a bona fide purchaser from the donee.
supporting_quote: "The position, as it appears to me is this. If a husband donates the whole of the thediathetam property to a son and the donee conveys it to a bona fide purchaser, the latter acquires good title and the wife's only remedy is a claim for compensation. If, however, the donee retains property conveyed to him and, as in this case, after, the death of the husband, the wife gives a transfer of her share to another son, that conveyance is good against the husband's donee. Her remedy is not only by way of a suit for compensation. She can assert her claim to her half share against the husband's donee and the transferee from her can do the same."
