statement: The defendant had notice of the trust when he executed deed D2, and thus is not entitled to priority under section 7 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance.
supporting_quote: In these circumstances the defendant cannot complain if it is presumed that he knew that' the property was held under deed P 2 in trust for Somasunderam Chettiar or that he willfully refrained from making any inquiries regarding the description of Narayan Chettiar in the deeds and the entries in the extract from the Register of Encumbrances.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 7 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance

statement: The appellants' case of a trust must fail as there is no evidence to support it, and they are bound by the previous ruling.
supporting_quote: "I do not see how it is possible for the appellants to succeed since there is no evidence whatever to establish their case of a trust."

statement: The intention of the testator was that on the death of Eliza or her husband, the property should vest in the survivor and their children. The direction in clause (b) did not over-ride the clear words of clause (a).
supporting_quote: Held, that the intention of the testator was that on the death of Eliza or her husband the property should vest in the survivor and the children. Held, further, that the direction in clause (b) did not over-ride the clear words of clause (a).

statement: Where the same property is seized and sold under two writs and neither seizure is registered, the purchaser under the writ upon which the property was first sold is entitled to priority by reason of the retroactive effect given to his Fiscal's conveyance under section 289 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: 'Where the same property is seized and sold under two writs and neither seizure is registered, the purchaser under the writ upon which the property was first sold is entitled to priority by reason of the retroactive effect given to his Fiscal's conveyance under the provisions of section 289 of the Civil Procedure Code.'
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 289.

statement: A party who could have raised an objection to a procedural irregularity in the court below but did not, cannot raise it later as an estoppel by election.
supporting_quote: "It is quite probable that had this course been adopted the ninth defendant would have taken appropriate steps immediately to make an independent claim to the incumbency against the fourth to eighth and tenth defendants. No such issue, however, was asked for and the case was disposed of on the merits."

statement: The burden rests on the unsuccessful claimant to prove that at the date of seizure he had the right which he claims.
supporting_quote: "The burden rests on him to prove that he had that right at the date of seizure (vide Silva v. Nona Hamine 1[(1906) 10 N. L. R. 44.] and Abubackar v. Tikiri Banda 2[(1926) 29 N. L. R. 132])."

statement: A defendant can assert a title that accrued after the institution of an action but before judgment in a subsequent action.
supporting_quote: "That the language used by the noble Lord is not to be limited by the facts of the case with which he was dealing is supported by the observation of Blackburn J., in the case of Newington v. Levy 1 [L. R. 6 C. P. (180).] I am inclined to think that the doctrine of res judicata applies to all matters which existed at the time of the giving of the judgment and which the party had an opportunity of bringing before the Court. "

statement: Order 22 Rule 10 of the Civil Procedure Rules is not limited to plaintiffs and their representatives.
supporting_quote: " As to the first contention we are not prepared to say that Order 22 Rule 10 can only apply to plaintiffs and their representatives. Nor has any authority been put before us to show that it does .... In the case in Rajaranee Dossee v. Debendra Nath Shau 3 the

statement: The court has the discretion to add new parties under section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code, and this addition does not result in misjoinder of causes of action.
supporting_quote: "No doubt the court has a discretionary power to allow or refuse the addition of new parties, but in this case the District Judge has exercised his jurisdiction in favour of the addition of the parties."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: There is a prima facie presumption that the possession of a usufructuary mortgagee enures to the benefit of the true owner, whether it be the person who actually gave him the usufructuary mortgage or the successor of that person.
supporting_quote: There is a prima facie presumption that the possession of a usufructuary mortgagee enures to the benefit of the true owner, whether it be the person who actually gave him the usufructuary mortgage or the successor of that person.

statement: The intention of the obligor to give and of the obligee to accept the new thing in extinction of the old obligation is essential.
supporting_quote: "The intention of the obligor to give and of the obligee to accept the new thing in extinction of the old obligation is essential. (Voet: 46-2-3.)"

statement: A deposit made in court within the stipulated time is sufficient without a previous offer, subject to an appropriate order regarding interest, costs, etc.
supporting_quote: "Subject to an appropriate order in regard to interest, costs, &c, in a particular case, a deposit made in court within the stipulated time is sufficient without a previous offer."

statement: The court has discretion to allow a party to deposit money after the time allowed in the conditions of sale provided no prejudice was caused.
supporting_quote: "I think the Court has the discretion to allow a party to deposit money after the time allowed in the conditions of sale provided no prejudice was caused."

statement: The appellants did not have the money with them to pay the respondent on February 6, 1940.
supporting_quote: It is clear that on the receipt of the letter dated February 5, 1940, at 2 P.M. the Proctor of appellant No. 2 would have known that the respondent was not in Colombo and would not be back in Colombo until the 11th. It was impossible for him, therefore, to receive the money from the office of appellant No. 2 at the specified time on February 6, 1940, as required by the letter of that date.

statement: The rule of intestate succession applicable under Muslim law should not be applied to the descendants of a devisee.
supporting_quote: Held , that on the death of a devisee his child would take according to the general Law and not according to the rule of intestate succession applicable to Muslims.

statement: A decree for partition does not extinguish the rights of fidei commissarii but merely sets apart a specific lot to which the rights of the fidei commissarii attach in place of the share which was originally burdened with the fidei commissum, unless the purchaser is a bona fide purchaser for value without notice.
supporting_quote: All it decides is that a purchaser from such a fiduciarius with knowledge of a fidei commissum cannot hold the land purchased as against a fidei commissarius. It affirms the principle that a man cannot hold what in conscience he knows he has no right to.

statement: The title of the purchaser at a Fiscal's sale does not, on the issue of the Fiscal's transfer, prevail over any intermediate alienation by the execution-debtor, unless the Fiscal's seizure is registered.
supporting_quote: the title of the purchaser at the Fiscal's sale does not, on the issue of the Fiscal's transfer, prevail over any intermediate alienation by the execution debtor, unless the Fiscal's seizure is registered.

statement: Orders under section 4(2) of the Ordinance do not give an indefeasible title to claimants, as they are merely admissions and not agreements on mutual concession between claimant and Crown.
supporting_quote: "I fail to see how the fact that the shareholders who do not come forward may claim a share of a land mentioned in an Order under section 4 -(i) could possibly affect the rights of the Crown to lands declared to be the property of the Crown by the conclusive Order referred to in 2 (2)."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 4(2)

statement: A purchaser for valuable consideration, without notice, obtains a legal estate in the property which is unanswerable to the jurisdiction of the court unless the purchaser can show that he had notice of a breach of trust.
supporting_quote: "I propose simply to apply myself to the case of a purchaser for valuable consideration, Without notice, obtaining, upon the occasion of his purchase, and by means of his purchase deed, some legal estate, some legal right, some legal advantage; and, according to my view of the established law of this Court, such a purihaser's plea of a purchase for valuable consideration without notice is an absolute, unqualified, unanswerable defence, and an unanswerable plea to the jurisdiction of this Court."

statement: In a possessory action, whether brought by the owner suo nomine or as lessee, the subject-matter is the right to possess the whole land without limitation in point of time, and the jurisdiction of the Court should be determined by the value of that right.
supporting_quote: "The question for decision is whether the test of jurisdiction in. a possessory action brought by a lessee is the value of the land or the value of the remaining period of the lease."

statement: A sale of land by a minor without the sanction of court is voidable, and the minor's remedy is by way of restitutio in integrum unless she has derived substantial benefit. In such cases, the minor must indemnify the other party and put them back to their original position.
supporting_quote: "In our Courts, as far as I have been able to discover, applications for restitutio in integrum have always been made to the Supreme Court by minors as well as by persons of full capacity and have been confined to cases in which the application is based on the discovery of fresh evidence or on allegation that the applicant has been surprised into a position of prejudice and disadvantage in the course of a judicial proceeding."

statement: A condition precedent to the appointment of a legal representative under section 7 of the Mortgage Ordinance (Cap. 74) is that evidence should be tendered that the value of the mortgaged property does not exceed Rs. 2,500.
supporting_quote: "A condition precedent to the appointment of a person to represent the estate of a deceased mortgagor under section 7 of the Mortgage Ordinance (Cap. 74) is that evidence should be tendered that the value of the mortgaged property does not exceed two thousand five hundred rupees."
statute_citation_verbatim: Mortgage Ordinance (Cap. 74), s. 7.

statement: A Commissioner appointed under the Partition Ordinance cannot be supplanted by a nominee of a party dissatisfied with the proposed scheme; it must be the Commissioner's scheme, as proposed or modified on directions of the Court, that is confirmed for entering the decree.
supporting_quote: "In this instance, there being no opposition forthcoming from any of the parties to the appointment, the Court appointed the Surveyor who had made the preliminary plan to carry out the partition. He duly effected the partition, and made his return to the Court showing on Plan No. 3,166 the division he proposed, and he also filed the schedule required by section 5."

statement: The proper course for the district Judge to follow is to remit the case to the Commissioner appointed under section 5 with direction for him to modify his scheme on the lines, more or less, of the scheme prepared by Surveyor Amarasekere and to submit it with a schedule of appraisement.
supporting_quote: It is not correct to say that the lots given to the appellants consist of entirely owita land. But as I observed in the case S. C. 27/D. C. (Inty.) Matara, No. 154/13,628* [ * Vide (1945) 46 N. L. R. 461-Ed. ] in which judgment was delivered today, the proper course for the district Judge to follow is to remit the case to the Commissioner appointed under section 5 with direction for him to modify his scheme on the lines, more or less, of the scheme prepared by Surveyor Amarasekere and to submit it with a schedule of appraisement.

statement: The Civil Procedure Code, Section 602 applies to actions for declaration of nullity of marriage under Section 607.
supporting_quote: "I hold that the present action may be regarded as coming within the terms of section 597 of the Code, and that section 602 applies to this action."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 597, 602, 604, 607

statement: In the absence of an ouster or something equivalent, a co-owner cannot initiate a prescriptive title by any secret intention in his own mind.
supporting_quote: "It is open to the Court, from lapse of time in conjunction with the circumstances of the case, to presume that a possession originally that of a co-owner, has since become adverse."

statement: A co-owner's title and possession are held in disregard of and unaffected by a deed of transfer if the deed is disputed and ignored by other co-owners, and such possession continues for 15 years after the execution of the deed.
supporting_quote: Possession continued in disregard of P8 and had so continued for 15 years after P8 had been executed. Consequently, it was not in reality a case in which the defendants-respondents, had acquired a prescriptive title, but rather a case in which their title and possession were held in disregard of and unaffected by P8.

statement: The informal writing P4 is of no force or avail at law as it is not contained in a notarial document.
supporting_quote: "The informal writing P4 is in form a mere agreement to retransfer, and it is of no force or avail at law as it is not contained in a notarial document."

statement: The Appeal Court can set aside the trial Judge's finding of fact if all the other known facts contradicted the declaration of the witness.
supporting_quote: Held, that the Appeal Court could set aside the finding of fact if all the other known facts contradicted the declaration of the witness.

statement: A servitude such as that of right to a footpath must be established by cogent evidence, as it affects the right of the owner of a land to the free and unfettered use of his land.

statement: A carrier by trade is governed by the Praetor's Edict 'De Nautis Caponibus et Stabulariis' under Roman Dutch law, and a carrier must show ordinary diligence in case of gratuitous carriage or the skill of an ordinary reasonable carrier in case of paid carriage.
supporting_quote: "A carrier by trade is governed by the Praetor's Edict 'De Nautis Caponibus et Stabulariis' [Digest Bk. IV Tit. 9.]"

statement: A defendant seeking to file an answer without giving security must provide sufficient details in their affidavit to indicate a reasonable ground for the defense, beyond merely stating 'I owe nothing'.
supporting_quote: "Doubtless, if it was true that you owed the man nothing as you swear that would be a good defence. But that is not enough. You must satisfy the Judge that there is reasonable ground for saying so."

statement: The amendment of the final decree was lawful and binding on the respondent, as it corrected an accidental slip or omission in allotting shares.
supporting_quote: "Clearly, therefore, there has been a 'slip or omission' in allotting the shares of the respondent and the plaintiff. Obviously, that slip or omission was not deliberate. It was accidental."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code, as amended by Ordinance No. 26 of 1930.

statement: A trial judge should not always stay proceedings when an interlocutory appeal is filed against his refusal to allow witnesses to be called at the trial.
supporting_quote: "I do not, of course, express the view that a trial Judge, should always stay proceedings when an interlocutory appeal is filed against his refusal to allow witnesses to be called at the trial."

statement: The court has the power to amend a consent order under section 189(1) of the Civil Procedure Code if there was an accidental slip or omission by counsel, even though it pertains to terms agreed upon by the parties.
supporting_quote: "Of consent, plaintiff to be entitled to half share of premises described in schedule to plaint with damages fixed at Rs. 100.00. 266 Writ for damages not to issue for 3 months from today. Each party to bear his own costs. Enter decree accordingly."
statute_citation_verbatim: "(1) The court may at any time, either on its own motion or on that of any of the parties, correct any clerical or arithmetical mistake in any judgment or order or any error arising therein from any accidental slip or omission, or may make any amendment which is necessary to bring a decree into conformity with the judgment."

statement: The legal consequences of the Fiscal's action under Section 288 of the Civil Procedure Code are null if the property sold was not in the occupancy of anyone, and this action does not interrupt the appellant's possession.
supporting_quote: "On the facts appearing in that report the Fiscal was not entitled to proceed under section 288 of the Civil Procedure Code. That section reads : 'When the property sold is in the occupancy of a tenant or other person entitled to occupy the same, and a conveyance in respect thereof has been made to the purchaser under section 286, the court shall order delivery thereof to be made by affixing a notice of the sale having taken place, both in English and in the vernacular language or languages prevailing within the district, in some conspicuous place on the property, and proclaiming to the occupant by beat of tom-tom, or in such other mode as may be customary, at some convenient place, that the interest of the judgment-debtor has been transferred to the purchaser, and the cost (to be fixed by the court) of such proclamation shall in every case he prepaid by the purchaser.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: "When the property sold is in the occupancy of a tenant or other person entitled to occupy the same, and a conveyance in respect thereof has been made to the purchaser under section 286, the court shall order delivery thereof to be made by affixing a notice of the sale having taken place, both in English and in the vernacular language or languages prevailing within the district, in some conspicuous place on the property, and proclaiming to the occupant by beat of tom-tom, or in such other mode as may be customary, at some convenient place, that the interest of the judgment-debtor has been transferred to the purchaser, and the cost (to be fixed by the court) of such proclamation shall in every case he prepaid by the purchaser."

statement: A sub-tenant is bound by a decree for ejectment entered against the tenant and it is the duty of the Fiscal to remove the sub-tenant as he is a person bound by the decree and deliver possession to the landlord.
supporting_quote: "A decree in ejectment passed against a lessee at the instance of a lessor is not only binding upon the lessee but also upon his subtenants provided they have no right independent of the right of their lessor in the demised premises."

statement: An error in the prohibitory notice regarding the name of the judgment-debtor does not render a sale to a bona fide purchaser invalid if it is a misdescription and not an illegality.
supporting_quote: "In the circumstances the error was a misdescription which did not amount to an illegality and that the sale to a bona fide purchaser could not be impugned on that ground by the judgment-debtor."

statement: A co-owner has no right to lease more than his undivided share of the common property.
supporting_quote: "A co-owner may give a lease of his undivided share in a land but he has no right to lease anything more than his share."

statement: Possession under a jus retentionis is not adverse possession and cannot found a title by prescription. Nor can the right to tender compensation for the improvements be barred by limitation.
supporting_quote: "Possession under a jus retentionis is not adverse possession and cannot found a title by prescription. Nor can the right to tender compensation for the improvements be barred by limitation."

statement: A purchaser who has compromised with the claimant is not entitled to succeed in an action founded on eviction.
supporting_quote: "Also [these actions fail] when the purchaser, before being condemned has voluntarily given up the thing to the plaintiff, or has compromised with him, or agreed to arbitration, or has submitted to the jurisdiction of an incompetent judge, or has referred the dispute to his adversary's oath, and has thus lost the thing by the ruling of an incompetent judge?"

statement: It is unsafe to take the course adopted by the learned District Judge in deciding on the genuineness of a disputed signature solely through comparison with admitted signatures without expert assistance.
supporting_quote: Apart from a bare denial that the defendant was either present or gave the promissory note, no attempt was made to prove the allegation in the answer that the note was a forgery. The District Judge accepted the defendant's allegation that the promissory note is a forgery and dismissed the plaintiff's action. He formed that conclusion on a comparison by him, unaided by any expert, of the signature thereon with genuine standards produced in the case. It is unsafe to take the course adopted by the learned District Judge.

statement: The Court should accept a higher offer for property sold on behalf of minors if it is deemed just and reasonable, even if the sale was initially confirmed by a Commissioner.
supporting_quote: "Having given my best consideration to the facts of the case, I have come to the conclusion that it is just and reasonable that the 1st respondent's offer should be accepted."

statement: Where a person receiving payment of rent is not the person who put the tenant into possession but someone claiming title as his assignee or successor, the mere fact of payment of rent without more is not conclusive and does not estop the tenant from disputing the payee's title and explaining the payment.
supporting_quote: where, as in this case, the person receiving the payment is not the person who let the payer into possession, but someone who is claiming title as his assignee or successor, the mere fact of paying money as and for rent without more is not conclusive and does not estop the payer from afterwards disputing the payee's title and leading evidence to explain the payment or payments made by him.

statement: The shares of the property should be allotted based on the Muslim law of intestate succession, with the widow and three children each receiving equal shares.
supporting_quote: I am therefore of opinion that the contention of the appellants is entitled to prevail, namely, that on Seiyedu Lebbe's death the property was divided equally between the widow on the one hand and the three children, Samsudeen, Sothumma and Habibu Nachchia, on the other.

statement: A final decree in a partition suit does not reopen the fidei commissary succession and confers an absolute title on parties to whom separate lots are given in lieu of their shares in severalty, unless the decree itself makes reference to the fidei commissum.
supporting_quote: "The learned Judge overlooks the real question in the case, namely, the fact that the partition decree was based on the fidei commissary succession set forth and adopted in the plaint in that case. The trial Judge went on to give judgment on that footing. He held that the present first defendant was entitled to the 41/48 shares he had bought from his brothers and sisters and that the 7/48 shares he had inherited, he found was subject to the fidei commissum and that the present plaintiff was entitled to that fractional share subject to claims for compensation. Neither the plaintiff nor the first defendant appear satisfied with these findings."

statement: A prohibition against alienation of property during the lifetime of a beneficiary in a will is valid if it is intended to benefit the children or family, and such prohibition cannot be overridden by court authority.
supporting_quote: "The failure to impose a penalty does not affect a prohibition made in a will such as this where the clear intention is to benefit the children (Sande-Webber's translation Ch. IV. section 3, p. 206)."

statement: Unless the language of the deed leads unambiguously to the conclusion that a donee who purchases a share from a co-donee must leave it to his lawful children, the alienee takes that share free from any restrictions.
supporting_quote: "I am unable to say that there is any such provision in P1. It seems to me that the only provision the donee has made in P1 is that if the donees die without acting upon the power given to them the property shall devolve on their lawful children, 1 would accordingly dismiss the appeal with costs."

statement: The burden of proving fraud must be on the plaintiff, and it must be established beyond reasonable doubt. A finding of fraud cannot be based on suspicion and conjecture.
supporting_quote: "In A. L. N. Narayanan Chettiyar and another v. Official Assignee, High Court, Rangoon, and another 1 [ 1941 A. I. R. (P C.) 93. ] it was held that fraud, like any other charge of a, criminal offence whether made in civil or criminal proceedings, must be established beyond reasonable doubt. A finding as to fraud cannot be based on suspicion and conjecture."

statement: A married woman who was married before July 1, 1924, cannot dispose of immovable property acquired before that date without the written consent of her husband.
supporting_quote: "A woman married before July 1, 1924, cannot dispose of immovable property acquired before that date without the written consent of the husband."

statement: A Kandyan woman who marries out forfeits her right to inherit from her father.
supporting_quote: "The defendant did not produce at the trial the marriage certificate of Ukku Hamy. That may be partly due to the fact that the plaint contained no allegation suggesting that the plaintiff's case was that Ukku Hamy was married in Deega."

statement: Illegitimate children cannot inherit from a collateral source, such as a legitimate child of the common mother.
supporting_quote: "Nowhere was it suggested that illegitimate children should be entitled to inherit acquired property from a collateral source, e.g., from a legitimate child of the common mother. There was no need to provide for the right of illegitimate children to inherit from their mother-because a mother makes no bastard."

statement: A point of law, which is a pure question of law and nothing more, can be raised for the first time in the Court of Appeal.
supporting_quote: "In Fernando v. Abeygoonesekera 1 it was laid down that a point of law, which is a point of law and nothing more, can be raised for the first time in the Court of Appeal"

statement: The testator intended to dispose of his undivided half-share, not just one-fourth share, and the plaintiff can defeat this intention by claiming her legal entitlement.
supporting_quote: "I agree to the order proposed by my brother Basnayake. My view is that the testator John Peiris, being under the erroneous impression that he was legally entitled to an undivided half-share of the premises, intended to dispose entirely of this half-share by his will P 4."

statement: A party prejudiced by a decree under the Partition Ordinance is entitled to receive damages upon mere proof that he has suffered damages by the act of the party against whom he brings the action.
supporting_quote: "Section 9 of the Partition Ordinance makes a decree obtained there under in the prescribed manner final and conclusive against all persons whomsoever whatever right or title they have in the property although all persons concerned are not named in any of the said proceedings, or the title of the owners or of any of them is not truly set forth therein. The special provision therein in the nature of a proviso which reads 'Provided that nothing herein contained shall effect the right of any party prejudiced by such partition or sale to recover damages from the parties by whose act, whether of commission or omission, such damages had accrued.'"

statement: For the purposes of taxation of bills of costs under section 21 of the Partition Ordinance, the value of the property is its actual value in the open market and not the value put upon it by the parties in their pleadings.
supporting_quote: "For the purposes of taxation of bills of costs under section 21 of the Partition Ordinance, the value of the property is its actual value in the open market and not the value put upon it by the parties in their pleadings."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 21 of the Partition Ordinance

statement: The Court has the power to make an order requiring the furnishing of security before an application to intervene after an interlocutory decree is allowed in a partition action.
supporting_quote: In a partition action the Court has power to make an order requiring, the furnishing of security before an application to intervene after inter�locutory decree is allowed.

statement: The court should allow a postponement where a material witness on whom summons has been served is absent, especially when the plaintiff seeks to prove prescriptive possession.
supporting_quote: Where a material witness on whom summons has been served is absent the Court should allow a postponement.

statement: An oral agreement to hold land in trust, even if not notarially attested, can be enforceable at law.
supporting_quote: To hold otherwise would allow the Statute of Frauds to be used us a protection or vehicle for frauds. Valliyammai Atchi v. Abdul Majeed (1947) 4S N. L. R. 289, followed

statement: An order is not final where it does not finally dispose of the rights of the parties and leaves them to be determined by the Courts in the ordinary way.
supporting_quote: The test of finality is whether the order 'finally disposes of the rights of the parties' where order does not finally dispose of those rights, but leaves them 'to be determined by the Courts in the ordinary way,' the order is not final.

statement: The applicant failed to comply with the condition of entering into good and sufficient security within one month from the date of application for conditional leave to appeal, as required by rule 3(a) of the Schedule to the Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Now in the present case it is undisputed that, before the expiry of one month from January 30, the applicant neither applied for nor obtained an extension of time under rule 3 (a) or at all. What the applicant contends, however, is that in tendering his security and making his application upon February 28, (i.e., within the month) he had done all that rule 3 (a) required to be done within the month."
statute_citation_verbatim: Rule 3(a) of the Schedule to the Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance (Cap. 85), Rule 7(1) of the Appellate Procedure (Privy Council) Order, 1921.

statement: The Court must determine whether the premises are reasonably required by the landlord for occupation, without considering the tenant's difficulties.
supporting_quote: "The tenant's difficulties do not come into the matter at all. The only thing that matters is the reasonableness of the landlord's requirement."

statement: The requirement of premises by a landlord is reasonable when considering the impact on both the landlord and tenant, as well as other relevant factors.
supporting_quote: "Furthermore, as I have said, there is nothing in the section to suggest that this one factor alone should be considered. I do not even think that to consider the requirement of the premises from the landlord's point of view exclusively would be any more reasonable than to consider it from the tenant's point of view exclusively."

statement: A retrospective statute is a statute that has effect from a date anterior to that on which it becomes law. Regardless of the time at which the tenancy commenced, it is unlawful for any landlord to demand, receive, or recover, and for any tenant to pay, or offer to pay, in respect of a period commencing on or after the day on which the Ordinance comes into operation in any area, any rent in excess of the rent which may lawfully be received or paid under the Ordinance.
supporting_quote: It shall not be lawful for the landlord of any premises to which this Ordinance applies- (a) to demand, receive or recover as the rent of such premises, in respect of any period commencing on or after the appointed date, any amount in excess of the authorised rent of such premises as defined for the purposes of this Ordinance in section 4 ; or (b) to increase the rent of such premises in respect of any such period to an amount in excess of such authorised rent. (1A) It shall not be lawful for the tenant of any premises to which this Ordinance applies to pay or offer to pay, as the rent of such premises, any amount in excess of the authorised rent of such premises as defined for the purposes of this Ordinance in section 4.
statute_citation_verbatim: Sections 3 (1) and 3 (1A) of the Rent Restriction Ordinance, No. 60 of 1942

statement: A subsequent erroneous addition to a description will not vitiate an adequate and sufficient definition of what is intended to pass by a deed, provided the original description was clear and certain.
supporting_quote: "It is settled law that any subsequent erroneous addition, as in this instance, will not vitiate an adequate and sufficient definition with certainty of what is intended to pass by a deed."

statement: A co-owner can institute an action for damages caused to the common property without joining the other co-owners as parties.
supporting_quote: "One co-owner can institute an action for damages caused to the common property without joining the other co-owners either as plaintiffs or defendants."

statement: A pre-emptive action can be brought against all co-owners in one action, even if the plaintiffs have different shares and are claiming relief alternatively.
supporting_quote: "The order of the learned District Judge is therefore set aside and the case remitted to the lower Court for trial of the issues other than the 10th, 12th, 13th and 14th issues. The plaintiffs will be entitled to the costs of appeal and of the argument in the lower Court."

statement: Section 348 of the Civil Procedure Code does not apply where a liability as surety is incurred before the institution of an action and after the dispute has been referred to arbitration.
supporting_quote: "That section applied only where a liability was incurred as surety for the performance of the decree after the institution of the action and before the entering of the decree."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 348 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A privy in estate to a party is not bound by an order of amendment to a decree if the interest was acquired prior to the amendment.
supporting_quote: "But in this case the 2nd defendant had acquired his interest under 2D1 anterior to even the application made by the plaintiff to have the decree amended. His rights therefore had accrued to him not subsequent to the order of amendment but prior to it and he cannot there�fore be deemed to be privy in estate to the 1st defendant"

statement: The principles of lis pendens and prior registration are applicable to decrees entered in respect of two competing pre-emption suits.
supporting_quote: "The principles of lis pendens and prior registration are applicable to decrees-entered in respect of two competing pre-emption suits."

statement: Entries of statements regarding title to land made in documents prepared under sections 10 and 11 of the Defence (Paddy Cultivation) Regulations, 1943, are admissible without further proof such as by calling the persons who wrote or made the entries.
supporting_quote: "Entries of statements regarding title to land made in documents which were prepared under sections 10 and 11 of the Defence (Paddy Cultivation) Regulations, 1943, fall under section 35 of the Evidence Ordinance and are admissible without further proof such as by calling the persons who wrote or made the entries or statements."
statute_citation_verbatim: Sections 34 to 38, 84 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: A fidei commissum is not created where the beneficiaries are not specifically and clearly designated.
supporting_quote: "While the intention to create a fidei commissum is unquestionable, it is an essential requisite to the constitution of a valid fidei commissum that the beneficiaries to be benefited must be specifically and clearly designated. In this respect the deed completely fails. I am therefore of opinion that the deed does not create a valid fidei commissum."

statement: The expression 'surviving donee' should be interpreted as 'other donee' in a fidei commissum in Ceylon, where the circumstances justify interpreting the term to ensure the homogeneity of the property as a family endowment.
supporting_quote: "These factors, in my opinion, justify the courts in Ceylon in interpreting the expression 'surviving' as 'other' in certain cases where perhaps the courts in England would hesitate to do so, and in doing so in the present case."

statement: On the death of either Ariyadasa or Piyatileke without lawful issue, the half share given to the person so dying would devolve absolutely on his lawful children.
supporting_quote: "(c) that on the death of either Ariyadasa or Piyatileke the half share given to the person so dying would devolve absolutely on his lawful children;"

statement: The 1st substituted defendant should be declared the de jure trustee of the Maviddapuram Kandaswamy Temple, given his long-standing management and the absence of a formal trustee.
supporting_quote: "In such circumstances any Court of equity would hold that, in the interests of the temple and all concerned, the 1st substituted defendant should be held and declared to be the de jure trustee of this temple, and I so declare him to be."

statement: Section 84(1) of the Ordinance does not apply to claims made under section 46(1).
supporting_quote: "The fallacy in this argument lies in ignoring proviso (ii) of section 84 (1). It is true that in the 'first example referred' to earlier A would have been entitled to claim Rs. 200 if the amount with which he was ' properly chargeable ' is regarded as Rs. 900 but the proviso (ii) proceeds to say that A cannot .claim anything more than Rs. 100 when it enacts that ' he shall not be entitled by virtue of this section to any relief greater than that provided by .... section 43 (3)."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 84(1) and proviso (ii)

statement: A donatio inter vivos where the gift is perfected by the intention to give coupled with acceptance by the donee, and there is no transfer of property, creates a chose in action for the donee.
supporting_quote: "In this case we are dealing with a donation which falls within the second category. The plaintiff's right under this donation was a chose in action and nothing more."

statement: Under the Kandyan law, a widow has the right to mortgage the estate of her deceased husband for the payment of his debts.
supporting_quote: "A widow having the administration of her deceased husband's estate may, in the minority of her children from necessity, mortgage the landed property; but it must be clearly to satisfy the most necessary and urgent wants of the family, otherwise the children might not be held liable to pay the debt. But in all cases where the children are grown up to fourteen or fifteen years of age, thier consent is necessary to such a mortgage being valid against them and their land"

statement: A deed of gift in consideration of marriage, to be irrevocable under the Kandyan Law Declaration and Amendment Ordinance, No. 39 of 1938, must not only be proved to be in consideration of a future marriage but also 'expressed to be' in consideration of a future marriage.
supporting_quote: "A deed of gift in consideration of marriage, to be irrevocable in terms of section 5 (1) (6) of the Kandyan Law Declaration and Amendment Ordinance, No. 39 of 1938, must not only be proved to be in consideration of a future marriage, but must also be ' expressed to be ' in consideration of a future marriage."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 5 (1) (b) of the Kandyan Law Declaration and Amendment Ordinance, No. 39 of 1938.

statement: An informal agreement for establishing an interest affecting land, such as a lease renewable from month to month, is not subject to the Statute of Frauds if it is not illegal and does not involve a definite term exceeding one month.
supporting_quote: "A promise, bargain, contract or agreement for establishing any interest affecting land must be embodied in a notarial document-a lease at will and a lease for any period not exceeding one month are excepted from the operation of the section."

statement: An action for use and occupation cannot be maintained against a person who claims to occupy the land as of right.
supporting_quote: "An action for use and occupation cannot be maintained against a defendant who claims to occupy the land as of right."

statement: A lessee under a notarial lease who has not been put in possession of the property leased can bring an action against third parties in possession of the property and compel them to surrender possession to him without making the lessors parties to the action.
supporting_quote: "The District Judge gave judgment for the plaintiffs. The only point that was argued by the appellants' Counsel was that the plaintiffs who did not get possession under P8 or P9 could not sue third parties without making the lessors parties to the action, as the lease in their favour. was for a period under ten years. He contended that such a lease did not amount to an alienation unlike a lease in longum tempus."

statement: A mortgagee cannot compel a puisne encumbrancer who acquires his title after the entering up of the decree in the mortgage action to be a party to the suit, and such an encumbrancer's failure to register the instrument under which he derives his title or register his address does not make him bound by the decree.
supporting_quote: "A mortgagee cannot possibly make a puisne encumbrancer who acquires his title after the entering up of the decree in the mortgage action a party to the suit and a puisne encumbrancer who acquires his title subsequent to the decree cannot possibly register the instrument under which he derives his title or register his address so that it may be in the registers at the date of filing of the plaint."

statement: Under Muslim Law, the principle of succession per stirpes is unknown and as among residuaries, the nearer in degree to the intestate excludes the more remote.
supporting_quote: "Besides, it is a well known doctrine that as among residuaries the nearer in degree to the intestate excludes the more remote. The 5th defendant, the niece of Amina Umma, is neither a sharer nor a residuary but she is in fact one who falls under the category of 'distant kindred' who can take only on the failure of sharers and residuaries. She would therefore be excluded by the residuary, the 4th defendant."

statement: A beneficiary cannot initiate an action for partition, only the trustee can do so.
supporting_quote: "The trustee is the person who can institute an action for partition for he is vested with title; a beneficiary cannot [ Daniel v. Saranelis Appu, (1903) 7 N. L. R. 163. ; Silva v. Silva, (1916) 19 N. L. R. 47]."

statement: The possession of an intestate and his heirs can be added together for the purpose of computing the period of ten years' adverse possession.
supporting_quote: "For the purpose of computing this period of prescription the possession of a deceased person and his executor or heir and of a person and his particular successor whether legatee or purchaser will be reckoned together"

statement: Deeds conveying undivided shares in land without clear boundaries create only undivided interests, not specific allotments.
supporting_quote: "Applying the test of precision which appears to me to be called for in such cases, I have taken the view that Rajapakse by the deeds 1 D 1 and P4 conveyed to his two children only undivided shares in the proportions of 2/3to 1/3 respectively."

statement: A party required to serve notice may do so by a writing signed by him 'by his Attorney', as that is permissible under the common law and there is nothing in Rule 5 to show that the right under the common law has been taken away.
supporting_quote: "It is, however, not difficult to take the view that Rule 6 applies only to what has to be done in Court and not to a notice of 'an intended application' referred to in Rule 2 in Schedule 1 to the Ordinance and not given with the assistance of the Court. Such a view of the law has the merit of not placing unnecessary technical difficulties in the way of a party wishing to appeal to His Majesty in Council."

statement: A right of way can only be claimed as appertaining to land, and it is personal in nature.
supporting_quote: "The simple answer to this claim is that it is personal from its very nature and that a right of way can only be claimed as appertaining to land."

statement: The plaintiffs are entitled to a right of servitude over the defendants' land for a footpath and water course, even if they cannot show that this was specifically granted.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me, therefore, that even assuming that the plaintiff is not in a position to show that the right of way had been granted over the Eastern portion, he is entitled by virtue of the right conferred on him by law to elect and to claim the right of way over the Eastern portion of defendants' land along lot 4."

statement: A plaintiff who has transferred their business and all associated debts to another party loses the right to sue for those debts, as the cession of action is complete.
supporting_quote: "There can be no question that requirements (1) and (2) are satisfied in the present case and inasmuch as no special formalities are necessary under our law for the assignment of a debt, the cession of action was complete when the plaintiff transferred to his children his entire business and the debts due to him. Thereafter he had no right to sue his debtors. That right passed to the cessionaries."

statement: Abandonment of an incumbency by a priest constitutes the forfeiture of that to which his pupils' rights of succession are attached, namely the incumbency itself.
supporting_quote: The abandonment of an incumbency by a priest, on the other hand, constitutes the forfeiture of that to which his pupils' rights of succession are attached, namely the incumbency itself. The priest remains a priest, but abandons his rights to the incumbency, upon which the pupillary rights of succession are dependent.

statement: A co-owner has the right to build and live on common land, provided that such use is reasonable and proportionate to their share of ownership.

statement: Section 17 of the Partition Ordinance does not prohibit the alienation or hypothecation, pending partition proceedings, of an interest to which a co-owner may ultimately become entitled by virtue of the decree in the pending action; if such an instrument is in effect a present alienation or hypothecation of a contingent interest, the rights of ownership (or the hypothecary rights) vest in the grantee automatically upon the acquisition of that interest by the grantor.

statement: The market value of shares, for estate duty purposes, should be based on the price a willing vendor and purchaser would reasonably expect, considering the nature of the business, risks involved, and any restrictions in the Articles of Association.
supporting_quote: "In regard to valuation, for purposes of estate duty, of shares (not being preference shares) held by a deceased person in a Company at the time of his death in September, 1940 Held , (i) that the price which the willing vendor could reasonably expect to obtain and a willing purchaser could reasonably expect to have to pay for the shares in question is the measure of the value contemplated in section 20 (1) of the Estate Duty Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Estate Duty Ordinance (Cap. 187), section 20 (1)

statement: When a bona fide possessor of property makes a claim to compensation for any necessary improvements made by him, the rents and profits which have been received from the property should be set-off against the expenses incurred in making the improvements.
supporting_quote: "But, curiously, although in strict law as explained above, a bona fide possessor is entitled to the benefit of fruits gathered by him during his possession, still, when it comes to a matter of calculating the amount of the compensation to be paid to him for improvements, the authorities are agreed that the rents and profits which have been received are to be set-off against the expenses incurred in producing those profits as well as in the general improvements of the property itself."

statement: A Court has no right to ignore or supersede the appointment made by a testator, as that would be substituting for the testator's mind the mind of the Court, which is totally indefensible.
supporting_quote: "I would emphatically say that the Court has no right to ignore or supersede the appointment made by a testator. That would be to substitute for the testator's mind the mind of the Court a course totally indefensible."

statement: An agreement in writing such as P1 can in law be revived only by another writing attested by a notary as required by section 2 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The 'extensions' the first plaintiff says he gave were not in law extensions of the agreement but were mere indications that the plaintiffs were willing to purchase Hapugahalande if the defendant could bring about its transfer. statement: A Court can entertain an action even after a Debt Conciliation Board has made an order 'hearing postponed sine die' if the transaction is not in form a mortgage or charge over property.

statement: In an action rei vindicatio, the plaintiff must establish dominium to the land in dispute or risk having their claim fail.
supporting_quote: 'To bring the action rei vindicatio plaintiff must have ownership actually vested in him-1 Nathan p. 362, s. 593 ' . . . . . . . ' This action arises from the right of dominium. By it we claim specific recovery of property belonging to us but possessed by someone else '- Pereira (1913 ed.) p. 300 quoting Voet 6.12.

statement: The exercise of a power of appointment must be closely examined to ascertain whether the fiduciary has acted within the strict limits of the mandate imposed on them.
supporting_quote: "Therefore, in my view, there was not a complete execution of her power or mandate, and the whole appointment, in consequence, fails."

statement: A fideicommissary gift involving a benefit to the family is valid upon acceptance by the fiduciary alone, enuring to the benefit of the fideicommissaries.
supporting_quote: "I would hold that P1 involves a benefit to the family and that Rasathangam's acceptance of It is sufficient acceptance on behalf of her children."

statement: The notice requirement under section 6 of the Partition Ordinance must be strictly followed, and failure to provide notice for an alternative scheme can invalidate subsequent orders.

statement: A mortgagee's rights under a deed can be enlarged by its terms, and in Ceylon, a mortgagee is not bound by all English law conceptions but must strictly fulfill the terms of the deed.

statement: The term 'acquired property' as used in the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 10 of the Kandyan Law Declaration and Amendment Ordinance does not have the same meaning as that term has in sub-section (3), and clauses (b) and (c) of sub-section (1) are not retrospective in their operation.

statement: An oral agreement for the sale of immovable property by the Crown is not valid unless it is saved by section 17 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance, which does not apply to such agreements.

statement: Under the Rent Restriction Ordinance, No. 60 of 1942, and the Rent Restriction Act, No. 29 of 1948, a landlord cannot demand or receive rent in excess of the authorized rent for any period commencing on or after the appointed date.

statement: An action to recover an alleged balance of the consideration for a sale of immovable property, where the deed does not recite that the full consideration has been paid and there is no statement in the attestation from which any promise or undertaking on the part of the vendor can be gathered, is prescribed in three years.

statement: An order of abatement in a partition action can be set aside without notice to all parties, making the subsequent proceedings valid.
supporting_quote: In my opinion the failure to notice the parties who should be noticed under section 405 of the Civil Procedure Code is an irregularity rendering the order made without notice liable to be set aside at the instance of the aggrieved party. statute_citation_verbatim: Section 405 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A decree entered on a mortgage bond, even if the bond was null and void due to the mortgagor being adjudged of unsound mind, is binding on the mortgagor and those claiming through her.

If it was executed by her in a lucid-interval it would, under the Roman Dutch Law, be considered valid. statement: A sub-tenant in occupation of premises under a contract of sub-tenancy entered into before an action for ejectment has commenced against the tenant is not bound by the decree in such an action unless he was joined as a party to the proceedings.

statement: A creditor may follow property sold by an heir, who takes only a defeasible title, even if the proceeds of sale were not applied towards the payment of the deceased's debts.

statement: Amendments to the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance operate retrospectively from July 17, 1911.

statement: A donee who has used violence on the donor can revoke the deed of gift, unless the donee has purchased any of the lands gifted prior to the institution of this action.

statement: The interest of a deceased partner in the partnership assets passed to surviving partners by reason only of a bona fide purchase for full consideration in money or money's worth which was paid to the vendor for his own benefit, thereby exempting estate duty on the market value of the deceased’s interest in goodwill and other partnership assets.

statement: A quia timet action should not be entertained merely because the rights of the plaintiff have been disputed by the defendant. statement: Property held by a fiduciary under a fidei commissum passes to the fiduciary's descendants as a joint fidei commissum, not separate fidei commissa.

statement: A valid fidei commissum can be created by a deed of gift that directs the donee to convey property upon their death, even if there is no specific conveyance from the donee.
supporting_quote: "The ruling in Dantuwa's case was once again expressly rejected. Learned Counsel have not referred me to any case in which doubts as to the correctness of the decision in Bibile v. Thambiah3[(1934) 36 N, L, R, 105,], counsel of great experience did not challenge the proposition that a deed of gift by way of dowry directing that 'if she, the dowry grantee, has issue she shall cause the properties to reach them when they come of age' was sufficient to create a fidei commissum in favour of the grantee's children notwithstanding the absence of any express indication as to what should happen in the event of the directions to the donee not being carried out."

statement: The court should not allow the first defendant to claim a trust was created when there is no clear evidence of such an arrangement.

statement: For the purposes of reckoning prescriptive possession, an administrator appointed to represent intestate heirs is deemed to represent those heirs and can plead any disability suffered by them during the period in question.

statute_citation_verbatim: Section 472 of the Civil Procedure Code and Section 13 of the Prescription Ordinance

statement: A landlord is not obliged to give notice before instituting an action for ejectment under section 9 of the Rent Restriction Act, No. 29 of 1948, where a tenant has sub-let the premises in contravention of section 9(1).

statement: A conditional gift is valid under Muslim Law, whereas a contingent gift is void.

statement: In a partition action, the standard of proof required to establish title is no different from that in any other civil suit.

statement: A would-be pre-emptor cannot claim to be in a better position by not receiving notice of the intended sale than he would have been if he had received such notice.
supporting_quote: "A would-be pre-emptor cannot claim to be in a better position by not receiving notice of the intended sale than he would have been if he had Received such notice."

statement: A person who has been in possession of property for a period exceeding the prescriptive period can acquire title to that property through prescription, even if they were initially only a beneficial owner.
supporting_quote: "In 1926 the plaintiff, believing herself to be not only the beneficial but the absolute owner of the undivided one-fourth share in question, went into occupation of the divided allotment of land represented by that share, and remained in occupation of it for over 19 years on the basis that she was entitled to possession in her own right. It therefore follows that, on the expiry of 10 years from the date of the conveyance of March 12, 1926, she acquired prescriptive title to the premises not only against the original vendor but also as against her father who, by acting contrary to his mandate, had acquired under the conveyance only the 'bare bones' of the legal estate."

statement: A person who, with knowledge of the vendor's intended fraud, joins the wrongdoer in a transaction for their mutual benefit is guilty of 'collusion' which can defeat the priority conferred by law under Section 7(2) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance.
supporting_quote: In other words, he entered into a collusive transaction with Thambimuttu and lent himself as a party to the latter's intended fraud on his previous vendors. This thoroughly disreputable transaction took place within a short time of the date on which the appellants' rights under 1D2 would have been strengthened by the acquisition of prescriptive title to the 1/4 share purchased by them in 1938.

statement: Rules 7 and 8 of the Schedule to the Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance have no application to a case where the decree, without affording any substantial relief or remedy, declares a right or status.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that these rules have no application to a case of this kind. What is the decree which has been appealed against ? It is a decree declaring that a certain document is a genuine last will. How is that decree to be executed ? A decree which declares a will to be genuine does not fall within any of the heads A to F in s. 217. Such a decree falls under head G of s. 217 which provides : ' Or it (the Court) may, without affording any substantive relief or remedy, declare a right or status '."

statement: The Supreme Court found that the appellant's story about the transfer deed and will was false due to documentary evidence showing Selvadurai, a key witness, was in Vavuniya at the time.

statement: An attorney's power of attorney must be strictly construed, and general words in a power of attorney are limited to the purpose for which the authority is given.
supporting_quote: "General words do not confer general powers, but are limited to the purpose for which the authority is given, and are construed as enlarging special powers when necessary, and only when necessary, for that purpose."

statement: A verbal transaction of sale is not a 'bill of sale' within the meaning of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, and thus does not require registration.
