statement: The mere fact that the title of a mortgagor is disputed at a sale is not by itself a reason for setting aside a sale.
supporting_quote: "It may, combined with other facts, afford ground for such a consequence. In this case the learned Judge has not found, and there is no evidence upon which we can say, that the purchaser was responsible for the distribution of the pamphlets. Further there is no material whatever in this case upon which it can be suggested that the claim asserted by Suriaratchi was not genuine."

statement: An amendment to a plaint that introduces a new cause of action, particularly one related to trust and prescription, should be refused if it would prejudice the defendant's plea of prescription.
supporting_quote: "The plaintiff instituted the action on the footing that he had a superior title to the defendant's and that the defendant was a trespasser and asked for a declaration in his favour and ejectment of the defendant. The amendment seeks to make out, as an alternative cause of action, that the title to the property remained in the defendant and that he held it in trust for the plaintiff and that the defendant was liable to execute in favour of the former a good and valid conveyance."

statement: Where certain co-owners obtained a Crown grant in their favour to the exclusion of the other co-owners by wilfully suppressing at the 'settlement' inquiry the fact that the latter were entitled to shares, held, that, by operation of section 92 of the Trusts Ordinance, the title of the holders of the Crown grant was subject to a trust in respect of the shares of those co-owners whose rights had not been disclosed.
supporting_quote: Held , that, by operation of section 92 of the Trusts Ordinance, the title of the holders of the Crown grant was subject to a trust in respect of the shares of those co-owners whose rights had not been disclosed.
statute_citation_verbatim: Trusts Ordinance {Cap. 72), s. 92

statement: A tenant cannot claim compensation for improvements from a person who does not derive title through the landlord but independently of him.
supporting_quote: "In the present case there cannot be any question but that the title of the second defendant was quite independent of and not at all derived from the defendant Alles and therefore the plaintiffs could not have claimed any compensation for their improvements from the second defendant whose predecessor-in-title, the first defendant's mother, also had nothing to do with the improvements and neither of whom were bound by any agreement express or implied between the plaintiffs and the first defendant. Both of them were perfect strangers to and had nothing to do with the plaintiffs and neither of them were bound by any acts or conduct of the first defendant."

statement: Under the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, section 35, when immovable property gifted by a deceased person is brought into collation, the legal title to it continues with the donee and does not vest in the administrator of the donor's estate.
supporting_quote: "When immovable property which was the subject-matter of a donation is brought into collation under section 35 of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, the legal title to it continues to remain with the donee and does not vest in the administrator of the deceased donor's estate."
statute_citation_verbatim: Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (Cap. 47), s. 35.

statement: A court has the power to grant relief against a mistake in deeds that results in a misdescription of the corpus which parties intended to and believed themselves to be dealing with.
supporting_quote: "I am in agreement with the view of my brother Gunasekara J. that this Court has power to grant relief against a mistake in the deeds of parties which results in a misdescription of the corpus which parties intended to and believed themselves to be dealing with."

statement: Where different parts of a deed are inconsistent with each other, effect ought to be given to that part which is calculated to carry into effect the real intention of the parties, and that part which would defeat it should be rejected.
supporting_quote: "where different parts of a deed are inconsistent with each other, effect ought to be given to that part which is calculated to carry into effect the real intention of the parties, and that part which would defeat it should be rejected."

statement: A father, when he makes a donation to his minor child under Roman-Dutch law, can authorize some other person by 'a special mandate' to accept the gift on the child's behalf.
supporting_quote: "Under Roman-Dutch law, a father, when he makes a donation to his minor child, can authorise some other person by ' a special mandate ' to accept the gift on the child's behalf."

statement: The earlier possession of a usufructuary mortgagee enures to the benefit of the cessionary for the purpose of defeating by prescription a subsequent claimant's superior title based on prior registration.
supporting_quote: "When the usufructuary mortgage bond was discharged by payment, D. was admitted to possession by the mortgagee on the footing that he was the person who had lawfully succeeded to the mortgagor's interests in the land. Held, that, in the circumstances of the case, the earlier possession of the usufructuary mortgagee enured to the benefit of D. for the purpose of defeating by prescription the subsequent claim of E. to have acquired superior title to the property on the ground of prior registration."

statement: A purchaser's payment of the full stipulated consideration strengthens his claim to retain the property, unless there is sufficient evidence to prove fraud.
supporting_quote: "It is no doubt true that the payment of the consideration for the purchase is by no means conclusive of the genuineness or honesty of the transaction. It is only one factor and, while it will not enable the purchaser to retain the property where he has participated in the fraud, vide Meera Saibo v. Ayan Sinnavan1[ (1927) 29 N. L. R. 84.], yet where there is not sufficient evidence to involve the purchaser in any fraud, or where it is merely a case of suspicion of his participation in a fraud, then the payment of the full stipulated consideration strengthens considerably the purchaser's claim to retain the land he has bought, vide Perera v. Menik Etana 2[(1918) 5 C. W. R. 258]."

statement: A minor's acceptance of a deed of gift must be through his own actions, not by a maternal uncle without lawful authority.
supporting_quote: "Without appointment by lawful authority Kanthar Sinnathamby could not act for Kanthavanam and it is not suggested that any such appointment existed. Therefore acceptance could only spring from Kanthavanam himself, if there was in fact acceptance."

statement: Clause 21 of the will did not create a valid fideicommissum and provided for only one grade of fidei commissaries.
supporting_quote: "I therefore take the view that clause 21 did not create a valid fideicommissum, and that the testator intended the appropriate shares in the Madampitiya property to vest absolutely, and without further restrictions, in each institute (or his substitute, as the case may be)."

statement: Mere lapse of time not satisfactorily explained should not bar the admission to probate of a will where such lapse of time has not affected the rights of any person.
supporting_quote: "I cannot understand why mere lapse of time not satisfactorily explained ought to bar the admission to probate of a will properly executed and acknowledged to be genuine and where such lapse of time has not affected the rights of any person."

statement: Where, in an action rei vindicatio, the defendant sets up a jus tertii, though he himself may not be claiming under that title, it will be sufficient and competent for the plaintiff to repel that plea by showing that a judgment secured by him against the third party operates as res judicata as between himself and the third party.
supporting_quote: Where, in an action rei vindicatio, the defendant sets up a jus tertii, though he himself may not be claiming under that title, it will be sufficient and competent for the plaintiff to repel that plea by shewing that a judgment secured by him against the third party operates as res judicata as between himself and the third party.

statement: Failure to register a lis pendens in a partition action as required by section 12 (1) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance deprives the decree entered in the action of the 'conclusive effect' which it would otherwise have under section 9 of the Partition Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "The one clear instance of a failure of jurisdiction laid down by the Privy Council is where the breach of a procedural provision results in the violation of natural justice. In the case before us there is no such violation."
statute_citation_verbatim: Registration of Documents Ordinance (Cap. 101), s. 12 (1); Partition Ordinance (Cap. 56), ss. 3, 9, 17.

statement: The failure to give notice of a sale is immaterial if the pre-emptor had no sufficient means to purchase the property at the time it was sold.
supporting_quote: "Held, that as plaintiff had no sufficient means to purchase the property at the time it was sold the failure to give her notice of the sale was immaterial."

statement: A purchaser who could have completed his title by prescriptive possession but has not done so and thereby suffers eviction is not entitled to sue for recovery of the purchase price and damages.
supporting_quote: "I am therefore of opinion that any action, whatever its form may be, where the validity of the title conveyed comes up for determination and decision against such title is given, a cause of action for breach of warranty will arise, provided, of course, the vendor had been duly noticed to warrant and defend the title conveyed by him."

statement: An action to have a gift revoked on the ground of subsequent birth of a child is not subject to Section 6 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that an action to have a gift revoked on the ground of the subsequent birth of a child is based on a cause of action 'not expressly provided for' in the Ordinance, and therefore becomes prescribed within 3 years from the time when the cause of action has accrued (Section 10)."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of the Prescription Ordinance (Cap. 55)

statement: In order to establish that the vendor had no shadow of title to the property conveyed, a very high standard of proof was required.
supporting_quote: "While I have some sympathy for the respondent, I consider that he has fallen short of proving that his vendor had 'no shadow of a title' to the property conveyed. It seems that in order to bring a party within the benefits of the exception referred to in the above case, a very high standard of proof is required and that it is not sufficient merely to adduce a situation from which it might be suspected or inferred that the vendor's title was unsound."

statement: When a party to an agreement to re-transfer repudiates at a point of time prior to the expiration of the period of the option, it is unnecessary for the other party to allege or prove tender.
supporting_quote: "I agree with the contention of learned Counsel for the appellants that the answer, taken as a whole, amounts in effect to a repudiation of the appellants' right to a re-transfer, in that the position taken up by the respondents is inconsistent with the acceptance of that right. It would seem, therefore, that the appellants have successfully brought themselves within the principle1 that when a party to an agreement to re-transfer repudiates at a point of time prior to the expiration of the period of the option, it is unnecessary for the other party to allege or prove tender."

statement: A will may be composed of numerous papers, which together make one instrument. The Court should consider the question whether, in the light of the evidence adduced in the particular case, the papers in question constitute a single instrument in conformity with the requirements of section 4 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance or whether they are 'separate and independent' documents.
supporting_quote: A will may be composed of numerous papers, which together make one instrument. In such a case, the Court should consider the question whether, in the light of the evidence adduced in the particular case, the papers in question constitute a single instrument in conformity with the requirements of section 4 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance or whether they are 'separate and independent' documents.
statute_citation_verbatim: It (the Will) shall be signed at the foot or end thereof by the Testator . . . such signature shall be made or acknowledged by the Testator in the presence of five or more witnesses present at the same time, and such witnesses shall subscribe the Will in the presence of the Testator, but no form of attestation shall be necessary.

statement: Under the Roman Dutch Law, a wife who is guilty of malicious desertion forfeits her right to recover property gifted as dowry upon dissolution of marriage.
supporting_quote: "Thus, the plaintiff has no cause of action to sue the defendant and to that limited extent, the decision in Fernando v. Fernando (supra) is of assistance to the defendant."

statement: For the purpose of reckoning the period of prescription, the action against a company must be taken to have been instituted on the date of the original plaint and not upon the amendment of the caption of the plaint.
supporting_quote: Held, that, for the purpose of reckoning the period of prescription, the action against the company must be taken to have been instituted on the date of the original plaint and not upon the amendment of the caption of the plaint.

statement: A lessee who consents to erect buildings on leased property and agrees to yield them up at the end of the lease cannot claim compensation for those improvements unless such a right was expressly or impliedly renounced in the contract.
supporting_quote: "For the same reason, there was-in the absence of agreement to that effect-no legal foundation for the exercise of the alternative right to be compensated for the loss of the improvements after the lease had expired."

statement: A court may grant a declaratory decree to protect future or contingent rights, provided the dispute is concrete and genuine and would serve some real purpose in future litigation between the same parties.
supporting_quote: "Cases may well occur in which such a decree would be justified to accomplish the ends of precautionary justice for the protection even of future or contingent rights. Vide the authorities cited in Hewavitarane v. Chandrawathie 2[(1951) 53 N. L. R. 169 at 174, 175.]"

statement: The Principal Collector of Customs had neither actual authority under sections 17 and 108 of the Customs Ordinance nor ostensible authority on behalf of the Crown to sell goods belonging to the Crown for non-payment of warehouse rent.
supporting_quote: "Their Lordships think therefore that nothing done by the Principal Collector or the Chief Secretary amounted to a holding out by the Crown that the Principal Collector had the right to enter into a contract to sell the goods which are the subject-matter of this action."
statute_citation_verbatim: Customs Ordinance (Cap. 185)-Sections 17, 22, 47, 108

statement: The absence of a document evidencing an emphyteusis is not an insuperable objection, but the practical difficulty in proving it without a document makes it improper for this court to establish an emphyteusis.
supporting_quote: the practical difficulty however in the way of a party seeking to establish an emphyteusis in the absence of a document is the difficulty of proving it, and so far as this particular case is concerned, in which the appellants do not rely upon a document as a starting point, it is in my opinion unnecessary to say more than that on the evidence adduced before the learned District Judge it would not be proper for this court to hold that an emphyteusis had been established.

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift can create a fideicommissum, but this does not affect its revocability.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion one can properly infer from the observations made by this learned Judge that the creation of a fideicommissum by a Kandyan deed of gift does not by itself affect its revocability."

statement: A deed of gift may be set aside on the ground that the relations between the donor and donee were at or shortly before the execution of the gift such as to raise a presumption that the donee had influence over the donor.
supporting_quote: Where a deed of gift executed by the plaintiff in favour of her grand-daughter was impugned by the plaintiff on the ground that undue influence was exercised on her by the prospective father-in-law of the donee- Held , that a deed of gift may be set aside on the ground that the relations between the donor and donee were at or shortly before the execution of the gift such as to raise a presumption that the donee had influence over the donor.

statement: A binna marriage, once validated by registration, does not forfeit the inheritance rights of a daughter.
supporting_quote: "For the reasons which I have given, the learned Judge was wrong in taking the view that Dingirimenika forfeited her paternal inheritance. The true position is that her conveyance P2 in favour of the plaintiff vested in him an undivided one-third share in the property, and that her outstanding one-sixth share passed to her son the 6th defendant by maternal inheritance."

statement: A mortgage decree does not necessarily extinguish the mortgage, but imposes a new charge on the land.
supporting_quote: "On the institution of lis pendens, the mortgaged land becomes liable to be affected by the judgment, upon decree it becomes actually so affected. By the operation of the same principle, the order for the sale is binding upon any subsequent purchaser until the order has been finally carried out. It thus imposes a charge which prejudicially affects him."

statement: In the circumstances, it would be wholly unreasonable to authorise a decree for ejectment if the effect of such a decree would involve the tenant in very considerable financial loss and throw him out of business altogether.
supporting_quote: "Held, that, in the circumstances, it would be wholly unreasonable to authorise a decree for ejectment."

statement: A lessor cannot sue his lessee for ejectment under the Rent Restriction Act for being in default of rent unless he can first establish the termination of the contract of lease either by due notice or by effluxion of time.
supporting_quote: But this does not relieve the landlord of establishing the termination of the contract (either by due notice or by effluxion of time) before claiming a decree for ejectment.

statement: A Court should be slow to give an unconditional special direction for partition that includes improvements made by a co-owner unless the Court is satisfied, upon examination of all relevant considerations, that such a scheme is practicable and just.
supporting_quote: But a Court should, I think, be slow to make such a direction unconditionally, unless the Court has perfectly satisfied itself, upon an examination of all the relevant considerations, that such a scheme of partition is practicable and just.

statement: The dismissal of a partition action determines the title of the defendant as against the plaintiff, and this determination is res judicata in subsequent actions between the same parties.
supporting_quote: In the present case after the two parties had filed their pleadings and after the trial had been fixed the 3rd defendant expressly invited the Court upon a named contingency to adjudicate on his claim without evidence. I do not think he can now be heard to say that there was no investigation of the dispute between him and the 5th defendant.

statement: A servitude giving right to a 'share of the water' in a well does not include the use of the well sweep if no mention of the well sweep is made in the grant.
supporting_quote: "A servitude giving right to a 'share of the water' in a well does not include the right to the use of the well sweep if no mention of the well sweep is made in the grant."

statement: A temple that is consistently used by the public, where members of the public make contributions and improvements are made to it over a long period, can be considered a charitable trust even in the absence of an express dedication.
supporting_quote: "When such consistent and uninterrupted public user is added to the fact that throughout a long period of time the public have been in the habit of making contributions, both of money and kind, it seems to me that this militates strongly against the contention of the defendants that the temple and all the gifts received by it were and are their private property."

statement: An order for abatement of an action due to the plaintiff's death can be set aside if the application is made within a reasonable time and the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from continuing the action.
supporting_quote: "In terms of section 403 of the Code the order could be set aside upon an application made by a person claiming to be the plaintiff's legal representative if the application was made within a reasonable time and it was proved that he was prevented by sufficient cause from continuing the action."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 403 of the Code

statement: An indorsee for value cannot be confronted with defenses inconsistent with the terms of a memorandum or indorsement made on the face of the instrument by both the maker and the payee.
supporting_quote: "Even, therefore, if as between the defendants inter se, the true position (unknown to the plaintiff) was that the note sued on ought to be regarded as having been discharged on 15th January 1948, that defence is not in my opinion .available as against the plaintiff."

statement: A defendant who does not object to the share allotted to him in an interlocutory decree and subsequently appears without contesting his share cannot later challenge the validity of a final decree entered on that interlocutory decree.
supporting_quote: "In spite of the fact that he sent the petition and gave a proxy to Mr. Kularatne 'to file all necessary papers' I find that no further steps were taken in that behalf either by the 1st appellant or by Mr. Kularatne. He was given due notice (see Journal Entry P9 of 8.9.38) of the confirmation of the scheme but did not choose to appear in person or by proctor to support the objection he had taken in P5."

statement: For the purpose of deciding the present action, a later decision should be taken as superseding earlier conflicting judgments between the same parties or their successors in title.
supporting_quote: "Both principles apply to the judgment and decree in C. R. case No. 4923, and it is for this reason that I consider the decisions in the two earlier cases to be of no importance. They were superseded by the decision in the third case which is res judicata as between the plaintiff and the 3rd defendant on the one hand and the contesting defendants on the other."

statement: A tenant who is protected by the Rent Restriction Act has a large beneficial interest in the property and should be able to maintain a possessory action against spoliators.
supporting_quote: "It seems to me that as against a spoliator the person dispossessed need not prove possessio civilis to be restored to possession. Wille on Landlord 526 and Tenant states in Chapter XV, ' If the landlord ejects the tenant either forcibly or illicitly he commits an act of spoliation against the tenant and the tenant is entitled to a mandament van spolie or order replacing him in occupation or possession of the premises immediately and before the landlord can take, any further legal steps and as a preliminary to any inquiry or investigation into the merits of the case. '"

statement: A co-owner's right of pre-emption cannot logically survive the severance of the bond of co-ownership itself, such as after common property has been partitioned into separate allotments.
supporting_quote: "Once that has taken place, the foundation of any previously acquired right of pre-emption is automatically destroyed."

statement: The sale was ad quantitatem for an extent of 44 acres, and the defendants are liable to compensate the plaintiffs for the value of the remaining 5 acres.
supporting_quote: "An. extent of A. 5 R. 3 P. 20 is outstanding, and the defendants are liable to compensate the plaintiffs for the value of that extent."

statement: The amount of security ordered to be furnished by the judgment debtor should not be unduly excessive and should reasonably safeguard the interests of the judgment creditor in the event of the judgment appealed from being eventually affirmed.
supporting_quote: "The amount of security should be such as would reasonably safeguard the interests of the judgment-Creditor in the event of the judgment appealed from being eventually affirmed in appeal."

statement: A court has the power to vacate proceedings and grant a fresh adjudication when a party was unable to attend due to illness, provided they had retained a proctor and there is no evidence of deliberate delay.
supporting_quote: "The petitioner explains her default at the trial has been due to her serious ailment about that period and on her recovery it was that she made this application to this Court to have the proceedings of the trial vacated and to permit her an opportunity of proving her claim."

statement: Where there has been a series of transactions, between two persons, of goods sold and delivered, each item of purchase constitutes a separate debt, and the mere occurrence of an item of purchase within the period of limitation does not keep the claim alive as to the older sales effected outside that period.
supporting_quote: "Where there has been a series of transactions, between two persons, of goods sold and delivered, each item of purchase constitutes a separate debt, and the mere occurrence of an item of purchase within the period of limitation does not keep the claim alive as to the older sales effected outside that period."

statement: A person claiming compensation for improvements must show reasonable grounds to think they had some right of ownership in the land.
supporting_quote: "Before a person can claim compensation for improvements effected upon a land on the ground that he made the improvements as a bona fide possessor of the land he must show that he had reasonable or probable grounds to think that he had some right of ownership in the land."

statement: An order of abatement made under section 396 of the Civil Procedure Code does not prevent a lessee from maintaining an independent action against a defendant, provided that the lessee's right to relief depends on the validity of his lessor’s title and the lessee had already instituted proceedings before the order of abatement.
supporting_quote: "Section 403 primarily affects only a plaintiff or his legal representatives. It is unnecessary to decide for the purposes of this appeal whether a person who, after the date of an order for abatement in an action relating to property, purchases or obtains an interest in that property from the plaintiff, would be prevented (as a privy) by some other principle of law"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 403 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A continuing invasion of a subsisting right constitutes in truth a continuing cause of action, and the remedy for such an invasion is not barred by limitation if instituted within three years from when the fresh cause of action arises.
supporting_quote: "Indeed, the contrary view would indirectly produce the anomalous result of converting the provisions of section 10 into a weapon for the extinction of a right which cannot in law be extinguished by prescription. Be that as it may, the circumstances of the present case, interpreted by reference to the conduct of the parties, are clearly distinguishable from those which arose in the earlier decisions."

statement: Alienation of property in fraud of creditors may consist of a series of colourable transactions in respect of the same property.
supporting_quote: "Alienation of property in fraud of creditors may consist of a series of colourable transactions in respect of the same property."

statement: An order for discovery of documents need not be made as a matter of course, but is discretionary and may be resisted by a claim of privilege although no express provision in this behalf is to be found in section 102 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "An order for discovery of documents need not be made as a matter of course, but is discretionary and may be resisted by a claim of privilege although no express provision in this behalf is to be found in section 102 of the Civil Procedure Code."

statement: An assignee of a judgment-debtor who has been adjudicated insolvent must be named as a respondent in proceedings under section 339 of the Civil Procedure Code for execution of a hypothecary decree, or the sale will be void.
supporting_quote: "Therefore, where a mortgagor against whom a hypothecary decree has been entered is subsequently adjudged insolvent and the hypothecary decree is thereafter transferred by assignment from the mortgagee to any other person, such assignee, when he applies for execution of the decree under section 339 of the Civil Procedure Code, must name as respondent the assignee in insolvency of the judgment-debtor and/or a person who has purchased the mortgaged property from the assignee in insolvency. Failure to do so will render null and void the sale in execution of the hypothecary decree."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 339 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: All seizing creditors, including secondary and tertiary mortgagees, are entitled to share the money in deposit rateably so long as it has not been appropriated to a particular decree holder or holders by an order of that Court.
supporting_quote: "The justice of the case requires-and that is the test laid down in the section-that all the seizing creditors, including the appellants, should share rateably."

statement: In a partition action, the Court is entitled to order the demolition of a building constructed by a co-owner contrary to the protests of the other co-owners and in violation of their rights as co-owners.
supporting_quote: "Where a co-owner puts up a building on the common land, he cannot compel any of his co-owners to take over such buildings and pay compensation."

statement: A co-owner is entitled to use a common lane for the purpose of reaching his land if by doing so he does not interfere with the substantial rights of other co-owners.
supporting_quote: He is a co-owner of the lane and as such co-owner he is entitled to use it as a lane for the purpose of getting to his land on the east if by doing so he does not interfere with the substantial rights of the other co-owners.

statement: A co-owner who makes a plantation on the land held in common is entitled to take the entire produce of that plantation until the co-ownership is put an end to by a decree of the Court or mutual agreement. Similarly, a co-owner who erects a building on the land held in common is entitled to possess it until the land is partitioned.
supporting_quote: A co-owner who makes a plantation on the undivided land is entitled to take the entire produce of that plantation until the co-ownership is put an end to by a decree of the Court or mutual agreement. Similarly a co-owner who erects a building on the land held in common is entitled to possess it until the land is partitioned.

statement: A mortgage over a co-owner's interests would be entirely unaffected by a subsequent amicable partition to which the mortgagee himself was not a consenting party; and even if he did consent, the provisions of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance must be satisfied before the subsisting hypothecary rights could be enlarged in some respects or reduced in others.
supporting_quote: "In Ceylon, at any rate, a mortgage over a co-owner's interests would be entirely unaffected by a subsequent amicable partition to which the mortgagee himself was not a consenting party ; and even if he did consent, the provisions of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance must be satisfied before the subsisting hypothecary rights could be enlarged in some respects or reduced in others."

statement: A donee retains the option to either retain his gift and renounce his share in the donor's estate, or bring the value of the property into collation if he wishes to participate in the inheritance.
supporting_quote: "Thus, if a father gave property to his son on the occasion of the son's marriage, and died intestate, the son had the option of renouncing all claim to share in his father's estate or of bringing the property into collation. If he chose the latter alternative, he had a further option of bringing in either the property itself or the value thereof."

statement: A purchaser at a public auction of immovable property is entitled to sue a notary for the refund of exorbitant fees paid under a mistake of fact to the notary for attesting the conditions of sale.
supporting_quote: "This appeal involves a question of some importance relating to the rights and obligations of a purchaser at a public auction of immovable property in regard to the notarial fees payable by him for having the conditions of sale attested."

statement: Under Roman-Dutch law, a stranger to a contract is entitled to claim the benefit of a stipulation made in his favour provided that he accepts it within the prescribed period.
supporting_quote: "Under Roman-Dutch law a stranger to a contract is entitled to claim the benefit of a stipulation made in his favour. This rule is subject only to the qualification that until the benefit stipulated for has been accepted by him he can be deprived of it by agreement between the contracting parties without reference to him."

statement: The nature of the security given by a claimant under section 146 of the Ordinance, which includes personal guarantees and mortgages, is not necessarily objectionable in form.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, the nature of the securities given by the appellant in the present case-namely, the personal guarantee of a surety coupled with a mortgage in favour of the Crown of the surety's interest in a specified allotment of land, was unobjectionable in form."

statement: An owner of immovable property is entitled to enjoy it without disturbance and without fear of unjustifiable interference from outsiders. If his enjoyment is disturbed by forcible ouster, the remedies of a rei vindicatio action or (in appropriate cases) of a possessory action are available to him; if it is seriously threatened, he may demand in quia timet proceedings a declaration of his rights so as to prevent in anticipation the apprehended invasion of his rights of ownership.
supporting_quote: An owner of immovable property is entitled to enjoy it without disturbance and without fear of unjustifiable interference from outsiders. If his enjoyment is disturbed by forcible ouster, the remedies of a rei vindicatio action or (in appropriate cases) of a possessory action are available to him ; if it is seriously threatened, he may demand in quia timet proceedings a declaration of his rights so as to prevent in anticipation the apprehended invasion of his rights of ownership.

statement: The cause of action for an actionable wrong does not arise until the plaintiff suffers actual damage, even if the wrongful act was committed earlier.
supporting_quote: "There is no 'cause of action' until everything has happened which would entitle the plaintiff to judgment. Now in delict, a wrongful act or omission does not always by itself entitle a person complaining of it to judgment. There are cases where it does, e.g., where contumelia is involved. But there are many cases where the wrongful act does not give the plaintiff a right to judgment unless damage has been sustained, and the damage need not be contemporaneous with the wrongful act .... There may be a wrong without, at the time, any damage, and after an interval damage may for the first time result."

statement: In the absence of an agreement on the point, a purchaser of immovable property would make a sufficient tender of the purchase price if he offers security which effectively guarantees payment of the price immediately upon the vendor's complete fulfilment of his reciprocal obligations.
supporting_quote: "In the absence of an agreement on the point, a purchaser of immovable property would make a sufficient tender of the purchase price if he offers security which effectively guarantees payment of the price immediately upon the vendor's complete fulfilment of his reciprocal obligations."

statement: If a will is shown to have been in the testator's possession, and is not forthcoming at his death, it is presumed to have been destroyed by him animo revocandi.
supporting_quote: "If a will is shown to have been in the testator's possession, and is not forthcoming at his death, it is presumed to have been destroyed by him animo revocandi."

statement: A proctor's fiduciary relationship to his client renders him liable to indemnify the client in respect of damages incurred by the client in a transaction whereby the proctor, in breach of his fiduciary duty, gains an advantage and his client suffers loss as the result of advice given by him and taken by the client. Such a breach falls under section 10 of the Prescription Ordinance of Ceylon.
supporting_quote: "A Proctor's fiduciary relationship to his client renders him liable to indemnify the client in respect of damages incurred by the client in a transaction whereby the Proctor, in breach of his fiduciary duty, gains an advantage and his client suffers loss as the result of advice given by him and taken by the client. The Prescription Ordinance of Ceylon, unlike the English Statute of Limitations, ' governs the whole of a jurisdiction which is general, including law and equity in one system '."
statute_citation_verbatim: "The Prescription Ordinance of Ceylon, unlike the English Statute of Limitations, ' governs the whole of a jurisdiction which is general, including law and equity in one system '. It is therefore applicable to an action for damages for breach of a fiduciary duty. None of its sections dealing with special causes of action is applicable to a breach of a fiduciary duty and, therefore, such a 13 breach falls under section 10."

statement: A conveyance granting ownership of land and buildings, with a personal servitude of habitatio for the grantee’s heirs, operates under Roman Dutch law to transfer full ownership subject to this personal right.
supporting_quote: "the instrument prima facie operates under the Roman Dutch law as a grant of the ownership of the land and buildings to A subject only to a personal servitude of habitatio in favour of B"

statement: The jus superficiarium can be created by an informal agreement between the landowner and the person who acquires the right, and once acquired, it can be alienated or transmitted to heirs.
supporting_quote: "Ahamado Natchia's case (supra) was considered (after a re-trial) in a second appeal by Lascelles C.J. and Middleton J. in (1906) 9 N.L. R. 331. They observed that 'an agreement between the landowner and the person who acquires the right' is the foundation of the jus superficiarium"

statement: In a partition action, co-owners should be given the lot carrying their improvements only if it does not cause substantial injustice to other co-owners.
supporting_quote: Although, in a partition decree, a co-owner should, whenever possible, be given the lot which carries his improvements, this principle should not be adhered to if, in the process of giving effect to it, substantial injustice is likely to be caused to the other co-owners.

statement: Under section 20 of the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, title to half of the diatheddam property acquired by a husband vested in his wife immediately upon the acquisition of the property before it was amended on 3rd July, 1947. This vesting did not affect the husband's right to sell or mortgage the property.
supporting_quote: "Such immediate vesting of title in the wife was not inconsistent with the husband's right to sell or mortgage the property."

statement: In a claim against the estate of a deceased person, the court should scrutinize the plaintiff's case with 'great jealousy' due to the lack of direct evidence and the passage of time.
supporting_quote: "It is the duty of the Court to scrutinise the plaintiff's case with ' great jealousy '."

statement: A deed operating as a disposition of a protected holding must be attested by a notary with the written consent of the Government Agent, and failure to do so renders the deed null and void.
supporting_quote: "A notary shall not attest any deed operating as a disposition of a protected holding unless the written consent of the Government Agent to such disposition shall have been previously obtained nor unless such deed shall have attached thereto the document by which the Government Agent granted his consent to the disposition sought to be effected by such deed. Such document of consent shall be specifically referred to by the notary in the attestation of such deed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 162(1) of the Land Development Ordinance, Chapter 320

statement: The relationship between the parties is not one of a lease of immovable property, but rather an agreement for the management and control of a business as a going concern.
supporting_quote: "It is abundantly clear therefore that the document itself is no lease and definitely not a lease of any immovable property. It is however contended on behalf of the defendant-appellant that under the document P1 the lessee was required to permit one Perera who was carrying on the business of oilman stores in a part of the premises No. 39, Brownrigg Street, to carry on that business there, and to permit the lessor to use and occupy a room in the upstairs of the said premises and those requirements indicate that there was in truth a letting of the entirety of the building No. 39, Brownrigg Street. Further, it is said that de facto possession of the premises having been given and the quantum of rent payable in respect of the premises in accordance with the provisions of the Rent Restriction Act, viz., Rs. 130 a month having been taken into computation in fixing the amount of 'rent' of Rs. 380 a month payable by the lessee under P1, all the essential elements necessary to constitute a letting and hiring of immovable property have been established. I do not think this argument is sound."

statement: Once a tenant is more than one month in arrears of rent, they forfeit the protection against eviction provided by the Rent Restriction Act.
supporting_quote: "I fail to see how he regains the protection only by the act of tendering the arrears before the institution of the action. The Rent Restriction Act has made heavy inroads into the common law rights of the landlord and I do not see anything oppressive in interpreting proviso (a) to mean that, having regard to the new and extensive rights conferred on a tenant, it is a condition precedent to the continued protection of the Act against eviction that the tenant shall pay the rent not necessarily as it falls due but at least within a month thereafter."

statement: A breach of a covenant to pay rent does not automatically entitle the landlord to cancel the lease, but requires the non-payment to be deliberate and persistent for two years, with proper notice given by the landlord.
supporting_quote: "It is well settled law that it is not in every case of failure to pay rent the landlord is entitled to ask for a cancellation of the lease. To claim such a right the non-payment must be deliberate and persistent or contumacious. That is not all. The lessee must be in arrear of rent for 2 years."

statement: A tenant who enjoys, under the Rent Restriction Act, a statutory right of occupation notwithstanding the termination of the earlier contract of tenancy must continue to pay 'rent' at the original monthly rate; if he fails to honour this obligation and is in arrear of 'rent' for one month after it has become due, section 13 (1) (a) may be brought into operation to eject him.
supporting_quote: A tenant need not formally tender payment of rent due when the landlord has in anticipation refused to accept it. A PPEAL from a judgment of the Court of Requests, Kalutara.
statute_citation_verbatim: Rent Restriction Act, No. 29 of 1948, ss. 13 (I) (a) and 14.

statement: The court should consider the hardship to all affected parties, including third persons such as tenants or sub-tenants, when deciding on an eviction case.
supporting_quote: "To attempt to define classes, hardship to whom and to whom alone (apart from the parties) can be taken into account (whether as an element entering into the party's hardship, or on its own account) appears to us an unhelpful line of approach to the construction of the proviso. The true view, we think, is that the county court judge should take into account hardship to all who may be affected by the grant or refusal of an order for possession-relatives, dependants, lodgers, guests, and the stranger within the gates-but should weigh such hardship with due regard to the status of the persons affected and their ' proximity ' to the tenant or landlord and the extent to which, consequently, hardship to them would be hardship to him."

statement: The entirety of Rasammah's vested interest in the tediatetam property passed to her heirs upon her death, as the new sections 19 and 20 have no application.
supporting_quote: "Accordingly, the entirety of Rasammah's vested interest in the tediatetam property (i.e., a 7/36 share) passed to the appellants as her heirs."

statement: A Viharadhipati does not forfeit his right to the office when he leaves the temple of which he is Viharadhipati and takes up residence in another of which he is also Viharadhipati.
supporting_quote: "The office of Viharadhipati is not one that can be abandoned by mere residence in another place. There is nothing in the Vinaya or the decisions of this Court which requires a Viharadhipati to reside in the temple of which he is Viharadhipati."

statement: A bhikkhu is free to renounce his right to the management of a vihare, and such renunciation is valid according to both ecclesiastical law and common law.
supporting_quote: "None of the authorities cited by Counsel support the proposition he was seeking to establish. There is nothing in the Vinaya or the decisions of this Court which forbids a bhikkhu from renouncing his right to the management of a vihare."

statement: A Viharadhipati is the principal bhikkhu of a temple, who need not be resident in the temple, and this role is equivalent to the incumbent before 1931.
supporting_quote: "Instead of the words 'the chief' in the earlier definitions of 'incumbent' the definition of 'Viharadhipati' contains the words 'the principal' and the only other change effected is that a Bhikkhu could be a Viharadhipati whether he was resident in the temple or not-a change which was probably made because a priest can be an incumbent of more than one temple."

statement: A plea of res judicata fails where the earlier judicial decision does not constitute a final pronouncement on the issue in dispute, and no privity can be assumed between a pupil and his tutor who is not proved to be the true incumbent.
supporting_quote: "For the purposes of a dispute concerning rights to the incumbency of a Buddhist temple, no privity can be assumed between a pupil and his tutor who is not proved to be the true incumbent. Indajoti's concession in his pleadings that Ratnapala had at a certain stage lawfully succeeded to the incumbency has no bearing on the plea of res judicata"

statement: A person in the position of an agent is generally treated by English law as an express trustee, and thus cannot plead the benefit of the Prescription Ordinance under section 111(5) of the Trusts Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "that, inasmuch as a person in the position of an agent is generally treated by English law as an express trustee, the provisions of section 111 (5) of the Trusts Ordinance precluded the defendant from pleading the benefit of the Prescription Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 111(5) of the Trusts Ordinance

statement: Where a stranger enters into possession of a divided allotment of property, claiming to be sole owner, although his vendor in fact had legal title only to a share, Corea v. Appuhamy (supra) has no application unless his occupation of the whole was reasonably capable of being understood by the other co-owners as consistent with an acknowledgment of their title.
supporting_quote: "Where a stranger enters into possession of a divided allotment of property, claiming to be sole owner, although his vendor in fact had legal title only to a share, Corea v. Appuhamy (supra) has no application unless his occupation of the whole was reasonably capable of being understood by the other co-owners as consistent with an acknowledgment of their title."

statement: A co-owner who makes a plantation on the common property with the acquiescence of his co-owners is entitled to possess the entirety of that plantation as against the other co-owners until the common ownership is terminated by a partition action.
supporting_quote: "It may now be regarded as well settled that a co-owner who makes a plantation or builds a house on the common property with the acquiescence of his co-owners is entitled to possess the entirety of that plantation or house as against the other co-owners until the common ownership is terminated by a partition action."

statement: When land which is owned in common has been amicably partitioned, a former co-owner is not, as a general rule, entitled to claim a right of way over a portion allotted to another co-owner unless it has been expressly granted or reserved in the cross-conveyances executed by the co-owners.
supporting_quote: When land which is owned in common has been amicably partitioned, a former co-owner is not, as a general rule, entitled to claim a right of way over a portion allotted to another co-owner unless it has been expressly granted or reserved in the cross-conveyances executed by the co-owners, even though a well-defined footpath had existed prior to the severance of the common property.

statement: This Court has the power to correct an accidental slip or omission in a judgment under Section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code, even if it involves granting relief that was not originally requested by the parties.
supporting_quote: "When an error of that kind has been committed, it is always within the competency of the Court, if nothing has intervened which renders it inexpedient or inequitable to do so, to correct the record in order to bring it into harmony with the, order which the Judge obviously meant to pronounce."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 189 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A tenant's claim for the recovery of a premium paid illegally to a landlord is subject to prescription unless public policy dictates otherwise.
supporting_quote: "I would accordingly hold that the tenant's claim in reconvention for the recovery of Rs. 1,800 paid as premium was prescribed."

statement: A stipulation for the benefit of a third party can be validly created, and such a third party can sue upon it if accepted.
supporting_quote: "What concerns the interest of a third person may also be ' in modo' ; that is to say, that although I cannot directly stipulate what concerns the interest of a third person, nevertheless, I may alienate my own property with the charge, that the person to whom I give it shall do something which concerns the interest of a third person. For instance, though I cannot stipulate in my own name directly that you shall make a present to James of Meerman's Thesaurus, I may effectually give you a sum of money or other thing subject to the charge of making such a present." [Pothier on Obligations Section 71.]

statement: A gift of land made to a prospective bride in contemplation of marriage must be returned if the marriage fails, even through the fault of the donor.
supporting_quote: But it would seem clear that where a man makes a gift of land to his prospective bride in contemplation of marriage, the intention of the parties would be that the gift shall be returned if the marriage fails to take place even through the fault of the donor.

statement: A donor may be regarded as having personally made a disposition of property by way of gift whenever the property effectually passes to the donee by an indirect process which was controlled at every stage by the donor himself.
supporting_quote: "In this context they are not eiusdem generis with the forms of 'disposition' previously enumerated ; they indicate that a donor may also be regarded as having personally made a disposition of property by way of gift whenever the property effectually passes to the 'donee' by an indirect process which was controlled at every stage by the 'donor' himself."

statement: A party who executes a conveyance which is unambiguously a deed of sale cannot lead parol evidence to show that it is a deed of mortgage, and this rule applies even if there is an agreement in the deed itself or a separate agreement for retransfer within a specified period.
supporting_quote: "The respondent did not rely on any proviso to section 92 of the Evidence Ordinance. Nor did he allege a trust of the kind which section 5 (3) of the 'Trusts Ordinance permits to be established by oral evidence. In the result, the learned trial Judge should not have admitted evidence for the purpose of contradicting, varying, adding to or subtracting from the terms of two notarial instruments each of which unambiguously purported to record a transaction between a vendor and his purchaser (not between a mortgagor and his mortgagee)."

statement: When a landlord makes it clear to his tenant that he will not accept further payments of rent, there is no obligation on the tenant to tender the rents as and when they fall due. However, the tenant remains liable to pay the rent when demanded and must bring the arrears into Court when an action in ejectment is instituted by the landlord.
supporting_quote: "It seems to have been thought, to judge by the letter 1D3, that when the plaintiff purchased these premises he became entitled to treat the 1st defendant as though he were a trespasser and no longer a tenant, but this was a wrong view to take and the plaintiff seems to have realized that when he filed his amended plaint. The letter 1D3 contains what is, to my mind, a repudiation of the 1st defendant's character as a tenant under the plaintiff and this, when coupled with the return of the rent, amounted to an unequivocal intimation by the plaintiff that any payment or tender for subsequent months would also be refused."

statement: A landlord who sells rented premises retains the right to sue the tenant for ejectment in order to give vacant possession to the vendee.
supporting_quote: When a landlord sells the rented premises it is open to him to sue the tenant thereafter in ejectment, in order to give vacant possession to the vendee.

statement: A donee of rented premises, who has been granted a life interest by the donor, is entitled to claim rent from the tenant upon the donor's death.
supporting_quote: Where a landlord donates the rented premises reserving a life-interest in his favour, the donee is entitled to claim the rent from the tenant on the death of the donor; it is not open to the tenant to continue to remain in possession and refuse to pay rent to the new owner on the pretext that he never attorned to the new owner.

statement: Section 335 of the Criminal Procedure Code does not apply in the case of an appeal under section 798 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: I do not think that the argument is sound. In the first place, section 798 confers a right of appeal 'from every order, sentence or conviction' for contempt; and it is at least doubtful whether this apparently absolute right of appeal is limited by any qualifying provision in the Criminal Procedure Code.

statement: A deed of donation by a Muslim grandmother to her grandchildren is revocable unless the deed explicitly states it as irrevocable.
supporting_quote: "The proviso to section 3 of the Muslim Intestate Succession and Wakfs Ordinance (Cap. 50) was enacted for the special purpose of relieving Judges in Ceylon of the responsibility of solving these knotty problems. The proviso expressly states : ' . . . no deed of donation shall be deemed to be irrevocable unless it is so stated in the deed . . .' "
statute_citation_verbatim: section 3 of the Muslim Intestate Succession and Wakfs Ordinance (Cap. 50)

statement: A tenant's liability to pay rent is not discharged merely because the landlord has accepted cheques in part payment and subsequently returned them, nor does such action render the tenant in default for a period of one month if they fail to pay within a reasonable time thereafter.
supporting_quote: "Moreover, the rent can be in arrear only from the day on which it became due, which is fixed by the terms of the contract of tenancy and cannot be varied by the unilateral act of the landlord in returning a cheque that he has taken as conditional payment. "

statement: It is not competent to the Court to leave a third share unallotted pending decisions in connected cases.
supporting_quote: "I am unable to hold that the legislature contemplated that in the circumstances such as those proved in the present case, the court shall have left a third share unallotted pending decisions in the connected cases."

statement: When an action for partition of a land is dismissed on the ground that the plaintiff has no title to the land, the Court has no jurisdiction to proceed to allot shares among the defendants if the defendants do not agree to ask for partition.
supporting_quote: When an action for partition of a land is dismissed on the ground that the plaintiff has no title to the land, the Court has no jurisdiction to proceed to allot shares among the defendants if the defendants do not agree to ask for partition.

statement: A person can claim a way of necessity for the purpose of going from one land owned by him to another, but such a right will not be granted if there is an alternative route, even if it may be less convenient and involve a longer journey.
supporting_quote: "The right of way will not be granted, if there is an alternative route to the one claimed although such route may be less convenient and involve a longer and more arduous journey."

statement: A purchaser's failure to appeal after being evicted does not absolve the vendor from liability for damages if the vendor was given sufficient notice and did not induce the vendee to appeal.
supporting_quote: "Having had ample notice of the proceedings in which the respondent was evicted and after being afforded every opportunity of intervening in those proceedings the appellant is not entitled to escape her liability on the ground that the respondent did not appeal, without even endeavouring to show that he had a reasonable chance of success in an appeal and that she did all she reasonably could to bring that fact to his notice and induce him to appeal."

statement: When money is deposited in Court as security for costs of appeal, failure to hypothecate the money is a fatal irregularity.
supporting_quote: When money is deposited in Court as security for costs of appeal in terms of section 757 of the Civil Procedure Code, failure to hypothecate the money is a fatal irregularity.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, s. 757

statement: The surviving spouse may validly sell immovable property of a deceased person in order to pay his debts.
supporting_quote: Now there is an unbroken line of decisions to the effect that the surviving spouse may validly sell the movable and immovable property of a deceased person in order to pay his debts.

statement: A vendor is not liable to refund the purchase price or pay damages in a case where they only professed to sell an incertum juris acting in good faith, doubting their own right but without certain knowledge that the thing was another's. This applies even if there is an express warranty.
supporting_quote: "The second defendant impressed me as an unsophisticated villager while the plaintiff obviously does not belong to the class of cultivators, though he calls himself a cultivator."

statement: A minor's future contingent interest cannot be validly sold by a curator without the Court’s sanction, and such sale is ipso jure void if not sanctioned.
supporting_quote: "The reason is that such a sale is ipso jure void, and dominium has not passed from the minor. Sande 1 : 1 : 79."

statement: A mortgagee cannot bring a second hypothecary action for the same matter where a previous action has been dismissed, and such actions are barred by sections 406(2) and 408 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, whether one regards the dismissal of the previous action brought by the appellant as a withdrawal of it under section 408 or an adjustment under section 408, the effect of the decree passed in that action is to preclude the appellant from bringing the same action again, notwithstanding the provisions of section 7 (1) of the Mortgage Act."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 406(2) and 408 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A sale by a judgment debtor or his heirs is void if it occurs after the seizure and registration of the notice of seizure, but not registered. If the seizure is not registered, the necessary implication is that a bona fide private alienee is statim securus.
supporting_quote: "If the seizure is not registered, the necessary implication of section 238 is that a bona fide private alienee is statim securus. I think that section 289, as regards relation back, must be read in the light of section 238"

statement: The court should set aside the interlocutory decree and direct the district court to add the petitioner as a party and proceed with the action.
supporting_quote: "I would set aside the interlocutory decree and direct the district court to add the petitioner as a party and proceed with the action."

statement: An action for partition is not necessarily an action to which section 547 applies, and the true position would seem to be that such an action is not necessarily an action for the 'recovery of property'.
supporting_quote: "So that when objections under that section is taken, the question to be decided is whether the real or substantial purpose of the action is to determine questions of title. If such be the case, the proper course, as approved by this Court in Hassen Hadjiar v. Marikcar 1 and Gooneratne v. Hamine 3 , is to afford to the plaintiffs an opportunity of obtaining administration."

statement: The Court has discretion to award permanent alimony without being bound by the amount awarded as alimony pendente lite, and is not limited to one-fifth of the husband's average net income for three years preceding the order.
supporting_quote: "In the instant case the plaintiff was awarded alimony pendente lite in a sum of Rs. 750 per mensem if she was permitted to reside in the house belonging to the defendant No. 10 Frances Road, Wellawatte, and Rs. 1,000 per mensem if she was not permitted to do so. The learned District Judge who made the order granting a separation has considered all the matters which were before the Judge who ordered alimony pendente lite as well as the facts and circumstances disclosed by the evidence led at the trial. The section in no way fetters the discretion of the Judge in deciding the amount of permanent alimony, nor is he bound by the amount awarded as alimony pendente lite."
statute_citation_verbatim: "615. (1) The Court may, if it thinks fit, on any decree absolute declaring a marriage to be dissolved, or on any decree of separation obtained by the wife, order that the husband shall, to the satisfaction of the court, secure to the wife such gross sum of money, or such annual sum of money for any term not exceeding her own life, as, having regard to her fortune (if any), to the ability of the husband, and to the conduct of the parties, it thinks reasonable ; and for that purpose may cause a proper instrument to be executed by all necessary parties. (2) In every such case the court may make an order on the husband for payment to the wife of such monthly or weekly sums for her maintenance and support as the court may think reasonable : Provided that if the husband afterwards from any cause becomes unable to make such payments, it shall be lawful for the court to 513 discharge or modify the order, or temporarily to suspend the same as to the whole or any part of the money so ordered to be paid, and again to revive the same order wholly or in part, as to the court seems fit"

statement: The court should have performed its duties under Section 25 of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951 to examine the title of each party and hear evidence in support thereof.
supporting_quote: "In this case the trial judge has failed to perform these duties and it is not too late for us to require him to perform them at another trial."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 25 of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951

statement: In disputes between co-owners, the general rule is that all co-owners should be parties to an action unless certain clear circumstances apply.
supporting_quote: "The general rule as to joinder is subject to exceptions which are made in certain clear circumstances."

statement: A co-owner is not entitled to maintain an action for a declaration of title to a building standing on the common property.
supporting_quote: "The right of the builder is limited to a claim for compensation, which he could enforce in a partition action under sections 2 and 5 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1853."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 2 and 5 of Ordinance No. 10 of 1853

statement: An interlocutory decree for partition, unless proceeded with, is useless for all purposes. It would not even support a plea of res judicata.
supporting_quote: "interlocutory decree for partition, unless proceeded with, is useless for all purposes. It would not even support a plea of res judicata"

statement: Where one co-owner uses a common property exclusively and makes profits by such use, he must account to the others for their share of the profits.
supporting_quote: "In the circumstances the defendants can be regarded as being in default only in so far as they have failed to pay the plaintiffs their share of the profits for working the mill"

statement: A stranger who purchases the entire property knowing that his vendor is only a co-owner cannot acquire a prescriptive title through possession alone, as ten years of adverse possession will not suffice without an ouster or something equivalent.
supporting_quote: "Such a purchaser cannot be said to have entered into possession as sole owner, for he had knowledge that there were others who owned shares in the land, and he will be presumed to have possessed the land as a co-owner. The ordinary rule which applies to possession by co-owners will then apply, viz., that before one can prescribe against the others there must be an ouster or something equivalent to an ouster."

statement: In construing the terms of a deed, the question is not what the parties may have intended, but what is the meaning of the words which they used.
supporting_quote: In construing the terms of a deed, the question is not what the parties may have intended, but what is the meaning of the words which they used.

statement: A conveyance coupled with a clause for reconveyance on payment of a certain sum of money within a stipulated period cannot be proved by oral evidence to have been in reality a mortgage.
supporting_quote: "where a person transferred a land to another by a notarial deed, purporting on the face of it to sell the land, it is not open to the transferor to prove by oral evidence that the transaction was in reality a mortgage and that the transferee agreed to reconvey the property on payment of the money advanced"

statement: Where a vendor undertakes to execute a conveyance of property before the expiration of a specified period and there is no corresponding obligation to call for a conveyance imposed on the vendee, the vendee's cause of action accrues immediately upon the vendor's failure to execute the conveyance within the specified period.
supporting_quote: Where a vendor undertakes to execute a conveyance of property before the expiration of a specified period and there is no corresponding obligation to call for a conveyance imposed on the vendee, the vendee's cause of action accrues immediately upon the vendor's failure to execute the conveyance within the specified period.

statement: The Court should remit the case to the lower court for further evidence regarding the due execution of certain deeds, particularly Deed No. 11385.
supporting_quote: In all the circumstances it is, in my opinion, desirable that the pro�ceedings should be remitted to the Court below to enable the plaintiff to produce the duplicate of Deed No. 11385 which is in the custody of the Registrar of Lands.

statement: A Notary who attests a deed is an attesting witness within the meaning of sections 68 and 69 of the Evidence Ordinance.
supporting_quote: A Notary who attests a deed is an attesting witness within the meaning of that expression in sections 68 and 69 of the Evidence Ordinance.
statute_citation_verbatim: Evidence Ordinance, ss. 68, 69

statement: A gift may be perfected by acceptance after the donor's death if the execution or fulfilment of the donation has been postponed till after the donor has died.
supporting_quote: "For the will of the donor and the donee were not at one before the donor's death, and after the death of the donor they could not be muted to the prejudice of the heir, who had acquired a real right to the property concerning which the donation had not been affected. "

statement: A minor donee cannot accept a gift on his own behalf, and acceptance by an uncle or other family member is not valid unless possession of the property by the donees was subsequently proved.
supporting_quote: "I am therefore of opinion that 'there was no valid acceptance on behalf of the minor donee in the present case."

statement: A notary can be regarded as an attesting witness within the meaning of section 68 of the Evidence Ordinance provided he knew the executant personally and can testify to the fact that the signature on the deed is the signature of the executant.
supporting_quote: Where a deed executed before a notary is sought to be proved, the notary can be regarded as an attesting witness within the meaning of section 68 of the Evidence Ordinance provided only that he knew the executant personally and can testify to the fact that the signature on the deed is the signature of the executant.
statute_citation_verbatim: Evidence Ordinance, s. 68

statement: A partition decree entered without any investigation of title does not have the conclusive effect provided by section 9 of the Partition Ordinance, but a decree entered after a defective or inadequate investigation of title is still conclusive as long as it has not been set aside on an appeal in the same action.
supporting_quote: Although a partition decree entered without any investigation of title does not have the conclusive effect provided by section 9 of the Partition Ordinance, a decree entered after a defective or inadequate investigation of title is conclusive, as long as it has not been set aside on an appeal in the same action.

statement: A mortgagee's act of bidding at a sale of mortgaged land does not necessarily constitute an unequivocal representation that there is no existing mortgage, and failure to disclose the mortgage does not prevent the mortgagee from asserting their interest.
supporting_quote: "If, as I think, the act of bidding does not work an estoppel, still less can the failure of the plaintiff to disclose his mortgage prevent him from now asserting his interest."

statement: In Kandyan Law, the fact of adoption for purposes of inheritance does not require a formal declaration or ceremony; instead, it requires reliable, clear and unmistakable evidence of the deceased's intention to adopt the child as heir.
supporting_quote: "All that is required is a clear and open manifestation of the fact of adoption of a child as heir whether the fact is made to appear by either word or conduct or both."

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift is revocable unless the circumstances, which constitute non-revocability, appear most clearly on the face of the deed itself.
supporting_quote: "The Supreme Court thinks it clear that the general rule is that such deeds are revocable, and also that before a particular deed is held to be exceptional to this rule, it should be shown that the circumstances, which constitute non-revocability appear most clearly on the face of the deed itself."

statement: A subsequent instrument, even though registered at a time before the grantor acquired his title, would prevail over an unregistered deed if the competing instrument remained unregistered at the time of the acquisition of title.
supporting_quote: "Thus, when a deed of transfer of immovable property is executed at a time when the grantor has no title to the property, the subsequent acquisition of title by the grantor would not only give the benefit of such title to the instrument already executed but would also give the grantee the benefit of priority by the registration of that instrument; if the competing instrument remained unregistered at the time of the acquisition of title, the subsequent instrument, even though it was registered at a time before the grantor acquired his title, would prevail over the unregistered deed."

statement: A cause of action to recover excess rent accrued immediately upon the payment of the money, and such recovery is barred by prescription after a period of three years from the date of payment.
supporting_quote: As this action was filed only on 5th May 1954, more than eight and a half years after the payment, it is clearly barred by the provisions of the Prescription Ordinance.

statement: A sum of money accepted as rent can be set off against the rent due, even if no physical passing of money occurred at the time of agreement.
