On the other hand, applying some of the tests indicated in the following observations of Lord Lindley in Ores/tam Life Assurance Society, Ltd. v. Bishop [L. R. (1902) A. C. 296.] to determine-whether there has been a receipt of a particular sum of money, I find no difficulty in agreeing with Mr. Ranganathan that a sum of Rs. 375 was

statement: A purchaser of premises is entitled to maintain an action under section 9 (2) of the Rent Restriction Act for the ejectment of a tenant and sub-tenant where the tenant had previously sub-let in contravention of section 9 (1).
supporting_quote: Where any premises or any part thereof is sub-let in contravention of the provisions of Sub-section (1), the landlord shall, notwithstanding the provisions of Section 13, be entitled in an action instituted in a Court of competent jurisdiction to a decree for the ejectment from the premises of his tenant and of the person or each of the persons to whom the premises or any part thereof has been so sub-let.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 9 (2) of the Rent Restriction Act No. 29 of 1948

statement: Documents admitted without objection at trial cannot be challenged on appeal regarding their admissibility, unless they are forbidden by law.
supporting_quote: "The question raised as to admissibility cannot therefore now be entertained."

statement: The court found that the last will of 1942 was destroyed by the testator with the intention to revoke it.
supporting_quote: "The order under appeal is set aside and the case is remitted with the finding of this court that the last will No. 6544 of 2nd January, 1942, was destroyed by the testator with the intention of revoking it."

statement: In cases where a will is prepared by or on the instructions of a party who takes a benefit under it, this court holds that such circumstances should generally excite suspicion and call for vigilant examination of evidence supporting the will.
supporting_quote: "The second rule extends to all cases in which circumstances exist which excite the suspicion of the Court."

statement: An entire land should be brought into a partition action when it is possessed in different portions by co-owners for convenience of possession, and the plaintiff cannot maintain an action in respect of one portion only.
supporting_quote: "Where a land is possessed in different portions by different co-owners for convenience of possession, a partition action cannot be maintained in respects of one portion only ; the entire land should be brought into the action."

statement: No person ought to be enriched at the expense of another (nemo cum damno alterius locupletior fieri debet) does not apply in this case as any unjust enrichment accruing to the defendant was at the expense of Ediriweera's creditors and not of the plaintiffs.
supporting_quote: Inasmuch as the execution of the conveyance by A actually resulted in his creditors being defrauded and any unjust enrichment accruing to B was at the expense of the defrauded creditors and not of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs could not avail themselves of the maxim that no person ought to be enriched at the expense of another (nemo cum damno alterius locupletior fieri debet).

statement: An obstruction of a private right of way is not actionable unless it is substantial.
supporting_quote: "No action will lie unless there is a substantial interference with the easement granted . . . The question whether any particular interruption amounts to an unlawful interference depends upon the nature of the right of way and of the locus in quo, and upon the general circumstances of the case."

statement: A lessee of one portion cannot claim from the other lessee a right of way by prescription over the other portion, nor is he entitled to claim a way of necessity.
supporting_quote: Therefore, where a land is divided by its owner into two portions and each portion is given on lease to a different person the lessee of one portion cannot claim from the other lessee a right of way by prescription over the other portion. Nor is he entitled to claim a way of necessity.

statement: The plaintiff did not inherit any share of the property from Vaithinather as she was a child of his fourth marriage, and only children of his first marriage would have been entitled to inherit it.
supporting_quote: "It appeared to us that this submission was accepted by learned counsel for the plaintiff as a correct statement of the law, but after the record was received back he intimated to us that if the finding on the fresh evidence that the property had been acquired by Vaithinather were affirmed he would contend that, on. the death of Vaithinather's. first wife, one half of the property devolved on the children, of the first marriage and that upon the death of Vaithinather the remaining half devolved equally on all his children."

statement: A transaction that is purported to be an exchange but is actually two separate sales should not be considered as an exchange for the purpose of pre-emption rights under Ordinance No. 59 of 1947.
supporting_quote: "We are satisfied that the facts established in the present case show that the transaction in question in fact constitutes two sales and not an exchange and that therefore plaintiff is entitled to pre-empt."

statement: A claimant of a servitude must establish the claim by clear and satisfactory evidence of the strongest kind, including clear and unmistakable evidence of the commencement of an adverse user for the prescribed period.
supporting_quote: Clear and unmistakable evidence of the commencement of an adverse user thereafter for the prescriptive period is necessary to entitle the licensee to claim a servitude in respect of the premises.

statement: A right of way over a neighbor's land can be granted if the alternative route is so difficult and inconvenient as to be practically impossible, especially in an urban area.
supporting_quote: "In my opinion, reasonable compensation or the just price the plaintiff must pay would be the market value of the strip of land. According to plan P. 1, lot has been surveyed as an area covering 2 .86 perches. The learned District Judge has stated in the course of his judgment that in the event of this Court disagreeing with his view that the route over the sea-shore constitutes reasonable access to the plaintiff's land, compensation shot calculated at Rs. 15,000 an acre which, according to the 1st defendant himself, is the price of land in this locality. On this basis, the value of lot 'Y' works out to Rs. 268, and I would order that a sum of RS.300 be paid to the defendants by the plaintiff as compensation for the which I decree to her of a right of footway from her land over in plan P. 1 to Gunananda Place."

statement: In the case of husband and wife governed by Tesawalamai, notice to warrant and defend title given to the husband is not necessarily a notice to the wife.
supporting_quote: The question that arises in the present case is whether the notice that has been held to have been given to the 1st defendant can be construed as a notice to the 2nd defendant as well. The 1st plaintiff in his evidence did not say that a separate notice was given to the 2nd defendant. The position taken up by him at the trial seems to have been that since the defendants are governed by the law of Tesawalawai the 1st defendant as the husband is the manager of the 2nd defendant's property and therefore notice to the 1st .defendant alone was sufficient.

statement: Persons claiming the right of pre-emption under section 2(1)(b) must first satisfy that they would be heirs of the intending vendor if he should then die intestate, and also satisfy that they are descendants, ascendants or collaterals within the third degree of succession.
supporting_quote: "Only in this way can full effect be given to all the words of section 2 (1) (b) and section 2 (2)."

statement: The indorsement on the note and the fact that the notes were attached to the bond and retained by the mortgagee and payee are conclusive to negative discharge by merger or novation.
supporting_quote: "In so far as this evidence relates to the meaning of the bond it was clearly inadmissible (vide section 91 of the Evidence Ordinance). The language of the bond together with that of the notes attached thereto speaks for itself and even if admitted without objection the Court could not properly act on such evidence. In so far as the questions and answers in re-examination are relied upon as supporting a separate and independent agreement upon a matter on which the bond was silent (see proviso (2) to section 92 of the Evidence Ordinance) they are not evidence against Misso of an oral agreement between Mohamedally and Pieris neither of whom went into the witness box. Furthermore if such an agreement was in fact made it is clear that it was not carried out as the notes were not ' cancelled ' in the manner provided in section 63 (1) of the Bills of Exchange Ordinance with regard to intentional cancellation."

statement: The correct method of counting the four generations for a fideicommissum is from the first fidei commissary heir to legatee, and only the fifth fideicommissary heir can exercise free discretion in regard to the property.
supporting_quote: "As to the method of counting the generations, in Holland and Friesland the general opinion of the Commentators has been accepted .... that it is not the first instituted or fiduciary heir who constitutes the first degree, and consequently only the fifth fideicommissary heir is able to exercise his free discretion in regard to the fideicommissary property"

statement: A plea of prescription should be carefully scrutinized and upheld only upon the clearest evidence of denial of the right of the de jure incumbent to exercise his office.
supporting_quote: "It is imperative that a plea of prescription should be carefully scrutinized and that such a plea should be upheld only upon the clearest evidence of the denial of the right of the de jure incumbent to exercise, his office."

statement: A statement made by a deceased person can be admitted as an admission against the representative in interest of the deceased, without needing to fulfill all conditions set out in section 32 of the Evidence Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "I am satisfied from reference to the English cases that the English Law rendered an 'admission' by a deceased person receivable without regard to the question whether it fulfilled the requirements which are mentioned in our section 32; and that accordingly it would be wrong to suppose that there was any intention to restrict the scope of section 18 only to statements of persons who are alive."

statement: In cases governed by the Amended Kandyan Marriage Ordinance of 1870, the production of a diga marriage certificate is sufficient to prove that the wife forfeited her paternal inheritance.
supporting_quote: "In cases governed by the Amended Kandyan Marriage Ordinance of 1870 the production of a diga marriage certificate is of itself sufficient to prove not only that the wife was married in diga but also that she forfeited her paternal inheritance"

statement: The Court is precluded from inquiring into any objections not notified to the Court within 30 days of the receipt of the Fiscal's report relating to the sale.
supporting_quote: It was necessary, therefore, as required by section 282 (2) of the Civil Procedure Code, that the grounds of objection to the sale should be notified to Court within thirty days of the receipt of the Fiscal's report relating to the sale, and the Court was precluded from inquiring into any objection not so notified.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 282(2) of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A judgment that fails to examine the title of each party in a partition action vitiates the decree if it has prejudiced the substantial rights of the parties.
supporting_quote: "Failure to examine the title of each party in a partition action vitiates the decree if it has prejudiced the substantial rights of the parties."

statement: An alienation in fraud of creditors is not ipso jure void and is valid unless it is set aside within the prescriptive period.
supporting_quote: "an alienation in fraud of creditors is not ipso jure void and is valid unless it is set aside within the prescriptive period"
statute_citation_verbatim: [1 Section 10, Prescription Ordinance. Ahamado Lebbe et al. v. Adam Bawa et al., 3 A. C. R. 1]

statement: The court should not admit a will to probate when the propounders fail to remove suspicions created by alterations in the will, especially if those alterations are significant and could indicate lack of due execution.
supporting_quote: "It was their duty if they expected to succeed in their application to remove the suspicion in regard to due execution created by the alterations in the will they sought to propound. They made no attempt whatever to do so."

statement: An interlocutory decree entered without the proper appointment of a manager for a lunatic defendant's estate, in contravention of the Civil Procedure Code, can be set aside and the defendant given an opportunity to file a statement of claim.
supporting_quote: "As the 1st defendant who was a lunatic at all material times was not represented in the case he would not, in my opinion, be bound by an interlocutory decree entered in the circumstances related above-vide section 480 read with section 501 of the Civil Procedure Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 480 read with section 501 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: A co-owner cannot bring an action for a declaration of title to a share of a building without the proper legal foundation, such as a notarial agreement or prescription.
supporting_quote: "It is clear beyond doubt that our law does not recognize the ownership of a building apart from the land on which it stands. In Samaranayake v. Mendoris 1[1 (1928) 30 N. L. R. 203.] Drieberg so held, and, if I may adopt some words in his judgment, if at the to this theatre building was erected the plaintiff had no interest in the land he cannot possibly be owner of the building in any sense, for it because the property of the soil-owner."

statement: A co-owner is not entitled to build or make other improvements on the common property after the institution of a partition action, unless such actions are necessary repairs.
supporting_quote: Of course a co-owner would be acting within his rights if he effects necessary repairs to a building even after the institution of partition proceedings. If a co-owner is permitted to build or plant the common property even after the institution of the partition action it might result in other co-owners having to pay compensation for improvements which they do not wish to have.

statement: A lessee's rights against a true owner claiming adversely to the lessor cannot be enforced under the general law in the absence of express covenants to the contrary.
supporting_quote: Having considered many of the subsequent cases I would hold that none of them have in any way qualified the principle laid down in Soysa v, Mohideen[5 (1914) 17 N. L. R. 279.] that the rights, if any, arising from a contract between a lessor and lessee cannot be enforced by the lessee as against fideicommissary owners who were not parties to the contract.

statement: Where an act is to be done within a specified time from a certain date, the day of that date has to be excluded for the purpose of computation of time.
supporting_quote: Held, that where an act is to be done within a specified time from a certain date, the day of that date has to be be excluded for the purpose of computation of time.

statement: Failure to hypothecate the sum of money in terms of section 757 within the extended time is a fatal irregularity.
supporting_quote: Where extension of time is allowed by Court beyond the period specified in section 756 (1) of the Civil Procedure Code for tendering security for costs of appeal, and cash in the amount ordered is accordingly deposited, failure to hypothecate the sum of money in terms of section 757 within the extended time is a fatal irregularity.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 750 (1), 756 (1), 757

statement: If time is not of the essence of a contract and one party fails to perform within a specified period, the other party can give notice that if the obligation is not complied with by a certain date, allowing a reasonable time, they will regard the contract as at an end.
supporting_quote: "where a time for the performance of a vital term in a contract has been stipulated for and one party is in mora by reason of his failure to perform it within that time, but time is not of the essence of the contract, the other party can make it so by giving notice that if the obligation is not complied with by a certain date, allowing a reasonable time, he will regard the contract as at an end."

statement: In the absence of acknowledgment by Andiris Rajapakse or his successors, the Crown Grant did not confer any rights on the grantees and shares in the land should be allotted based on Don Andiris being the sole owner.
supporting_quote: "The nature of that possession could not be altered by the bare execution of the grant unaccompanied by the acknowledgment by Andiris Rajapakse or any of his successors of any right of co-ownership in the representatives in interest of Don Tiyadoris.'"

statement: A party can always prove the prescription of his predecessors-in-title and only a party cannot prove the prescription of a part who is not a party to the action.
supporting_quote: "A party can always prove the prescription of his predecessors-in-title and only a party cannot prove the prescription of a part who is not a party to the action."

statement: In cases of concealed fraud, the equitable principle can be applied even if there is no independent act of concealment when the tort itself is done furtively.
supporting_quote: "Two men acting independently, steal a neighbour's coal. One is so clumsy in his operations, or so incautious, that he has to do something more in order to conceal his fraud. The other chooses his opportunity so warily, that he can safely calculate on not being found out for many a long day. Why is the one to go scot free at the end of a limited period rather than the other (loc. cit. p. 364)."

statement: A fidei commissum which comes to an end with the first generation of fideicommissaries, i.e., with the fiduciary's children who are free to dispose of the property as they wish, is also a fideicommissum in favour of a family.
supporting_quote: "A fideicommissum which comes to an end with the first generation of fideicommissaries, i.e., with the fiduciary's children who are free to dispose of the property as they wish, is also a fideicommissum in favour of a family."

statement: A donor may revoke a gift for ingratitude, provided the donee's conduct is sufficiently serious to be considered ungrateful.
supporting_quote: "It would be unwise to lay down a hard and fast rule as to what conduct on the part of a donee may be regarded as ingratitude for which a donor may ask for revocation of his gift. Voet's view is that ingratitude for which a donation may be revoked must be ingratitude which a court does not regard as trifling."

statement: A single surviving coparcener's interest in a Hindu undivided family property is still considered joint family property, despite the individual ownership rights of the surviving coparcener.
supporting_quote: To my mind it would make a mockery of the undivided family system if this temporary reduction of the coparcenary unit to a single individual were to convert what was previously joint property belonging to an undivided family into the separate property of the surviving coparcener [1 (1953) 55 N. L. R. 496, 501.]

statement: The court held that even if the signatures were compared correctly, the plaintiff still failed to prove due execution of the deed because section 69 of the Evidence Ordinance requires proof that the signature of the person executing the document is in their handwriting.
supporting_quote: "Such rights as the plaintiff has in the land in suit must, therefore, be restricted to those acquired by her otherwise than through deed No.154."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 69 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: The interests which devolved on the paternal uncle Samadu (2nd defendant) were not subject to any restrictions as regards alienation, and he was free to deal with them as he pleased.
supporting_quote: "Therefore that 1/6 share out of Mahakumath Umma's 1/3 share out of Hashim's 1/2 share of Asana Marikkar's interests in the three lands in question devolved, on Mahakumath Umma's death, on her uncle Samadu (2nd defendant). The interests which thus devolved on the 2nd defendant were not subject to any restrictions as regards alienation, and be was free to deal with them as he pleased."

statement: A contract of sale of land between Muslims is governed by the general law—the Roman-Dutch Law and the legislation applicable to such a transaction. Donations involving fidei commissa are excluded from the scope of Muslim Law, making them subject to Roman-Dutch Law.
supporting_quote: "The sale by Mohideen, his wife and two sons to the 2nd defendant, is therefore not a transaction to which the Muslim Law applies, but one which is governed by the Roman-Dutch Law."

statement: A will can create a valid fideicommissum even if the fiduciary does not have personal benefit from the property.
supporting_quote: "The possibility of a fiduciary burdened with administrative duties, without having any rights of enjoyment for himself, seems to have sprung from obiter dicta of de Villiers C. J., (afterwards Lord Villiers) in Strydom v. Strydom's Trustee (1894) 11 S. C. 425, which were based upon a mistranslation of D. 36. 2.26.1 ( recording what is called Papinian's case)."

statement: A will can be used to prove a fideicommissum even if the probate has not been registered, provided that certain conditions are met.
supporting_quote: "For the reasons stated above I am of opinion that section 2 of the Registration of Old Deeds and Instruments Ordinance 1947 does not prevent a will from being used to prove a trust or fideicommissum in a case where the probate has not itself been registered as provided in that section."
statute_citation_verbatim: Registration of Documents Ordinance (Cap. 101), ss. 7, 8 (a) (6), 10 (2), 26

statement: A District Court is not the proper forum to adjudicate on the validity of a determination made by the Land Commissioner that a particular land which is sought to be acquired by him is of the description contained in section 3 (1) of the Land Redemption Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Having regard to the limited and special jurisdiction of a District Court in land acquisition proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act, a District Court is not the proper forum to adjudicate on the validity of a determination made by the Land Commissioner that a particular land which is sought to be acquired by him is of the description contained in section 3 (1) of the Land Redemption Ordinance."

statement: A grantee of land under the Land Development Ordinance transfers the land to a person without obtaining the prior written consent of the Government Agent as required by section 42, the transfer is null and void and does not have the effect of passing any right or title to the transferee.
supporting_quote: Where a grantee of land under the Land Development Ordinance transfers the land to a person without obtaining the prior written consent of the Government Agent as required by section 42, the transfer is null and void and does not have the effect of passing any right or title to the transferee.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 42 of the Land Development Ordinance

statement: On the death of a monthly tenant, the tenancy does not automatically pass to his executor or executrix.
supporting_quote: "I am unable to find in any of these statements support for the view that on the death of a monthly tenant the tenancy passes automatically to his executor or executrix."

statement: Mere willingness to pay the rent does not discharge the obligation to pay the rent. To constitute tender, the readiness to pay must be accompanied by production of the money that is offered in satisfaction of the debt.
supporting_quote: "Mere willingness to pay the rent does not discharge the obligation to pay the rent. At no time did the defendant on his own showing pay the rent."

statement: The Court can order the sale of a portion of land and allot another portion to the parties in a partition action.
supporting_quote: In our opinion paragraphs (c) and (e) of section 26 of the new Partition Act read together authorise the Court to allot one portion of a land to a party or a set of parties and to order the sale of another portion and the division of the proceeds of the sale among other parties alone or among them and some or all of the parties to whom the former portion is allotted.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 26 (2) (c) (e) of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951

statement: In a partition action, the court must examine each party's title and determine which of the orders mentioned in section 26 should be made.
supporting_quote: "On the date fixed for the trial of a partition action or on any other date to which the trial may be adjourned, the court shall examine the title of each party and shall hear and receive evidence in support thereof and shall try and determine all questions of law and fact arising in that action in regard to the right, share, or interest of each party to, of, or in the land to which that action relates, and shall consider and decide which of the orders mentioned in section 26 should be made."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 25 of the Partition Act No. 16 of 1951

statement: An omission to give a party an opportunity of being heard is not merely an omission of procedure but is a far more fundamental matter in that it is contrary to the rule of natural justice embodied in the maxim audi alteram partem.
supporting_quote: "As stated in Shaw v. The Attorney General [ 1 (1870) 2 P.& D.156. ] a judgment obtained in such circumstances has the 'incurable vice of being contrary to natural justice because the proceedings are ex parte and take place in the absence of the party affected by them '."

statement: The Court has discretion to alter the date fixed for deposit of preliminary survey fees prior to its expiration in an appropriate case, even under section 10(1) of the Partition Act.
supporting_quote: Where, in a partition action, a date is fixed for preliminary survey fees to be deposited by the plaintiff, section 10 (1) of the Partition Act does not preclude the Court, in an appropriate case, from subsequently allowing a longer period for the deposit, provided that the alteration of the date is made prior to the expiration of the time originally fixed.
statute_citation_verbatim: Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951, ss. 8, 10 (1)

statement: A plaintiff can seek a possessory remedy to quiet possession against acts of disturbance, even if they were not physically dispossessed but had to assert their rights in court.
supporting_quote: "If the opinion which I have just expressed is erroneous I would hold that the equivalent of the possessory remedy 'uti possidetis' is available to the plaintiff to be quieted in possession against acts of disturbance."

statement: When a right of way becomes attached to a land by prescriptive user and that land is transferred, the servitude itself passes even though it is not specially mentioned in the deed of transfer.
supporting_quote: "It follows that when the praedium of which the servitude forms a part is transferred, the-servitude itself passes even though it is not specially mentioned in the deed of transfer."

statement: A quorum of 7 members was sufficient to constitute a valid meeting for the appointment of a principal in this pirivena, as per the agreement between the Sabha.
supporting_quote: "I am therefore of opinion that a quorum of 7 was sufficient to constitute a valid meeting."

statement: The Fiscal's authority to execute a decree by seizure and sale of the judgment-debtor's immovable property does not automatically cease upon payment in full of the decree, but requires an order from the Court.
supporting_quote: "It would appear from the provisions of the Code which regulate the Fiscal's powers and duties that it was never intended that he should be called upon to decide matters within the ambit of the Court's powers."

statement: The lands in question have vested absolutely in the Crown and are not owned by the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: (a) that the lands in question formed a part of the kapu panguwa, belonging to the Pattini Dewale of Hanguranketa, 205 (b) that the plaintiff was by virtue of deed No. 6032 of 28th October 1946 entitled to possess them, (c) that the Land Commissioner purported to acquire them under the Land Redemption Ordinance, and that the Crown took possession of them on 8th March 1934, (d) that the lands fall within the category of lands liable to be acquired under the Land Redemption Ordinance, (e) that the plaintiff is not the owner of the lands in question, (f) that the lands have vested absolutely in the Crown, (g) that the decision in the D. statement: Execution of a judgment against an appellant should be allowed unless real and substantial justice requires that execution should be stayed, with the burden on the appellant to establish this exception.
supporting_quote: "The principle appears to be that execution will be allowed unless 'real and substantial justice requires that execution should be stayed '. The burden of establishing this exception is upon the appellant"

statement: An action for specific performance of an agreement to sell land is not an action in respect of land within the meaning of section 9 (b) of the Civil Procedure Code, and a Court has no jurisdiction to try such a case merely on the ground that the land in question is situated within the local limits of its jurisdiction.
supporting_quote: "An action for specific performance of an agreement to sell land, is not an action in respect of land within the meaning of section 9 (b) of the Civil Procedure Code. A Court, therefore, has no jurisdiction to try the case merely on the ground that the land in respects of which the contract was made is situated within the local limits of its jurisdiction."

statement: A district court has the power to order that the costs of execution of an order for the payment of costs made in a partition action under the Partition Act should be recovered from the judgment-debtor.
supporting_quote: "In an action instituted under the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951, it is competent for the Court to order that the costs of execution of an order for the payment of costs made in the final decree should be recovered from the judgment-debtor."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 208 and 209 of the Civil Procedure Code relating to the recovery of costs of execution are applicable to proceedings under the Partition Act.

statement: A guardian cannot be compelled to sell a minor's immovable property merely because he has negotiated a sale of it.
supporting_quote: "The fact that the guardian having completed negotiations to sell a minor's immovable property obtains the authority of the Court, gives the Court no authority to compel him to sell any more than it has authority to compel the purchaser to buy."

statement: The prohibition against alienation imposed by the will does not extend to shares that passed to heirs on a child's death.
supporting_quote: "I am of opinion that the prohibition against alienation imposed by PI does not extend to the shares that passed to her heirs on Cecilia death. The appellant is therefore entitled to succeed."

statement: Sections 658 and 659 of the Civil Procedure Code apply to the investigation of claims to property sequestered after judgment under section 3 of the Crown Debtors Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "I hold, therefore, that sections 658 and 659 apply to the present case."
statute_citation_verbatim: sections 658 and 659 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: For a cause of action to arise on a loan of money without any prior agreement as to the date of repayment, it must be after the lender has made demand and the debtor fails to repay within the specified time.
supporting_quote: "The cause of action to sue for the recovery of a loan given without any agreement as to the time of repayment does not arise until the lender has asked the borrower for the return of the money and he fails to repay the money within the time specified in the lender's demand."

statement: The court has no power to add a party under section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code or section 16 of the Mortgage Act, No.6 of 1949.
supporting_quote: "I am therefore of opinion that the Court has no power to add the 2nd respondent as a party under section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 18 of the Civil Procedure Code or section 16 of the Mortgage Act, No.6 of 1949

statement: An appellate court should not disturb the findings of fact without strong evidence to the contrary, especially when the trial judge had the opportunity to observe witnesses.
supporting_quote: "If the evidence as a whole can reasonably be regarded as justifying the conclusion arrived at at the trial, and especially if that conclusion has been arrived at on conflicting testimony by a tribunal which saw and heard the witnesses, the appellate court will bearing mind that it has not enjoyed this opportunity and that the view of the trial judge as to where credibility lies is entitled to great weight."

statement: A notary's statement in a deed regarding the passing of consideration is insufficient to establish valuable consideration without additional evidence, especially when the surrounding circumstances suggest otherwise.
supporting_quote: "Relying on a recent judgment of this Court in Diyes Singho v. Herath[ 1 (1962) 64 N. L. R. 492.] learned counsel contended that the notary's statement in the attestation of those deeds regarding the passing of consideration is by itself insufficient to prove that 3D1 and 3D2 were for valuable consideration."

statement: The right to claim specific performance of an agreement to sell immovable property is excluded by the terms of the contract, particularly by clause 8 which constitutes a substituted obligation and the sole obligation upon the vendors in the event of failure to secure conveyance.
supporting_quote: "It is only in the absence of agreement to the contrary that the Roman-Dutch law confers on a purchaser under an executory contract the right to select one of two alternative legal remedies under the Roman-Dutch law, namely, specific performance or damages. But we have here a categorical stipulation that if the primary obligation is not fulfilled for any reason whatsoever, two specified sums shall immediately become due."

statement: A contract for stifling a prosecution cannot be enforced.
supporting_quote: "All bargains tending to stifle criminal prosecution whether by suppressing investigation of crime, or by deterring citizens from their public duty of assisting in the detection or punishment of crime are void as against public policy."

statement: For a deed to be valid, the notary and witnesses must sign it in the presence of the party executing the document at the same time.
supporting_quote: "The requirement of the section is not satisfied if the notary and the witnesses sign the deed at another place and at some other time. They must sign it then and there in the presence of the maker."

statement: A grandfather can validly accept a donation on behalf of a minor donee, provided the donor has allowed such acceptance.
supporting_quote: "I would therefore hold that the donation to the 2nd plaintiff was a valid one. But there is a further reason why the acceptance in this case should be considered to be good, and it is that the donor had allowed the accep�tance to be made by the grandfather on behalf of his minor child."

statement: Statements made by a person regarding their own marriage can be relevant under section 32(5) of the Evidence Ordinance even if the marriage took place in a foreign country, provided they relate to a long time past and are incapable of direct proof.
supporting_quote: The provision is an exception to the rule against hearsay and has been enacted primarily to meet a situation where the matter sought to be established involves remote facts of family history, which are incapable of direct proof. In the words of Lord Blackburn in Sturla v. Freccia 1 the ground is cc that they were matters relating to a long time past, and that it was really necessary to relax the strict rules of evidence there for the purpose of doing justice
statute_citation_verbatim: section 32 (5) of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: In a rei vindicatio action, it is highly dangerous to adjudicate on an issue of prescription without first going into and examining the documentary title of the parties.
supporting_quote: "It has been said before, and I think it will bear repetition, that in a rei vindicatio action it is highly dangerous to adjudicate on an issue of prescription without first going into and examining the documentary title of the parties"

statement: The Supreme Court held that the settlement of 1930, which divided the estate among the widow and three respondents, was valid given the uncertainty in the law regarding adoption at the time.
supporting_quote: "The uncertainty was not removed at the time of the settlement and could not but have been prominently before the minds of the experienced lawyers who represented the parties at the relevant time."

statement: Non-compliance with Section 18 of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance does not prevent the creation of a partnership, but merely prevents evidence of the partnership being adduced in certain circumstances.
supporting_quote: "All that it does is to prevent evidence of the partnership being adduced in certain circumstances. It was, accordingly, competent to the defendant in the present case to show that the business between himself and the plaintiff did not constitute a co-ownership but is a partnership."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Cap. 57), s. 18.

statement: An action for pecuniary loss suffered by the dependants of a person killed by the negligent act of a defendant is barred after two years from the date of death, as governed by section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: 'No action shall be maintainable for any loss, injury, or damage, unless the same shall be commenced within two years from the time when the cause of action shall have arisen.'
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 9 of the Prescription Ordinance (Cap. 55)

statement: The court should strictly adhere to the provisions of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951, when dealing with partition actions.
supporting_quote: "It is imperative that in an action such- as a partition action which gives the decree under it (Section 48 (1)) an effect which is ' final and conclusive for all purposes against all persons whomsoever, whatever right, title or interest they have, or claim to have, to or in the land to which such decrees relate ', the provisions of the Partition Act should be strictly observed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 48 (1) of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951.

statement: Section 48(1) of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951 does not deprive a party who has not been duly served with summons of the right to claim that an interlocutory decree has not been properly entered and should be vacated.
supporting_quote: "I find it impossible to hold that section 48 (1) was intended to deprive a party who had not been duly served with summons of the right to claim that the decree had not been properly entered, and should therefore be vacated, in order that his claim might be investigated."
statute_citation_verbatim: Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951, s. 48 (1)

statement: In a partition action, a declaration can be obtained regarding rights over land outside the subject matter of the action only if it is specifically addressed within the scope of the case.
supporting_quote: It is not clear how in a partition action a declaration can be obtained tl1a.t a land outside the land to be partitioned is subject to a servitude, for this in effect is what the plaintiff seeks. Our attention was drawn by Mr. Chelvanayakam who appeared for the 3rd defendant-respondent to the case of Kanthia v. Sinnatamby 1[1 (1913) 2 l. Notes of Cases 19.] where it was held that such a declaration could not be granted.

statement: In an action for goods sold and delivered, the defendant must prove that there was a definite period of credit and that at the end of that period the debt became payable and that the date on which the debt became payable is more than a year from the date of institution of the action.
supporting_quote: In such a case the defendants must in order to succeed in their plea prove that there was a definite period of credit and that at the end of that period the debt became-payable and that the date on which the debt became payable is more than a year from the date of institution of the action.

statement: An opportunity should be given under section 756 (3) of the Civil Procedure Code to rectify an omission in a bond where an appellant deposited money as security for costs of appeal but omitted to hypothecate it by bond.
supporting_quote: Held, that an opportunity should be given under section 756 (3) of the Civil Procedure Code to rectify the omission
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 756 (3), 757

statement: A judgment of the Supreme Court dismissing an appeal from an order of a District Court refusing to set aside a sale of property in execution of a decree is a final judgment within the meaning of Rule 1 (a) of the Schedule to The Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance, even if the property sold was purchased by the judgment-creditor himself.
supporting_quote: "I do not think such a distinction can be validly drawn for the reason that the Privy Council decision in Krishna Pershad Singh v. Moti Chand 3 which was followed in Subramaniam Chetty v. Soysa2 was given in a case where the property sold in execution of the decree was purchased by the judgment-creditor."

statement: A third party can intervene in a pending rei vindicatio action where he proposes to obtain a declaration of title and consequential relief in his own favour, if the plaintiff does not object.
supporting_quote: "Now in this action the plaintiff is dominus litis, and just as he cannot be compelled to fight a litigant not of his own choice if he objects to an intervenient coming into the case, I also think that where he does not object to the intervention, such intervention should be allowed unless there is something in the rule which forbids it."

statement: A conveyance by the executor of a share of the estate to a devisee, even if not in direct opposition to the terms of the will, cannot be impugned on the ground that the executor admitted an unmentioned beneficiary to equality with those named in the will after a long period.
supporting_quote: "In regard to the devise to the testator's father it was submitted on the authority of Livera et al. v. Gunaratna 2[2 (1914) 17 N. L. R. 289.] a that although he predeceased the testator the fideicommissum did not lapse and that his interests were transmitted, on the death of the testator, to his heirs of whom undoubtedly Abdul Hameed was one."

statement: Failure to supply stamps for the Supreme Court decree is fatal to the reception of an appeal in testamentary proceedings.
supporting_quote: "The appeal is rejected with costs."

statement: The possession of one co-owner is the possession of all co-owners, and such possession cannot be ended by any secret intention in the mind of the possessing co-owner. Ouster or something equivalent to ouster must occur for a period of over ten years for prescription among co-owners.
supporting_quote: "It is settled law (Corea v. Appuhamy1 and Cadija Umma fl. Don Manis2) that the possession of one co-owner is the possession of the other co-owners and that possession qua co-owner cannot be ended by any secret intention in the mind of the possessing co-owner. The possession of one co-owner does not become possession by a title adverse to or independent of that of the others till ouster or something equivalent to ouster takes place."

statement: In an appeal from a decision of the District Court in a testamentary proceeding, the proper stamps for the decree of the Supreme Court must be delivered together with the petition of appeal to the Secretary of the District Court as required by Part II, Head F-Miscellaneous of Schedule A to the Stamp Ordinance.
supporting_quote: We are of the opinion that even in an appeal from a decision of the District Court in a testamentary proceeding the proper stamps for the decree of the Supreme Court must be delivered together with the petition of appeal to the Secretary of the District Court as required by Part II F-Miscellaneous of Schedule A to the Stamp Ordinance. Failure to do so is fatal to the reception of an appeal.

statement: The failure to tender notice of security contemporaneously with the receipt of the petition of appeal by the Judge is fatal to the appeal and not curable by sub-section 3.
supporting_quote: "Having regard to the wide terms in which sub-section 3 of section 756 is expressed would be inclined to grant relief to the appellant but am precluded from doing so by the decision in De Silva's case which has laid down that the failure to tender notice of security contemporaneously with the receipt of the petition of appeal by the Judge is fatal to the appeal and not curable by sub-section 3."

statement: A bond hypothecating money as security for costs must be executed before the Judge, Secretary or Chief Clerk in accordance with section 757 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "This bond has not been executed either before the Judge or the Secretary and therefore section 756 (1) read with section 757 has not been complied with."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 757 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: A donor who dedicates immovable property to the Buddhist Sangha cannot subsequently derogate from their own grant by attempting to contradict the representation in the dedication that the property belonged to them.
supporting_quote: "a man shall not derogate from his own grant"

statement: The court should determine the case based on the pleadings and issues set forth by the parties, rather than introducing irrelevant matters.
supporting_quote: "Under our system of Civil Procedure it is well established that what the Court has to determine is the case set up by the pleadings of the parties."

statement: The Ceylon State Mortgage Bank is not liable to pay damages suffered by a debtor in consequence of parate execution levied by it, under section 63 of the Ceylon State Mortgage Bank Ordinance, against the property mortgaged to it by the debtor.
supporting_quote: "Unless it has exercised its powers negligently, the Ceylon State Mortgage Bank is not liable to pay damages suffered by a debtor in consequence of parate execution levied by it, under section 63 of the Ceylon State Mortgage Bank Ordinance, against the property mortgaged to it by the debtor."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 63 of the Ceylon State Mortgage Bank Ordinance

statement: Where a person agrees by notarial deed to sell immovable property to another, the deed does not operate as a sale so as to transfer title, even when delivery of possession of the property and payment of the purchase price have been made. Such a deed is not a deed transferring title but is an agreement relating to the future transfer of title, and title does not pass until a further notarial deed is subsequently executed transferring the title.
supporting_quote: Where a person agrees by notarial deed to sell immovable property to another, the deed does not operate as a sale so as to transfer title, even when delivery of possession of the property and payment of the purchase price have been made. Such a deed is not a deed transferring title but is an agreement relating to the future transfer of title, and title does not pass until a further notarial deed is subsequently executed transferring the title.

statement: An application for letters of administration comes to an end with the death of the applicant prior to the issue of letters. Accordingly, where the last will of the deceased person is discovered after the death of the applicant for letters, application for probate of the will may be made without taking any steps to vacate an order absolute entered in the previous administration proceedings.
supporting_quote: "An application for letters of administration comes to an end with the death of the applicant prior to the issue of letters. Accordingly, where the last will of the deceased person is discovered after the death of the applicant for letters, application for probate of the will may be made without taking any steps to vacate an order absolute entered in the previous administration proceedings."

statement: The court held that the reference of the issue of forgery to a separate action was within its discretion and did not prejudice the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: "There was also the additional circumstance that at the claim inquiry following on the seizure the Judge had come to a clear finding of possession in favour of the 1st and 2nd defendants. The prayer of the 3rd defendant in effect sought a declaration against the 1st and 2nd defendants that he was the owner of the premises. In this state of affairs am of opinion that it was within the discretion of the court to order what was an action within an action to be tried separately and not to enlarge the scope of the trial beyond the limits desired by the plaintiff who set the machinery of the court in motion to obtain relief only for herself and not relief for a third party whom she did not even make, in the first instance, a defendant."

statement: The jurisdiction of the courts cannot be taken away by anything short of express words.
supporting_quote: "My own view is that the jurisdiction of the courts cannot be taken away by anything short of express words. I am fortified in that view by the opinion of the Privy Council in Bennett and White (Calgary) Ltd. V. Municipal District of Sugar City 2[2(1951) A. O. 786 at ], and the opinions of the judges of Canada and South Africa."

statement: The mere duration of possession alone is insufficient to establish a presumption of ouster in favor of a co-owner, unless there are additional circumstances that tend to show the probability of an ouster and the difficulty or impossibility of adducing proof of it.
supporting_quote: "If the ratio decidendi of the decision in Rajapakse v. Hendrick Singho is that acquiescence, on the part of a purchaser of an undivided interest, in the exclusive possession of the entire land and the appropriation of its profits by the other co-owner, is a circumstance from which the adversity of the possession of the other co-owners can be inferred, then that decision may be in consonance with the dicta of Bertram C.J. and Ennis J. to which I have earlier referred."

statement: When the fidei commissaries are a class, and there is one fidei commissum created in favor of that class, the members of the class who are to take must be ascertained only when the fiduciary dies.
supporting_quote: There is only one fidei commissum in the present case. The class consisted of Charlotte Caroline's children. Since Alfred predeceased his mother and ceased to be a member of the class, his transferee got nothing on his purchase, because the members of the class who were to take must be ascertained only when Charlotte Caroline died.

statement: A contract can bind a person and their heirs, executors, and administrators under certain conditions.
supporting_quote: "In order to settle the disputes arising out of ancient law, we decree, in general terms, that every stipulation, whether it consists in giving anything, doing anything, or both giving something or performing some act, shall be transmitted both to and against heirs, whether any special mention has been made of them or not"

statement: Any person who does any act, which may tend to hinder the course of justice or show disrespect to the Court's authority, commits contempt of Court within the meaning of section '7 of the Courts Ordinance.
supporting_quote: Any person who does any act, which may tend to hinder the course of justice or show disrespect to the Court's authority, commits contempt of Court within the meaning of section '7 of the Courts Ordinance.
statute_citation_verbatim: section '7 of the Courts Ordinance

statement: It is a contempt of court to act in breach of an undertaking given to a court.
supporting_quote: "It is a contempt of court to act in breach of an undertaking given to a court."

statement: A threat by a donee to cause bodily injury to the donor constitutes an act of ingratitude and is, therefore, a valid ground for the institution of action by the donor to have the deed of gift set aside.
supporting_quote: "A threat by a donee to causa bodily injury to the donor constitutes an act of ingratitude and is, therefore, a valid ground for the institution of aft action by the donor to have the deed of gift set aside."

statement: Prescription does not begin to run against the donee until the death of the donor, and in such a case, the donee, as remainder-man, is entitled to the benefit of the proviso to section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: Where a person donates immoveable property reserving to himself a life interest prescription does not begin to run against the donee until the death of the donor. In such a case, the donee, as remainder-man, is entitled to the benefit of the proviso to section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance, and adverse possession against the donor cannot be counted against the donee.
statute_citation_verbatim: Prescription Ordinance (Cap. 55), proviso to section 3

statement: In proceedings under section 327 of the Code, once a petition is numbered as a plaint, the burden of establishing possession or the right to possess falls on the judgment creditor.
supporting_quote: "I am definitely of the view that once a petition has been numbered as a plaint the onus of establishing possession or the right to possess is upon the judgment creditor who, as against the claimant, has all the obligations which the law casts upon a 'plaintiff in a regular action."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 327 of the Code

statement: The court held that the plaintiff's title to a 1/10 share of the land was valid, despite the existence of a deed of donation.
supporting_quote: "By the deed P 4 Arumugam gave the land in dispute and another land by way of donation to Velupillai ' for and in consideration of the love and affection' he had for his son, reciting as his title the deed P 2. The deed of donation contains a recital that the two lands donated, which were of the value of Rs. 2,500/, were subject to a mortgage debt of Rs. 1,500/ and interest which was to be paid and settled by the donee. It seems to me that the donor was making it clear in the deed that the gift was subject to an encumbrance, and that it was the duty of the donee to free the lands of that encumbrance. Undoubtedly the donor would benefit to that extent, but I am unable to say that the consideration for the donation was anything except love and affection, which is the consideration recited in the deed. I therefore do not regard the deed as a transfer for valuable consideration."

statement: Under Kandyan Law, a deed of gift given by a parent to his daughter after her marriage is revocable if there is no evidence that it was given in pursuance of a promise made before the marriage.
supporting_quote: "Under Kandyan Law, if a parent donates immovable property to his daughter some time after the latter's marriage, the deed of gift is revocable if there is no evidence that was given in pursuance of a promise made before the marriage. In such a case, the mere fact that the deed states that it is given 'for and in consideration of the marriage' and 'by-way of dowry' can make no difference."

statement: The words in a deed are to be construed most strongly against the person who uses them, if so doing works no wrong.
supporting_quote: "It is a maxime in law, that every man's grant shall be taken by construction of law most forcible against himself. Quaelibet conce8sio fortissimo contra donatorem interpretanda, which is so to be understood, that no wrong be thereby done; for it is another maxime in law, Quod legis constructio non facit injuriam."

statement: A landlord cannot avoid the operation of the prohibition contained in section 13 (1) (c) of the Rent Restriction Act by a mere statement on oath that the premises are required for the purpose of trade or business. He must place before the Court evidence sufficient to convince it of the truth of his claim.
supporting_quote: "A landlord cannot avoid the operation of the prohibition contained in that section by a mere statement on oath that the premises are required for the purpose of trade or business. He must place before the Court evidence sufficient to convince it of the truth of his claim."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 13 (1) (c) of the Rent Restriction Act, No. 29 of 1948

statement: In proceedings for the appointment of a representative of a deceased under the proviso to section 31 (2) of the Mortgage Act, No. 6 of 1949, it is not necessary to hear all the heirs of the deceased prior to making the appointment.
supporting_quote: "In any event any defect in the proceedings for the appointment of a representative of a deceased person entitled to notice cannot affect the decree in a mortgage action or the sale of the mortgaged property because it is not essential that the representative of a person entitled to notice should be a party to the mortgage proceedings."

statement: A servitude of the nature claimed by the plaintiff, analogous to a right of way of necessity, arises only on the making of an order by the Court and damages can be claimed from that date.
supporting_quote: "In such a case, damages can be returned only from the date of the order of the Court granting the servitude."

statement: A deed creating a charitable trust must be interpreted according to the religious beliefs of the person who executed it, and admissions made by trustees in previous actions are relevant for this interpretation.
supporting_quote: "For such purpose, admissions made by the trustees in previous action concerning the trust are relevant"

statement: The word 'owner' in the Land Redemption Ordinance means a person possessing the attributes of ownership under the general law.
supporting_quote: "The rights of an owner under the general law of Ceylon are comprised under three heads, namely, (1) the right of possession and the right to recover possession; (2) the right of use and enjoyment; and (3) the right to alienate. These three factors are all essential to the idea of ownership but need not all be present in an equal degree at one and the same time."
statute_citation_verbatim: Land Redemption Ordinance, No. 61 of 1942, 8.3

statement: Parties who waive their right of appeal cannot come to this Court by way of appeal.
supporting_quote: "Therefore. I reject the appeal, but since the procedure adopted on and after the 1st of August, 1960, including the order of the 5th of September, 1960, is illegal, I quash, all proceedings on or after the 1st of August, 1960, and the order of the learned District Judge, dated 5th September. 1960, and send the case back for further hearing."

statement: A pupil is considered a privy of his tutor and cannot re-agitate questions decided in an earlier action involving the tutor, provided the pupil claims under the same title as the tutor.
supporting_quote: "Now although an incumbency is an office, I have tried to show in my judgment in Podiya v. Bumangala Thero (supra) that it is an office to which rights in property attach; and for that reason I think the principle of res judicata would apply."

statement: The Land Commissioner, as the judicial tribunal whose action is being tested, may be brought before a higher court through an application for certiorari if his determination under section 3 of the Land Development Ordinance is challenged.
supporting_quote: "their Lordships consider that if the authority of a Land Commissioner to make a determination under section 3 of the Land Development Ordinance is challenged the appropriate procedure is by way of an application for certiorari"

statement: A judgment-debtor who sells property pending seizure and buys it for himself subsequently from the execution-purchaser is not protected by section 238 of the Civil Procedure Code, as the words 'all persons' do not include the judgment-debtor.
supporting_quote: "The Section was designed and enacted to protect persons against the acts of the judgment-debtor and not to protect or to benefit the judgment-debtor himself. Accordingly, it cannot protect a judgment-debtor who sells property pending seizure and buys it for himself subsequently from the execution-purchaser."
statute_citation_verbatim: 238. When a seizure of immovable property is effected under a writ of execution and made known as provided by section 237 and notice of the seizure is registered before the first day of January, nineteen hundred and twenty-eight, in the book formerly kept under section 237 or is registered on or after the first day of January. Nineteen hundred and twenty-eight, under the Registration of Documents Ordinance, any sale, conveyance, mortgage, lease, or disposition of the property seized, made after the seizure and registration of the notice of seizure and while such registration remains in force is void as against a purchaser from the Fiscal selling under the writ of execution and as against all persons deriving title under or through the parchaser.

statement: Section 348 of the Civil Procedure Code applies only to security given before the court under specific provisions of the Code, not to pre-action surety bonds.
supporting_quote: "The application of section 348 should, therefore, be limited to security taken before the court under the provisions of the Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 348 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A sale of immovable property in favour of an unincorporated society cannot pass title if it is not clear whether the transferor meant to benefit the present members of the society as individuals or to benefit the society as a quasi-corporation.
supporting_quote: "An unincorporated society, not being a juristic person, has no legal capacity to acquire property. Accordingly, a sale of immovable property in favour of an unincorporated society or association (in the present case the transferee was the ' Village Welfare Society, Veemankamam ') cannot pass title if it is not clear whether the transferor meant to benefit the present members of the society as individuals or to benefit the society as a quasi-corporation."

statement: Where a judgment-debtor re-enters an open land two days after the execution of a proprietary decree, such subsequent re-entry does not amount to a hindrance offered to the judgment-creditor in taking complete and effectual possession within the meaning of section 325 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Where, two days after execution of a proprietary decree in respect of a land, the judgment-debtor re-entered the land (which was an open one)- Held , that the subsequent re-entry by the judgment-debtor did not amount to a hindrance offered to the judgment-creditor in taking complete and effectual possession within the meaning of section 325 of the Civil Procedure Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 287 (2), 323, 325, 326.

statement: The District Judge should consider expert evidence regarding the genuineness of handwriting, but may also independently compare signatures for verification.
supporting_quote: "I think the modern view is to accept the expert's testimony if there is some other evidence, direct or circumstantial, which tends to show that the conclusion reached by the expert is correct; provided, of course, the Court, independently of the expert's opinion, but with his assistance, is able to conclude that the writing is a forgery."

statement: The Court has no jurisdiction to decide claims or disputes not referred to it for its determination under the Land Acquisition Act.
supporting_quote: "The jurisdiction of the Court under the Act is purely statutory and the Court has no power to determine claims or disputes not referred to it for its decision."

statement: A judgment debtor who remains on a land which is the subject-matter of the action does not become entitled to claim the benefit of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance by so remaining, and that in the instant case the fact that when the plaintiffs sought to obtain possession of the lands, the defendants urged that no due diligence had been shown in executing the writ of possession was an indication of a right existing in another person.
supporting_quote: It is common ground that after the decree in D. C. Kurunegala Case No. 17767 the defendants continued to be in possession of the lands and to enjoy the produce. The 2nd defendant was (the 1st having died) in possession of them even at the time of this action. It is urged that a judgment debtor who remains on a land which is the subject-matter of the action does not become entitled to claim the benefit of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance by so remaining, and that in the instant case the fact that when the plaintiffs sought to obtain possession of the lands, the defendants urged that no due diligence had been shown in executing the writ of possession was an indication of a right existing in another person.

statement: A judgment against a fiduciary in respect of the same fideicommissum is res judicata as against the fideicommissary.
supporting_quote: "Finally we may add that a judgment pronounced against a fiduciary will also damage a fideicommissary, unless the adverse judgment has occurred through the fault of the fiduciary; whether the suit was raised against the fiduciary before restoration in regard to a particular item or to the whole inheritance."

statement: A decision by a bench of five or more Judges convened by the Chief Justice under Section 51 (1) of the Courts Ordinance carries in my opinion, the same authority as a decision of a Full Bench.
supporting_quote: "I agree generally with the observations of My Lord the Chief Justice subject however to the following : i A decision by a bench of five or more Judges convened by the Chief Justice under Section 51 (1) of the Courts Ordinance carries in my opinion, the same authority as a decision of a Full Bench."
statute_citation_verbatim: Courts Ordinance (Cap. 6), s. 51(1)

statement: A person who occupies land and improves it in the mistaken belief that he has a lease of the property, or a lessee who lawfully occupies under a lease and makes improvements, is entitled to compensation if his term of lease is prematurely terminated by operation of law.
supporting_quote: "An improver who lawfully occupies under a lease and in that capacity makes improvements is entitled to compensation if his term of lease is prematurely terminated by operation of law."

statement: The only fee leviable in respect of a stall in an Urban Council market is that fixed by by-law.
supporting_quote: "For these reasons I would affirm the judgment appealed from and dismiss the appeal with costs."

statement: The Crown has not expressly or impliedly agreed to be bound by all the terms of the Schedule Rules of the Privy Council Ordinance, and laches cannot be imputed to the Crown.
supporting_quote: 'I would accordingly hold that, although there has been, in the circumstances of this case, a lack of due diligence on the part of the officers of the Crown, laches cannot be imputed to the Crown; and, therefore, that the provisions of Schedule Rule 25 do not apply to the Crown.'

statement: Parol evidence can be used to establish an express or constructive trust when the surrounding circumstances indicate that the beneficial interest was not intended to pass, even if the conveyance is in form absolute.
supporting_quote: A deed In those terms-transferring ownership of the half share to Ponnuthurai was necessary to effectuate the purpose for which Ponnuthurai wanted the plaintiff's assistance. The crucial issue, when the question is trust or no trust, is: What did the parties intend so far as their intention can be gathered from the surrounding circumstances?

statement: In an action to set aside a deed of transfer on the ground that it was executed in fraud of creditors, the plaintiff must allege and prove either absence of consideration or actual fraud on the part of the purchaser.
supporting_quote: "In Perera v. Menik Etana 1 [15 O. W. R. 258.] , which is a somewhat similar case, Shaw, J., sitting alone, held that in an action to set aside a deed on the ground that it was executed in fraud of creditors, the plaintiff has to allege and prove either that no consideration on the transfer was paid or actual fraud on the part of the purchaser."

statement: A letter acknowledging a debt and promising to pay within a specific time period constitutes a written promise under Section 6 of the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "In my view Section 12 contemplates merely an acknowledgment of the debt. In the letter P3 there is not only an acknowledgment that the amount is due but also a clear promise to pay this amount within a month. I would, therefore, construe this letter as a written promise to pay the amount: accordingly, Section 6 and not Section 8 of the Prescription Ordinance applies to the facts of this case."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prescription Ordinance (Cap. 55), ss. 6, S, 12.

statement: A document which has not been listed in accordance with the requirements of section 19 (2) (a) of the Partition Act is nevertheless admissible in evidence for the purpose of cross-examining a party in order to contradict him with a former statement made therein by him inconsistent with his evidence.
supporting_quote: "Every party to the action shall, not less than thirty days before the date of trial of the action, file or cause to be filed in court a list of documents on -which he relies to prove his right, share or interest to, 336 of or in the land together with an abstract of the contents of such documents. No party shall, except with the leave of the court which may be granted on such terms as the court may determine, be at liberty to put any document in evidence on his behalf in the action if no such, list as aforesaid has been filed by or on behalf of him in court, or if that document is not specified in a list so filed, or if an abstract of the contents of that document has not been so filed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951, s. 19 (2) (a)

statement: A procedural enactment is imperative and non-compliance with its requirements is fatal. The security for appeal must be executed before the District Judge or Secretary of the Court as per section 757 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Enactments regulating the procedure in Courts seem usually to be imperative and not merely directory. If, for instance, an appeal from a decision be given with provision requiring the fulfilment of certain conditions, such as giving notice of appeal and entering into recognisances, or transmitting documents within a certain time, a strict compliance would be imperative and non-compliance would be fatal to the appeal."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 757 of the Civil Procedure Code.

statement: When preparing a preliminary plan in a partition action, it is irregular for a Surveyor to survey and include land other than that referred to in the plaint without an additional commission from the court.
supporting_quote: "When preparing a preliminary plan in a partition action it is irregular for a Surveyor, in the absence of an additional commission issued to him under section 23 (1) of the Partition Act, to survey and include in the corpus any land other than that which is referred to in the plaint and which his commission authorises him to survey."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 23 (1) of the Partition Act, No. 16 of 1951

statement: A person cannot avail themselves of earlier possession for the purposes of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance if the deed of gift does not purport to transfer title to the disputed land.
supporting_quote: "Since the deed of 1946 in bis favour did not purport to transfer to him title to Lot 2, he is not, for the purposes of section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance, a person who claims the Lot under Appuhamy, whose earlier possession is therefore of no avail to him. I would accordingly hold that the plaintiff's action was not entitled to succeed."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prescription Ordinance, s. 3.

statement: The petitioner is entitled to a certificate under Rule 26 of the rules in the schedule to The Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance that he is the proper person to be substituted or entered on the record in place of the deceased plaintiff.
supporting_quote: "I do not think, however, that it is possible to take a similar view in regard to D. C. Colombo Case No. 2882. The averments and the prayer in the plaint in that case (the issues on which the trial proceeded are not before me) make it clear that the action was one in which the plaintiff, as trustee, sought to vindicate his legal title to the premises in suit. If the averments are true the trustee was bound under potion 13 of the Trusts Ordinance (Cap. 72) to maintain the action."

statement: The right of using a foot-path does not include the right to take a vehicle over that path.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that the right of using a foot-path includes the right to take a vehicle over that path. I think it is nothing more than the right of being able to come and go on foot."

statement: The plaintiff-appellant is not entitled to access lot 2 for the purpose of gathering dried leaves that fall from his live fence, as he has direct access to a public lane.
supporting_quote: "and, in my opinion, it is on this basis that the further claim of the plaintiff to be entitled to access to lot 2 for the purpose of gathering the dried leaves that fall from his live fence should be considered."

statement: Under the Thesawalamai Regulation, on the death of a woman who has married a second time and leaves sons by her first marriage and a daughter by her second, the property she received as dowry on her first marriage goes exclusively to the sons.
supporting_quote: "But it is to be understood that if she has daughters by her first husband she is obliged to give them, as well as the daughters by her second husband, their dowries from her own doty property; and if the son or sons marry or wish to quit her, she is obliged to give them the hereditary property brought in marriage by their father and the half of the acquired property obtained by the first marriage, after deducting therefrom the dowry which may have been given to the daughters."

statement: A plaintiff cannot rely on a title which he did not have at the commencement of the action.
supporting_quote: "There is nothing in the Trusts Ordinance, or in any other provision of any law that I am aware of, which states that a person may bring such an action in respect of temple property and at some subsequent date clothe himself with title to the property by obtaining a vesting order, and notwithstanding defects of title at the time of the institution of the action is entitled to escape from the consequences of bringing an action at a time when he had not the right to do so."

statement: A claimant must satisfy the conditions specified in section 7 to be exempt.
supporting_quote: To qualify for exemption under section 7(1) (c) there must be income of an " established " trust. A trust such as the one in the present case cannot be validly established unless it falls within the definition of " charitable trust " contained in section 99 (1) of the Trusts Ordinance. This definition imludea any trust " for the benefit of the public or any section of the public " falling within any one of a number of categories which extend to such purposes as the relief of poverty and the advancement of education or knowledge. To satisfy the definition contain d in the Income Tax Ordinance therefore the trust must be a charitable trust " of a public character ": to be a subsisting charitable trust at all it must be a trust for the benefit of the public or some section of it. In order to determine this question

statement: A trust is valid only if it constitutes a charitable trust as defined in section 99.
supporting_quote: To qualify for exemption under section 7(1) (c) there must be income of an " established " trust. A trust such as the one in the present case cannot be validly established unless it falls within the definition of " charitable trust " contained in section 99 (1) of the Trusts Ordinance. statement: A trust is considered charitable and of a public character if it benefits the public or a section of the public, such as for relieving poverty or advancing education.
supporting_quote: To qualify for exemption under section 7(1) (c) there must be income of an " established " trust.
