statement: A decree absolute for default that has been passed against a defendant by a District Court can operate as res judicata in a subsequent action between the same parties in respect of the same subject-matter.
supporting_quote: "A decree absolute for default that has been passed against a defendant by a district court is one to which section 207 of the Civil Procedure Code applies and can, therefore, operate as res judicata in a subsequent action between the same parties in respect of the same subject-matter."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 84, 85, 86, 188, 192, 206, 207.

statement: In Ceylon, the common law remedy for forfeiture of benefits is not abrogated by sections 617 and 618 of the Civil Procedure Code, but remedies under these sections are complementary to the action available under the common law. Parties cannot have both remedies and must elect one or the other.
supporting_quote: "The common law remedy was not abrogated as a result of the enactment of those sections (sections 617 and 618 of the Civil Procedure Code), but rather remedies envisaged by these sections are complementary to the action available under the common law. However . . . the parties cannot have the benefit of both remedies but should elect to claim either the remedy under the common law or those available under the Civil Procedure Code."

statement: The Court has the inherent power to exclude a lot which has been wrongly included in the corpus of a partition action, under section 839 of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: "Therefore we respectfully differ from the ruling in Luinona's case (supra) which is not binding on us. In this connexion the following observations of Mahmood, J., in Narsingh Das v. Mangal Dubey[1 (1883) 5 Allahabad 163 at p. 172. ] are apposite :- " Courts are not to act upon the principle that every procedure is to be taken as prohibited unless it is expressly provided for by the Code, but on the converse principle that every procedure is to be understood as permissible till it is shown to be prohibited by the law. As a matter of general principle prohibitions cannot be presumed.""
statute_citation_verbatim: "section 839 of the Civil Procedure Code"

statement: A guardian ad litem's admission of a plaintiff's claim under Section 72 of the Civil Procedure Code does not constitute an adjustment within the meaning of Section 408, and thus does not require the court’s leave as per Section 500.
supporting_quote: "Section 500 of the Civil Procedure Code which debars a guardian of a minor from compounding an action without the leave of the Court refers to such an adjustment of an action as is mentioned in section 408 and is not applicable to an admission made by the guardian in terms of section 72."
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 72, 408, 500.

statement: The burden of proof regarding the termination of successive interests and any disability lies with the party claiming prescriptive possession.
supporting_quote: "It is, in short, a question of fact wherever long continued exclusive possession by one co-owner is proved to have existed whether it is not just and reasonable in all the circumstances of the case that the parties should be treated as though it had been proved that that separate and exclusive possession had become adverse at some date more than ten years before action brought."

statement: A party to a contract who repudiates the agreement prior to the expiration of the option period is not required to allege or prove tender of performance.
supporting_quote: "I would respectfully follow the decisions referred to above and hold that the plaintiff was under no legal obligation after the receipt by him of letter D.2 to allege or prove a tender of the balance purchase price."

statement: A Court, applying well established equitable doctrine, will not allow the appellants to require performance by the respondent of her part of the bargain without being ready and willing to perform their part.
supporting_quote: "It would in their opinion be contrary to well established equitable principles that the appellants should at the same time obtain payment of the second sum of Rs. 15,000 and retain the lands which they had agreed to transfer unless they could show that time was of the essence of the contract."

statement: A secured creditor of an estate is entitled to decline to rely on his security and claim payment out of the entire estate, but this right can be lost by laches or other equitable defenses.
supporting_quote: It is quite true that as a general rule a secured creditor of an estates entitled to decline to rely on his security and to claim payment out of the estate as a whole ; though it must be remembered that if he does so his action releases the secured property into the general pool of assets and the creditor does not make a side deal, as was done here, with the specific devisees of the land subject to the mortgage with the intention of exempting their property from any contribution at all towards the satisfaction of his debt.

statement: The doctrine of res judicata operates to prevent the plaintiff from re-agitating a question that was decided in earlier proceedings, even if the decision was erroneous.
supporting_quote: "Since the same question is sought to be raised by the plaintiff in the present case, and in respect of the same subject matter, the plaintiff would appear to be estopped by the doctrine of res judicata from doing so."

statement: The correct approach to the evidence of experts is that their opinion should be used to assist the judge in forming his own opinion, not as conclusive proof.
supporting_quote: "The expert's opinion is relevant but only in order to enable the Judge himself to form his own opinion."

statement: A party who was not a party to the partition action is not bound by the interlocutory decree if lis pendens had not been properly registered, but does not have the right to intervene and set aside the interlocutory decree.
supporting_quote: "That is all that sub-Section 3 provides. A person who was not a party to the partition action is not bound by the interlocutory decree if lis pendens had not been properly registered. This does not mean that he is entitled to intervene and have the interlocutory decree set aside."

statement: A si sine liberis decesserit clause does not per se create a tacit fidei commissum in favor of the grandchildren of the testator.
supporting_quote: "Where a last will bequeaths property to the children of the testator, the presence therein of a si sine liberis decesserit clause--e.g., 'provided however that on the death of anyone of them leaving no issue, his or her share shall devolve on the survivor or survivors and their children' -does not per se create a tacit fidei commissum in favour of the grandchildren of the testator."

statement: A pre-emptor cannot claim to be in a better position by not receiving notice of the intended sale than he would have been if he had received such notice.
supporting_quote: "A would be pre-emptor cannot claim to be in a better position by not receiving notice of the intended sale than he would have been if he had received such notice. "

statement: The amendments to sections 40 and 41 of the Workmen's Compensation Ordinance are retrospective in operation.
supporting_quote: "I would, therefore, hold that section 6 (3) of the Interpretation Ordinance has no application to the present case."

statement: Under the law of the United States, the plaintiff does not have a maritime lien or other charge enforceable by action in rem for expenses incurred in pursuance of a statutory duty imposed by Title 46 of the Code.
supporting_quote: I am satisfied that the Plaintiff has not proved that under that law a maritime lien or other charge enforceable by action in rem arises in its favour.
statute_citation_verbatim: United States (of America) Code, Title 46, s. 678

statement: A binna married daughter would re-acquire binna rights if the father, during his lifetime, brought her into the mulgedera and had her married in binna.
supporting_quote: "Thereafter, if it be contended that a daughter, who is married in binna, has forfeited her rights, it must be shown that she severed herself from her parental home before the death of the father. It is going out in diga and severance from the mulgedera during the lifetime of the father which brings about forfeiture, and not merely a temporary departure"

statement: A lessee can plead the benefit of the Rent Restriction Act where the premises are occupied by him under a notarial lease which has terminated by effluxion of time.
supporting_quote: "A lessee can plead the benefit of the Rent Restriction Act where the premises in question are occupied by him under a notarial lease which has terminated by effluxion of time."

statement: An action filed against more than one defendant, where some of them were alive and some had died prior to the institution of the action, is not necessarily a nullity.
supporting_quote: I do not think that the same considerations apply to an action filed against more than one defendant, where some of them were alive and some had died prior to action. We have not been referred to any authority which decides that such an action is a nullity. I can see no reason why it should be a nullity, for it is surely good as against the living defendants.

statement: In construing a contract, the court should focus on the substance of the transaction rather than just the form and terminology used.
supporting_quote: "In construing a contract the Court will look at what the contract really is and not at what the parties say it is. What the Court has to consider is not the mere name given to it but the substance of the transaction and decide what it would in truth and in fact amount to on a consideration of all the facts relating to it."

statement: The ultimate legatees do not have the full enjoyment of the devised property until a specified age exceeding twenty-one years, and some other third party is to be paid an annuity out of the income from the property. The legatees can only claim title to the property on attaining majority if the third party dies earlier.
supporting_quote: Where a testator has made it clear in his will that not only are the ultimate legatees not to have the full enjoyment of the devised property until they attain a specified age exceeding twenty-one years, but also that some other third party is to be paid an annuity out of the income from the property, then, the Court will not give the legatees enjoyment of the property as absolute owners on their attaining majority, unless the third party dies earlier.

statement: A person acting in two distinct capacities can, for the purpose of a contract, be regarded as capable of entering into an agreement with himself.
supporting_quote: "A person acting in two distinct capacities can, for the purpose of a contract, be regarded as capable of entering into an agreement with himself."

statement: The court held that the plaintiff's purported appointment as viharadhipati was without authority, and thus he cannot be ejected by the defendant who also lacks lawful appointment.
supporting_quote: "I would dismiss the appeal with costs."

statement: When the Public Trustee is appointed to be custodian trustee of any trust, in terms of section 41 of the Public Trustee Ordinance, he is not vested with title to the trust property until a vesting order is executed. Until then, the title remains in the trustees other than the custodian trustee.
supporting_quote: "When the Public Trustee is appointed to be custodian trustee of any trust, in terms of section 41 of the Public Trustee Ordinance, he is not vested with title to the trust property until a vesting order is executed. Until then the title remains in the trustees other than the custodian trustee."
statute_citation_verbatim: Public Trustee Ordinance (Cap. 88)-Section 41

statement: The proper question for decision upon an application for an interim injunction is whether there is a serious matter to be tried at the hearing. If it appears from the pleadings already filed that such a matter does exist, the further question is whether the circumstances are such that a decree which may ultimately be entered in favour of the party seeking the injunction would be nugatory or ineffective if the injunction is not issued.
supporting_quote: The proper question for decision upon an application for an interim injunction is 'whether there is a serious matter to be tried at the hearing' (Jinadasa v. Weerasinghe1 [ 1 (1929) 31 N. L. R. 33. ] ). If it appears from the pleadings already filed that such a matter does exist, the further question is whether the circumstances are such that a decree which may ultimately be entered in favour of the party seeking the injunction would be nugatory or ineffective if the injunction is not issued.

statement: A person entitled to pre-empt has the right to buy property for the price proposed or at market value, and a sale without giving notice to those entitled to pre-empt is a denial of their right.
supporting_quote: "The obligation to give to those entitled to pre-empt the opportunity of doing so is implicit in the law and the failure to give them that opportunity by giving the prescribed notice can rightly be regarded as a refusal to fulfil that obligation."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 6 of the Thesawalamai Pre-emption Ordinance provides: '....... within three weeks of the date of publication of a notice under section 5, any person to whom the right of pre-emption is reserved by this Ordinance, may either tender the amount stated in such notice and buy the property from the intending vendor, or enter into an agreement to buy it.'

statement: A vested interest is an assured and certain right, as opposed to a contingent or conditional one.
supporting_quote: "When the word 'vested' is used in this sense, Austin (Jurisprudence vol. 2, lect. 53) points out that in reality -a right of one class is not being distinguished from a right of another class but that a right is being distinguished from a chance or possibility of aright"

statement: The first bond is not an essential part of the cause of action in a hypothecary action, and can be produced in evidence to prove the debt.
supporting_quote: "How the debt was created is for this purpose immaterial and the first bond is not therefore an essential part of the cause of action. It can without being pleaded be produced in evidence to prove the debt."

statement: The court held that the land described as Lot C of 21 perches was not part of a larger common property but belonged exclusively to the first defendant's heirs.
supporting_quote: "I do not think this is a case where a lot was separated off for mere convenience of possession and as a temporary arrangement. It is much more likely to have been intended as a permanent mode of possession, and the lot so separated off would, with the lapse of time and exclusive possession, cease to be held in common with the rest of the land."

statement: A co-owner of a land cannot maintain an action for declaration of title to a building standing on the common property.
supporting_quote: The question that arises for decision on this appeal is whether a co-owner of a land can maintain an action for declaration of title to a building on the common property. The plaintiff claimed that he was entitled to 1/20 share of a land called Medaweraniyewatta situated in the village of Tittapattara and a tiled boutique built thereon by one James Appu his predecessor in title.

statement: Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code cannot be used to introduce a new 'matter in dispute' involving an entirely new cause of action which is inconsistent with the original cause of action.
supporting_quote: Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code which authorises the court to permit a person to be substituted or added as plaintiff in specified circumstances cannot be employed to introduce a new 'matter in dispute' involving an entirely new cause of action which is inconsistent with the cause of action which was pleaded between the original plaintiff and the defendant.
statute_citation_verbatim: section 13 of Civil Procedure Code

statement: Co-owners can maintain an action against one another to have their use to a common road vindicated and any obstruction removed, even if the co-owner has obstructed the use of the road.
supporting_quote: Held , that it was open to A and B to maintain an action against C to have their use to the common road vindicated and the obstruction removed.

statement: A person who improves land on the faith of a document from the owner which turns out to be void in law is entitled to compensation for those improvements, and may retain possession until compensated.
supporting_quote: "There is a further fact which has a direct bearing on the question, and this is that the improvements were made with the knowledge and consent of that owner and on the representation of the owner that if he made the improvement he was to have the right to possess and enjoy it for so long as he wished on payment of the specified ground rent. Such a person has not the possessio civilis. This is a circumstance which might deprive him of the right to claim compensation in other cases, but where, as in this instance, his claim is in effect against the person with whose knowledge and consent those improvements were made, it has been found possible to give him the rights of a bona fide possessor though in point of fact he has not the possessio civilis."

statement: The court should not infer malicious desertion based on one party's unwillingness to live with the other, especially when both parties initially wanted to resume their conjugal life.
supporting_quote: These answers reveal the plaintiff's unreasonable attitude. The following further evidence shows how uncompromising he was.

statement: An appellate court should not reverse a trial judge's findings of fact unless there is a strong countervailing consideration.
supporting_quote: "It may have been assumed or it may have been stated without being recorded that they were received from predecessors in the family or by some other form of family tradition. Neither the trial Court nor the Supreme Court rejected any part of the evidence tendered on the ground that it was not legally admissible under section 32 (5) of the Evidence Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Evidence Ordinance, s. 32 (5)

statement: A deed that grants property to a donee with the children and their heirs, executors, administrators and assigns having the right to possess or do whatever they please with the property does not necessarily create a fideicommissum.
supporting_quote: "Instead, the persons to be benefited being the children of the donee, he expressed the view that the additional words 'their (i.e., the children's) heirs, executors, administrators and assigns' could be construed as used for the purpose of conferring on the children an absolute and unfettered right in the property conveyed."

statement: The period of prescription for the appellant's claim began to run from September 25, 1954, when the valuation report was furnished to the court, rather than after October 23, 1956, when the court ordered payment.
supporting_quote: "Payment could in law have been demanded by the appellant immediately after 25th September 1954, and the period of prescription began to run from that date. I am of opinion that the defendant was entitled to succeed also on the issue of prescription."

statement: Where any premises are sold by a landlord while a tenant is in occupation thereof, the purchaser can either insist on the vendor giving him vacant possession or, with notice to the tenant in occupation of the premises, elect to take the premises with that tenant. If the purchaser fails to give notice of election to the tenant, the contract of tenancy between the vendor and the tenant subsists and it is only the vendor who is competent to terminate that contract of tenancy.
supporting_quote: Where any premises are sold while a tenant is in occupation thereof, two courses of action are in law open to the purchaser. He could either insist on the vendor giving him vacant possession of the premises or with notice to the tenant in occupation of the premises elect to take the premises with that tenant. If the purchaser fails to elect to take the premises with the vendor's tenant in occupation thereof, the contract of tenancy between the vendor and the tenant subsists and it is only the vendor who is competent to terminate that contract of tenancy.

statement: In a testamentary action, the proper stage for determining whether property alleged to belong to a testator should be excluded from the estate is not when conflicting claims to administration are being considered by the Court.
supporting_quote: "The short point arising on this appeal relates to the proper stage at which the District Court should, in the course of a testamentary action, adjudicate upon a dispute as to whether property alleged to belong to a testator should be excluded from the property of the estate on the ground that it is property belonging to another."

statement: The standard rent for premises Nos. 102 and 104 is the amount of the joint assessment made in November 1941, unless the board fixes separate rents.
supporting_quote: In the absence of such a fixation by the board, the 1941 assessment still holds good, and the standard rent has to be calculated on that basis.

statement: An action based on co-ownership can be defeated by showing that the business was carried on in a de facto partnership, with no written agreement as required by the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Where an action is instituted in respect of a business on the false basis that the plaintiff and defendant are co-owners of the business it is open to the defendant to show that the business was carried on by the plaintiff and himself in a de facto partnership and not as co-owners, that there was no agreement in writing as required by section 18 (c) of the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance 1840 and that consequently the action was not maintainable."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance (Cap. 57) s. 18 (c)

statement: The sale of sweep tickets is the sale of a chose in action, and Section 10 of the Prescription Ordinance applies with a three-year prescription period.
supporting_quote: "In my view, therefore, section 8 of the Prescription Ordinance only applies to 'goods which are capable of being physically delivered' and not to the sale of incorporeal things such as a chose in action. In the latter case, Section 10 applies and the period of prescription would be three years."
statute_citation_verbatim: Prescription Ordinance, ss. S, 10.

statement: A judgment of the Supreme Court reversing an order of a District Judge allowing the application of a person to be added as a party to a pending mortgage action is not a final judgment in a civil suit or action within the meaning of section 3 and rule 1 (a) of the Rules in the Schedule to the Appeals (Privy Council) Ordinance.
supporting_quote: "Now the suit or action before us is the action, on the Mortgage Bond No. 3514. That action is still pending and has not yet been decided and in that action no judgment has yet been given."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 3 of the Ordinance states that the right of parties to civil suits or actions in the Supreme Court to appeal to Her Majesty against the judgments and orders of such Court shall be subject to and regulated by the Rules in the Schedule. Rule 1 (a) of the Rules in the Schedule states that an appeal shall lie as of right from any final judgment of the Court where the matter in dispute on the appeal amounts to or is of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards, or where the appeal involves directly or indirectly some claim or question to or respecting property or some civil right amounting to or of the value of five thousand rupees or upwards.

statement: There was fraud and collusion within the meaning of section 7 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance, as evidenced by the fiduciary's breach of duty to protect the plaintiff's interests and the defendant's knowledge of this.
supporting_quote: "While the main weight of the argument for the defendant before the Board was put on the hypothesis which their Lordships have rejected, reliance was also placed on the reasons given by the Chief Justice for setting aside the finding of fraud and collusion. The Chief Justice said :- For the purpose of bringing a deed within the ambit of section 7 (2) it is not sufficient to establish that the person who obtained the deed was an unscrupulous person who would take undue advantage of any situation for the purpose of gain or that he had been punished for evasion of revenue laws or that he had committed fraud on previous occasions. Fraud or collusion in obtaining the particular deed in question must be established."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 7 of the Registration of Documents Ordinance

statement: The discretionary power to register an instrument in a new folio under Section 14(1) of the Registration of Documents Ordinance must be exercised only when registration according to the rule laid down in the main section is not feasible, or in special circumstances such as registering a final decree of partition.
supporting_quote: "The discretionary power conferred on the Registrar by the proviso must be exercised only in a case where registration according to the rule laid down in the main section is not feasible, or in a case in which the entry in a new folio is proper in the special circumstances of a case, e.g., when registering a final decree of partition"
statute_citation_verbatim: Registration of Documents Ordinance, ss. 1, 12, 13, 14 (1)

statement: A servitude is one and indivisible, meaning it must be shown legally to exist at each and every point on the strip of land over which it is claimed. If the claimant fails to prove its existence at any one of such points, the servitude disappears not at that point only but at every other point.
supporting_quote: "Servitude is one and indivisible, in the sense that it must be shown legally to exist at each and every point on the strip of land over which it is claimed and if the claimant fail to prove its existence at any one of such points, the servitude disappears not at that point only but at every other point."

statement: A person alleging that he is fideicommissarius under a deed is not entitled to file an action for a declaration preventing the fiduciarius or the transferee of the interests from effecting useful improvements on the fideicommissary property.
supporting_quote: "A person, alleging that he is fideicommissarius under a deed, is not entitled to file action for a declaration that the deed created a fideicommissum and to prevent the fiduciarius, or the transferee of the interests of the fiduciarius, from effecting useful improvements on the fideicommissary property."

statement: Property given and dedicated as Sanghika property need not be or contain a temple, and succession to such property may be governed by the terms of the act of dedication to the exclusion of Buddhist rules of succession.
supporting_quote: "Property given and dedicated as Sanghika property need not be or contain a temple. 197 Succession to Sanghika property (whether a temple or not) may be governed by the terms of the act of dedication to the exclusion of the Buddhist rules of succession."

statement: A renunciation by a Viharadhipathi of his right to be Viharadhipathi may be inferred from facts and circumstances, but such an inference will not be drawn if the matter is left in a state of doubt.
supporting_quote: "Although a renunciation by a Viharadhipathi of his right to be Viharadhipathi may be inferred from facts and circumstances, such an inference will not be drawn if the matter is left in a state of doubt."

statement: An amendment of a plaint may be allowed under section 93 of the Civil Procedure Code before the hearing of the action. (Observations to the contrary in Lebbe v. Sandanam (1963) 64 N. L. R. 461, disapproved.)
supporting_quote: The Court has power to permit a plaintiff to plead an alternative cause of action by way of amending his plaint, if no injustice can possibly result to the defendant and so long as the amendment does not have the effect of converting an action of one character into an action of another and inconsistent character. ( Lebbe v. Sandanam (1963) 64 N. L. R. 461, discussed and distinguished.)
statute_citation_verbatim: section 93 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: A party who acquires a new and independent title to the subject matter of a previous litigation subsequent to a decree in that earlier action is not barred by res judicata from setting up that new title.
supporting_quote: "As the appellants are setting up a new and independent title which they acquired after the decree in the earlier case, to the Lot in dispute, we hold that their cause for claiming is different from the claim they set up in the earlier action and it is not barred by the plea of res judicata."

statement: The Court's power under section 93 of the Civil Procedure Code is limited to correcting errors in pleadings and cannot be used to set up a new case, convert an action into another character, take the action out of limitation provisions, add a new cause of action, prejudice existing rights, or change the substance of the action.
supporting_quote: "As the power is limited to the correction of errors, it follows that the Court has no power to make alterations- (a) which set up a new case, (b) which have the effect of converting an action of one character into an action of another character, (c) which have the effect of taking the action out of the provisions governing the limitation of actions in the Prescription Ordinance or any other enactment of law, (d) which have the effect of the addition of a new cause of action, (e) which have the effect of prejudicing the rights of the other side existing at the date of the proposed amendment, and (f) which have the effect of changing the substance or essence of the action."
statute_citation_verbatim: 93 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The word 'motion', as used in section 91 of the Civil Procedure Code, does not necessarily mean a written motion. Section 408 requires parties to notify their settlement to court by motion, but does not require a written memorandum for settlements under section 408.
supporting_quote: "Further, when parties finally settle their disputes and notify the terms of the compromise to Court, the Court is bound to enter the terms of then' settlement and then pass a decree (vide section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code). This is a step in the course of regular procedure specifically provided for by the Civil Procedure Code and is not a step incidental to the proceedings. Consequently, there is no requirement that section 91 should be complied with when parties enter into a settlement under section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code."
statute_citation_verbatim: section 408 of the Civil Procedure Code

statement: The Court held that the execution of deed P2 has not been duly proved, as it was not produced in proper custody and only a certified copy was examined.
supporting_quote: "Perhaps he had section 90 of the Evidence Ordinance in mind when he made the statement above quoted , but he does not appear to have considered the terms of that section as carefully as he should have. That section reads- 'Where any document purporting or proved to be thirty years old is produced from any custody which the court in the particular case considers proper, the court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, that it was duly executed and attested by the persons by whom it purports to be executed and attested.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 90 of the Evidence Ordinance

statement: A partition decree entered when any one of the parties was dead at the time of such entry is void and of no avail in law.
supporting_quote: "A partition decree entered when anyone of the parties was dead at the time of such entry is void and of no avail in law."

statement: A co-owner cannot erect a building or structure without the previous consent of the other co-owners, except that a co-owner can only put to use a co-owned property for the specific use intended by all co-owners without the consent of the other co-owners.
supporting_quote: In Muthaliph's case the co-owners allotted to themselves separate portions of the co-owned land and left a narrow passage, marked in pink in the plan produced in that case, as a right of way to be used by the co-owners. One of the co-owners built on this passage and another co-owner brought an action to restrain him from erecting buildings on this passage. It was held that this pink portion which was meant as a passage was still in the co-ownership of all the co-owners and since the co-owners have agreed that this should be put to a particular use, namely as a passage, another co-owner could not put it to any other use.

statement: A fidei commissum in favour of particular members of a family is different from a fidei commissum in favour of a family as a class. In the former case, if the gift was not accepted by the fidei commissaries, the donor could revoke the gift so far as it related to the fidei commissaries and their children.
supporting_quote: A fidei commissum in favour of particular members of a family is different from a fidei commissum in favour of a family as a class. L gifted a land to C and C's husband E subject to a fidei commissum in favour of their two sons D and P and their lawful children. The gift was accepted by the two fiduciaries but was not accepted by the fidei commissaries. Held, that, since this was not a fidei commissum in favour of a family as a class, it was open to the donor, in view of the non-acceptance by the fidei commissaries, to revoke the gift so far as it related to the fidei commissaries and their children.

statement: The burden of proving that the defendant is not the owner lies with the plaintiff when the question is whether any person is the owner of something of which he is shown to be in possession.
supporting_quote: "When the question is whether any person is owner of anything of which he is shown to be in possession, the burden of proving that he is not the owner is on the person who affirms that he is not the owner."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 110 of the Evidence Ordinance.

statement: The plaintiff failed to establish that there was an encroachment on his Lot by the defendants.
supporting_quote: In this state of things the only conclusion I can come to is that the plaintiff has failed to establish that there was an encroachment on his Lot by the defendants, and I would therefore set aside the judgment of the learned Judge and dismiss the plaintiff's action with costs.

statement: Entries in a Grains Tax Register are relevant and admissible evidence on the question of title to land.
supporting_quote: "Entries in a Grains Tax Register are relevant and admissible evidence on the question of title to a land."

statement: An express prohibition against alienation out of the family of a legatee or donee is itself sufficient to create a fideicommissum in favour of the members of the family.
supporting_quote: "Such, it would seem, was also the view of the Privy Council in the South African case of Josef and Others v. Mulder and Others[(1903) A. C. 190.], where husband and wife married in community transferred by deed to their son certain immovable property for valuable considera�tion, stipulating that the same ' shall never be sold or parted with in favour of a stranger but shall permanently remain among legal heirs '. The decision that the deed created a fidei commissum implies that the Privy Council considered that the legal heirs were sufficiently indicated (though not expressly) as the persons to be benefited by the prohibition."

statement: The Sinhala word 'bharakaraya' in the context of a deed of gift does not create a fideicommissum, as it is equivalent to 'assigns'.
supporting_quote: "Therefore, we the said Donors hereby gave full power unto the said Donees Kalinga Thamis Nona and Dinayadura Abaran Silva to hold and possess subject to the aforesaid regulations the said undivided portion of land and all the rights title interest and privileges of us the said Donors in and to the same, and after their lifetime their heirs executors administrators and assigns to hold and possess subject to the Government regulations the same uninterruptedly for ever or to deal with the same as please."

statement: A deed of transfer of immovable property executed by a minor is voidable and not void.
supporting_quote: "A deed of transfer of immovable property executed by a minor is voidable and not void."

statement: A sale of immovable property is voidable if the consideration afforded is so much an undervalue as to amount to laesio enormis, and a general permission from the Court under Section 8 of the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance does not confer on a married woman the liberty to deal with her immovable property without specific conditions.
supporting_quote: "There are no doubt persuasive arguments to support either construction. Certainly, the wording of section 8 is wide enough to admit of the latter approach. Nevertheless their Lordships are of opinion that the preponderating arguments tell against it."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 8 of the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (Cap. 57)

statement: The Court of Appeal of Sri Lanka holds that the jurisdiction to grant equitable relief against forfeiture for non-payment of rent exists under Ceylon law.
supporting_quote: "Having regard to this long line of decisions to which I have referred, I must take it as well settled law that the principle which obtained under the English Law is followed in Ceylon"

statement: Excess sums paid by way of rent during the three years immediately anterior to the date when the tenant makes default in the payment of rent are available to the tenant for deduction from the rent due from him.
supporting_quote: Those three years commence on April 1, 1956, and end on March 31, 1959. Although the defendant has paid sums in excess of the authorised rent upto October 31,1957, only the excess paid during the period of 19 months commencing on April 1,1956, and ending on October 31,1957, being the period falling within the aforesaid three years, is in law available to him for deduction from the rent due from him.

statement: A daughter who accepts a dowry after her mother's death does not lose her right to the acquired property of her deceased mother, as provided by section 20(2) of the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance in its pre-amended form.
supporting_quote: "Under the Thesavalamai, a daughter who was given a dowry on her marriage that took place after the death of her mother did not, by accepting the dowry, lose her right to her share of her deceased mother's thediatheddam which vested in her by operation of section 20 (2) of the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance in the form in which it stood prior to its amendment by section 6 of Ordinance No. 58 of 1947."
statute_citation_verbatim: Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance (prior to amendment by s. 6 of Ordinance No. 58 of 1947), s. 20 (2)

statement: The rule of succession applicable to Buddhist temples is presumed to be the sissyanu sisya paramparawa, and the onus of proving any other rule of succession lies with the person alleging it.
supporting_quote: "Under our law, it will be presumed that the rule of succession applicable to Buddhist temples is the sissyanu sisya paramparawa. The onus of proving any other rule of succession is on the person alleging it."

statement: The 10th defendant, who is the adhikari of Kovilakanda Purana Viharaya, should be recognized as having a legal right to represent the temple in an assertion to sanghika property.
supporting_quote: "For the limited purposes of the present case, points of dispute Nos. 4, 5, 9 and 10 should, in my opinion, have been answered in favour of the 10th defendant, while point of dispute No. 8 should have been answered in favour of the temple."

statement: The running of prescription in favor of the defendant was not arrested merely because he had left the temple in obedience to the decree of Court in action No. 3760.
supporting_quote: "It is the duty of the Courts to see that no party is placed at a disadvantage by an act of Court."

statement: A person who was not a party to the partition action can intervene and have an interlocutory decree set aside if lis pendens was not properly registered, even after the decree is entered.
supporting_quote: "In considering the effect of section 48 (3), Sinnetamby, J., said at 503, 'In the case of persons who are not parties to the action, however, sub-section 3 provides, inter alia, that the fact that the lis pendens had not been properly registered would deprive the decree of its final and conclusive effect.'"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 48 (3) of the Partition Act

statement: An executor's obligation to pay a minor the sum of money to which they are entitled must be discharged by paying it into court, not directly to the minor.
supporting_quote: "The question that arises for decision is whether the executor's obligation to pay the petitioner the sum of Rs. 5,000 was legally discharged by their payment by a cheque for Rs. 5,000 to her, a minor. The circumstances surrounding this payment as stated above are not satisfactory and one important feature that the executors have not explained satisfactorily is why they paid by cheque despite the letter she wrote to them through their Proctors requesting them not to pay the money to her father and expressing her wish to get this sum of money deposited in the Post Office Savings Bank."
statute_citation_verbatim: "Section 553 of the Civil Procedure Code provides- 'Every executor and administrator shall file in the District Court, on or before the expiration of twelve months from the date upon which probate or grant of administration issued to him, a true account 510 of his executor ship or administration, as the case may be, verified on oath or affirmation, with all receipts and vouchers attached, and may at the same time pay into court any money which may have come to his hands in the course of his administration to which any minor or minors may be entitled.'"

statement: Section 56 of the Debt Conciliation Ordinance does not bar a civil court from entertaining an action on a mortgage bond, but only actions in respect of the validity of any procedure before the Board or the legality of any settlement.
supporting_quote: "The contention raised relates to the want of jurisdiction of the Court while the provision of the Ordinance prevents the regularity or the validity of the conduct of the business before the Board being called in question"
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 56 (a) (ii) of the Debt Conciliation Ordinance, Cap. 81.

statement: An executor or administrator cannot make a valid sale or pledge of the assets as security for, or in payment of his own debt.
supporting_quote: "If the executor be also specific legatee, a sale or mortgage from him of the specific legacy for satisfaction of his private debt will be safe, unless it can be shown that the purchaser or mortgagee knew there were debts unpaid."

statement: A co-owner can eject a trespasser from the land, which is held in common, without joining the other co-owners.
supporting_quote: "It is also settled principle of law that a co-owner can eject a trespasser from the land, which is held in common, without joining the other co-owners"

statement: A purchaser of different lands under the same deed of sale is entitled to recover such part of the purchase price paid by him as is proportionate to the value of the lands of which he has been unsuccessful in obtaining possession.
supporting_quote: "I therefore hold that the plaintiff is entitled to recover such part of the purchase price paid by him as is proportionate to the value of the lands of which he has failed to get possession."

statement: A right of servitude of light and air cannot be acquired by prescription through mere enjoyment, i.e., the mere fact that a neighbor has not built on their land for any length of time.
supporting_quote: "A right of servitude of light and air cannot be acquired by prescription by mere enjoyment, i.e., by the mere fact that the neighbour has not built on his land for any length of time. Pillay v. Fernando (1912) 14 N. L. R. 13S not followed."

statement: A partition action should be sent back to the trial court when new evidence, such as a marriage certificate, is produced that was not available during the initial hearing.
supporting_quote: We think it just and proper that we should set aside the judgment and decree and send the case back to the trial court in order that the certificate of the marriage registration may be produced.

statement: A plaintiff's registration of a lis pendens in the wrong folio does not convert that wrong folio into the correct one.
supporting_quote: Where a deed has been registered by the defendant in the wrong folio, the plaintiff's registration of the lis pendens in that folio cannot convert the wrong folio into the correct folio.

statement: A plaintiff may amend their pleadings to seek additional reliefs that are consequent on issues raised by the defendant, even if those reliefs appear inconsistent with earlier claims.
supporting_quote: "In the instant case, the plaintiff has not sought to amend the body of his plaint. The reliefs that the plaintiff is now seeking for are consequent on the issues raised by the counsel for the defendant which suggest that it was the plaintiff who had repudiated his terms and obligations under the deed of partnership by practising on his own. Even if one party accepts the repudiation of the other party the contract itself is not abrogated (vide Chitty on Contracts, Vol. 1, 22nd Edition, p. 323)."

statement: A claimant before the Acquiring Officer can move to have his claim amended after it is referred to court, different from what he had stated in his claim to the Acquiring Officer.
supporting_quote: "I am of the view that a claimant before the Acquiring Officer can move to have his claim amended after it is referred to Court, because the procedure provided for civil suits is applicable to proceedings before the Court: Sec. 93 of the Civil Procedure Code enables a party to have his pleadings amended provided the amendment sought does not offend against certain well defined principles which have time and again been stated in several cases."

statement: When two parties are entitled under the same decree to recover from each other sums of different amounts, the party entitled to the smaller sum shall not take out execution against the other party.
supporting_quote: "When two parties are entitled under the same decree to recover from each other sums of different amounts, the party entitled to the smaller sum shall not take out execution against the other party"

statement: A fideicommissum simplex is created when a donor transfers property to a fiduciary with the power of alienation, but the gift-over is to the legal heirs of the fiduciary if the fiduciary does not exercise the power of alienation.
supporting_quote: "The deed of gift created a fideicommissum simplex and that, as the transfer of 1st January 1924 was not a permitted alienation, the legal heirs of the fiduciary would be entitled to the property on the death of the fiduciary."

statement: A deed of donation creating a fideicommissum or usufruct, executed by a Muslim after Ordinance 10 of 1931 came into force, is governed by the Roman Dutch Law.
supporting_quote: "In view of these clear provisions any deed of donation executed by a Muslim, after Ordinance 10 of 1931 came into force, which creates a fideicommissum or usufruct, is clearly governed by the Roman Dutch Law, which is the law applicable in the Maritime provinces."

statement: The acceptance of a donation by the major brother on behalf of his minor siblings is valid if the donor has allowed such acceptance.
supporting_quote: However, it is now clear from Abeyewardene v. West that in the case of a donation made by parents, acceptance of the donation by the brother-in-law and the brothers of the minor donee is good, for the reason that the donors have allowed such acceptance to be made on behalf of the minor child.

statement: A clause which vests property in the donees 'and their heirs executors administrators and assigns' is merely a mode of vesting the full dominium in the donees themselves.
supporting_quote: "Therefore all the right title claim and interest of me the said donor and of my heirs executors administrators and assigns in and to the said four portions of land hereby gifted shall vest in the above-named three children of my said son and in the children that may be born to him in the future and their heirs executors administrators and assigns and they may after the death of the said Marthelis Silva and Sethan Silva Hamine possess the same, for which I have hereby granted and set over the same as a gift."

statement: A Si sine liberis decesserit clause does not necessarily indicate an intention to create a fideicommissum in favor of the children of a deceased devisee.
supporting_quote: "But the mere fact that the children of one deceased donee are thus nominated as heirs after the death of another donee is no indication of an intention to fetter the property in the hands of a donee who in fact has issue."

statement: Where a fideicommissum created by Last Will designates not only the children of the devisees but also includes their grandchildren, the rights of the grandchildren whose father predeceased his mother are unaffected.
supporting_quote: The rights of a devisee's grandchildren whose father predeceases his mother (the devisee) are not affected.

statement: The seizure of a car under a hire-purchase agreement without proper legal procedures is unlawful and intended to cause wrongful loss.
supporting_quote: "If the seizure was unlawful the accused obviously intended to cause wrongful loss to Senanayake."

statement: A Kandyan's right to revoke a deed of gift is not an equitable right, but rather a statutory right given by the Declaration and Amendment of Kandyan Law Ordinance (Cap. 59).
supporting_quote: "The right of the donor to revoke his deed of gift is not an equitable right since the donee, under a Kandyan deed of gift, had full dominium over the property"

statement: A Kandyan deed of gift executed after the Kandyan Law Declaration and Amendment Ordinance came into operation is irrevocable if the donor has expressly renounced his right to revoke, even if an undertaking was given by the donee to give succour and assistance during the donor's lifetime.
supporting_quote: "A Kandyan deed of gift executed after the Kandyan Law Declaration and Amendment Ordinance came into operation is irrevocable if the donor has expressly renounced his right to revoke and, although an undertaking was given by the donee to give succour and assistance to the donor during the donor's life-time, the undertaking was not one of the conditions on which the grant was made to the donee by the donor."

statement: A notice for a monthly tenancy must be given at the beginning of a month and terminate at the end of that same month.
supporting_quote: "If the tenancy commences on the first day of a calendar month, the month's notice may be given at any time on the first day of a subsequent month and it is effective to terminate the lease at the end of that month."

statement: A District Court's order nisi for probate is valid even if no respondent is named or heirs are not mentioned, provided the court exercises its discretion to serve notice appropriately.
supporting_quote: An Order Nisi is an order which the Court may make on a petition by way of summary procedure; as the words indicate, it is an order which will take effect unless cause is shown against it. The party against whom relief is sought must be made a respondent to the petition, and a copy of the Order Nisi should be served on him (Section 374 (c) Civil Procedure Code) so that he may have the opportunity of showing cause against it.
statute_citation_verbatim: Civil Procedure Code, ss. 374 (c), 525

statement: The transaction between the parties was not a lease of a building but of a business, and the defendant's position while occupying the premises is no more than that of a licensee.
supporting_quote: "I have no doubt, on a consideration of the indenture and the contemporaneous writing, that the transaction was merely one of placing the lessee in charge of the hotel business for a definite period with a view to his carrying it on for three years : the lessee was also, in order to fulfil this Agreement, put in possession of the premises in which that business was being run. There was no agreement here to rent the premises, nor was the rent agreed on between the parties payable in respect of the premises. The defendant's position while he is in occupation of those premises is no more than that of a licensee."

statement: The Court found that the plaintiffs had established a prescriptive title to the land based on Dr. M. G. Perera's possession from 1941 to 1953.
supporting_quote: "Their Lordships consider that Mr. Wickremasinghe when he referred to 'the land' was clearly referring to that which was bought in 1941 and sold in 1953, i.e. the 50 acres 27 perches, and this being established, they cannot accept that there was no evidence on which a finding of 10 years uninterrupted possession of that land-regard being had to its nature, i.e., mainly jungle land-could properly be made."

statement: A sale under the Partition Act does not preserve life interests, usufructs, or other encumbrances declared in an interlocutory decree.
supporting_quote: "it is clear that when, in pursuance of an order for the sale of a land, a certificate of sale of the land is entered in terms of section 46 of the Partition Act, the title which the certificate of sale confers on the purchaser of the land and buildings thereon is free from any life interest or usufruct which may be declared in favour of a person in the interlocutory decree entered under section 26, read with section 48, of the Act"
statute_citation_verbatim: section 46 of the Partition Act

statement: In a partition decree assigning lots to a family group without defining the interests of the members inter se, subsequent actions may be instituted for further partitioning.
supporting_quote: "Where a partition decree assigns certain lots to a number of persons as a group who derive their title from the same source, without defining the interests of the members of that group inter se, a subsequent partition action may be instituted for the purpose of partitioning the land comprising the lots which were assigned to that group."

statement: The Supreme Court of Sri Lanka has the power to exercise its revisional jurisdiction over partition decrees, even when such decrees are stated to be conclusive against all persons.
supporting_quote: "I do not think that the insertion of the words I have quoted from section 48 (1) made any difference. The phrase is entirely tautologous."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 48(1) of the Partition Act, which provides: 'Every decree for partition or sale under this Act shall be good and conclusive against all persons whomsoever, subject to the decision on any appeal which may be preferred therefrom; and the right, share or interest awarded thereby shall be free from all encumbrances whatsoever other than those specified in that decree.'

statement: No intervention can be allowed in a partition action after an interlocutory decree has been entered.
supporting_quote: We are of the view that the application to set aside the decree and to be allowed to intervene could not possibly succeed, because no intervention can be allowed after interlocutory decree has been entered.

statement: A person is not entitled to intervene subsequently and have an interlocutory decree set aside on the ground of failure to register the action duly as a lis pendens under the Registration of Documents Ordinance, once an interlocutory decree has been entered in terms of section 26 of the Partition Act.
supporting_quote: "Where interlocutory decree has been entered in terms of section 26 of the Partition Act, a person is not entitled to avail himself of the provisions of section 48 (3) in order to intervene subsequently and have the decree set aside on the ground of failure to register the action duly as a lis pendens under the Registration of Documents Ordinance."
statute_citation_verbatim: Section 70(1) of the Partition Act

statement: Where, pending a partition action, a co-owner gifts to certain persons the shares to which he will be declared entitled in the action, the interests which are allotted in that action to the donor pass automatically to the donees when the final decree is entered.
supporting_quote: Where, pending a partition action, a co-owner gifts to certain persons the shares to which he will be declared entitled in the action, the interests which are allotted in that action to the donor pass automatically to the donees when the final decree is entered.

statement: The appellant's new argument that the respondent had not shown a right of way over the whole width of Lot D was not open to them as it was not raised in the Courts below.
supporting_quote: "In all these circumstances their Lordships are satisfied that the point was not open to the appellant and it follows that the appeal must fail."

statement: A right of way of necessity cannot be granted if there is another though less convenient path along which access can be had to the public road.
supporting_quote: "The onus lies on a person who claims a right of way of necessity to show that it is necessary for him to claim this right and when there is an alternative convenient route he cannot make this claim."

statement: An action for pre-emption on the basis of co-ownership is not maintainable in respect of a share of a land which has been possessed and dealt with in divided lots by amicable partition among the shareholders, with each other's knowledge and consent.
supporting_quote: "The larger land, as now depicted in the Plan X filed and on record was originally owned by one Vairathai. By P1 of 1920, Vairathai donated to her grand-daughter Perianayagam, the 2nd Plaintiff, an undivided one-third share of the larger land. Thereafter by P2 of 10th September 1929, Vairathai donated to her niece Kaveriammah another undivided one-third share of the larger land described as being of an extent of two and a quarter lms. Finally by deed No. 10175 of 21st October 1929 (3D5), Vairathai donated to her son Vairamuttu, of the larger land, a 'one-third share on the East in extent according to possession three-quarter fan., bounded on the East by the property of Perianayagam, on the West by the property of Perianayagam and on the South by Lane'."

supporting_quote: (1) That the evidence called on behalf of. the plaintiff was " more reliable " than the evidence called on behalf of the defendants since the plaintiff was able to produce the original deed on which he claimed the lands in question and also one of the attesting witnesses to prove the due execution of the deed whereas the defendants were unable to produce the original or a certified copy of their deed.
